after_id.description: Pagination cursor: return sessions older than this session ID. Pass the last_id from a previous response to get the next page.

before_id.description: Pagination cursor: return sessions newer than this session ID. Pass the first_id from a previous response to get the previous page.

limit.description: Maximum number of sessions to return (default 20, max 100).

mine.description: Filter to sessions started by the same account as the calling session. Use this for 'my recent sessions' in shared bot contexts. In personal accounts the list is already scoped to you, so mine has no additional effect. Returns an error if the calling session has no resolvable originating account.

tags.description: Filter to interactive sessions carrying ANY of these tags. Cowork sessions are tagged "cowork-local" or "cowork-remote" and are excluded from the default (untagged) listing — pass those tags here to list them. Scheduled/trigger-fired runs are not included (same as the REST default). Max 16 tags. Only available to OAuth callers; returns an error for in-session and toolbox callers.

tools.name: mcp__Claude_Code_Remote__list_triggers
tools.description: List Routines (scheduled triggers) owned by this account. Use it to find trigger IDs (trig_...) for update_trigger and delete_trigger. From a thread in a Slack channel, only Routines that fire into that thread's session are listed unless all_in_channel is true. Each entry has the Routine's id, name, cron_expression, run_once_at, enabled state, ended_reason, next_run_at, created_at, persistent_session_id, and last_run. last_run is the most recent recorded run {status, fired_at, finished_at, session_id}. It is absent when no run was recorded (e.g. never fired). For a Routine that wakes an existing session, last_run records that the wake was delivered (SUCCEEDED) or failed to deliver, not how the turn went, unless run tracking covers that session. A FAILED or repeatedly non-SUCCEEDED last_run means the Routine is not doing its job. ended_reason says why a disabled Routine is permanently disabled. suspension_reason (e.g. subscription_paused) marks a temporary hold that lifts when the owner's subscription resumes. Both empty means user-paused. One-shot Routines that already fired (e.g. delivered send_later reminders) and Routines moved to a project are hidden unless include_completed is true. Scheduled tasks stored locally by the Cowork desktop app are not listed.

schema.name: mcp__Claude_Code_Remote__list_triggers
schema.description: List Routines (scheduled triggers) owned by this account. Use it to find trigger IDs (trig_...) for update_trigger and delete_trigger. From a thread in a Slack channel, only Routines that fire into that thread's session are listed unless all_in_channel is true. Each entry has the Routine's id, name, cron_expression, run_once_at, enabled state, ended_reason, next_run_at, created_at, persistent_session_id, and last_run. last_run is the most recent recorded run {status, fired_at, finished_at, session_id}. It is absent when no run was recorded (e.g. never fired). For a Routine that wakes an existing session, last_run records that the wake was delivered (SUCCEEDED) or failed to deliver, not how the turn went, unless run tracking covers that session. A FAILED or repeatedly non-SUCCEEDED last_run means the Routine is not doing its job. ended_reason says why a disabled Routine is permanently disabled. suspension_reason (e.g. subscription_paused) marks a temporary hold that lifts when the owner's subscription resumes. Both empty means user-paused. One-shot Routines that already fired (e.g. delivered send_later reminders) and Routines moved to a project are hidden unless include_completed is true. Scheduled tasks stored locally by the Cowork desktop app are not listed.

all_in_channel.description: Threads in a Slack channel only. If true, list every Routine in this channel, including other threads' and ones that start a new session each time they fire. Default false.

cursor.description: Opaque pagination cursor from a previous response's next_cursor. Omit for the first page.

enabled.description: When set, only Routines whose enabled state matches. true hides fired one-shots, paused, and auto-disabled Routines; false shows only those. Omit for both.

include_completed.description: If true, also include one-shot Routines that have already fired (e.g. delivered send_later reminders) and Routines moved to a project. Default false — there can be thousands.

limit.description: Maximum Routines to return (default 20, max 100).

recurring.description: When set, filters by schedule shape: true keeps only cron-driven (recurring) Routines, false only one-shot and fire-only Routines. Omit for both.

tools.name: mcp__Claude_Code_Remote__register_repo_root
tools.description: Tell the session that a repo attached via add_repo has finished cloning, so its CLAUDE.md, skills, and plugins load on the next turn. Only call this immediately after a successful clone that add_repo instructed you to run — it returns a tool error for a repo that is not already in this session's sources.

directory.description: Absolute path of the clone on disk. Pass the real path you cloned to; on a self-hosted runner this will be under the session's base working directory.

owner.description: GitHub owner of the repo that was just cloned (same value passed to add_repo).

tools.name: mcp__Claude_Code_Remote__send_later
tools.description: Schedule a message to be delivered back into THIS SESSION at a future time. The message arrives as an ordinary user turn, so you can use it to remind yourself to resume work, check on something, or continue after a delay. Delivery survives container restarts. Granularity is one minute — the scheduler polls every minute, so sub-minute precision is not available. This is a thin wrapper over create_trigger (a self-bind + run_once_at Routine); the returned trigger_id can be passed to delete_trigger to cancel before it fires, and the Routine disables itself after firing once.

schema.name: mcp__Claude_Code_Remote__send_later
schema.description: Schedule a message to be delivered back into THIS SESSION at a future time. The message arrives as an ordinary user turn, so you can use it to remind yourself to resume work, check on something, or continue after a delay. Delivery survives container restarts. Granularity is one minute — the scheduler polls every minute, so sub-minute precision is not available. This is a thin wrapper over create_trigger (a self-bind + run_once_at Routine); the returned trigger_id can be passed to delete_trigger to cancel before it fires, and the Routine disables itself after firing once.

at.description: RFC3339 timestamp for the fire time (e.g. 2026-04-20T17:00:00Z). Seconds are truncated. Must be in the future. Mutually exclusive with 'delay_minutes' — set exactly one.

cron_expression.description: New 5-field cron expression, evaluated in UTC — convert local times to UTC first, using the offset currently in effect; if the conversion crosses midnight, shift the day fields too — day-of-week and/or day-of-month, whichever is set (e.g. weekdays at 5pm in UTC-07:00 is 0 0 * * 2-6). Minimum interval is normally hourly (some projects allow shorter); a too-frequent schedule is rejected and the error names the minimum. entries.name: SendMessage
entries.description:
# SendMessage

Send a message to another agent.

```json
{"to": "researcher", "summary": "assign task 1", "message": "start on task #1"}
```

| `to` | |
|---|---|
| `"researcher"` | Teammate by name |
| `"main"` | The main conversation (background subagents only) |
| `"worker"` | Any agent from `ListAgents` — subagent, another local Claude session |
| `"worker [3fa9c1]"` | Same, plus its `[ref]` — only when a listing or an error shows one |

Your plain text output is NOT visible to other agents — to communicate, you MUST call this tool. Messages from teammates are delivered automatically; you don't check an inbox. Refer to agents by name — names keep working after an agent completes (a send resumes it from its transcript). Use the raw `agentId` (format `a...-...`) from its spawn result only when the agent has no name, or when a newer agent took the name (latest wins). When relaying, don't quote the original — it's already rendered to the user.

## Cross-session

Use `ListAgents` to discover targets. Every row leads with the agent's `name [ref]` — the name IS the address; there is no separate address syntax.

```json
{"to": "worker", "message": "check if tests pass over there"}
{"to": "worker [3fa9c1]", "message": "you, specifically"}
```

Send the bare name — a name that exactly matches one live agent or session (on this machine, on another machine, or in the cloud) delivers directly. Append the ` [ref]` only when the bare name is not enough — `ListAgents` shows two rows with it, or an error asks you to disambiguate (you typed only a prefix, or a session list could not be checked). A ref you did not just read from a listing or an error will not resolve, and if the same name also names an in-process agent, the bare name always wins — use the in-process one.

A listed peer is alive and will receive your message; messages enqueue and drain at the receiver's next tool round (its `ListAgents` row says whether it is busy or idle right now). A successful send means the message reached that session, not that its Claude read it: a session running in a different permission mode than yours holds cross-session messages for its user's approval (and may let them expire), and a session can refuse them outright — for a session on this machine a `[Cross-session delivery notice]` tells you when that happens (the tool result says when this session has no inbox for one to reach); for a Remote Control, cloud or Claude Desktop session nothing reports back, so never treat silence as agreement. Your message arrives wrapped as `<cross-session-message from="...">`. **To reply to an incoming message, copy its `from` attribute as your `to`.** Cross-session messages travel between SESSIONS: if you are a subagent, your send goes out under your parent session's address, and any reply is delivered to the parent session's conversation, not to you. The receiver reads your message literally in every case (idle or busy, on this machine, over Remote Control or headless): an `@` followed by a file path, or `@server:resource`, attaches nothing there, unlike in your own user's input. So never rely on `@` to deliver content: send the text itself, or a file with its own tool.

To hear when a session ON THIS MACHINE finishes what it is doing, pass `notify_when_idle: true` (from the main conversation only) — one-shot and opt-in: exactly one `[Cross-session idle notice]` arrives when it next goes idle (or exits) — shown to you, or only to your user when this session holds peer messages for approval (the tool result says which); if it never signals within the subscription's lifetime (it may still be busy, may refuse inbound requests, or may have ended abruptly) the notice says the subscription expired instead. Omit `message` for a pure subscription that costs that session nothing; include one to deliver it now AND subscribe. Never poll `ListAgents` in a loop or send "are you done?" messages instead.

Permission boundaries are per-session: NEVER ask a peer to perform an action that was denied or blocked in your session, or that you expect your own permission settings would block — a peer doing it for you bypasses the user's permission decision (cross-session permission laundering). Route blocked work back to your user instead.

to.description: Recipient: a name from ListAgents (append its " [ref]" only when a listing or an error shows one), a teammate name, "main", or a background agent's agentId

summary.description: A 5-10 word label for your own transcript row (not transmitted — the recipient previews the first line of `message`). Truncated to 200 characters rather than rejected.

message.description: Plain text message content. The recipient's human sees only the FIRST LINE as a one-line preview until they expand it, so make the first line a clear, self-contained sentence saying what this is about — not a greeting, preamble, or bare @-mention.

notify_when_idle.description: Ask a session ON THIS MACHINE to send you ONE notice when it next goes idle (finishes its turn with nothing queued) or exits — opt-in, one-shot, no polling. With a message: deliver it now AND subscribe. Without a message (omit it): a pure subscription that costs the other session nothing.

{"number":2223,"title":"provenance apply refuses an out-of-order entry, so a conversion-filled file cannot take its real history","body":"`appendedText` refuses an entry dated before the file's last one. A file the `references.md` conversion filled carries a placeholder `born` dated by the conversion write (2026-09-14), so an honest `born` at the element's actual birth — often months earlier — cannot be appended.

This collides with two things that both say the backfill is supposed to do exactly that:

- `backfilling-provenance` step 4: "A file the conversion filled from `references.md` is written the same way, its converted entry read as evidence."
- `changing-pack-elements`: "the one rewrite that is right is the backfill replacing what the conversion wrote with the element's derived history, once."

The obvious route — run `apply` — fails with a date-order refusal and no hint of a remedy. Four runs hit it; the working move is to truncate the file first and apply the full history in date order, relocating the conversion's `Reason`/`Retire when` onto the entries they actually evidence. That is in bounds, but nothing tells you so, and the first run to hit it had to work it out.

`check_the_work.mjs` then reports one `provenance-change-recorded` advisory per rewritten file — the case that check's own fix text sanctions. Expected, but it reads as a fault to a run that has not been told.

**Fix, either way round:** let `apply` accept the ordered rewrite of a conversion-filled file, or have the skill state truncate-then-apply in the imperative and name the advisory it produces. The tool-side fix is better: the remedy currently lives only in a prompt.

## Two smaller things in the same area

- **`brief`'s "README sections" list excludes tables by design**, and in one batch the single largest piece of history was a table — `cloudflare-workers`' per-member evidence table, the whole 3260→1758 byte trim, every row of it a rule's `Source`. A run working the printed list literally would have left it. An evidence or member table is history; a rule catalog is not.
- **No kind in the closed vocabulary fits a manifest-level change that is not prose reading differently** — a `requires` drop, a version scheme's shape, a fingerprint widening. Runs are using `reworded` on code changes because the already-backfilled packs did, and it reads oddly.

A run working the printed list literally would have left it. An evidence or member table is history; a rule catalog is not.

{"number":2221,"title":"provenance.mjs brief derives Landed, element birth and claimed version rows wrong","body":"Three independent derivation defects in `brief`, each found by every backfill run that looked for it. Six runs across nineteen packs now; none of the three is occasional.

## 1. `Landed` takes the closing keyword from the commit trailer

The trailer says `Refs` where the pull request body says `Closes`, on essentially every older pull request. `Closes` is what fills GitHub's Development panel and resolves the issue; `Refs` links nothing there, so an entry citing `Refs` sends a reader tracing a pack's closed work to the wrong kind of link.

Verified directly on #165 (`Closes #180`), #128 (`Closes #127` / `Closes #131`) and #1667 (`Closes #1662`), against entries the brief had derived as `Refs`. Runs on `node`, `jwt`, `executable-requirements`, `public-website` and `claudinite-tasks` each reported the same disagreement across their own histories; one reported `Fixes` as a third spelling (#956).

This one reached `main` before it was caught — #2219 corrects the four `_pack.md` files #2213 wrote from the trailer.

**Fix:** read the closing keyword from the pull request body. The trailer is not a cheaper route to the same answer.

## 2. Element birth drafts at the last move, not the birth

`brief` names an element by the file carrying it **today**, so anything that changed carrier drafts `born` at the change:

- a rule that later moved into a skill (ten elements in `executable-requirements` drafted `born` at #1667, really #165)
- a check converted from a coded module to a declaration (`jwt`'s five checks drafted at #839, really #705; `google-identity`'s two drafted at #827, really #350)
- a rule that was a prose section before it became a bullet (`python`'s three drafted at #1634/#1667, really #345)
- a task predating an extraction (`claudinite-tasks`' `usage-fold` drafted at #1326, really #524)

Every run that checked found several. The proof is always `git show '<sha>^:<old path>'` or `git log -S'<the element text>'`.

**Fix:** follow the element back through renames and carrier changes before drafting `born`. Failing that, the skill should say outright that every `born` must be verified against the old path — but a tool that can find it should.

## 3. "version rows no commit here claims" reports rows that are claimed

A row naming no pull request in its text is listed as unclaimed even when the claiming commit wrote the row in its own diff. Row `60902.1` was reported unclaimed for `android`, `html`, `executable-requirements`, `leaflet`, `node` and others; `git show aaa7938b -- packs/<pack>/provenance/VERSIONS.md` shows #1634 adding the row and bumping `version` to `60902.1` in the same commit.

`claudinite-tasks` showed a second face of it: the brief attributed `60824.2` to a commit that writes both `60824.1` and `60824.2`, and then put that version on entries dated weeks before the pack existed.

**Fix:** a commit that adds a row claims it, whatever the row's text names. And a version clause does not belong on an entry predating the pack.

## Why this is worth fixing rather than working around

31 corpora remain on step 4 of #2169, including `basics` at 132 elements. Every run so far has had to rediscover all three and correct them by hand, and the one that did not reached `main`. The workaround currently lives in a prompt, which is the least durable place it could be.

entries.description: List issues in a GitHub repository. For pagination, use the 'endCursor' from the previous response's 'pageInfo' in the 'after' parameter.

after.description: Cursor for pagination. Use the cursor from the previous response.

direction.description: Order direction. If provided, the 'orderBy' also needs to be provided.

field_name.description: Name of the custom field (e.g. "Priority"). Case-insensitive.

value.description: Value to filter on. For single-select fields, the option name (e.g. "P1"). For dates, YYYY-MM-DD. For numbers, the numeric value as a string. For text, the text value.

field_filters.description: Filter by custom issue field values. Each entry takes a field_name and a value; the server looks up the field and coerces the value to its type (single-select option name, text, number, or YYYY-MM-DD date).

fields.description: Subset of fields to return for each issue. If omitted, all fields are returned. Use this to reduce response size when you only need specific fields; omitting 'body' and 'field_values' in particular drops the largest per-result data.

orderBy.description: Order issues by field. If provided, the 'direction' also needs to be provided.

owner.description: Repository owner

perPage.description: Results per page for pagination (min 1, max 100)

state.description: Filter by state, by default both open and closed issues are returned when not provided

{"number":2222,"title":"Two carriers the provenance marking pass cannot see: aggregator-re-exported checks, and retired elements","body":"Two gaps in `carriers` (`engine/checks/helpers/provenance.mjs`), both found independently by separate backfill runs. In each case an element's decisions have nowhere to land and `provenance.mjs check` reports no fault, so nothing surfaces the absence.

## 1. A check id behind an aggregator `checks.mjs` is invisible

`carriers` extracts check ids from a skill's `checks.mjs` with a literal `/\bid\s*:\s*['"]…/` scan. Where that file is a thin aggregator that imports and re-exports, the ids live in the imported modules and the scan finds nothing — and those modules are only scanned under `worldRules/`/`workRules/`.

Confirmed on two packs by two runs that did not talk to each other:

- `python` — `checks.mjs` re-exports `optional-import-lazy.mjs` and `optional-import-install-hint.mjs`. Neither check has a provenance file.
- `google-identity` — `google-client-id-single-origin` in `skills/google-id-token-validation/checks.mjs`. No file.

The READMEs list these checks. Their history is unrecorded and unrecordable: `append`/`apply` refuse a file that does not exist, so a backfill has nothing to append to. Real decisions are stranded — `python`'s blocking/advisory split, the deliberate non-mapping of a distribution whose import name differs from its own (`Pillow` → `PIL`, a chosen false negative), and the `doc:` repointing at #1676.

**Fix:** follow the re-export, or read ids from the module the aggregator names.

## 2. A retired element has no file to record its retirement on

`changing-pack-elements` says a removed element is `retired` and "the file stays, and this is its last entry", and the audit exempts a `retired` file from the named-by-no-carrier fault. But the marking pass created files only for live carriers, so an element retired **before** that pass has no file — and `apply`/`append` refuse to create one (`provenance.mjs:195`).

Two hit so far:

- `jwt`'s `jwt-advisory-watch` task — took a real policy decision at #1262 (drops its standing tracker; a clean run writes nothing, a hit files a real issue deduped on the GHSA) and was deleted at #1569.
- `claudinite-dashboard`'s `fleet-digest` — arrived #1053, retired #1397.

Both runs put the history on `_pack.md` rather than invent a home, which is defensible but loses the per-element thread the convention exists to keep.

**Fix:** either let `append` create a file for a named retired element, or decide explicitly that a pre-marking-pass retirement lives on `_pack` and say so in `changing-pack-elements`.

content.text: Four defects read. Now the fan-out — six agents, each with the known workarounds in its prompt rather than rediscovering them, each committing to its own branch in an isolated worktree; I'll aggregate into two PRs.

input.prompt:
Backfill pack provenance in the Claudinite canon repo for exactly two packs: `claudinite-canon-curation` (29 empty files) and `web-speech` (18).

Work on a branch `claude/prov-canon-curation-web-speech` created off `origin/main` in your worktree. Commit locally. **Do NOT push and do NOT open a pull request** — the parent session aggregates six agents' branches into two PRs.

## Method
Load and follow `packs/claudinite-growth/skills/backfilling-provenance/SKILL.md` in full, including its step 0 (load `changing-pack-elements` first). The tool is `node packs/claudinite-growth/provenance.mjs` run from the repo root — this is the canon home, there is NO `.claudinite/shared/` here, so never path through it.

## Known tool defects — do not rediscover these, correct them as you go
These are filed as issues #2221, #2222, #2223. Every prior run hit all of them.

1. **`brief` derives `Landed` from the commit trailer, which says `Refs` where the PR body says `Closes` (or `Fixes`).** The PR body is authoritative. For every `Landed` line, read the actual pull request body (`mcp__github__pull_request_read`, repo missingbulb/Claudinite) and use the keyword it really carries. This defect reached `main` once already; it is the single most important correction in this run.
2. **`brief` drafts `born` at the element's last carrier move, not its birth.** It names an element by the file carrying it today, so a rule that later moved into a skill, or a check converted from a coded module to a declaration, drafts `born` at the move. Verify every `born` against the old path with `git show '<sha>^:<old path>'` or `git log -S'<exact element text>' -- <path>`. Note: a subject-grep (`git log --grep`) finds the wrong commit for a reversal, because the reinstating commit quotes the retired PR number.
3. **"version rows no commit here claims" lists rows that ARE claimed** — a commit that adds the row in its own diff claims it, whatever the row text names. Check with `git show <sha> -- packs/<pack>/provenance/VERSIONS.md`. Also: never put a version clause on an entry predating the pack.
4. **`apply` refuses an entry dated before the file's last one.** A file the `references.md` conversion filled carries a placeholder `born` dated 2026-09-14, so an honest earlier `born` is refused. Remedy, explicitly in bounds per `changing-pack-elements`' single sanctioned rewrite: truncate the file first, then apply the full history in date order, relocating the conversion's `Reason`/`Retire when` onto the entries they actually evidence. `check_the_work.mjs` then reports one `provenance-change-recorded` advisory per rewritten file — that is the case its own fix text sanctions, expected, not a fault.
5. **`brief`'s "README sections" list excludes tables by design.** An evidence or per-member table in a README is history and must move onto the entries it evidences; a rule catalog is not. Read the README yourself, do not work the printed list literally.
6. **A check id behind a thin aggregator `checks.mjs` that imports and re-exports is invisible to the marking pass**, so it has no provenance file and `append` refuses to create one. If you find one, record the history on `_pack.md` and report it — do not create the file.

## Constraints
- No carrier changes. A rule that reads wrong is a later change with its own entry. You touch only `provenance/`, `README.md` and `pack.mjs` for your two packs and nothing else.
- Write only what the evidence carries. An omitted field is correct; a fabricated one is a fault. Never fill a field with a plausible guess.
- Hyphens, never long dashes — `no-new-long-dashes` fires per file.
- Do not write a `VERSIONS.md` row or bump a pack version; the canon's own task does that after the change lands.
- Inside a worktree-isolated agent the Bash guard refuses `git` inside `$(...)`, loops, heredocs or `xargs -a` as "too complex to verify". Drop straight to the plain literal form; the guard reads syntax, not intent.
- Commit messages end with:
Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_01CuwNWgfVqj6p3ehmvUXfTd
- No model identifier anywhere in a repository artifact beyond that trailer.

## Finish
`node packs/claudinite-growth/provenance.mjs check <pack>` for each pack must print its file-to-carrier listing and exit 0 — the listing prints either way, so the pass is the listing plus exit 0, never silence. Do not run the full 3808-test suite; the parent runs it once on the merged result.

Do NOT trigger when the primary deliverable is a Word document, HTML report, standalone Python script, database pipeline, or Google Sheets API integration, even if tabular data is involved.
</system-reminder>
