> * Add product-wiki pack: the self-growing product research wiki standard
>
> Six checks (layout, page-sections, growth-log, sources, freshness advisory,
> and a fixed isolation barrier composed on the barriers engine), ~30 lines of
> RULES.md prose for what checks can't carry, and a weekly run_daily growth
> task whose worker doc owns the compile-once/refine-in-place research method
> (cited claims, dated growth log, PR-never-merge delivery, no fabricated
> growth). The wiki set is structural — everything under product/ except the
> reserved product-requirements/ (human-reviewed sink, the one crossing point)
> and sample-data/ is wiki space — so there is no manifest to drift and a
> renamed wiki folder stays checked and barred.
>
> Verified: 23 unit tests (fixture repos, violation-first), the full corpus
> suite (307 passing), a clean conformance sweep on the canon itself, and a
> 12/12 end-to-end mutation matrix against the real GoogleCalendarEventCreator
> tree (pre-adoption fires exactly the expected findings; post-adoption is
> clean; the barrier fails closed on an empty product/).
>
> * Harden the product-wiki checks from adversarial review (Refs #302)
>
> Review findings applied:
> - freshness keyed a page's age on ANY date-shaped string in the Growth log
>   section, so a recent date inside an old entry's prose silently reset the
>   staleness clock — the one failure mode the advisory exists to observe. It
>   now shares lib.mjs's DATED entry grammar (and round-trip calendar
>   validation) with the growth-log check, discarding far-future typos, and
>   takes an injectable ctx.now so the 45-day boundary is pinned by test.
> - "+"-marked bullets bypassed the dating and citation rules; the shared
>   BULLET/DATED grammar now covers -, * and +.
> - section headings inside fenced code blocks satisfied page-sections and
>   hijacked which lines the section checks scanned; all section readers now
>   blank fenced content (an embedded template is neither a section nor a log).
> - a hard-wrapped Sources bullet whose URL lands on its continuation line was
>   a blocking false positive; bullets are judged over their whole block, and a
>   bare URL now verifies (the invariant is reachability, not link typography).
> - layout flagged a freshly written, not-yet-staged scaffold; it now accepts
>   untracked files (ctx.files) alongside tracked ones.
> - the fixed barrier's crossing findings carried the engine's generic "add a
>   reviewed exception" fix text — an instruction that cannot resolve a
>   pack-shipped barrier's finding; defineBarrier gains an additive
>   crossingExcuse override (default text unchanged) pointing at the accept
>   lever, and the edge switches matchUniqueFilenames off so agent-written wiki
>   filenames never become repo-wide barred bare names.
> - dedup: path constants, bullet/date grammar, and the heading contract are
>   spelled once in lib.mjs and shared by every check, the manifest, and the
>   barrier; the reserved-subtree test uses the barriers engine's under().
> - docs: RULES.md no longer restates check-enforced rules or names a specific
>   consumer; packs/README.md's ratio line matches the new 37-check tally; the
>   redundant reasonless-accept CLI test half (owned by checks/test/
>   runner.test.mjs) is dropped.
>
> * product-wiki pack: adopt the product-wiki/ root layout (Refs #302)
>
> The standard's canonical layout is now product-wiki/ (not product/), with the
> reviewed sink at product-wiki/product-requirements/ and sample-data/ reserved —
> matching the consumer restructure. Path constants live once in lib.mjs so the
> change is: PRODUCT_ROOT/SINK_DIR/SAMPLE_DATA_DIR/INDEX_README/SINK_README + the
> wikiPages regex, which the manifest marker/detect, the layout check, and the
> isolation barrier all follow. Comments, RULES.md, README.md, the worker doc, the
> catalog rows, and the fixture tests are repointed to product-wiki/.

# Backfilling a pack's provenance

The marking pass gave every carrier an empty file; this is how the history goes in. It is a
one-off done by hand because the judgment is what the pass is for: which sentence of a README
is history, which commit was the decision, which field the evidence carries and which it does
not. The tool gathers; every call it cannot make honestly it hands over rather than guessing,
so the sections it prints without a draft under them are the run's work, not its leftovers.

## The run, per pack

0. **Load [changing-pack-elements](../changing-pack-elements/SKILL.md) first.** The run edits
   `provenance/`, `README.md` and `pack.mjs`, each of which forces it - but `apply` writes
   through the tool rather than `Edit`, and the pre-edit guard reads only `Edit`/`Write`, so
   nothing holds the run until the Stop hook, with every file already written.
1. **Take one pack** and list what is owed: `node packs/claudinite-growth/provenance.mjs
   check <pack>` prints what each file is named by and which are empty; a file holding only
   the conversion's entry is owed too (in a member the tool is
   `.claudinite/shared/packs/claudinite-growth/provenance.mjs`).
2. **Write the brief**, source-first: `provenance.mjs brief <pack> > brief.md` (an element
   list after the pack narrows it to those files) reads every empty file's history out of
   git, pull request first: each commit's body once, then a draft entry per element it bore
   or changed with the fields git vouches for - the date, the kind, the actor, the model,
   the carrier as `Mechanism`, `Landed` with the version - and the commit's shared fields in
   one `entry-defaults` fence ahead of its entries. Read the tracker comments and the issues
   each body names on GitHub; `history <pack> <element>` prints one element's raw evidence
   where the brief's derivation looks wrong. A shallow clone reads as no history: unshallow
   before trusting an empty brief.
3. **Work the commit inventory before the drafts.** The drafts cover what a carrier's own
   text shows changing, which is less than the pack's history; the brief's *every commit that
   touched this pack* table is the rest, each row carrying the files it touched, the version
   row that claims it, and what it drafts. Two kinds of row are where the decisions hide. A
   row reading **NOTHING DRAFTED** changed something no carrier's text shows - a manifest
   field, a rule's rationale moving out to the README - so read its files before passing it.
   A row marked **sweep** is kept out of the drafts because a sweep usually re-wraps what it
   touches, but where its diff shows it *deciding* something about one element, that element
   owes the entry: touching twelve packs is not deciding nothing here. Read the version rows
   with them, the claimed ones and the *version rows no commit here claims* section alike -
   a row is the maintainer's own words for the decision a version was cut for, and often the
   only place a move is described as a decision at all.
4. **Derive the entries from that evidence before re-reading the rule**, then diff against
   what the rule implied. The first entry is `born` - where the lesson came from, why it
   says what it says, who decided, the carrier and its trigger and why (`Mechanism`), what
   lost (`Rejected`), what would retire it, and `Landed` as the pull request and pack
   version. Then one entry per decision the history shows: a rewording, a split, a move
   into a skill, a conversion to a check, a severity change, a policy change. A file the
   conversion filled from `references.md` is written the same way, its converted entry read as
   evidence: the `Reason` and `Retire when` go on the entries they evidence, and the
   placeholder `born` dated by the references write goes with the rest of the file.
5. **Write only what the evidence carries.** A field with nothing behind it is omitted,
   never filled with a placeholder or a plausible guess: a fabricated rationale lets a
   future review reaffirm a rule on false grounds, which is worse than no rationale. An
   element whose history the evidence does not reach gets a `born` entry that says only
   what is known - the date and commit it first appears in - and stays as short as that.
   Where the pack's evidence names a member per rule rather than rule by rule, the shared
   `Source` goes on the defaults fence and the per-element one is left off: an attribution
   split finer than the evidence is a guess wearing a citation.
6. **Write the entries in hyphens**, not long dashes - `no-new-long-dashes` fires on
   every file that carries one, and a backfill writing a pack's history in one pass earns
   the finding twenty-nine times over and a second commit to undo it.
7. **Edit the brief, then apply it**: `Source`, `Reason`, `Rejected` and `Retire when` go on
   the commit's defaults fence where every element it bore shares them, and on one entry
   where they are its own; a draft the commit did not decide is deleted, and the kind a
   draft guessed (`reworded` for any later commit) is corrected to what the change was.
   `provenance.mjs apply <pack> brief.md` validates every entry as one batch, appends each
   once under its defaults, and writes nothing while any one is refused; run twice it
   appends nothing. An entry the brief cannot carry - a split across files, a declined
   candidate - goes through `append <pack> <element>`, the entry on stdin. A mechanism the
   pack shares across elements - why a skill loads on these paths, why the release set
   vendors as stubs - is written once, on the element that owns it, and cited from the
   others.
8. **Trim the README and the manifest's header comment in the same change.** Each sentence
   of history the README holds (the "distilled from" paragraph, the "until #n", the "kept
   as it was", a mechanism's reasons) is evidence this run has already read, so it moves
   onto the entry it evidences and leaves the README, which keeps only what a person
   adopting the pack does with it. Work the brief's *README sections* list rather than its
   sentence tells: the tells find history that dates or numbers itself, while a section
   explaining why an element reads as it does carries neither and is the half most often
   left behind. The header comment of `pack.mjs` is the pack-level
   record `_pack.md` is written from - why the pack exists, why it fingerprints as it does
   or not at all, what it carries and why - so its decisions become `_pack` entries and the
   header keeps what a reader of the code needs: what the pack is, in a few lines. Report
   both files' bytes before and after in the pull request body.
9. **Candidates the history shows were turned down** - an extraction the owner declined, a
   conversion judged not checkable - go on `_declined.md`, kind `declined`, with `Source`,
   `Reason` and `Actor`, so the next pass reads them before nominating.
10. **Finish with `provenance.mjs check <pack>` reporting no fault** - it prints its
    file-to-carrier listing either way, so the pass is that listing alone and exit 0, never
    silence - the repo's offline suite green, and a pull request carrying the pack's
    provenance files, its trimmed README, its trimmed manifest and nothing else, titled `Provenance: backfill <pack>` and referencing
    the tracking issue. One pack per pull request is the default, and a pack whose elements
    arrived across several pull requests stays one; what a run costs is the reading, so
    packs whose history is one pull request apiece batch into one. Predict the automerge
    policy as each pack's `provenance/`, `README.md` and `pack.mjs` - the manifest trim is
    part of the method - and name the packs rather than reaching for a `packs/**` wildcard,
    which stops the policy being a prediction of the diff.

## What never happens here

- No carrier changes. A rule that reads wrong is a later change with its own entry; the
  backfill records what was decided, not what should have been.
- No entry restates the rule. The carrier is the description; the entry is the decision.
- No `Actor` is an email, no session id or quoted exchange lands in a canon file, and no
  field is written to look complete.

# sheepdog — the fleet enforcer marker

Declaring this pack marks a repo as the **fleet enforcer**: the one repo that covers and maintains
every repo under an owner. It's opt-in — a dedicated `sheepdog` repo declares it (it is **not** seeded
by `--init`).

It contributes the pieces only a fleet enforcer needs — the **cross-repo sweeps** — plus their
config schema and the scheduled tasks that run them. The rest of the machinery — running the
daily-run (the orchestrator), the task engine (`engine/scheduler/`), scheduling — is Claudinite
**core**, because the update task and the daily-run are Claudinite's own responsibility, not
the pack's.

**Five tasks** — separate, because they close on unrelated conditions. The **roster sweep**
([check-fleet-roster.mjs](tasks/fleet-roster/check-fleet-roster.mjs)) walks the fleet once and
answers two questions from that one walk: *is this repo a member*, converging `fleet-adoption`
issues ([adoption-issues.mjs](tasks/fleet-roster/adoption-issues.mjs)), and *is that membership
still meaning anything*, converging `fleet-drift` issues
([drift-issues.mjs](tasks/fleet-roster/drift-issues.mjs)). The second question exists because
per-project scheduling made every member maintain itself and removed the last outside look at one:
self-maintenance cannot detect its own absence. They share a walk rather than a task each because
each used to re-derive the other's classification and the two could disagree
([#788](https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/issues/788)); what stays separate is the two
**issue families**, never the enumeration. The **missing-packs task**
([fleet-add-missing-packs](tasks/fleet-add-missing-packs/task.md)) asks whether a member's declared pack
set still *matches the repo* — by fingerprint on its weekly scan
([scan-for-needed-packs.mjs](tasks/fleet-add-missing-packs/scan-for-needed-packs.mjs)), or from what the
owner named on a forced run ([force-add-packs.mjs](tasks/fleet-add-missing-packs/force-add-packs.mjs)) —
and, per member with work, converges an `add-packs` work-list issue **in that member** and fires that
member's own scheduler at its adopt-requested-packs task (grow_with_claudinite): the fan-out model
([#749](https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/issues/749)) — the enforcer dispatches, the member
executes. It exists because a pack's `detect`
fingerprint is consulted exactly once, at bootstrap's `--init`: the update flows backfill the seeded packs
and each declared pack's `requires` closure but never re-fingerprints, so a member that grows into a
pack after adoption is never told the pack exists. The **usage sweep**
([aggregate-fleet-usage.mjs](tasks/fleet-usage/aggregate-fleet-usage.mjs)) asks *what does the fleet
actually use* and writes `usage-fleet.GENERATED.json` — a file, not issues, because it reports a
measurement rather than a condition to converge. It exists because a member folds its own skill-usage
numbers and can therefore only say whether a skill loads *there*; whether a skill earns its place at
all is fleet-shaped, and nothing inside a member can see it. The **pack-seed sweep**
([check-fleet-pack-seeds.mjs](tasks/fleet-pack-seeds/check-fleet-pack-seeds.mjs)) asks *does each member
declare what this fleet standardizes on* and **adds the declaration** where it is missing. It exists
because some packs need a parameter no member can derive — the answer is a fact about the fleet, and canon
cannot supply it either, since a bootstrap run does not know which fleet it is bootstrapping into. Only
this repo knows: it is the fleet.

**The pack-seed sweep is the one that writes to members**, and it stays narrow on purpose: one pack
declaration from this repo's `packSeeds` list, one PUT to the member's default branch guarded by the blob
sha the read returned, idempotent, no issue in either direction. Three rules keep it safe. It **names no
pack** — every id comes from the config, so the enforcer never becomes a second place packs are known. It
**gates on the member's own mount**: a declared pack whose code is absent is a blocking `config` error
there, and a member's mount carries only what it declared as of its last converge, so the sweep writes
only where the pack is already on disk — `not-vendored` is a wait, not a finding, and members converge
nightly, so the rollout needs no coordination. And it **seeds, never overrides**: a member that already
declares the pack, or already carries a config for it, keeps both — the fleet's list is a floor, and a
choice a repo made is a decision the sweep cannot second-guess. A dormant member is never written to.

Because it seeds and never overrides, **a wrong seed reaches each member exactly once and then sticks**
— correcting it here un-writes nothing, so it has to be right before the sweep runs. This repo states
a seeded pack's config in **two** places: the `packSeeds` entry the fleet is given, and its own entry
for that pack, which is what a session *here* runs. For every seeded pack this repo also declares,
those two must carry the **same** config — nothing compares them at seed time, and a member has no way
to know what the enforcer kept for itself. Agreement is **exact**, because nothing here may know one
pack's defaults: spell a default out on both sides rather than leaving one implicit. A pack the fleet
standardizes on but this repo does not itself run has nothing to agree with.

A pack arriving with canon reaches the fleet that already exists through a **baseline migration** instead
(a `declarePacks` op, applied by each member's own update run in the same transactional commit that
vendors the pack's code). This sweep is the **standing** half: a migration record is dated and retires,
while the sweep keeps converging every member the fleet acquires after it is gone.

**One manual lever, riding the same task machinery** — [force-fleet-baseline.mjs](tasks/fleet-baseline/force-fleet-baseline.mjs)
fires every covered member's own `claudinite-scheduler.yml` with `overrides: FORCE_TASKS=update`,
which is the same button the owner would press in that repo's Actions tab, pressed across the fleet in
one run. It is a **dispatcher, not a maintainer**: each member converges its own mount, with its own
token, under its own delivery policy, and this writes nothing to any member — one queued Actions run
each, and no commit, issue or comment. Under per-project scheduling the fleet needs no push in the
ordinary case; this is for the un-ordinary ones — a canon change the fleet should pick up *now*, or the
tail of members whose next slot is hours away while someone is standing by. A forced run bypasses
the update task's precondition, so a member with nothing to do converges to a cheap no-op: over-using it is
wasteful, never unsafe. A **dormant** member is skipped and reported (it stopped its own scheduler on
purpose); `include_dormant` overrides that. Canon is skipped — its own update self-skips — but the
enforcer repo is **not**: it is an ordinary member, and leaving it out would make the one repo the owner
is watching the one repo that did not move.

**The pack ships no workflow.** The standalone fleet-baseline workflow — and the `.github/` managed
copy it forced every enforcer to host, deliverable only by the withhold-and-hand-to-the-agent path
([#649](https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/issues/649)) — was retired on 2026-08-11
([#749](https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/issues/749); the
[`fleet-baseline-task`](migrations/2026-08-11-fleet-baseline-task/migration.mjs) record removes
lingering copies). The lever is now the [`fleet-baseline`](tasks/fleet-baseline/task.md) task,
`frequency: manual`: never due on any cadence, run by pressing *Run workflow* on the vendored
scheduler with `overrides: FORCE_TASKS=fleet-baseline` (plus `REPOS=…`, `DRY_RUN=true`,
`INCLUDE_DORMANT=true`). It fires each member's own scheduler with `FORCE_TASKS=update` and does
**not** wait: a dispatch queues a member's own run, and each member reports its own outcome where it
always does.

**Where the code lives** — each sweep sits **inside its task's folder**, because only that task's
`worker.mjs` uses it. The pack root holds just what they all
need: [fleet-api.mjs](fleet-api.mjs) (cross-repo REST primitives — read-only toward members but for the
one `putFile` the pack-seed sweep needs) and
[fleet-config.mjs](fleet-config.mjs) (the one reader of the entry `config` below).

**Config** — this repo's `.claudinite-checks.json` carries, as its `packs` entry for this pack:

```json
{ "id": "sheepdog", "config": { "owner": "missingbulb", "kind": "user", "exclude": ["owner/repo-a"],
                                "canonRepo": "missingbulb/Claudinite", "staleDays": 14,
                                "packSeeds": [{ "id": "<a pack>", "config": { … } }] } }
```

`owner` (default: this repo's owner) is who to cover; `exclude` is the repos deliberately kept out of
the fleet (a full `owner/name` each) — a repo is kept out by adding it here. `kind: "user"` today; org
support is a later addition. `canonRepo` (default `<owner>/Claudinite`) is what a member's stamped ref
is measured against — named rather than inferred, because a ref tells you nothing about where it came
from. `staleDays` (default `14`) is how far behind is too far. `packSeeds` (default: **none**) is what
this fleet wants every member to declare — each `{ id, config? }`, seeded into members that lack it. This
list is the **only** place a pack is named: the sweep carries the mechanism, the fleet carries the
choice. All three default, so an existing sheepdog config keeps working untouched.

**Classification** — the roster, usage and pack-seed sweeps are ordinary **pack tasks**,
not fleet mechanisms. Their *implementation* — an account-spanning PAT — happens to scan every repo
under the owner, but their declaration, scheduling, and lifecycle are exactly those of any pack task.
None declares the `fleet` signal; the cross-repo reach lives in the implementation, never in how a
task is wired. (The task files carry the same note.)

**No agent, no session scope, anywhere in this pack.** Every task here is `agent_model: none`; the
agentic work a fleet operation needs happens in the *member*, run by that member's own executor
under its own grant. That is not an implementation detail but the trust model
([#749](https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/issues/749)), learned the hard way: the first
fleet-add-missing-packs design ended in an enforcer-side agent stage, and its very first production
run stopped at `needs-human` because the enforcer's executor is — correctly — scoped to the enforcer
repo alone. What crosses a repo boundary is an issue and a `workflow_dispatch`, both over the
`FLEET_GITHUB_TOKEN` PAT; the deprecated task-level `session_scope`
([scheduled-tasks.md](../core/scheduled-tasks.md)) has no place here.

**A SCANNED finding is a recommendation, never a verdict.** The `pack-declaration` conformance check was
deliberately retired ([engine/checks/README.md](../../engine/checks/README.md)) because whether to
declare a pack is the project's call — a marker is a way to *suspect* a pack is wanted, never proof it
must be. The scan must not re-introduce that check one rung further out: it opens an issue in the member that
the member's own agent (then a reviewer) acts on, its body says "suspects", and a `not planned` close
is a standing answer the scan honours rather than reopening weekly. A **forced** addition is the other
thing entirely — a decision already made, by the one person entitled to make it — so its issue carries
the config and the interview answers with it, and the member's agent adopts what it says rather than
re-judging whether it was wanted.

**The scan fingerprints against CANON, not against this repo's mount.** A consumer's
`.claudinite/shared/` carries the vendor set for the packs *it* declares — four, for a sheepdog repo —
so running the fingerprints out of the mount would test every member against a handful of packs and
report the whole fleet as perfectly fitted. That failure is silent by construction, so the sweep
shallow-clones `canonRepo` to scratch, loads the corpus from there, refuses to run at all on a corpus
too small to be canon, and **states the denominator in its report** (*"fingerprinted against N canon
packs from `owner/Claudinite`"*). Fetching also makes the fingerprints current rather than as-of this
enforcer's last baseline: a pack added to canon this week is one the fleet should be measured against
this week.

**Undecidable is not a non-match.** Most fingerprints are answerable from a path listing, and the sweep
answers those over one tree call per member. A fingerprint that reads file *contents* is resolved by a
bounded prefetch of exactly the files it asked for; one that greps every source file exceeds that budget
and is reported **undecided**, never `false`. The member's own agent — which has the repo checked out —
settles those exactly (`localFits`, [tasks/fleet-add-missing-packs/fingerprint-fit.mjs](tasks/fleet-add-missing-packs/fingerprint-fit.mjs)).
A truncated tree listing makes every non-match on that repo undecided for the same reason: "we did not
look" and "we looked and it isn't there" are different facts, and only one is safe to act on.

**How they run** — as the pack's [`fleet-roster`](tasks/fleet-roster/task.md) (`daily`),
[`fleet-add-missing-packs`](tasks/fleet-add-missing-packs/task.md)
(`weekly`), [`fleet-usage`](tasks/fleet-usage/task.md) (`daily`) and
[`fleet-pack-seeds`](tasks/fleet-pack-seeds/task.md) (`daily`) and
[`fleet-baseline`](tasks/fleet-baseline/task.md) (`manual`) scheduled tasks, each with its
sweep as `prework`. All are `agent_model: none` and `expected_outcome: none` — what only a repo edit
can finish is the member's own adopt-requested-packs task's, ceilinged at `open-pr` *there*,
because declaring a pack switches on checks that run in the member's CI the moment they land, so it is
always reviewed; the usage sweep is `merged-pr`, because its output IS a tracked file and an
auto-merging PR keeps that write inside the outcome taxonomy, lets this repo's CI gate a malformed
file, and makes the daily PR stream a browsable audit trail. The pack-seed sweep is `none` for a
different reason: its write goes to **other** repos, and the ceiling describes what a task may do to its
own. The roster is daily on its coverage question's cadence, and its freshness half rides along
rather than gating itself on a weekly clock it would have to compute — two extra reads per covered
member, and a drift verdict that is silent unless the root cause changed; usage is
daily because the members fold daily; pack seeds is daily because a member becomes writable the moment
its nightly converge vendors the pack, and daily makes that "the next morning". There is **no coverage workflow** — preprocessing
runs Action-side inside this repo's one scheduler workflow, so the repo Actions secret is already
reachable there; each task's `required_secrets: ['FLEET_GITHUB_TOKEN']` stamps the name into that
workflow's env and is what asks the owner for it (a fine-grained PAT spanning the owner's repos:
Metadata read, **Contents read and write**, Issues read/write — the roster's freshness half adds
no scope, and the pack-seed sweep is what raises Contents from read-only across the fleet to
read/write, because writing one declaration into each member is its whole job; Contents write on
this repo also covers baseline-migration retirement). A workflow that exists only to hold a secret is redundant
([packs/core/scheduled-tasks.md](../core/scheduled-tasks.md)) — the force-baseline workflow above is
not that: it exists because the operation is manual, and it reads the same secret only incidentally.

**The one scope the read-only sweeps don't need** — the two fan-out tasks (fleet-baseline,
fleet-add-missing-packs) add **Actions: read and write** on the owner's repositories to that PAT.
Dispatching another repo's workflow is an Actions *write*, so a token scoped for the read-only
sweeps alone answers `403` on every member. Both report that per repo as `no-permission` and fail
the run rather than retrying: it is a grant to fix once, not a transient.

**What freshness measures** — by **version**, not by date (#786). The update flows stamp
`engineVersion` and `packVersions` and deliberately never write `ref` or `updated`, so on a maintained
member the stamped ref is FROZEN and its age measures nothing; `behind` is `installed < canon`, per
component, and the drift issue names the version that is missing. There is no window to tune, because
nothing is being estimated — `staleDays` governs only the legacy date measure, kept for a member still
declaring the retired `baselining` mechanism.

**Full-roster reporting** — every sweep's report enumerates the whole fleet, not just its findings.
Each repo under the owner lands in the report under exactly one named state — covered, dormant,
uncovered, opted out, archived/fork, unknown, fresh, behind, fitted, out of scope, inactive today,
skipped with a reason — and the repos a sweep deliberately never measures (the enforcer itself, canon) are
named as such rather than silently absent. The sheepdog provides data on the fleet regardless of
state: a roster that names only the exceptions has silent holes, and a reader cannot tell "fine"
from "fell out of the report".

**When they fail** — a repo whose declaration the roster cannot read is `unknown` to **both** its
questions, never uncovered and never behind; a member whose *mount probe* fails is `unknown` to the
freshness question alone, because its declaration was read and the coverage verdict stands; a member
the fit scan cannot read is `unknown`, never fitted, and a member whose scheduler refused the
fan-out dispatch is named and fails the run — a work list nobody will act on is not a green
outcome; a member the pack-seed sweep cannot read or write is `unknown`, never assumed converged: no issue opened, no open issue closed on its
behalf, and a non-zero exit. A non-zero preprocessing subprocess fails the task, and the scheduler
converges one open `needs-human` issue for it.

{"number":905,"title":"Claudinite growth: mint the headless-browser canon pack","body":"Fleet sweep (dispatch #869) found one unhomed technology: **driving a real browser from your own process**. This mints `packs/headless-browser/`. Tracker: #642.

No PR template exists in this repo, so this body is written from the commit.

## Why it is a gap

Three members drive a browser from code, for three different reasons, and no canon pack owns it. The nearest coverage stops short:

- **`basics/writing-tests`** owns *which* engine a UI golden needs (rasterizer vs browser), the tolerance a browser golden may carry, self-skipping where no browser is present, and the re-baselining gate. It says nothing about getting a browser, controlling the page's world, or capturing from it.
- **`executable-requirements`** owns the spec layout, coverage/gallery gates and the determinism *principles*; its worked recipes are jsdom/satori and Flutter. Its adoption interview names Playwright as a possible mechanism and homes no rules about it.
- **`html`** owns markup gotchas and hand-a-console-snippet verification — the case where the agent has *no* browser.

This gap was found and explicitly deferred by the 2026-08-02 sweep ("Second gap found, **not** authored this run — headless-browser screenshotting … Recorded here so it is not lost"). This run authors it, plus a third exemplar that sweep named and this one read in full.

## Evidence — every rule traces to a named member's real file

| Member | What it drives a browser for | Files read |
|---|---|---|
| **EdFringeNow** | pinned-Chromium visual-requirements harness | `product/requirements/shared/harness/browser.js`, `capture-tools.js`, `render-case.js`, `case-helpers.js`, `.github/workflows/ui-requirements.yml` |
| **CrosswordChat** | goldens for surfaces a rasterizer can't draw, **and** generated store artifacts | `dev/requirements/ui/render/page-to-png.js`, `dev/build/make-store-assets.mjs`, `package.json` (`playwright-core`) |
| **ClaudiniteWebsite** | interactive responsive verification | `.claudinite/local/packs/claudinite-website/skills/site-visual-check/SKILL.md` |

`EdFringeAllocator` carries a vestigial fourth instance (`old/requirements.txt`, `playwright>=1.40.0`) in a retired prototype — noted, not leaned on.

Two of them hit the same wall (a browser screenshot is not bit-stable across machines) and solved it opposite ways — CrosswordChat lets the build float and takes a per-case tolerance; EdFringeNow pins the driver version, refuses to run on any other, jails the fonts and passes rasterisation flags. That disagreement is the substance of the pinning rules, and is why a pack beats a rule.

## What is in it

19 prose rules in four sections — getting a browser; replacing the page's world; fonts and rasterisation; capture. The ones that cost a member the most:

- **A CLI window-size flag is not a viewport.** A narrow one renders clamped and crops, which reads as a horizontal-overflow bug in every section of a page that has none. Cost ClaudiniteWebsite a phantom bug hunt.
- **Vendoring the web fonts is half the job.** Every glyph they lack comes from the *machine's* installed fonts, so the rendering becomes a record of that font set. Cost EdFringeNow a red CI lane: one string measured wider on the runner, wrapped, and every card below moved down a line.
- **Freezing CSS animation does not freeze the Web Animations API** — `element.animate` keeps running and the capture races it.
- **A bounding box is viewport-space and goes stale** — drivers scroll before clicking, so a rect measured before a click means somewhere else after one.
- **Clip at an element's box rather than screenshotting the element** — an element screenshot scrolls, and a scroll dismisses the hover state you came to capture.

## Shape

- **Prose only, `worldRules: []`.** Named reason: every grounded case is runtime browser behaviour (a secure origin gating geolocation, font fallback deciding layout, a scroll dismissing a hover state) or a judgment about a harness's shape. Neither has a repo-state signature a check could read without asserting that some particular call still exists — the shape the corpus rejects outright. Same posture as `web-speech` and `html`.
- **Fingerprinted on source, not on a dependency manifest** — a driver module specifier or a `.launch(` call in JS/TS. EdFringeNow drives a *globally installed* Playwright with no dependency entry anywhere, so a manifest scan would miss it. Verified against both members' real source lines, and quiet on prose and on a `L.map(` call.
- Written stripped: no member paths, product nouns or concepts in `RULES.md`. Provenance is one paragraph in `README.md`, matching the `flutter` / `leaflet` convention.

## Verification

- `node --test $(git ls-files '*.test.mjs')` — **1798 pass, 0 fail** (includes the pack-directory drift test, the pack-version guard, the catalog tally and the badge guard).
- `node engine/checks/check_the_world.mjs` — **0 blocking**; the pack contributes no advisory (its `rules-line-length` finding was fixed by wrapping, not waived).
- `packs/directory.GENERATED.md` regenerated by its own test, never hand-edited.

Write surface is `packs/` only. Auto-merge deliberately not armed — a new canon pack is the owner's call.

{"number":949,"title":"Growth promote: 20 lessons from 8 members' local packs","body":"Central promote stage of the growth lifecycle (`canon-curation/growth-promote`), dispatched via #870.

**Targets swept** (per the dispatch's Context — local packs changed in the window): ClaudiniteWebsite, EdFringeNow, GoogleCalendarEventCreator, LaughCounter, MissingBulbWebsite, Sheepdog, TLDR, VascularColoring.

Read every target's local packs (`RULES.md` prose and any local checks), generalized each candidate, and deduped against the **whole** corpus before landing anything — most candidates were rejected as already-covered (several already promoted from these same repos in earlier runs). 20 genuinely new, portable lessons survived; all landed at the prose rung — each is judgment, in-flight/runtime behavior, or signature-less tool-usage knowledge, so none had a reliable static signature a check could carry.

One commit per landing file:

- `packs/basics/RULES.md` — Grep's silent `output_mode` default, verifying claims about real named people, an egress block vs. a publisher 403, a litmus test for cross-file comment content, piping through `tail` losing the exit code, proving a repo-scanning check silent against real sources.
- `packs/git-github/skills/git-github-advanced/SKILL.md` — a locally-refused git mutation after a server-side merge, a shallow checkout breaking `git merge-base`, preferring `git push` over the MCP file-write tools' transcription risk, recognizing a CI infrastructure outage, `get_job_logs`'s `failed_only`/`job_id` requirement.
- `packs/core/RULES.md` + `packs/core/scheduled-tasks.md` — a duplicate dispatch trigger as your own claim-echo, resolving a mounted skill's links against its real canon path rather than the `Skill` tool's announced base directory.
- `packs/grow_with_claudinite/extracting-lessons.md` — never capture a rule that teaches routing around a permission/security denial (directly relevant to this task's own judgment).
- `packs/grow_with_claudinite/skills/unattended-agents/SKILL.md` — a `[Merge Without Review]` warning on a licensed unattended merge is expected, and a background subagent sharing the parent's working directory can make its WIP/branch look like the parent's own.
- `packs/basics/skills/writing-tests/SKILL.md` + `packs/basics/skills/bug-investigation/SKILL.md` — restoring a see-it-fail mutation via `git checkout`/`stash` not a stale `.bak`, testing a retry/requeue helper twice with a different actor for identity-arbitrated mechanisms, a stateful simulator modeling what the real engine writes not the rule's stated intent, and quoting a run's own log rather than reasoning forward from a bug theory.
- `packs/headless-browser/RULES.md` — reinstalling a browser-driver package can pull a version mismatched with the environment's pinned browser.

**Notable rejections** (already covered, confirmed by reading the current canon rather than assumption): the `search_issues`/`fields`/`per_page` MCP-token-limit cluster (ClaudiniteWebsite, MissingBulbWebsite, Sheepdog, GoogleCalendarEventCreator) — already fully covered in `git-github-advanced`'s "Cap and qualify" section; `ScheduleWakeup` needing `prompt` (ClaudiniteWebsite) — already in `basics/RULES.md`; several git/GitHub, Playwright/headless-browser, HTML-parsing and research-methodology items from EdFringeNow, GoogleCalendarEventCreator, LaughCounter, MissingBulbWebsite and VascularColoring that matched existing canon rules verbatim or near-verbatim (confirming those repos were earlier promotion sources). Full per-lesson breakdown logged on the tracker issue.

No stub pack minted — every landing lesson had an existing canon owner.

Refs #99 (tracker log comment follows once this lands)

| origin | landed | generalized rule |
|---|---|---|
| EdFringeNow | `git-github-advanced/SKILL.md` | A deleted workflow's old runs outlive it in the Actions tab, and no session tool can clear them — the MCP toolset has no `actions:write` DELETE endpoint; hand it to the owner. |
| TLDR | `unattended-agents/SKILL.md` | Parallel background agents that each dump external content to disk need a collision-proof filename, not a shared generic one — a shared scratchpad path races and silently truncates. |
| EdFringeNow | `headless-browser/RULES.md` (fold into the driver-reinstall rule) | A reinstall at the repo root can dodge the version-mismatch failure and still dirty `package.json`/lockfile/`node_modules`, needing a manual revert. |

- EdFringeNow's "never `curl api.github.com` for a run's status" — near-verbatim in `git-github-advanced/SKILL.md`'s "To confirm a non-PR run" section.
- EdFringeNow's "`pull_request_read method=get_status` is a dead signal" — near-verbatim in `git-github-advanced/SKILL.md`'s "To read a PR's CI result" section.
- No stub pack minted — every lesson had an existing canon owner.

Verification: `node --test $(git ls-files '*.test.mjs')` → 2100/2100 pass. `check_the_world.mjs` → 0 blocking, 60 advisory (all pre-existing, none touching the edited files).

entries.name: mcp__github__pull_request_read
entries.description: Get information on a specific pull request in GitHub repository.

after.description: Cursor for pagination, used only by the get_review_comments method. Pass the endCursor from the previous page's PageInfo to fetch the next page.

method.description:
Action to specify what pull request data needs to be retrieved from GitHub. 
Possible options: 
 1. get - Get details of a specific pull request.
 2. get_diff - Get the diff of a pull request.
 3. get_status - Get combined commit status of a head commit in a pull request.
 4. get_files - Get the list of files changed in a pull request. Use with pagination parameters to control the number of results returned.
 5. get_commits - Get the list of commits on a pull request. Use with pagination parameters to control the number of results returned.
 6. get_review_comments - Get review threads on a pull request. Each thread contains logically grouped review comments made on the same code location during pull request reviews. Returns thread metadata and comments with nullable current and original line-range coordinates (line, start_line, original_line, original_start_line). Current coordinates are omitted when unavailable, such as for outdated comments. Use cursor-based pagination (perPage, after) to control results.
 7. get_reviews - Get the reviews on a pull request. When asked for review comments, use get_review_comments method. Use with pagination parameters to control the number of results returned.
 8. get_comments - Get comments on a pull request. Use this if user doesn't specifically want review comments. Use with pagination parameters to control the number of results returned.
 9. get_check_runs - Get check runs for the head commit of a pull request. Check runs are the individual CI/CD jobs and checks that run on the PR.

owner.description: Repository owner

perPage.description: Results per page for pagination (min 1, max 100)

{"number":346,"title":"web-speech: convert the two signature-bearing gotchas into web-speech-io skill checks, keep the rest as prose","body":"Reworks the prose-only `web-speech` pack per the pattern PR #350 set: keep the pack, add a skill for the activity, move the gotchas that have a **file-scoped signature** into check-the-work rules (deleting their prose), and leave the genuinely signature-less runtime gotchas as prose.

## What changed

**The pack stays, mostly prose, and now mounts a skill.** `packs/web-speech/pack.mjs` keeps its content-grep `detect` and its `prose: 'RULES.md'`, and adds `skills: ['web-speech-io']`. `RULES.md` drops the two converted bullets and its "prose only" framing (enforcement-silent — the README, not the prose, maps how each rule is enforced).

**New skill `web-speech-io`** (activity: wiring browser speech recognition or synthesis) — a minimal SKILL.md (trigger + one pointer paragraph, no re-teaching to drift) and a `checks.mjs` owning two rules, discovered by `skills/registry.mjs` and run at every Stop and in CI. The failure message is the rule:

| Rule | Severity | Signature |
|---|---|---|
| `web-speech-no-window-api-in-service-worker` | blocking | a Window-scoped speech API (`SpeechRecognition`/`webkitSpeechRecognition`/`SpeechRecognitionPhrase`, or `speechSynthesis`/`SpeechSynthesisUtterance`) referenced in the source file an MV3 `manifest.json` names as `background.service_worker` — with a recognition-vs-synthesis tailored fix per line |
| `web-speech-recognition-feature-detected` | advisory | a source file constructing `new webkitSpeechRecognition(` with no unprefixed `SpeechRecognition` fallback anywhere in the file |

**Relevance gates** (a skill check runs on every repo): rule 1 scopes to the single file an MV3 manifest names as its service worker, and only when that path is the project's **own authored source** (`ctx.files`) — a built/bundled worker artifact that merely concatenates document-context source is out of scope; rule 2's gate is the anti-pattern itself, suppressed the moment the file mentions the unprefixed name (a conservative gate that would rather miss than false-flag). Both exclude the skill's own directory so its fixtures never flag the corpus repo.

**Why only two of the seventeen convert** — I re-examined every gotcha against #350's bar (a file-scoped signature covering the grounded cases, verified against `missingbulb/CrosswordChat`'s `extension/src/speech/*` and its manifest). Two have honest signatures and convert; the folded worker-facet of "prefer chrome.tts over speechSynthesis" rides rule 1 (its content-script autoplay reason has no signature and stays prose). The other fifteen are runtime/behavioural — settle-once cycles, n-best reading, the error taxonomy, the pause watchdog, on-device/biasing semantics, port-disconnect handling, lazy `getVoices()` (top-level detection needs an AST, not a regex), terminal-event resolution, SSML absence — with no reliable static signature, so they stay `web-speech` prose. That asymmetric split (two checks, a substantial prose residue) is the honest outcome; the signature-less residue is what the checks' comments document as out of scope.

## Tests

10 new fixture tests (scratch-repo harness), each rule proven both directions — violating fixtures find at the right severity/line, clean ones (a chrome.tts worker, a bundled worker artifact, a non-MV3 manifest, speech outside the worker, an unprefixed feature-detect, an injected constructor, a non-source file) stay quiet — and mutation-tested red (neutering each `run()` fails exactly the violating-fixture tests, 2 and 1 respectively). Full suite: 427 pass. Whole-repo sweep: clean (no new acceptance needed).

Catalogs updated (`packs/README.md` row → `0 (2 in its skill) / 15`, `skills/README.md` entry) to satisfy `catalog-completeness`; the pack's `skills` list satisfies `skill-ownership`.

{"number":362,"title":"web-speech: check-the-world for mic capture released on pagehide","body":"## What & why

Lessons-learned capture from a CrosswordChat session that audited the extension's microphone lifecycle. The extension relied on the browser's implicit page teardown to release the recognizer — no `pagehide` handler — which isn't reliable under **bfcache** (page suspended, not destroyed, mic still held).

Per review, this ships as a **check, not prose** (promotion ladder — a check relieves every session's context where prose only relocates it), and specifically **check-the-world**: a repo that opens the mic but releases it nowhere on `pagehide` is a standing leak however long ago it merged, so the scope is the whole tracked source, not the diff.

## The check — `web-speech-capture-released-on-pagehide` (blocking)

Owned by the `web-speech-io` skill (its third rule), alongside the two existing check-the-work rules. Fires when:
- the repo **opens the mic** — a `getUserMedia(` call, or a file that references the recognizer API **and** `.start()`s it — **and**
- **no source file anywhere** registers a `pagehide` handler (`addEventListener('pagehide', …)` / `onpagehide`).

The failure message carries the rule (bfcache rationale + the fix); there is **no prose copy** to drift from.

**Blocking**: a mic left held after teardown is a real device leak (indicator stays lit, device pinned), so it fails the stop rather than just warning. Conservative gate keeps that honest (the codebase's "rather miss than false-flag" bar):
- repo-wide `pagehide` **presence** satisfies it — the release may live in whichever context owns the stream (content script, popup, side panel, offscreen doc);
- test/fixture files are out of the acquisition scan (a mocked `getUserMedia` opens no device);
- a recognizer **named but never `.start()`ed** is not a live capture;
- the one legitimate exception — a capture in an offscreen document torn down via `closeDocument` — rides **accept-with-reason**, the check-the-world exemption path.

## Tests

Red-first fixtures co-located in `capture-pagehide-teardown.test.mjs`, including the **CrosswordChat before/after shape** (capture in one file, `pagehide` teardown in another → clean). Full CI suite green (483 tests); `checks/run.mjs` clean (the now-blocking rule does not self-flag the corpus).

## Routing note

Chose the `web-speech` domain over `chrome-extension`: this is the voice-I/O capture lifecycle, and bfcache/`pagehide` are general browser behavior, not MV3 mechanics. Deliberately left out the popup-blur / offscreen-`closeDocument` specifics from the originating lesson doc — that session captured in a content script and exercised neither.

Closes #363

method.description:
Action to specify what pull request data needs to be retrieved from GitHub. 
Possible options: 
 1. get - Get details of a specific pull request.
 2. get_diff - Get the diff of a pull request.
 3. get_status - Get combined commit status of a head commit in a pull request.
 4. get_files - Get the list of files changed in a pull request. Use with pagination parameters to control the number of results returned.
 5. get_commits - Get the list of commits on a pull request. Use with pagination parameters to control the number of results returned.
 6. get_review_comments - Get review threads on a pull request. Each thread contains logically grouped review comments made on the same code location during pull request reviews. Returns thread metadata and comments with nullable current and original line-range coordinates (line, start_line, original_line, original_start_line). Current coordinates are omitted when unavailable, such as for outdated comments. Use cursor-based pagination (perPage, after) to control results.
 7. get_reviews - Get the reviews on a pull request. When asked for review comments, use get_review_comments method. Use with pagination parameters to control the number of results returned.
 8. get_comments - Get comments on a pull request. Use this if user doesn't specifically want review comments. Use with pagination parameters to control the number of results returned.
 9. get_check_runs - Get check runs for the head commit of a pull request. Check runs are the individual CI/CD jobs and checks that run on the PR.

> self-widening guard is untouched, so policy sources stay unreachable even
> inside the named folder, and an unusable path invalidates the whole policy.
>
> wiki-growth moves from the repo-wide `doc-changes` to the wiki root it
> already anchors its precondition on.
>
> * Intersect policy terms with &&, so a scope can narrow rather than widen
>
> A policy list is a union: adding `doc-changes` beside `under:product-wiki`
> authorizes docs everywhere in the repo, which is the opposite of "docs
> under that folder". `&&` inside a term is the narrowing operator — every
> part must cover the file, and every part's whole-diff constraint must hold.
>
> Whitespace around it is accepted wherever a person writes one and collapsed
> by policyExpression, so the stamped trailer stays a single token and its
> regex is unchanged; the request lane's Automerge: line widens to the rest
> of the line and stops lowercasing, since an under: path is case-sensitive.
> A composite or a whole-policy word inside an && term is an authoring error,
> and work-item's pure grammar mirror now fences the under: path shape the
> drift guard caught it accepting.
>
> wiki-growth declares `under:product-wiki/ && doc-changes`.
>
> ---------

{"number":827,"title":"Declared checks are JSON, one file per pack","body":"Closes #826.

The four conversion rounds left 25 pattern-rule declarations as 25 modules averaging 17 lines each — all of them data. This makes them data: one JSON file per pack, discovered structurally.

## The format

A pack's declarations are the array in `packs/<pack>/declared-checks.json`; a skill's live in its own `declared-checks.json` beside the `checks.mjs` that still lists its coded rules. The pack registry discovers both the way it discovers packs themselves — **no import, no manifest line: writing the declaration adds the check.**

A declaration carries `id`, `severity`, `failureMessage`, and its assertions with their `what`/`fix`. What it no longer carries:

- **no comments** — JSON cannot hold one, so the no-comments-on-a-check rule is enforced by construction rather than by review;
- **no `description`** — the failure message stands on its own;
- **no `doc` pointer** — a declared check states its own case rather than deferring to prose;
- **`why` → `failureMessage`**, named for what it is: the line the agent reads when the check fires.

Regexes are strings in `/pattern/flags` form, compiled at load. `scanFiles`/`excludeFiles`/`pathExists` still read any other string as an exact repo path; a plain string at a strictly-pattern key is an authoring error, reported with the key that got it and the value it got.

```json
{
  "id": "gha/label-create-before-add",
  "severity": "advisory",
  "failureMessage": "--add-label fails when the label does not exist yet — GitHub will not create it on demand",
  "scanFiles": "/^\\.github\\/workflows\\/[^/]+\\.ya?ml$/",
  "scanTracked": true,
  "checkEachFile": [{
    "whenFileMatches": "/--add-label/",
    "require": "/label create/",
    "what": "uses --add-label with no idempotent `gh label create … || true` beforehand",
    "fix": "create the label idempotently before adding it, so the workflow survives its first run"
  }]
}
```

## What moved

| pack / skill | before | after |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `github-actions` | 5 modules | `declared-checks.json` |
| `chrome-extension-release` | 5 modules | `declared-checks.json` |
| `product-wiki` | 5 modules | `declared-checks.json` |
| `basics` | 3 modules | `declared-checks.json` |
| `aws-sam` | 2 modules | `declared-checks.json` |
| `web-speech-io` | 2 modules | `declared-checks.json` |
| `google-id-token-validation` | 2 modules | `declared-checks.json` |
| `unattended-agents` | 1 module | `declared-checks.json` |

Rules with a hand-written `run(ctx)` are untouched and stay their own modules listed in the manifest — `handler-path`, `privacy-permission-alignment`, `layout`, `routine-structure` and the rest. `product-wiki/lib.mjs` drops the two page-classifier regexes it was exporting only for the checks; the declaration owns them now, with no second copy to drift from.

## Engine

- `patternRule(declaration)` compiles pattern strings and maps `failureMessage` onto the field the finding renderer reads; `loadDeclaredChecks(dir)` reads and caches a directory's declarations, so the registry and a test share one compiled set rather than each re-parsing.
- The registry appends a pack's declarations to its world rules and a skill's to its skill checks, reaching the compiler **lazily — only where a declaration file exists** — so a tree carrying just the pack machinery (the hook fixtures, a minimal mount) loads exactly as before.
- `--list` prints a declared rule's failure message in the description column and leaves the doc column empty.
- Two deliberate cross-tree reaches are accepted with reasons in `.claudinite-checks.json`: the registry reaching the compiler, and the shared test harness reaching the loader so a pack test proves the same rule object the runner runs.

## Verification

- World sweep: **finding-for-finding identical** to `origin/main` — the same 0 blocking, 28 advisory, same list.
- `--list`: identical on **id and severity for all 88 rules**.
- **1613 tests pass**, six new: regex-string compilation with flags, the authoring-error message, `failureMessage` reaching the finding, the loader's absent-file and cache behaviour, and the registry discovering a pack's and a skill's declarations. Each was seen to fail against a mutated engine before being kept.
- The pack tests' assertions are unchanged in substance — they now resolve their rule through `declaredCheck(dir, id)` instead of an import.

{"number":908,"title":"The remaining conversion tranches: work scope, field-named scan sets, and the value-set consumers","body":"The rest of the conversion order in #880, after #891 / #895 / #896: tranches 4 and 5, plus the re-judgment of what is genuinely left.

## Tranche 4 — the work-scope vocabulary

A declaration may carry `scope: "work"`: it judges the **change**, not the repo, and gains three assertions over surfaces `work.mjs` already exposes.

| assertion | reads | converts |
|---|---|---|
| `checkBranchCommits` | the branch's commit messages since the base | `task-lifecycle` |
| `forbidIntroducedMergeCommits` | merges this change introduces (never the base's own) | `squash-merge-history` |
| `forbidAddedValueInArray` | a parsed array's values, head against base | `cer/permission-added-store-issue` |

Scope stays a *placement* decision: a coded rule's scope is the manifest list it sits in, and a declaration — which has no list — states it, with the registry routing declared specs into `worldRules`/`workRules` so `normalizeManifest` still stamps the one answer.

`forbidAddedValueInArray` compares **sets**, never the text diff — appending a JSON array element re-touches the line above it (the trailing comma), which is exactly why the coded rule read the base.

Side effects worth naming:
- `packs/chrome-extension-release/lib/manifest-permissions.mjs` is deleted with its sole consumer; the four permission keys are now spelled in the two declarations that watch them, with a drift-guard test holding them equal.
- Both converted messages had to come down to the `declared-check-messages` discipline the coded rules never faced.
- `ruleTester` now invokes through `runRule`, so a work-scoped rule gets its fluent surface in a test exactly as in a run.

## Tranche 5 — a third `scanFiles` form: files named by a parsed field

`scanFiles` took a regex or an exact path; it now also takes an object that reads the file set out of **another parsed document** — `inParsedFilesMatching` (+ `whereFileContains`), `namedByField` (fanning out over an array met along the path, `defaultingTo` standing in where an entry omits the name), and `withSuffix` for a field naming a directory. Names resolve against the **naming file's** own directory, and a name pointing outside the run's file set is dropped silently.

The assertion half: `checkParsedFiles`' `everyScannedFile` (read the scan set as documents) and `requireFieldMatching` — `requireField` for the case where a field present but blank is still not a value.

Converts, modules deleted: `web-speech-no-window-api-in-service-worker` (the file an MV3 manifest names as `background.service_worker`, MV3-gated, authored source only — its skill now carries declarations alone, so `checks.mjs` goes too) and `firebase/functions-node-pin`. `firebase/lib.mjs` stays: the predeploy rule still reads the config's own arrays.

## What I did NOT land, and why

Two items from the plan's tranche 1 do not survive contact with their rules:

- **`matchAnyValueOfSet` has no faithful customer today.** For `python-optional-import-top-level` the value set is only half the check: the dist→import-name mapping is a *transform* (`-`/`.` → `_`), and deciding which token of `from a.b import c` is the package is import-statement semantics, not a word-bounded alternation — `from mypkg import tensorflow` would flag. That is precisely the class-C failure mode the rule exists to avoid. For the two narration rules the forbidden-id set is harvested **per scanned file's directory**, which the value-set pair scopes per rule (v2, as the design already noted).
- **`requireFieldValueInSet` for class E's enum slice would add a reader, not remove one.** `task-declaration-shape` stays coded either way (cross-field conditionals), so extracting `FREQUENCIES` from `slots.mjs` by regex leaves the module's own import in place and creates a second, weaker reader of the same source.

The `configSchema` manifest seam — the plan's other named surface — is now #911, as its own issue.

## Verification

`node --test $(git ls-files '*.test.mjs')` after each tranche (1827 pass, 0 fail); `check_the_world` on the whole tree at 0 blocking. Each conversion authored red-first against the coded rule's own fixtures, with the module deleted in the same commit.

{"number":1693,"title":"Promote three member packs onto the canon shelf","body":"Closes #1692

CrosswordChat and LaughCounter each grew a local pack beside a canon pack they had never declared, so the same rules were being maintained twice. This lands the residue where the canon already owns the territory, and opens one new pack for the facet nothing covered.

## `packs/web-speech` — widened

Six API-contract checks and two rules, from CrosswordChat's `local/browser-speech`.

The rules canon already carried are untouched: the screen-capture constraint trap, the 1.2 s / 1.8 s endpoint window, the biasing gate, the error taxonomy, the lazy voice list, the `chrome.tts` relay. What is new:

- **Interim results are a signal, not input.** They arrive on the *same* `result` event as the finished utterance and are revised several times per utterance, so a handler that delivers `results[i][0].transcript` acts on words the user had not finished saying — and acts again on each revision.
- **The echo guard belongs in the application, not at the capture layer.** Chrome's automatic echo cancellation is a loopback of *page* playout: it attenuates `speechSynthesis` and never sees `chrome.tts`, whose audio the OS renders. That residual echo cannot be reached by any capture constraint, which is why matching the transcript against what you just spoke is the design rather than a stopgap — and why reaching for `suppressLocalAudioPlayback` means the guard that would have worked never gets written.

Two existing rules each take one clause: run the mic preflight even when permission is already granted (otherwise the device is warmed only on the first grant), and treat voice order and speaking rate as user-facing settings rather than constants.

The six checks are pack-level rather than skill-bundled, since they judge the API contracts themselves rather than where the code runs. All six parse the call site rather than grepping for a name, comments stripped first — so a wrapper that delegates its terminal handling, a constraints object hoisted into a constant, and a switch that dispatches side effects rather than mapping a value all stay quiet. What unites them is that their breach is **silent**: nothing throws, nothing logs, and the app keeps showing a live session while the user is heard by nobody.

## `packs/macos` — widened

`swift-toolchain-gate` only. The pack's prose already carried the rule — `/usr/bin/swift` is a stub present on every Mac that pops an 8 GB install prompt rather than failing, so `command -v swift` must sit behind `xcode-select -p`. The check was the missing half.

LaughCounter's other two local checks do not come across: they are hardcoded to `mac/Sources/` and `AudioHub.swift`, and canon already holds generalized equivalents in `signal-teardown-routing` and `sudden-termination-vs-teardown`. `references.md` is created here on its first entry.

## `packs/host-page` — new

Being a guest in a web app you do not own. `web-scraping` acquires a site's data from outside it, `chrome-extension` covers how your code reaches the page, `headless-browser` drives a browser you own — none covers what to do once you are inside somebody else's page.

Eleven rules, generalized off CrosswordChat's `local/host-page-adaptation` with its evidence citations stripped (the `xwd__` token, `page-adapter/`, the REQ ids, the fixture paths). Three checks, sharing one failure mode: an observer that outlives its feature, a synthetic event that does not bubble, and one aimed outside the app root all leave `dispatchEvent` returning true and the page simply not responding — indistinguishable from "the app rejects untrusted events", which is the wrong conclusion and an expensive one to back out of.

Declared by hand. There is no honest fingerprint: a content script, a `dispatchEvent` and a `MutationObserver` are equally the shapes of code running on its *own* page, so a marker that cannot tell a guest from a host would suspect the pack in every DOM repo in the fleet.

## Consumer safety

Nine rules become blocking here, and canon CI cannot see a consumer. **No fleet member declares `web-speech`, `macos` or `host-page`** — checked across all sixteen — so nothing turns red overnight and the change is genuinely additive, which per `consumer-safe-changes.md` makes the rehearsal fixture the honest answer rather than a migration record.

`voice-on-a-host-page` is a new fixture shape: a member declaring `web-speech` and `host-page` over source in the exact shape all nine rules engage on — a recognizer wired for every terminal event, interim results gated on `isFinal`, a total error map, a preflight releasing its tracks in a `finally`, an observer that disconnects, synthetic input that bubbles and targets a node inside the app. It proves the rules inert on a conforming consumer rather than passing by dodging the gates. CrosswordChat is about to become exactly this shape (#396).

`macos-app` gains a diagnostic script for the same reason: `swift-toolchain-gate` scans shell and workflow files, of which that fixture had none, so the rule would have passed there vacuously.

Writing the fixture caught two faults in this PR's own work, which is the point of it: the synthetic keystroke was not using the helper-and-spread idiom `host-page`'s own rule prescribes, and the recognizer lacked the `pagehide` teardown `web-speech` already required.

## Folders touched

```
packs/web-speech/     6 checks + shared call-site helpers, 2 rules and 2 clauses,
                      references entries for all six, rule index and checks table
packs/macos/          swift-toolchain-gate + its test, references.md created
packs/host-page/      new pack: manifest, 11 rules, 3 checks, README index,
                      references, badge, VERSIONS
packs/                directory.GENERATED.md regenerated; README.md catalog entry
vendoring/rehearsal/  the voice-on-a-host-page shape, and a script for macos-app
```

## Verification

All three gates green on the current head:

- Full canon suite over the CI test roots — **3,258 of 3,258 pass**.
- `check_the_work.mjs` (the Stop-hook runner) — **exit 0**.
- `check_the_world.mjs` — **0 blocking**.

Three findings were fixed along the way, two of which only the work-scope runner sees:

- `catalog-completeness` — `packs/README.md` is a *hand-maintained* index, so a new pack does not appear in it by existing on disk. Added, and the `web-speech` / `macos` counts corrected.
- `consumer-safe-change` — resolved with the fixtures above.
- `squash-merge-history` — the branch had picked up a merge commit while resolving a base-branch conflict. Rebased out; the branch is three commits.

The `pack-version-claimed-once` failure this PR originally sat behind was fixed on `main` by #1680 and is closed as #1694.

{"number":2059,"title":"Claudinite canon: prose to checks","body":"Two rules the shelf's prose carried that no check did. Both are declared checks — patterns over files, the ladder's highest check rung — and both ship `since: 2026-09-15`, so they bite at their real severity once the two-week window closes.

## What converted

| Prose | Became | Severity |
|---|---|---|
| `web-speech` — *"Voice lists load lazily — an empty `getVoices()` means 'not ready yet', not 'no voices'"* | `tts-voices-cached-empty` | blocking |
| `macos` — *"Notarize the distributed container, then staple it"* | `notarize-then-staple` | blocking |

**`tts-voices-cached-empty`** flags a module-scope `const/let/var … = speechSynthesis.getVoices()`. That call answers empty until the browser has loaded voices, so the cache stays empty for the page's life and every utterance falls back to the OS default voice — nothing throws, nothing logs, which is exactly what the pack's other call-site contracts exist to catch. A file that refreshes from a `voiceschanged` listener is spared, comments are stripped first, and test scaffolding and built bundles are out of scope.

**`notarize-then-staple`** flags a script or workflow that runs `notarytool submit` where nothing in the repo runs `stapler staple`. An unstapled artifact carries no ticket of its own, so Gatekeeper has to reach Apple the first time a user opens it — and never has to on the machine that submitted it, which is why the failure only ever appears on somebody else's Mac. Scoped to scripts, workflows and source: markdown neither flags nor excuses, so a runbook naming the command cannot silence the check.

## Proof

Each check has a fixture suite with a violating case and a false-positive guard per escape. Every guard was proved by mutating the declaration and watching that case bite, then restoring:

- removing `unlessFileMatches` → the `voiceschanged` case fires; removing `scanIgnoringComments` → a block-commented example fires; removing the test/vendor exclusions → the fake and the bundle fire.
- removing the comment anchor from `flagFilesMatching` → a commented-out `notarytool submit` fires; neutering `unlessSomeFileMatches` → both staple-present cases fire; widening `scanFiles` to markdown → the runbook case fires.

Both checks were also run over this repository's real tree and report nothing.

## The deletion test

Both paragraphs stay whole, each carrying something its check does not:

- the voice rule also covers a lazy memo *inside* a function (`cached ??= getVoices()`), which the module-scope signature cannot see;
- the notarization rule also carries `--wait`, `stapler validate`, and *which* container to staple.

## Notes

- Neither pack is declared here, so neither check runs in the canon; `check_the_world` and `check_the_work` are both clean, and the sweep gained no new advisory.
- The full suite is green apart from the six `packs/claude-code-web-users-support/test/session-start.test.mjs` cases that read the ambient `CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ATTENDED` and are red in every unattended session — #2031, already open, unrelated to this diff. They pass with the variable unset.
- Pack versions and `VERSIONS.md` rows are deliberately untouched: both are derived on the base branch after this lands.

> * Declared checks: one file per pack, not one file per rule
>
> The 25 pattern-rule declarations from the four conversion rounds were 25
> modules of ~17 lines each, all data. A declaration is a table row, not a
> module: reading a pack's declared surface meant opening five files, the
> shared constants were re-imported per rule, and each manifest carried an
> import line and a list entry per declaration.
>
> Each pack now keeps its declarations in one declared-checks.mjs — a named
> export per rule (so the tests still import one directly), default export
> the array the manifest spreads into its rule list. The three skills inline
> their declarations into the checks.mjs array they already had. Rules with a
> hand-written run(ctx) stay their own modules.
>
> Nothing behavioural moves: `--list` is byte-identical against main (88
> rules), the world sweep finds the same 0 blocking / 28 advisory, and the
> 1607-test suite passes with only import lines changed.
>
> * Declared checks are JSON: no comments, no doc pointer, failureMessage
>
> Owner review on #827: the file that holds only declarations should not be
> code. A pack's declarations are now the array in
> packs/<pack>/declared-checks.json (a skill's in its own beside checks.mjs),
> discovered structurally by the pack registry and compiled by the pattern
> engine — no import, no manifest line; writing the declaration adds the check.
>
> The format drops what the declaration was borrowing from prose. No comments
> (JSON cannot hold one, so the no-comments rule is enforced by construction),
> no `description` and no `doc` pointer — a declaration states its own case —
> and `why` is renamed `failureMessage` for what it is: the line the agent
> reads when the check fires. Regexes are strings in /pattern/flags form,
> compiled at load; a path-or-pattern key still reads a plain string as an
> exact path, and a plain string anywhere else is reported with the key that
> got it.
>
> The registry reaches the compiler lazily, only where a declaration file
> exists, so a tree carrying just the pack machinery loads as before. Both
> deliberate cross-tree reaches are accepted with reasons.
>
> Findings are unchanged: the world sweep is finding-for-finding identical to
> main, and `--list` matches on id and severity for all 88 rules (a declared
> rule now prints its failureMessage where a coded rule prints its
> description, and no doc pointer). 1613 tests pass, six of them new — the
> regex-string compilation, the authoring-error message, failureMessage on the
> finding, the loader's cache, and the registry discovering a pack's and a
> skill's declarations — each seen to fail against a mutated engine.
