=== committed-expecteds-owners
## 2026-09-01 · born · converted from references.md (RULES-4)
- **Reason:** A case's success criterion encodes what the owner accepted, which is exactly what
  makes a green suite meaningful sign-off rather than self-grading — the expecteds are an approval
  record, so their authorship is the whole property. Recovered from the rule's own pre-#467 text
  (cut by 2f3e4e9a as “consequence prose arguing for a rule rather than enabling it”, before
  this pack had a references.md to hold it).
- **Mechanism:** prose
- **Retire when:** Reaffirm while the owner approves expecteds; retire if sign-off moves to another
  artifact.
=== doc-first-red
## 2026-09-01 · born · converted from references.md (RULES-2)
- **Reason:** This is the mechanism that makes the document *the* spec rather than documentation: it
  cannot drift into wishfulness, because an unproven statement is a red build, not a stale sentence.
  Recovered from the rule's own pre-#467 text (cut by 2f3e4e9a as “consequence prose arguing for a
  rule rather than enabling it”, before this pack had a references.md to hold it).
- **Mechanism:** prose
- **Retire when:** Reaffirm while the coverage gate runs on every build; retire if the gate stops
  being blocking.
=== kind-way-requirement
## 2026-09-01 · born · converted from references.md (RULES-3)
- **Reason:** One mechanism forced onto everything green-lights claims it can never check — the
  same lesson `packs/basics/references.md` records as `(writing-tests-1)`, where a UI-snapshot
  coverage gate “covered” behavioural leaves it could not observe (#429). That cross-pack
  corroboration is why kinds are routed rather than unified. Recovered from the rule's own pre-#467
  text (cut by 2f3e4e9a as “consequence prose arguing for a rule rather than enabling it”,
  before this pack had a references.md to hold it).
- **Mechanism:** prose
- **Retire when:** Reaffirm alongside the writing-tests entry; retire only if both are retired
  together.
=== leaf-carries-stable
## 2026-09-01 · born · converted from references.md (RULES-1)
- **Reason:** A recycled id silently rebinds history to a different requirement: ids are what cases,
  commits and review discussion key on, so reuse corrupts the record rather than merely confusing a
  reader — and it does so without any failure. Recovered from the rule's own pre-#467 text (cut by
  2f3e4e9a as “consequence prose arguing for a rule rather than enabling it”, before this pack
  had a references.md to hold it).
- **Mechanism:** prose

=== mismatch-surface-actual
## 2026-09-01 · born · converted from references.md (RULES-5)

# AWS SAM (Serverless Application Model)

Portable, project-agnostic gotchas for the AWS Serverless Application Model and the API-Gateway/CloudFront stack it deploys — true for any SAM project read cold.

- **`BuildMethod: esbuild` strips the entry's subdirectory from the Handler path.** With a single entry point in a subdirectory (`EntryPoints: [src/handler.mjs]`), SAM's esbuild builder writes the bundle to `<artifact-root>/handler.js` — esbuild's default `outbase` is the entry's own dir, so the subdirectory is dropped. Set `Handler: handler.handler`, not `src/handler.handler`. `sam build` succeeds either way; the wrong value fails only at first invoke with `Runtime.ImportModuleError: Cannot find module 'src/handler'`.
- **esbuild must be a regular `dependency`, not a `devDependency`.** SAM's esbuild builder runs a *production-only* `npm install` in its scratch dir, so a `devDependency` esbuild is skipped and the build fails with "Cannot find esbuild." Declare it in `dependencies` (it isn't bundled into the artifact unless the handler imports it), or put it on the runner's `PATH` before `sam build`.
- **CloudFront won't forward `Authorization` via a *custom* origin-request policy** — a custom `AWS::CloudFront::OriginRequestPolicy` listing `Authorization` is rejected at deploy ("The parameter Headers contains Authorization that is not allowed"). To forward it to the origin while keeping it out of the cache key (so public GETs share one cached entry), attach the **managed** `AllViewerExceptHostHeader` policy (id `b689b0a8-53d0-40ab-baf2-68738e2966ac`) plus a custom cache policy that omits `Authorization`. Cache key and origin forwarding are independent controls — a `CachePolicy` defines the cache key, an `OriginRequestPolicy` defines what reaches the origin — so set them separately to cache public reads yet still deliver `Authorization` for authenticated writes. Use the *ExceptHostHeader* variant specifically: forwarding the viewer `Host` to an API Gateway origin returns 403.

content.content:
# AWS SAM (Serverless Application Model)

- **A deploy role must be able to drive the transform and CloudFront, or change-set creation fails
  with the real reason hidden.** The `Serverless-2016-10-31` transform runs as a macro, so the
  deploy principal needs `cloudformation:*`, and CloudFront management needs `cloudfront:*`, both at
  `Resource: "*"` (scope the *data-plane* grants to your stack instead). `sam deploy` surfaces only
  `Waiter ChangeSetCreateComplete failed` — the actual `AccessDenied` is visible only in the
  CloudFormation console's **Change sets** tab. Don't paper over it with `AdministratorAccess`.
  (deploy-role-must)

- **A brand-new AWS account can't create a CloudFront distribution until AWS verifies it.** The
  deploy fails
  `AccessDenied: Your account must be verified before you can add new CloudFront resources` — an
  account-level anti-abuse gate, not an IAM or template bug. Open a Support case to get the account
  verified, and launch against the origin URL directly meanwhile. (brand-new-aws)

- **A failed first `CREATE` must be cleaned up before you retry.** A stack left in
  `ROLLBACK_COMPLETE` (and a SAM managed-bucket stack stuck in `REVIEW_IN_PROGRESS`) can only be
  *deleted*, never updated. And any resource with `DeletionPolicy: Retain` survives the rollback
  orphaned, so the retry then fails `already exists` until you delete the orphan too.
  (failed-first-create)

- **Review the change set before applying — `Replacement: True` on a stateful resource is a
  data-loss hard stop.** Replacement creates a *new, empty* resource; a DynamoDB table shows it
  whenever an immutable property (its `KeySchema`/`AttributeDefinitions`) changes. Enable stack
  **termination protection** too — it's a one-time CLI/API call (`update-termination-protection`),
  not expressible in the template body. (review-change-set)

- **A custom request header turns even a public GET into a preflighted CORS request.** Any
  non-simple header (e.g. a client-version header) makes the browser send an `OPTIONS` preflight, so
  the API's CORS `AllowHeaders` must list that header or the real request is blocked *in the
  browser* — while server-side unit tests that never run the CORS layer stay green.
  (custom-request-header)

- **Reach AWS from a session with the AWS CLI or a boto3 script — there is no AWS MCP tool.** A
  stack's real state comes from a CLI call (`aws cloudformation describe-stacks …`) — the last
  green deploy workflow only reports the last *deploy*, not the current stack state. The CLI is
  **not pre-installed on the cloud/web runner** (nor `boto3`/`sam`), so declare its install in the
  **environment setup script** (`pip install awscli`, or the official bundle) rather than per
  session; point it at the sandbox proxy's CA bundle (`AWS_CA_BUNDLE`) if a call fails TLS
  verification. (reach-aws-session)
===== SKILL sam-template
---
name: sam-template
description: Shaping a SAM template's CloudFront, API Gateway CORS, cache and DynamoDB index resources — forwarding Authorization, non-http origins, what a CDN hit skips, TTL over invalidation, GSI backfill. Use when editing a SAM template.yaml or template.yml.
metadata:
  body: guidelines
  force-load-on-file-edits-paths:
    - "**/template.yaml"
    - "**/template.yml"
---

# SAM template resources

## CloudFront and the cache

- **CloudFront won't forward `Authorization` via a *custom* origin-request policy** — a custom
  `AWS::CloudFront::OriginRequestPolicy` listing `Authorization` is rejected at deploy ("The
  parameter Headers contains Authorization that is not allowed"). To forward it to the origin while
  keeping it out of the cache key (so public GETs share one cached entry), attach the **managed**
  `AllViewerExceptHostHeader` policy (id `b689b0a8-53d0-40ab-baf2-68738e2966ac`) plus a custom cache
  policy that omits `Authorization`. Use the *ExceptHostHeader* variant specifically: forwarding the
  viewer `Host` to an API Gateway origin returns 403. (cloudfront-wont-forward)

- **A CDN cache hit is served before the request reaches the origin or its authorizer**, so you
  cannot enforce request auth on a *cacheable* read without edge compute (Lambda@Edge) — and keying
  the cache per token destroys the hit rate that justified caching. Treat cacheable endpoints as
  public by design, and protect only uncached (write / per-user) paths at the authorizer.
  (cdn-cache-hit)

- **Prefer a short CloudFront TTL over per-write cache invalidation.** Invalidation is billed per
  path beyond a small monthly free allowance, so a write-through design that invalidates on every
  write is a cost trap; a short TTL plus optimistic local rendering hides the propagation delay from
  the writer. (prefer-short-cloudfront)

## API Gateway CORS

- **API Gateway HTTP API (v2) rejects a `chrome-extension://` origin in CORS `AllowOrigins`** with
  `BadRequestException: Invalid format for origin`, accepting only `http(s)://…` or `*`. An API
  fronted by a browser-extension (or other non-`http`) origin must therefore set `AllowOrigins:
  ['*']` and rely on its **JWT authorizer**, not CORS, as the security boundary. (api-gateway-http)

## DynamoDB

- **Adding a DynamoDB GSI does not backfill existing items.** The `UpdateTable` is additive and
  indexes only items that already carry the index's key attributes; rows written earlier stay
  invisible until each is rewritten with those attributes. Plan an explicit backfill pass if
  pre-existing data must appear in the new index. (adding-dynamodb-gsi)
===== SKILL sam-build-and-deps
---
name: sam-build-and-deps
description: Declaring a SAM Lambda's build dependencies — esbuild as a regular dependency for SAM's production-only install, and bundling the AWS SDK packages the handler imports instead of trusting the managed runtime's copy. Use when editing package.json or the build settings of a SAM template.
metadata:
  body: guidelines
  force-load-on-file-edits-paths:
    - "package.json"
    - "**/template.yaml"
    - "**/template.yml"
---

# SAM build and dependencies

- **esbuild must be a regular `dependency`, not a `devDependency`.** SAM's esbuild builder runs a
  *production-only* `npm install` in its scratch dir, so a `devDependency` esbuild is skipped and
  the build fails with "Cannot find esbuild." Declare it in `dependencies`, or put it on the
  runner's `PATH` before `sam build`. (esbuild-must-be)

- **Bundle the AWS SDK into the Lambda artifact rather than relying on the managed runtime's copy.**
  The runtime doesn't ship every SDK sub-package (a missing one fails only at invoke), and its
  bundled SDK minor version drifts under you. Declare and bundle the SDK packages you import, and
  pin a non-EOL runtime explicitly rather than letting it float. (bundle-aws-sdk)

 Portable, project-agnostic gotchas for the AWS Serverless Application Model and the API-Gateway/CloudFront stack it deploys — true for any SAM project read cold.
 
-- **`BuildMethod: esbuild` strips the entry's subdirectory from the Handler path.** With a single entry point in a subdirectory (`EntryPoints: [src/handler.mjs]`), SAM's esbuild builder writes the bundle to `<artifact-root>/handler.js` — esbuild's default `outbase` is the entry's own dir. Set `Handler: handler.handler`, not `src/handler.handler`; `sam build` succeeds either way, and the wrong value fails only at first invoke with `Runtime.ImportModuleError: Cannot find module 'src/handler'`.
 - **esbuild must be a regular `dependency`, not a `devDependency`.** SAM's esbuild builder runs a *production-only* `npm install` in its scratch dir, so a `devDependency` esbuild is skipped and the build fails with "Cannot find esbuild." Declare it in `dependencies`, or put it on the runner's `PATH` before `sam build`.
 - **CloudFront won't forward `Authorization` via a *custom* origin-request policy** — a custom `AWS::CloudFront::OriginRequestPolicy` listing `Authorization` is rejected at deploy ("The parameter Headers contains Authorization that is not allowed"). To forward it to the origin while keeping it out of the cache key (so public GETs share one cached entry), attach the **managed** `AllViewerExceptHostHeader` policy (id `b689b0a8-53d0-40ab-baf2-68738e2966ac`) plus a custom cache policy that omits `Authorization`. Use the *ExceptHostHeader* variant specifically: forwarding the viewer `Host` to an API Gateway origin returns 403.
 - **A deploy role must be able to drive the transform and CloudFront, or change-set creation fails with the real reason hidden.** The `Serverless-2016-10-31` transform runs as a macro, so the deploy principal needs `cloudformation:*`, and CloudFront management needs `cloudfront:*`, both at `Resource: "*"` (scope the *data-plane* grants to your stack instead). `sam deploy` surfaces only `Waiter ChangeSetCreateComplete failed` — the actual `AccessDenied` is visible only in the CloudFormation console's **Change sets** tab. Don't paper over it with `AdministratorAccess`.

{"number":185,"title":"flutter/node pack detect: match monorepo subdir markers","body":"## What

A lessons-learned improvement surfaced while landing #165 in the ShoutsAndWhispers consumer.

The `flutter` and `node` packs fingerprinted a **repo-root** `pubspec.yaml` / `package.json`. A monorepo that keeps its Flutter app in `app/` and its Node functions in `functions/` (exactly ShoutsAndWhispers' layout) therefore failed `detect()`, and the consumer had to declare the pack **plus** an `accept`-with-reason just to satisfy the `pack-declaration` check.

Now `detect()` matches the marker at the repo root **or one directory down** — a monorepo's `app/` / `functions/` / `server/` dir — but **never deeper**, so a stray `pubspec.yaml`/`package.json` in a nested example or fixture tree can't trip detection. This mirrors the `android`/`ios` packs, which already match subdir markers (`android/app/src/main/AndroidManifest.xml`, `ios/Runner/Info.plist`).

## Verification

- New `checks/test/pack-detect.test.mjs` — 5 cases per pack: marker at root, one directory down (monorepo), two-or-more deep (must NOT match), no marker, and basename-only (`pubspec.yaml.bak` must NOT match).
- Full unit suite: **87/87** pass.
- `node checks/run.mjs` conformance sweep: clean.

## Follow-up (separate repo)

Once this ships and ShoutsAndWhispers re-syncs its `.claudinite/`, flutter/node will detect there and the `accept`-with-reason in its `.claudinite-checks.json` becomes an inert no-op (there's no stale-acceptance check, so it's harmless) — can be cleaned up opportunistically.

Closes #184

{"number":204,"title":"Pack environment requirements: corpus-owned generic script, packs declare the rest","body":"Closes #208.

Gives the corpus a **pack-driven cloud environment model**, so projects stop hand-rolling per-repo setup scripts and version hooks; the install logic lives with the technology.

## The model
- A pack declares what a web session needs in an optional **`env`** field (`label`, `setup`, `probe`). `setup`/`probe` may be a string **or a function of per-repo params** the project supplies in `.claudinite-checks.json` under **`packConfig`** (packs can require projects to state parameters about their usage — e.g. where `node` runs `npm ci`).
- **`packs/env.mjs`** drives it from the repo's *active* packs: **`install`** (run each fragment in the checkout), **`check`** (web-only SessionStart assert), **`plan`** (preview).
- **Pure probes, no version flag.** `check` asserts each requirement *directly* (Flutter on PATH, `node_modules` present) — the probes are the source of truth. A genuinely new requirement fails its probe and prompts a re-paste; the limited drift (a changed-but-still-present requirement) is accepted.
- **One corpus-owned generic script** — [`environment-setup.sh`](https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/blob/claude/pack-env-requirements/environment-setup.sh) at the corpus root, synced into every consumer's `.claudinite/`. Projects commit **no** copy; they wire the check hook and paste the corpus script (cd → sync → git hygiene → `env.mjs install`).

## First declarations
- **`flutter`** — the Flutter SDK. **`node`** — `npm ci`, per-repo `dirs`.
- The two git configs (`merge.ours.driver`, `rerere.enabled`) live in the generic script as cheap universal hygiene.

## Validation
- `node --test checks/test/*.test.mjs skills/*/*.test.mjs` → **104/104**; `node checks/run.mjs` clean; CI green.

## Consumers (separate PRs, depend on this landing + mount re-sync)

{"number":2164,"title":"Claudinite canon: prose to checks","body":"Two conversions, both **A** rows of [`docs/declarative-checks/rule-inventory.md`](../blob/main/docs/declarative-checks/rule-inventory.md) in a pack that had never been swept against it. `flutter` shipped zero checks and 10 prose rules; it now ships two checks and nine rules.

## What converted

| Prose | Became | Severity |
|---|---|---|
| `packs/flutter/RULES.md` — *"**Anything that fetches must be injectable**: map tile providers, avatar images. Widget tests block real HTTP … so a `NetworkImage`/network `TileProvider` in the tree means error boxes, not screenshots."* (inventory row 8) | **`flutter/network-fetch-in-widget-tree`** | blocking (`since: 2026-09-20`) |
| `packs/flutter/RULES.md` — *"**Inject the clock.** Any widget that formats or compares times takes a `Clock` port; relative time rendered from `DateTime.now()` is untestable and drifts goldens."* (inventory row 5) | **`flutter/device-clock-not-injected`** | blocking (`since: 2026-09-20`) |

Both are declared checks — patterns over files, the ladder's highest check rung — and both are **forbidden patterns**, so neither pins a call site in place. `since` puts them inside the two-week window, so a repo with a backlog sees them advisory first and they bite at their real severity once someone has had time to clear it.

**`flutter/network-fetch-in-widget-tree`** scans `lib/ui|screens|widgets/**.dart` — the tree the pack's own architecture rule keeps free of platform concerns — and flags `Image.network(`, `NetworkImage(`, `CachedNetworkImage(`/`…Provider(` and `NetworkTileProvider(`. `main.dart` and the adapters beside it are out of scope deliberately: that is where the real provider is legitimately constructed and handed down, which is the shape the rule asks for. The call anchor is what separates constructing a fetcher from naming one, so a type test (`p is NetworkImage`) and a substitute whose name merely extends the constructor's are both quiet.

**`flutter/device-clock-not-injected`** scans `lib/**.dart` except `lib/testing/` (the shipped fakes pin their own clock) and flags the argument-less `DateTime.now()`. A file declaring a `class …Clock` is exempt — the class implementing the port is the one place the read belongs — and `DateTime.utc(…)`/`DateTime.parse(…)` are not clock reads.

## See-it-fail

Both declarations were written with detection neutered first: all **6** violating fixtures went red against a pattern that cannot match, and the 12 clean cases passed. Then each false-positive guard was mutated in turn, watched to bite, and restored:

| Mutation | Case that bit |
|---|---|
| widen the widget-tree scope to every Dart file | the adapters/`main.dart` wiring, and the test file |
| stop blanking comments (both rules) | the comment naming the constructor it warns about |
| drop the call anchor from the provider names | `p is NetworkImage` |
| widen the clock rule's scope past `lib/` | `tool/generate_fixtures.dart` |
| drop the `class …Clock` exemption | the class that implements the port |
| stop excluding `lib/testing/` | the fake world's pinned clock |
| match any `DateTime` constructor, not `now()` | `DateTime.utc(1970)` / `DateTime.parse(s)` |

`packs/flutter/test/network-fetch-in-widget-tree.test.mjs` (10 cases) and `packs/flutter/test/device-clock-not-injected.test.mjs` (8 cases).

**"Already covered" was tested, not reasoned.** A fixture repo declaring **all 37** canon packs, carrying one `lib/ui/show.dart` that breaks both rules, was swept with `check_the_world`: the two new rules are the only things in the catalog that see it. Nothing else in the corpus scans Dart at all.

## Deletion test

- **`Inject the clock.` is deleted whole.** The architecture rule two bullets above it already states that the clock enters the UI as a port, and the check's failure message carries the consequence (untestable, the golden drifts) with its `fix` naming both the port and the one place the read belongs. Nothing was left for the paragraph to carry. This is the `rules-append-only` advisory's *deliberate retirement* case, named here as that check asks.
- **`Anything that fetches must be injectable` stays whole.** It also carries the substitute recipe — a canvas-drawn `ImageProvider` needing no asset files — a remedy the finding's `fix` line does not state.

## Also

- `packs/flutter/references.md` is new, created on its first entry as the prose skill prescribes: one `check:` entry per check, each written so a later `rule-revalidation` pass can reaffirm or retire it.
- Pack version and `VERSIONS.md` are deliberately untouched — both are derived on the base branch after this lands.

## Green before the PR

- `node --test $(git ls-files '*.test.mjs')` → **3757 pass / 0 fail** (3739 before, +18).
- `check_the_world` exit 0, **0 blocking**; its advisory set is byte-for-byte the same as `main`'s on the same tree (`file-placement` ×227, `design-doc-status-banner` ×4, `rules-line-length` ×1, all pre-existing). Neither new rule fires here — this repo declares no `flutter` and carries no Dart.
- `check_the_work` → 0 blocking, 1 advisory: the `rules-append-only` note on the retired rule, answered above.

## Examined and left as prose

- **`research-project`'s "upload paths are session-specific"** — the inventory suggests banning `[REDACTED:env:CLAUDE_ADDITIONAL_DIRECTORIES]`, `/tmp/uploads`. Nothing in the corpus names those paths: the signature is the inventory author's invention, not the rule's, so converting it would ship an enumerated path list nobody has evidence for. Rejected on the same ground as `flutter`'s forbidden-import-prefix list.
- **`web-scraping`'s "prefer metadata over element positions"** — a positional selector inside a query call is a genuine static signature and the nearest miss. Detection is not confident in Python: `stripComments` is JS-shaped, so a `#` comment is not blanked, and the guard that would blank it (`^[^#]*`) breaks on the `#id` selectors the pattern must keep seeing. Left as prose; the pack's README verdict ("no checks — every rule is about a *remote* service's behaviour") stands for the rest of it.
- **`flutter`'s `flutter analyze` at zero issues** — convertible in shape (a workflow running it without `--fatal-infos`), but the check would rest on an unverified claim about that flag's default, and no Flutter toolchain is reachable from this session to verify it against a real run.
- **`flutter`'s import boundary, golden mechanics and test-runner rules** — re-derived; the 2026-07-26 → 2026-08-30 tracker rejections still hold (the forbidden-prefix list is unbounded, the rest is runtime or authoring judgment).

{"number":1634,"title":"Every pack's RULES.md carries rules, not a description of the pack","body":"Closes #1632

The same audit #1625 got, across the other 25 packs. Every one opened its `RULES.md` with a paragraph describing what the pack covers ("Portable, project-agnostic practices for …", "This document defines how the owner wants … run"), and several framed their sections the same way. It changes nothing a session does, every session in every declaring repo pays for it, and each pack's `README.md` plus its manifest's `ruleRoutingGuidance` (what renders into `directory.GENERATED.md`) already carries it — I checked each one before dropping it.

**Dropped:** 25 intro paragraphs; the playbook framing in `research-project` and `spec-driven-product` (what the class is, "a default to adapt, not a contract"); `basics`'s four section preambles, including the skill list the session's own skill roster already carries; `headless-browser`'s scope note; `macos`'s "these are the rules that cost the most to learn" and "Two consequences"; `node`'s "Two that recur".

**Kept as rules, re-keyed:** `macos`'s usage-description paragraph becomes **Reaching for a protected resource**; `research-project`'s interaction-cadence paragraph becomes two bullets; `python`'s three section-shaped rules become trigger-keyed bullets at the ration (280 → 150 words).

**Left alone:** the paragraph-form instruction in `executable-requirements` and `research-project` — it is prose-shaped, but it instructs, and rewriting it is a rewrite of substance rather than this sweep. Corpus non-rule prose is 2,900 → 1,080 words, and what remains is nearly all of that kind. Those two, plus `spec-driven-product`, read as manuals whose procedure would sit better in a skill; worth a separate look.

Pack READMEs take the two new rule rows (`macos`, `research-project`) and recounted word columns where a dropped preamble had been counted into a rule. Every touched pack bumps its version with a `VERSIONS.md` row.

35:-# Spec-Driven Product Working Procedures — a portable playbook
36:-
37:-This document defines **how the owner wants a spec-driven product project run**, as a **bootstrap to
38:-drop into a new project of this class** from day one. The class: **build and ship a small end-user
39:-product against an executable specification — every requirement is a numbered leaf claimed by exactly
40:-one executable proof of the right kind, expected results are owned by the owner, and releases cut
41:-automatically while `main` stays green.** The archetype is a UI-centric product (a browser-extension
42:-panel, a small web or mobile app) and the examples lean that way, but the discipline applies wherever
43:-observable behavior can be specified leaf by leaf — read "surface", "render", and "server" as whatever
44:-they mean for your project.
45:-
46:-It is written to be project-agnostic: it carries the durable working procedures and none of the
47:-product, stack, or harness specifics of any particular project. Those live elsewhere — platform
48:-gotchas in the project's technology packs, release mechanics in its release pack or release doc, and
49:-the concrete spec, harness, and commands in the project's own docs. General test-trust practices
50:-(see-it-fail, snapshot hygiene, the re-baselining approval procedure, capture-artifact-first) are
51:-corpus canon in the writing-tests skill; this pack assumes them and adds the class's development loop
52:-on top.
53:-
54:-Treat it as a **default to adapt, not a contract**: when a rule here doesn't fit, say why and drop it;
55:-when the project needs a rule this document lacks, add it in the project's own docs first. The
56:-non-negotiable is the spirit: **the spec is executable, the expecteds belong to the owner, the real
57:-code produces every actual, and the product ships on green.**

content.content:
Two halves of one problem: nothing said where a piece of content belongs,
    so it defaulted into the baseline pack — which is where the GitHub Actions
    cron doctrine landed in the first place.
    
    Routing (#559). Every pack.mjs now declares routing: { belongs, excludes },
    each side capped at 20 words, with excludes naming the pack that owns the
    other side. A new blocking check (pack-routing-declared, basics) holds
    canon and consumer local packs alike to it, relevance-first on a pack.mjs
    in the sweep. The pack-prose loader emits the whole set as a routing table
    at session start, for every pack discovered rather than only the active
    ones — a consumer holds just the packs it vendored, so the discovered set
    is already what it can route into. Declarations filled in for all 27 canon
    packs and the home's two local packs.
    
    Cron doctrine (#556). Moved out of packs/basics/scheduled-tasks.md into a
    bundled skill in the pack that owns Actions platform behaviour:
    github-actions/skills/github-actions-scheduling. It states what schedule:
    actually guarantees (late fires, dropped fires, the 60-day inactivity
    disable, the Upptime measurement) and what follows — never depend on a
    firing happening or on when it happened, stay idempotent and self-catching,
    catch up the most recent slot only, keep off :00, say "about hourly,
    best-effort", and don't debug a late run as a bug before checking whether
    GitHub fired at all.
    
    Closes #559
    Refs #556
    
    Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
    Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_01UeXiMjUB2tcQ1gJ7TqTrHB
    
    * Routing: a boundary true of every pack routes nothing
    
    The two local packs both excluded "anything portable to a consuming repo",
    which is the local-pack rule restated — true of either by definition, so
    the row said nothing about which of the two a piece of content belongs to.
    Point them at each other instead: canon-curation is the fleet-facing
    curation of the shared corpus, claudinite is the home's own non-portable
    working rules, and each excludes names the other.
    
    Adds the general rule to the routing section in packs/README.md: state
    what separates a pack from its nearest neighbours, since a boundary that
    holds for every pack carries no routing information and wastes the row.
    
    Refs #559
    
    Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
    Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_01UeXiMjUB2tcQ1gJ7TqTrHB
    
    * Pack manifest spec: routing, skills and scoped rules declared, not checked
    
    Renames the routing field to ruleRoutingGuidance, and moves its enforcement
    off a conformance check and onto the pack definition itself.
    
    engine/pack_loader/pack-schema.mjs is the spec: every field a pack.mjs may
    carry, which are required, and the constraints on each. The loader validates
    every manifest against it — canon and consumer local packs alike — so an
    incomplete declaration is a blocking config error at load, the same class as
    invalid JSON in .claudinite-checks.json. Reported, not fatal: a pack with an
    incomplete declaration still loads and still runs its checks. The vocabulary
    is closed, so a typo like `rule:` fails loudly instead of being ignored.
    packs/basics/pack-routing-declared.mjs and its test are gone.
    
    The manifest now also carries what the pack README used to state:
    
    - `skills: [...]` names the bundled skills, held to the skills/ tree in both
      directions — an undeclared directory is a skill nothing announces, and a
      declared name with no directory is a manifest that lies.
    - `worldRules` / `workRules` replace the single `rules` array, so a rule's
      scope is its placement. The loader flattens both into the `rules` array the
      runners walk, stamping each rule's scope from the list it came from. A rule
      module may still carry `scope` for the dispatch seam that reads it off the
      rule object, but the two must agree — a mismatch is a load error.
    
    Test fixtures that build a fake corpus now copy pack-schema.mjs beside the
    registry, and the vendor set grew by that one file.
    
    Refs #559
    
    Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
    Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_01UeXiMjUB2tcQ1gJ7TqTrHB
    
    * Pack READMEs: drop what the manifest now carries
    
    With skills and scope-split rules declared on pack.mjs, a pack README's
    checks table and skills table are a second copy of the manifest — and they
    had already drifted: basics/README.md listed a skill-ownership check the
    pack does not carry, and omitted catalog-completeness and
    comment-classification.
    
    Strips both tables from every pack README, and deletes the five files that
    were nothing else: github-actions (activation line + two tables) and the
    four stub packs (android, ios, app-store-release, play-store-release),
    whose one non-derivable sentence — the expected first source — moves into
    the manifest header comment where the rest of the stub note already lives.
    
    The other 22 READMEs stay: they carry provenance, design rationale, scope
    notes against sibling packs, and an index of their RULES.md prose — none
    of which the manifest holds. "Most packs lose the README" turned out to be
    "most packs lose the duplicated tables".
    
    catalog-completeness now looks for the pack DIRECTORY in the catalog rather
    than a README inside it, since a pack need not have one, and the catalog's
    five affected rows link the directory instead.
    
    Refs #559
    
    Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
    Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_01UeXiMjUB2tcQ1gJ7TqTrHB

# spec-driven-product pack

A project-class pack (prose, declared — no fingerprint) for the recurring class: build and ship a
small end-user product against an executable spec — every requirement a numbered leaf claimed by
exactly one right-kind proof, expected results owner-owned, releases automatic while `main` is green.
Its enforcement deliberately lives inside the declaring project (the committed coverage gate and
allowlist the playbook requires), so the pack itself ships no checks; the sections are loop and
judgment, kept as prose.

Distilled from the two worked examples of the class in the owner's fleet:
missingbulb/GoogleCalendarEventCreator's executable-requirements methodology (`dev/requirements/` —
the origin) and missingbulb/TLDR's adaptation of it (`dev/requirements/`,
`dev/docs/ui-testing-guideline.md`, which adds the cross-tier server kind). The general test-trust
rules both build on are corpus canon already, and are pointed to rather than restated here.

## Rules (`RULES.md`)

| Rule | Severity | Reason | Enforcement |
|---|---|---|---|
| One numbered document states the product | medium | complexity | prose: <50 words |
| A leaf is what the harness asserts | medium | complexity | prose: <100 words |
| Every leaf carries a stable id. | high | complexity | prose: <50 words |
| Doc-first, red by default. | high | correctness | prose: <50 words |
| The spec drives the tests | high | correctness | prose: <100 words |
| Enforce the bijection with a coverage gate | high | correctness | prose: <50 words |
| A kind is one way to assert | low | complexity | prose: <50 words |
| A kind may be a singleton. | low | complexity | prose: <50 words |
| Give each kind's runner a named lane | medium | performance | prose: <50 words |
| Actuals come from the real code. | high | correctness | prose: <50 words |
| Committed expecteds are the owner's approval record | high | correctness | prose: <50 words |
| The contract takes two honest shapes. | medium | complexity | prose: <100 words |
| On a mismatch, surface both and ask | high | correctness | prose: <50 words |
| Expected changes ride the normal review flow | high | correctness | prose: <50 words |
| One rule, sibling leaves per enforcing tier | medium | complexity | prose: <50 words |
| Prove a rule where it is enforced | medium | correctness | prose: <50 words |
| When breadth of targets is the value | medium | complexity | prose: <50 words |
| Prove each target against a real sample | high | correctness | prose: <100 words |
| Adding a target is a documented flow | low | complexity | prose: <50 words |
| Name what the harness cannot reach | high | correctness | prose: <100 words |
| Mark a deliberate gap at its leaf | high | correctness | prose: <100 words |
| Embed regenerated renders in the spec | medium | complexity | prose: <50 words |
| Regenerate, never hand-edit. | high | correctness | prose: <50 words |
| main is always releasable, automation releases | high | correctness | prose: <100 words |
| The version users see moves deliberately. | medium | correctness | prose: <50 words |

The deterministic golden-image method the gallery leans on is canon in the writing-tests skill —
matching the render engine to the surface (a bit-exact rasterizer for inline-styled/SVG surfaces, a
headless browser for pages that use grid/vars/emoji/form-widgets), bundled fonts, capturing a
host-page surface with styles inlined, and a drift gate on the embedded gallery.

// test-trust rules the playbook leans on (see-it-fail, snapshot hygiene,
// re-baselining approval) stay in the writing-tests skill; release mechanics
// stay in the platform's release surface (e.g. the chrome-extension pack's).

  version: '60920.1',

    Pack badges: a mark per pack, and a README row bootstrap and baselining maintain (#525)
    
    * Pack badges: a mark per pack, and one usage row for the README
    
    A consuming repo can now show which Claudinite packs it runs. Every pack
    declares its own mark on its manifest — `badge: { file, color, glyph }` —
    and engine/badges/render.mjs turns that declaration into the file the pack
    names. Nothing in the engine names a pack, so a new pack ships its badge
    with no edit anywhere else, and the glyph is a stroked SVG path rather than
    text so the mark renders identically wherever it is loaded.
    
    The rendered SVGs are committed: a README loads its artwork over HTTP, and a
    pack's badge rides its directory into a consumer's vendor set exactly like
    its prose and skills — so a consumer points at its own
    `.claudinite/shared/packs/<id>/badge.svg` with no network dependency here.
    They keep the plain `badge.svg` name a consumer pastes into a README rather
    than GENERATED-in-the-filename; engine-tests/badges/render.test.mjs is the
    drift guard that naming would otherwise buy, re-rendering every badge and
    failing when a tracked file and its manifest disagree.
    
    This repo's own README gets the row as a single generated strip
    (docs/pack-usage.svg) rather than one image per pack: core must not name the
    packs it runs, and a strip rendered from .claudinite-checks.json names none
    of them — it also costs one line of vertical space and stays correct when
    the declaration changes. The pack catalog gains the same marks beside its
    rows, and documents the field.
    
    Closes #526
    
    Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
    Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_01VwUpr4zTLChbLKeQWFnoR6
    
    * Badges: the file owns its artwork, the tool leaves the engine, the row leaves the strip
    
    Reworking the badges on review:
    
    - A manifest declares only the path — `badge: 'badge.svg'`. The colour and the
      glyph live in the SVG, where they are visible to anyone who opens the file
      and editable without touching a manifest. The tool never invents either: it
      PARSES both out of the file it is about to rewrite, so a set-wide restyle is
      one template edit plus one `restyle` run while each pack keeps its identity.
    - The renderer moves to dev/tools/badges/ (tests in dev/tools/tests/, a new CI
      root). Nothing at session time reads a badge, and the engine is what runs
      pack content and what every consumer vendors — a maintainer-side image
      generator is neither. The engine now knows nothing about badges at all; the
      badge FILES still ride their pack's directory into a consumer's vendor set.
    - docs/pack-usage.svg is gone. The README shows the pack badges themselves, one
      line of images. That means a core file names the packs it runs, which the
      barriers config bars — so it is now a reviewed exception rather than a
      workaround, with the pack row held to the resolved declaration by a test, so
      the row cannot drift out of step the way a hand-written list would.
    - The README's H1 goes with it: the row is the header, with the tagline beside
      it on the same line.
    
    Closes #526
    
    Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
    Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_01VwUpr4zTLChbLKeQWFnoR6
    
    * Badges: the README row becomes a bootstrap/baselining surface
    
    - The barriers config no longer guards README.md, so the README may name the
      packs it runs; the reviewed exception that bought the same thing is gone with
      it, and the `# Claudinite` title is back above the row.
    - Adopting Claudinite now WRITES the row, and the nightly keeps it true: it is a
      fourth surface on the one wiring converge bootstrap Part 6 and baselining both
      call. A repo's row is derived from its declaration each night, so it cannot go
      stale the day the repo declares its next pack — which is the whole reason it
      is not hand-written. The row sits between `<!-- claudinite:packs -->` markers,
      so it re-converges in place wherever a repo moves it and anything the repo
      writes after the closing marker on that line stays its own.
    - The repo has the last word. The converge materializes
      `"badges": { "readme": "auto" }` into `.claudinite-checks.json` rather than
      inferring the default from absence, so the knob sits where anyone would look
      for it; `"off"` stops both halves — no more updates, and no re-adding a row
      the repo has deleted.
    - The row a consumer gets and the row this repo shows are one format: the canon
      home never baselines (no mount to refresh), so its own row is asserted against
      what that converge would write rather than against a second copy of the shape.
    
    Verified against a simulated consumer with the corpus actually mounted: the row
    resolves to `.claudinite/shared/packs/<id>/badge.svg` for canon packs and
    `.claudinite/local/packs/<id>/badge.svg` for the repo's own, the `requires`
    closure included. The consumer-isolation barrier needed no widening for that —
    checked directly, with a quoted-mount-path control proving it was armed.
    
    Closes #526
    
    Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
    Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_01VwUpr4zTLChbLKeQWFnoR6

# product-wiki pack

The self-growing product research wiki standard: a repo keeps its
market/user/competitor research as agent-maintained wikis under `product-wiki/`
(Karpathy's LLM-wiki pattern — compile findings once, refine in place, cite
everything), walled off from the code so nothing can silently depend on
unreviewed research, with one human-reviewed crossing point. Declared by the
project (fingerprint: `product-wiki/product-requirements/README.md` — the sink is
the standard's one structural constant). Takes **no config**: the layout is the
standard.

## The standard

- `product-wiki/` at the repo root. Two reserved children with fixed meaning:
  **`product-wiki/product-requirements/`** — the human-reviewed distillation of the
  wikis into product requirements, the **only** `product-wiki/` content the rest of
  the repo may reference, never auto-grown — and **`product-wiki/sample-data/`** —
  small illustrative assets a wiki claim points to (never test fixtures).
- **Everything else under `product-wiki/` is wiki space** — any names, any nesting.
  A wiki page is a `README.md` at depth ≥ 2 under `product-wiki/` outside the two
  reserved subtrees. The folder is the classifier; there is no wikis manifest
  to drift, and a renamed wiki folder is still a wiki folder — still checked,
  still barred.
- Every wiki page **opens with `## Key insights`** — up to seven bullets, one
  terse plain-words line each, carrying what the research found, ahead of every
  other section. The body is the research record; the header is what makes it
  readable, so a human who reads only the header understands what was researched
  and what came of it.
- Every wiki page also carries `## Sources` (every source bullet carrying its
  real URL), `## Growth log` (dated bullets, newest change appended per pass),
  and `## Open questions` (the research backlog the growth passes work from).
- Growth is scheduled research: the pack's weekly scheduled task
  ([tasks/wiki-growth/task.md](tasks/wiki-growth/task.md)) reads
  the wikis, researches what their own open questions flag, writes back cited,
  and delivers an unmerged PR. Most passes correctly change nothing.

## Rules (`RULES.md`)

Two rules, for the sessions that only read the wiki:

| Rule | Severity | Reason | Enforcement |
|---|---|---|---|
| Working on a requirement or spec | high | correctness | prose: <50 words |
| Building on `product-wiki/` elsewhere | critical | correctness | prose: <50 words + check (`product-wiki-isolation`) |

Everything about *editing* a page — the `## Key insights` header, citation, correction without
deletion, the growth log, sample-data, the no-fabricated-growth stop — is the
[`writing-wiki-pages`](skills/writing-wiki-pages/SKILL.md) skill, forced for `product-wiki/**` by
its own `force-load-on-file-edits-paths`: the PreToolUse guard holds a file tool aimed there until the
session has loaded it, and the `skill-loaded-before-editing` work rule catches an edit made
another way. The weekly task loads it by name.

## Checks

| Check | Severity | Reason | Enforcement |
|---|---|---|---|
| `product-wiki-layout` | high | correctness | check: blocking |
| `product-wiki-page-sections` | medium | complexity | check: blocking |
| `product-wiki-key-insights` | medium | complexity | check: blocking |
| `product-wiki-growth-log` | medium | correctness | check: blocking |
| `product-wiki-sources` | high | correctness | check: blocking |
| `product-wiki-freshness` | medium | correctness | check: advisory |
| `product-wiki-isolation` | critical | correctness | check: blocking (fixed barrier) |

`product-wiki-key-insights` enforces the header's **shape** — it leads every other
section, it is bullets only, it carries at least one and at most seven, and no
bullet runs past **140 characters**, about one line (a bullet's indented
continuation lines count as part of it, so hard-wrapping is free). The tight cap
is the point: a header is worth having only if it is faster to read than the
page, and the failure mode in practice is a bullet that keeps qualifying itself.
*Which* insights lead, how plainly they are worded, and keeping them true as
research moves is judgment — that lives in RULES.md and the growth worker, and
no check can score it. The missing heading itself is
`product-wiki-page-sections`' finding, never double-reported.

`product-wiki-freshness` is advisory **by design**, not as a maturity stage: it
is time-driven (a repo goes stale with no change to its tree), and a
wall-clock-dependent finding must never block a Stop or fail CI. It fires per
page after 45 days without a growth-log entry — the in-repo observer for "the
unattended growth channel silently stopped firing". Silence it with
`rules: {"product-wiki-freshness": "off"}`.

## Skill

| Skill | Trigger |
|---|---|
| [`writing-wiki-pages`](skills/writing-wiki-pages/SKILL.md) | any edit under `product-wiki/` — held by the guard until loaded |
| [`explore-link`](skills/explore-link/SKILL.md) | the owner hands over a URL (`/explore-link <url>`) — mine it for product, market, usage and pricing insights and fold them into an existing wiki page |

The two growth lanes differ only in who chooses the source: the weekly task picks
its own from the pages' open questions, the skill is given one.

## Scaffold template

```
product-wiki/
  README.md                        # index: what lives here, why it's walled off
  product-requirements/README.md   # the human-reviewed sink (required)
  <YourWiki>/README.md             # one folder per wiki — seeded like this:
```

```markdown
# <YourWiki>

What this wiki tracks, in a sentence or two.

## Key insights

- The non-obvious thing this research found, in one plain line.
- ...up to seven; short beats clever, no citations, no hedges.

## <Your content sections>

## Sources

- [Title](https://real.url/)

## Open questions

- What should the next growth pass look into?

## Growth log

- **YYYY-MM-DD** — initial seed.
```

## Excusing a deliberate crossing (accept, not except)

`product-wiki-isolation` is a **fixed** barrier — its edges are pack code, so a
consumer cannot add the barrier mechanism's per-rule `except` entries to it. Each
crossing finding's own fix text says so and names the lever that works: a
top-level (or pack-entry) **accept**:

```json
"accept": [
  { "rule": "product-wiki-isolation", "path": "docs/inventory.md",
    "reason": "historical ledger — enumerates the wikis it catalogs" }
]
```

Matched by rule id + exact path (or a `dir/` prefix for a subtree); the reason
is mandatory. Unlike a barrier rule's own `except`, accepts are **not**
staleness-audited — prune one by hand when the crossing it excused is gone.

## Bootstrap ordering

Declaring the pack before scaffolding `product-wiki/` yields two `layout` findings
plus the barrier's fail-closed empty-glob finding — three blocking arrows all
pointing at the same two-file scaffold. That is deliberate: a declaration is a
statement of intent, unlike an unconfigured barrier graph's no-op (where
config absence means "nothing declared").

## Known gaps

- **User research has no first-party evidence channel.** The pack's market and competitor halves
  cite public URLs; its user half has no in-repo home for interviews, tickets or call notes, so a
  user-research page is sourced from public proxies — review sites, forum threads, competitors'
  testimonials — which satisfies every check while describing other people's customers. The
  remedy is honest labelling, in [`writing-wiki-pages`](skills/writing-wiki-pages/SKILL.md).
  A raw evidence layer was considered and declined: no repo has qualitative input waiting, a
  committed transcript puts customer PII in git history permanently, and the layer's central
  "immutable" promise is unenforceable by checks that read the tracked tree rather than history.

- The barrier engine never scans `*.test.mjs`/test files as sources, so a test
  importing from wiki space is invisible to `product-wiki-isolation` — covered
  by prose (nothing a test asserts against belongs under `product-wiki/`), not
  fought in code.
- Accepts against `product-wiki-isolation` are pruned by hand (no staleness
  audit — see above).
- The weekly growth task rides the repo's own scheduler
  ([the writing-tasks skill](../claudinite-growth/skills/writing-tasks/SKILL.md));
  a repo without a `taskScheduler` anchor gets no unattended growth — the freshness
  advisory is the backstop that surfaces that, and the owner phrase "grow the
  product wiki" runs the same worker method in-session.
=== PACK
// Project-aspect standard pack: the self-growing product research wiki
// (compile-once/refine-in-place, cited, dated, isolated behind the reviewed
// product-requirements crossing point). The folder is the classifier: the two
// reserved names (product-requirements/, sample-data/) have fixed meaning;
// everything else under product-wiki/ is wiki space. Fingerprinted by the
// standard's one structural constant — the sink.
import { SINK_README } from './lib.mjs';

export default {
  version: '60920.2',
  minEngineVersion: '60822.1',
  ruleRoutingGuidance: {
    belongs: 'agent-maintained market, user and competitor research wikis — cited pages, growth logs, the reviewed product-requirements sink',
    excludes: 'how the product is built or specced — that is spec-driven-product; requirement proofs are executable-requirements',
  },
  marker: SINK_README,
  detect: (ctx) => ctx.tracked.includes(SINK_README),
  // The isolation wall (product-wiki-isolation) and the skeleton check
  // (product-wiki-layout) are both declared checks in this pack's
  // declared-checks.json. They are a designed pair: the barrier's glob target
  // fails closed on an empty product-wiki/ expansion, and layout owns the
  // missing-skeleton complaint. A declared check is run by the engine, so this
  // pack needs nothing else declared for its wall to stand (#1681 dropped the
  // `barriers` requirement, vestigial since the wall stopped being code).
  // Editing the wiki tree is the writing-wiki-pages skill's territory — its own
  // `force-load-on-file-edits-paths` names product-wiki/**, and the guard holds a file tool aimed
  // there until the session has loaded it — so the page rules are read once, by
  // the session that edits, rather than carried as prose by every session.
  // Adoption interview: the standard takes no config (the layout IS the config),
  // but a wiki with no research scope is a hollow skeleton — the answers frame
  // WHICH wikis get seeded and what the competitor set is measured against. They
  // record as intent on the entry (`answers`), never as config. Read the repo's
  // own product brief/spec first and confirm, rather than re-asking cold.
  questions: [
    {
      id: 'product',
      prompt: "What is the product — what does it do, and what is the core value it delivers? If the repo already carries a product brief or spec, read it and confirm rather than asking cold.",
      distill: 'recorded as intent on this entry (the pack takes no config); it names what the research is about and frames every seeded wiki',
    },
    {
      id: 'users',

=====README
# aws-sam pack

Active when the repo has a SAM `template.yaml`/`.yml`.

## Rules (`RULES.md`)

| Rule | Severity | Reason | Enforcement |
|---|---|---|---|
| The deploy role drives transform and CloudFront | high | correctness | prose: <100 words |
| A new account waits for CloudFront verification | medium | correctness | prose: <100 words |
| Clean up a failed first CREATE | high | correctness | prose: <100 words |
| Review the change set for Replacement | critical | correctness | prose: <100 words |
| A custom header preflights any GET | medium | correctness | prose: <100 words |
| Reach AWS by CLI or boto3 | low | complexity | prose: <100 words |

The template-shape gotchas (CloudFront `Authorization` forwarding, the CDN hit that skips the
authorizer, TTL over invalidation, non-`http` CORS origins, GSI backfill) are the
[`sam-template`](skills/sam-template/SKILL.md) skill, forced for `**/template.yaml` and
`**/template.yml`, and the build dependencies (esbuild as a regular dependency, bundling the SDK) are
[`sam-build-and-deps`](skills/sam-build-and-deps/SKILL.md), forced for `package.json` and the
template. The `esbuild-dependency` and `cloudfront-authorization` checks below carry their rules'
mechanical halves regardless.

## Skills

| Skill | Trigger |
|---|---|
| [`sam-template`](skills/sam-template/SKILL.md) | any edit of `template.yaml` / `template.yml` — held by the guard until loaded |
| [`sam-build-and-deps`](skills/sam-build-and-deps/SKILL.md) | any edit of `package.json` or the template — held by the guard until loaded |

## Checks

Each SAM gotcha with a false-positive-free signature in the template or the package manifest (the last two read it through the minimal YAML parser in `engine/checks/helpers/`).

| Check | Severity | Reason | Enforcement |
|---|---|---|---|
| `aws-sam/handler-path` | high | correctness | check: blocking |
| `aws-sam/esbuild-dependency` | high | correctness | check: blocking |
| `aws-sam/cloudfront-authorization` | critical | correctness | check: blocking |
=====PACK

// Three of the pack's gotchas have structural checks (via the minimal YAML
// parser); the rest are prose, in RULES.md or in the skill scoped to the file they concern.
export default {
  version: '60920.1',

    belongs: 'serverless AWS stacks: SAM template shape, Lambda handler paths, esbuild bundling, API Gateway and CloudFront gotchas',

};

{"number":567,"title":"Personal preferences as a pack, and one general primitive: a pack's own session-start step","body":"Personal interaction preferences are the concern of **one fleet's people**. The canon is mounted by every fleet that adopts Claudinite, which makes it both the wrong host for one group's preferences and the wrong authority on where they live — yet `preferences/<email>.md` sat here, and the session-start step fell back to a hardcoded `raw.githubusercontent.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/main/preferences` URL.

So the whole mechanism becomes **a pack**, and neither the engine nor the fleet enforcer learns what it is.

## The one thing core learns

The other end of the session already had the primitive: the SessionEnd runner discovers `session-end.mjs` in every active pack's directory, runs it bounded and fail-soft, and — in its own words — *"never names the pack whose step it runs, and never learns what one does."*

**`engine/pack_loader/run-pack-session-start.mjs`** is the symmetric half, on the same terms, with one difference: a session-start step's output *is* the contribution, so it is forwarded into the session context under the same `<!-- pack:id -->` marker the prose injector uses. It closes a real gap — prose is a **file**, fixed at vendor time and identical for every repo and person that mounts it, so a pack whose content is only knowable at session time had nowhere to put it but a core step naming that pack.

Two bounds keep the loan honest: every step is killed at a timeout, and its contribution is capped with the truncation stated in the injected text. Neither is a knob a pack can raise.

## The pack

`packs/claude-code-web-users-support/` — named for the **surface**, not the feature. A Claude Code *web* session runs for a signed-in person, in a managed container; a terminal session does neither. That difference is what makes a class of capability possible at all, and preferences are its first member.

| file | what it is |
|---|---|
| `pack.mjs` | `seededByDefault`, plus the adoption question that asks where the store is |
| `store.mjs` | the one resolver of the entry config, shared by the step and the rule |
| `session-start.mjs` | reads this user's file — local-first, then fetch, fail-soft at every miss |
| `store-configured.mjs` | one **advisory** rule, so a declared-but-unconfigured pack is not silently inert |
| `RULES.md` | the prose a session gets when the pack is active |

```json
{ "id": "claude-code-web-users-support", "config": { "repo": "missingbulb/Sheepdog" } }
```

**The engine now says nothing about preferences anywhere.** The setting, its resolver, its validation and the hook step are gone from `repo-context.mjs`, `engine/checks/README.md`, `bootstrap.md` and `vendoring/DESIGN.md`, replaced by the general contract. What the barriers rule already forbade — core naming a specific pack — is now true of this too.

## The enforcer doesn't know either

The sheepdog sweep first named the pack and carried its parameter, which made the enforcer a *second* place packs are known — the same coupling, one level out. So it is generalized:

| was | is |
|---|---|
| `fleet-preferences` | **`fleet-pack-seeds`** |
| `preferencesRepo: "…"` | **`packSeeds: [{ id, config? }]`** |

The sweep converges whatever declarations the **fleet** names in its own sheepdog config, and names no pack itself. Its contract is the migration op's, for the same reason: **seed, never override** — a member that already declares the pack, or already carries a config for it, keeps both. A test pins the constraint rather than trusting the prose: the sheepdog pack's sources may not contain the pack's name or the word "preferences" at all.

## The rollout: `declarePacks`, and a re-converge

The migration op follows the same move: **`settings`** (write a top-level key) becomes **`declarePacks`** (declare a pack and its config, seed-never-override). The record seeds the existing fleet with the store named.

That surfaced a real ordering bug in the class: **a declared pack whose code is not in the mount is a blocking `config` error**, and baselining vendors *before* it applies notes — so a seeded pack would red every member for a night. Baselining now **re-converges the mount when a note changed the declaration**, so both halves land in the one transactional commit. The rehearsal harness mirrors the same second pass (verified: the `re-converge` step fires and the fixture comes out green).

## What the owner has to do

**Nothing for today's fleet** — every member declares the pack on its next baselining, with the store named, mount and declaration in the same commit.

For the sweep to keep seeding afterwards (new members, a deleted entry), `FLEET_GITHUB_TOKEN` needs Contents *write* across the owner's repos. Until then the sweep fails loudly and the scheduler converges a `needs-human` issue.

## Verification

- **1296 tests, 0 failures.** World sweep **0 blocking**.
- The runner's 8 tests were written first and watched fail; they cover discovery, activation gating, config hand-off, ordering, and every fail-soft path (crash, non-zero exit, hang, over-cap, silence).
- **Consumer rehearsal green** in all four fixture shapes × both modes — including the new re-converge.
- Live: the orchestrator runs `selftest, load-active-prose, pack-session-start, mount-skills, env-check, interview-check`, and the pack's step injects under `<!-- pack:claude-code-web-users-support -->`.
- Rebased onto `18b86a3`; the `agent_preprocessing` → `prework` rename main landed (#685) is adopted in the new task.

{"number":741,"title":"sheepdog: fleet-add-missing-packs — parameterised scan, plus a forced mass-add","body":"## The problem

`fleet-fit` answered one question — *what might a member want that it does not declare?* — and answered it one way, by fingerprint, over the whole fleet, weekly. The owner's other question has the same shape and no home: **put this pack on these repos, with this config, now.** Its second stage is identical (adopt-pack against a member, one reviewed PR); only the first stage differs, because nothing is being suspected — the answer was already decided.

A second task would have duplicated the agent stage to change the work list's provenance. So the task is **parameterised** instead, and renamed for what it actually does.

## What changed

**Renamed** `packs/sheepdog/tasks/fleet-fit/` → `fleet-add-missing-packs/`, and the sweep `check-fleet-fit.mjs` → `scan-for-needed-packs.mjs` (it is now one half, not the whole task).

**Parameters, with no defaults** (`params.mjs`). Two call sites, each stating what it wants in full:

- the weekly run — `prework: 'node worker.mjs --scan-for-needed-packs=true --repos=all-covered-members'`, so what the cadence does is written in the file a reader opens first;
- a **forced** run — the scheduler's manual-run override bag, which the prework subprocess already inherits as `CLAUDINITE_OVERRIDES`. Overrides win over the command line, because that is what forcing *is*.

```
FORCE_TASKS=fleet-add-missing-packs
SCAN_FOR_NEEDED_PACKS=false
REPOS=Alpha Beta Gamma
ADD_PACKS=some-pack
PACK_CONFIG=some-pack.repo=owner/Store
PACK_ANSWER=some-pack.store=owner/Store — where the files live
```

`all-covered-members` is a **keyword the caller sends**, not a fallback the worker assumes — no call site can reach the whole fleet by omission. Values are space-separated because the bag splits keys on commas (asserted against the engine's own `parseOverrides`).

**The force half** (`force-add-packs.mjs`) converges the same work-list issues from a decision instead of a fingerprint, carrying the declaration entry — `config` *and* the owner's interview `answers` — rendered as the JSON that will land in the file. It writes nothing to any member; the adoption is still the agent's, through adopt-pack, one reviewed PR per member.

**Refusal is total.** A force throws before a single issue is written on: an unknown pack id (which would be a blocking settings error in the member), a repo that is not a covered member or is dormant, `all-covered-members` as a force target, and — per the owner's ruling — **any adoption-interview question the run did not answer**. Partial mass additions are the state hardest to see and hardest to undo.

**A real defect fixed along the way.** The worker never wrote `CLAUDINITE_REQUEST_AGENT`, so the conditional handoff never fired and this task's agent stage never ran at all. It now requests the agent iff a member is actually on the work list — quiet weeks still cost nothing.

**Continuity.** Open issues still labelled `fleet-fit` are adopted onto the new label rather than orphaned. Scanned (`Pack fit: …`) and forced (`Add packs: …`) issues share the label but keep separate lifecycles: a fingerprint going quiet must never retract a request a human made, and a scoped scan never closes issues for members it did not look at.

## Testing

- `packs-tests/sheepdog/tasks/fleet-add-missing-packs/params.test.mjs` — no defaults, override precedence, the comma/space coupling pinned against `engine/scheduler/run.mjs`, and each guard.
- `packs-tests/sheepdog/tasks/fleet-add-missing-packs/force-add-packs.test.mjs` — every refusal, target resolution, body fidelity, and the forced-issue closer (including that it never closes a scanned issue).
- Existing suite updated for the rename. Full run: **1409 pass, 0 fail**; `check_the_world.mjs`: **0 blocking**.

{"number":750,"title":"Fleet fan-out model: the enforcer dispatches, the member executes (#749)","body":"Closes #749.

## The problem, proven in production

`fleet-add-missing-packs`' first real run (Sheepdog#137) stopped at `needs-human`: its dispatch asked the **enforcer's** executor to run adopt-pack against four member repos, and that session is — correctly — scoped to the enforcer repo alone. Meanwhile `fleet-baseline` already embodied the model that works: the enforcer presses each member's own scheduler button, and everything agentic happens inside the member. This PR makes that fan-out the model for both fleet operations, and gives the engine the two properties the model needs.

## Engine

- **`manual` frequency** — the operator-lever non-cadence: never due on any schedule (`dueSlots` skips it), runs only when `FORCE_TASKS` names it; the forced slot is synthesized from the anchor date + the existing per-run marker.
- **Forced-only runs** — a run carrying `FORCE_TASKS` evaluates *only* the forced tasks, so a fan-out firing twenty members means exactly one task in each, not one plus each member's coincident backlog. To keep skipped-over slots due, the success watermark (`lastSuccessTime`) now counts **schedule-event runs only**.
- **Non-blocking forced runs** — an override-carrying dispatch gets a per-run concurrency group (stub + canon's own workflow), so a fan-out is never queued behind — or silently pending-cancelled by — the hourly cron.

## Sheepdog pack

- **`fleet-baseline` is now a `manual` agentless task** — dispatch only. Retired with the workflow shape: the `.github/` managed copy (deliverable only by #649's withhold-and-hand-to-the-agent path) and the 45-minute follow/report half, which is what forced the lever to be a workflow at all. Lever: *Run workflow* → `overrides: FORCE_TASKS=fleet-baseline[,REPOS=…][,DRY_RUN=true][,INCLUDE_DORMANT=true]`. The new `2026-08-11-fleet-baseline-task` migration removes lingering member copies (agentic, over the credential that holds `workflows`); the superseded 2026-08-05 record is annotated and is a permanent no-op by construction.
- **`fleet-add-missing-packs` is agentless.** Both halves converge an `add-packs` work-list issue **in the member** (`protocol.mjs`: `Add packs: requested for this repo` / `Add packs: suspected from this repo’s shape`, with requested entries rendered as a parseable JSON block) and fire that member's scheduler at `adopt-requested-packs`. All refusals stand: unknown pack id, non-member/dormant target, the fleet keyword as a force target, any unanswered interview question — each fails the whole run before anything is written. A `not planned` close of the suspected issue remains a standing decline; satisfied requests close `completed` on the weekly visit; members with open work are re-fired (the retry loop).
- `fireScheduler`/`classifyDispatch` move to the pack root — the shared floor both fan-out tasks press the button through.

## Member side (grow_with_claudinite)

- **New `adopt-requested-packs` task** (`manual`, sonnet, `open-pr` ceiling): prework requests the agent iff this repo has an open `add-packs` work list (empty re-fires end quietly); the agent adopts *requested* entries verbatim, *confirms* suspicions against the checkout (where `localFits` settles the content-reading fingerprints the REST sweep deferred), declines with reasons, one reviewed PR. Runs on the ordinary Action token — no fleet secret, which is the point.
- The protocol file is byte-identical in both packs (they may not import each other); `protocol.test.mjs` pins the copies together and pins the fired task id to the member task's directory id.

## Testing

- Engine: forced-only, forced-beats-due, `manual` never-due/fires-when-forced (`run.test.mjs`).
- Sheepdog: per-member issue convergence for both halves (open/rewrite/close/`not_planned`), refusals, body↔`entriesIn` round-trip, scope/dispatch classification tables, worker override plumbing pinned against the engine's parser.
- Member: end-to-end prework gate through the real `main()` with fetch stubbed (request file written iff work exists; PRs filtered; unreadable list fails loudly).
- Full run: **1404 pass, 0 fail**; `check_the_world.mjs`: **0 blocking**.

Sheepdog's own `.github/workflows/fleet-baseline.yml` was already removed (missingbulb/Sheepdog#145).

{"number":792,"title":"sheepdog: merge fleet-census and fleet-freshness into one roster sweep","body":"Closes #788.

## The problem

`fleet-census` (daily) and `fleet-freshness` (weekly) walked the same fleet and classified the same
repos, twice, from two independently-maintained pieces of code — each with its own
`paged(gh, '/user/repos?affiliation=owner')`, owner filter, empty-enumeration guard,
home/canon/archived/fork/excluded skips, and `readDeclaration` per repo.

The freshness sweep's header said it "takes coverage as given". It could not: the census's verdict
lived in another process on another cadence, so it re-derived the whole thing — and the two had
drifted apart:

- **`exclude` was applied at different points.** The census tested it only after finding a repo
  uncovered, so an excluded repo still carrying a declaration read **covered**; the freshness sweep
  tested it before reading anything, so the same repo read **out of scope**.
- **`unknown` meant different things.** An unparsable declaration failed the census run; a 500 from
  canon's compare failed the freshness run. Neither knew the other had happened.

## The change

One task, `fleet-roster`, replacing both. One enumeration, one declaration read per repo, one
roster; two views over it.

| file | holds |
|---|---|
| `tasks/fleet-roster/check-fleet-roster.mjs` | config, canon branch, enumeration, the single per-repo classification pass, and the two pure views |
| `tasks/fleet-roster/adoption-issues.mjs` | the `fleet-adoption` label, bodies, convergence, coverage report section |
| `tasks/fleet-roster/drift-issues.mjs` | the `fleet-drift` label, `classifyFreshness`, the mount probe, convergence, freshness report section |

The two issue families stay distinct — they close on unrelated conditions — and neither imports the
other, pinned by a test. Both report renderers are carried over verbatim and printed as two sections
of one summary, so every open `fleet-adoption` and `fleet-drift` thread converges as it does today.

The walk reads each repo's declaration **once** and adds the two mount reads only for members the
freshness question actually measures. The disagreements between the views are now deliberate and
tested: an excluded-but-covered repo is `covered` to one and `out of scope` to the other; canon is an
ordinary covered member to one and never measured by the other.

### Behaviour change: `unknown` is per-question

An unreadable or unparsable **declaration** is unknown to **both** halves — it is the input they
share. A failed **mount probe** (scheduler read, canon compare) is unknown to the **freshness** half
alone; the coverage half already read that declaration successfully and keeps its verdict. Either
kind fails the run, so nothing is downgraded to silence. Previously a compare outage erased a repo
from the freshness picture while the census, in its own run, reported it fine.

### Cadence: daily, and it costs API calls rather than saving them

Stated plainly in `task.md`, `task.mjs` and the commit, because "two walks become one" suggests a
saving that is not there. The freshness probe now runs daily too — roughly **two extra REST reads per
covered member** on the six days that used to be coverage-only. Against the live fleet (12 repos
under the owner) that is on the order of 120 extra reads a week, versus a 5000/hour limit. The
alternative was half a task computing its own weekly gate, which would reimplement dueness
(stateless in the engine: a slot is due iff its time falls in `(last successful run, now]`).
`convergeDrift`'s silence on an unchanged verdict is what keeps the faster cadence from becoming
noise.

What the merge buys is one roster instead of two that can disagree, one report, one failure boundary,
and the duplicated enumerate-and-classify code deleted. Drift converging within a day rather than a
week is the side benefit.

### The frozen marker

`drift-issues.mjs` still writes `<!-- fleet-freshness: <state> -->`, pinned by a test. Renaming it to
match the merged task would read any drift issue written by the old task as `unrecorded` and comment
a spurious verdict change on the first run after this lands. Freezing it is safe whichever way that
falls — it costs nothing if no such thread is open, and prevents the spurious comment if one is — so
the marker keeps the retired task's name and a comment at the site says why.

## Migration

No baseline migration record, and this is now checked against the live enforcer rather than reasoned
about (see Verification):

- Both retired tasks are `agent_model: 'none'`, so neither ever produced a dispatch issue for
  `resolve-dispatch`'s `task-gone` path to find.
- Run records are log lines, not state keyed by id.
- The enforcer's `sheepdog` config entry carries `owner`, `kind`, `exclude`, `packSeeds` and a
  `digest` key (its local pack's, ignored by `parseSheepdogConfig`). **No key names a task.**
- The retired ids survive only as historical rows in the two GENERATED usage aggregates
  (`usage-fleet.GENERATED.json`, `.claudinite/local/usage.GENERATED.json`), keyed
  `sheepdog/fleet-census`. `foldTaskRuns` carries prior rows forward while they are inside its
  window and never validates an id against the tree, so a retired task simply stops receiving rows
  and ages out.

The next converge vendors the new task and drops the two old ones.

## Verification

- `node --test $(git ls-files '*.test.mjs')` — **1544 pass, 0 fail**.
- `check_the_world.mjs` — **0 blocking, 34 advisory**, against 35 on the base. The
  `task-phase-discipline` advisory that `fleet-census/task.md` carried is cleared rather than
  inherited; the remaining `rules-line-length` one on `packs/sheepdog/RULES.md` predates this branch
  (my own added lines are wrapped at 100).
- `check_the_work.mjs` — exit 0. `engine/selftest.mjs` — 5 probes passed.
- **See-it-fail**: the new walk tests were checked against a deliberately broken implementation —
  reading the declaration twice, and letting a probe failure poison the coverage verdict — and went
  red on exactly the assertions carrying those claims (5 of 12), green again on restore.
- **Against the live enforcer** (`missingbulb/sheepdog`, shallow clone): its own local pack
  `local/sheepdog-local` carries **no** reference to either retired task — the one risk a canon-side
  grep structurally cannot see — and the only references outside the vendored mount are the
  historical usage rows described above.

**Not verified:** whether any `fleet-drift` issue is currently open in the enforcer. A public clone
serves git reads only, not the issues API, and the frozen-marker decision is safe either way, so I
did not attach the repo with credentials to find out. Nor is the sweep exercised end to end — this
session holds no `FLEET_GITHUB_TOKEN`. Doing that means a forced `fleet-roster` run on the Sheepdog
repo after this lands.

## Out of scope

- **#786** — that freshness judges by stamped `ref` age, which the update flows never refresh.
  `classifyFreshness` moves file unchanged and the bug moves with it.
- The `per-project-scheduling`, `task-prework` and `skill-usage-metrics` DESIGN docs keep their
  references to the two retired tasks: they record what those initiatives built at the time, and
  rewriting them would falsify that record. Live pointers (`README.md`, `packs/README.md`, the pack's
  own `README.md`/`RULES.md`/`pack.mjs`/`fleet-api.mjs`/`fleet-config.mjs`, `docs/future-directions.md`,
  the canon local pack's lesson) are all repointed.
- The other merges weighed alongside this one — `fleet-baseline` + `fleet-add-missing-packs` as one
  dispatcher, `fleet-pack-seeds` folded into `fleet-add-missing-packs` — are separate calls, neither
  taken here.
