{"number":301,"title":"Add product-wiki pack: the self-growing product research wiki standard","body":"Refs #302.

## Summary

A new project-aspect standards pack, `packs/product-wiki/`, encoding the self-growing product research wiki that GoogleCalendarEventCreator just adopted (missingbulb/GoogleCalendarEventCreator#678) — the Karpathy "LLM wiki" pattern: compile findings once, refine in place, cite everything, keep a dated growth log.

**The standard is structural, not configured.** Under `product/`, two reserved names have fixed meaning — `product-requirements/` (the human-reviewed distillation, the only `product/` content the rest of the repo may reference, never auto-grown) and `sample-data/` (illustrative assets). Everything else under `product/` *is* wiki space — any names, any nesting. No wikis manifest exists anywhere, so a renamed or added wiki folder stays classified, checked, and barred with nothing to drift. Fingerprint: `product/product-requirements/README.md` (the sink is the standard's one structural constant). The pack takes no config; a config object on its entry is itself a blocking finding. Path constants, the bullet/date grammar, and the section-heading contract are spelled once in `lib.mjs` and shared by every check, the manifest, and the barrier.

### Checks (6)

| Rule | Enforces | Severity |
|---|---|---|
| `product-wiki-layout` | the `product/` skeleton (index + sink) exists — tracked or freshly written | blocking |
| `product-wiki-page-sections` | every wiki page carries `## Sources` / `## Growth log` / `## Open questions` (code fences don't count) | blocking |
| `product-wiki-growth-log` | log bullets (`-`/`*`/`+`) lead with a real `YYYY-MM-DD` date; seeded pages have ≥1 entry | blocking |
| `product-wiki-sources` | every Sources bullet carries its real URL (markdown link or bare; judged over the wrapped bullet block) | blocking |
| `product-wiki-freshness` | a page whose newest **entry-leading** log date is >45 days old gets a nag | **advisory** (time-driven findings must never block; injectable `ctx.now` for tests) |
| `product-wiki-isolation` | nothing outside `product/` may reference wiki space; `product-requirements` is the one crossing point | blocking (fixed barrier via `defineBarrier`) |

The fixed barrier uses `from: "."` / `to: "product/*"` — fail-closed on an empty expansion, auto-bars new `product/` children, strictly stronger than the consumer's current hand-declared enumerated-`from` rule (which its adoption PR will prune) — with `matchUniqueFilenames` off so agent-written wiki filenames never become repo-wide barred bare names. One small **additive** barriers-engine extension rides along: `defineBarrier` accepts a `crossingExcuse` override (default text unchanged), because a pack-shipped barrier's findings must point at the excusal lever that actually works for it (a reasoned `accept`) rather than the engine's per-rule `except` instruction, which a consumer cannot apply to pack code.

### Prose (RULES.md, ~30 lines)

Only what checks can't carry, per the promotion ladder: the sink is human-reviewed only; compile-once/refine-in-place; cite-or-don't-write and correct-with-note; no fabricated growth (most passes change nothing); sample-data ≠ test fixtures; unattended growth always lands as an unmerged PR; the owner phrase "grow the product wiki".

### Routine (run_daily)

A weekly fleet task (`run_daily/wiki-growth.mjs`, gated on the full-sweep day — research arrives on the world's clock, not the repo's) whose worker doc owns the growth method: read the wikis end to end, research only what their own `## Open questions` flag, write back cited, one dated log entry per touched page, deliver as a `claude/product-wiki-growth/<date>` PR that never self-merges, track grew/blocked on a standing issue, stay silent on clean no-ops. The freshness advisory is the in-repo backstop that surfaces a silently-dead growth channel.

## Verification

- **Unit:** 31 tests in `pack.test.mjs` (fixture repos, violation-first; every check has pass and violation cases, incl. the fence/`+`-bullet/wrapped-bullet/untracked-scaffold regressions, a pinned 45-day boundary via injected clock, accept plumbing through the real CLI runner, and the run_daily gate contract).
- **Corpus:** full suite green — 315 tests; conformance sweep on the canon itself clean (incl. the barriers pack's own tests over the engine change).
- **End-to-end (real consumer):** a 12/12 mutation matrix against a scratch clone of GoogleCalendarEventCreator — pre-adoption fires exactly the two expected finding groups; post-adoption is fully clean; `git mv MarketWiki Market` stays clean; deleting `product/` fails closed; prose crossings caught; sink crossing open; aged logs advisory-only.
- **Adversarial review:** 8 parallel finder angles + verification; the 7 confirmed findings (freshness date-scan loophole, misleading barrier fix-text, unique-basename layer, `+`-bullet bypass, fenced-heading spoofing, wrapped-source false positive, untracked-scaffold wedge) are fixed in the second commit. One PLAUSIBLE finding deliberately not fixed and documented in-code instead: the no-config guard rides the layout rule id (a runner-level `acceptsConfig` manifest seam is the eventual home once a second pack needs it), and accepts against the fixed barrier aren't staleness-audited (stated in the pack README).

## Adoption (follow-up, ordering is load-bearing)

An unknown pack name is a blocking config error in consumers, so GoogleCalendarEventCreator declares `product-wiki` only **after** this merges and its mount re-syncs. Its adoption PR then: adds the declaration, deletes its hand-written barriers entry (subsumed), deletes its local `dev/routines/product-wiki-growth/` (the canon worker is its new home) and repoints inbound references, and adds the missing `## Open questions` to UsersWiki.

{"number":396,"title":"scheduler: due-slot math + schedule config key (Phase 0 groundwork)","body":"Starts the vendored Actions scheduler for per-project maintenance scheduling (#394, DESIGN §2–3, MIGRATION Phase 0). This is the first, pure, well-tested slice of `engine/scheduler/`; **no behavior change** — nothing schedules or dispatches yet.

## What's here

- **`engine/scheduler/slots.mjs`** — the stateless due-slot math the scheduler runs each hour over the Actions run ledger (no watermark file). The whole model: consider only the *single most-recent* scheduled slot per frequency, and it's due iff its time falls in `(lastSuccess, now]`.
  - Misses self-heal to exactly one catch-up per frequency — never a backfill storm.
  - Hourly never backfills (its most-recent slot is always the current hour).
  - First run (no prior success) evaluates every frequency — the fresh-adoption smoke test.
  - Resolves the daily anchor ± offsets (anchor-dated slot ids, including the `daily-2h` hour-wrap when `dailyHour < 2`), the weekly weekday, and the monthly day-of-month with month-length clamping.
  - Pure: `now` and `lastSuccess` are always injected, so due-ness is deterministic and fully testable.

- **`schedule` config key** — added to `CONFIG_KEYS` with load-time range validation (`dailyHour` 0–23, `weeklyDay` Sun–Sat, `monthlyDay` 1–31). Absence is legal (defaults live in `slots.mjs`); its declaration is the per-repo cutover marker for the rollout.

## Tests

- `engine-tests/scheduler/slots.test.mjs` — slot math across the seven frequencies: miss→catch-up, double-run dedupe, first-run, hour-wrap, month-clamp, weekly rollback, hourly no-backfill, the full daily growth chain.
- `engine-tests/context.test.mjs` — `schedule` validation: valid / partial / absent, plus out-of-range and misshaped values.

Full suite green (508 tests) and the conformance sweep is clean for this change (0 blocking).

## Not in this PR (follow-on Phase 0 work)

`run.mjs`, `discover.mjs`, the signal collectors, `dispatch.mjs`, `validate-dispatch.mjs`, `verify-outcome.mjs`, `model-map.mjs`, `executor.md`, the workflow stub, the task-folder conversions, new checks, and the doc rewrites — each lands separately on top of this foundation.

{"number":479,"title":"Wire the three signal-collector ctx keys that nothing ever set","body":"`engine/scheduler/signals/index.mjs` reads three keys off `ctx` that `run.mjs`'s construction never populated. Each fell through its `?? null` fallback on every real run, so the precondition arm it feeds was unreachable code.

## What was dead

| key | feeds | consequence |
|---|---|---|
| `ctx.manifestVersion` | `release.manifestVersion` | `store-release`'s manifest-ahead trigger never fired — the task could only fire on `commits.substantiveChange`, so a manifest bump that landed as a bot/housekeeping commit, or one whose release failed days ago, was never retried |
| `ctx.hasLocalPacks` | `localPacks.present` | `growth-dedup`'s "no local packs → skip" arm never fired — `present` stayed `null`, never the explicit `false` the self-skip tests for, so a repo with zero local packs dispatched an **opus** agent on a 1800s budget to prune nothing |
| `ctx.retentionDays` | `conversationLogs.retentionDays` | `conversation-extract`'s age-based retention prune never fired. **A regression**: the old form ran this weekly via `fullSweep`, retired on the stated grounds that this signal replaced it — so quiet repos' logs have been aging past retention with nothing to collect them |

## Where the values come from

All three are read **from disk at `root`**, not over the API. The scheduler runs Action-side inside the repo checkout and `run.mjs` already holds `root` (it passes it to preprocessing as `CLAUDINITE_REPO_ROOT`), so a disk read is equivalent to the retired gate's API read for a scheduled run and strictly cheaper — no round-trip, no rate budget, no base64 decode — and the tree read is the tree the run would ship.

- **manifest** — `manifest.json`, `src/`, `public/`, `dist/`, first with a `version`; the retired `run_daily` gate's paths and its leading-`v` tolerance, recovered from `08c88ce~1`.
- **local packs** — a directory under either local root, canonical `.claudinite/local/packs/` or pre-rename `.claudinite/local_packs/`, matching the collector's own `touches()`. Those roots now have **one** definition shared by the presence probe, the collector's path test, and the fleet reader.
- **retention** — through `run.mjs`'s existing `packConfigFor`, keyed by the `retention_days` **parameter** rather than a pack name, so core names no pack (the `barriers` rule).

The new `signals/local.mjs` is the one place that touches the filesystem. The collectors keep their `ctx.X ?? null` injection seam untouched and still unit-test against a fake `gh` with no repo on disk.

## Behaviour that changes

No precondition's logic, thresholds, or `context` changed. Two preconditions now reach arms they previously could not:

- **`growth-dedup` now skips** where it previously dispatched, on any repo with no local packs — an opus agent per day per such repo, reclaimed.
- **`conversation-extract` now runs daily** on a quiet repo that has a `conversation-logs` branch and configured retention. This is the retired weekly sweep coming back, as designed — but it is a new daily opus dispatch on repos that were silent before.
- **`store-release`** gains its manifest-ahead trigger on extension repos. No effect on this repo (no manifest).

## Tests

Each key had a unit test that hand-built a shape the collector could not emit, so the suite was green while the plumbing was dead. Red-first, `engine-tests/scheduler/signal-context.test.mjs` failed on the pre-wire construction with `null !== '1.4.0'`, `null !== false`, `null !== 10` — the fallbacks firing.

The unit seams stay (the preconditions are pure functions worth testing directly) but now record what they do not prove. Reachability is asserted through the **real** construction: a checkout on disk → `loadConfig` → `buildSignalContext` → `collectSignals` → the actual precondition. The file also carries the **class guard** — every `ctx.<key>` the collectors read must be a key the real construction produces, with the two legitimate exemptions (`commits`, `canonHead`) named and justified — verified to fail when a key is unwired. The next unwired ctx read fails a test instead of becoming a permanent null.

698 → 707 tests, all passing. `check_the_world` unchanged at 0 blocking / 7 advisory (one pre-existing finding shifts line number); `check_the_work` clean. Vendor set 125 → 126 files, import-closed, 0 errors.

## Also

Five task docs said the declaration field is `model:`; it is `agent_model:`. Corrected in `growth-extract`, `growth-dedup`, `conversation-extract`, `wiki-growth`, `repo-tidy` — field name only, nothing else touched.

Refs #394

{"number":494,"title":"Baselining audit: six independent fixes to the run_daily → tasks ports","body":"Six independent findings from a code-level audit of the `run_daily` → `tasks` ports, one commit each so they revert independently. Two are real behaviour bugs in the nightly (items 4 and 5); the rest correct claims that are false today and would license a wrong deletion later.

Baseline and final both: `check_the_world` 0 blocking / 7 advisory (identical finding set), `check_the_work` clean, full suite green — 715 → 722 tests across 64 files.

---

### Item 3 — `baselining/task.md` claimed a deterministic home that does not exist

**Confirmed, and worse than "just normalization".** `task.md` §3 told the agent that interview status *and* declaration normalization "are already handled deterministically by preprocessing (converge-wiring)". `convergeWiring` does exactly three things — the scheduler workflow (hashed cron + declared secrets), the settings hooks, and removal of the retired `CLAUDE.md` corpus import. It never reads or writes `packs`. Neither claim was true of it.

The other candidate is dead too: `migrations/active_migrations/2026-07-19-local-pack-namespace.mjs` says in its own header it "holds no ops of its own", and `declTokenFor` has **zero** callers outside `engine-tests/pack_loader/pack-registry.test.mjs`. The only implementation was the worker prose retired in #412's E4 rewrite, which dropped the step and left the claim behind.

**Changed:** name `convergeWiring`'s real set; move interview status to where it actually lives (the mild SessionStart note + adopt-claudinite's stale-answer hygiene check, both of which reach the agent as findings); state plainly that normalization is unimplemented, including the consequence — the `local-pack-namespace` record's `legacyPresent` can never reach zero and its `retire: 'auto'` never fires. Normalization is **not** implemented here; that stays an open decision.

**Also found (not fixed here):** the migration record is itself stale. It probes `.claudinite/local_packs/<id>/pack.mjs` and tests for a `local_packs/` prefix, but `LOCAL_DECL_PREFIX` is now `local/` and `LOCAL_PACKS_SUBDIR` is `.claudinite/local/packs`. So it only detects the legacy layout — a repo on the current layout reads clean regardless.

### Item 4 — a missing `maintenance.delivery` was a hard nightly failure

**Confirmed, and it is a code regression against two docs that already describe the right behaviour:**

- `engine/checks/README.md` — "`--init` seeds `auto-merge` and **the nightly sweep backfills a missing key**".
- `packs/basics/skills/engineering-practices/SKILL.md` — "have the automation materialize the explicit value into every file it maintains instead of interpreting absence … a missing key becomes drift the automation repairs".

The backfill was lost with the worker prose. `normalizeDelivery(undefined) → null → process.exit(1)`, and the only writer left is `check_the_world --init` at first adoption, so an affected repo failed baselining every night with nothing that could ever fix it.

**Changed:** `resolveDelivery(raw) → { delivery, materialize }`, splitting the two cases the old code conflated. Absent (or content-free — no intent to honour) materializes the default into `.claudinite-checks.json` *before* the converge, so the repair rides the same maintenance commit and the repo self-heals in one cycle. Unrecognized stays a hard failure. Legacy `push`/`auto`/`pr` aliases unchanged.

Also excluded a materialized key from the `onlyStamp` revert — that branch discards a change set consisting solely of `.claudinite-checks.json` and would have thrown the backfill away every night, so the fix would never have landed.

### Item 5 — auto-merge was armed only on the cycle that opens the PR

**Confirmed.** `enableAutoMerge` sat inside `if (!reuse)` alongside PR creation, and the arm is deliberately best-effort (`.catch(() => {})`) — which makes one attempt the wrong number. Three ordinary ways a PR ends up unarmed forever: the mutation failed on the opening cycle; the repo had not enabled auto-merge yet; or `maintenance.delivery` flipped `review → auto-merge` while the PR was open. Every later run takes the reuse path and never revisits it.

**Changed:** the arm moved below the `if (!reuse)` block, so it is attempted every cycle whenever delivery is `auto-merge`. Still best-effort; arming an already-armed PR is a no-op. The reuse path needs the PR's `node_id`, which `openMaintenanceBranch` discarded, so the find is now `openMaintenancePull` returning the whole PR, with `openMaintenanceBranch` a thin wrapper over it (behaviour and existing tests unchanged).

**Not done:** disarming on the reverse flip (`auto-merge → review`) on an open PR. That is the mirror gap but needs a disable mutation and a decision about clobbering a hand-armed PR — its own item.

### Item 6 — dedup's Context: "binding" vs "focus"

**Confirmed.** `dispatch.mjs` renders "binding scope — do not re-decide it" and `executor.md` "never re-decide or widen it", while `growth-dedup/task.md` said only to "focus" the re-check.

**Reading chosen: binding — and what it binds is the *yardstick*, not the local surface.** The doc cannot opt out of what the machinery enforces, so binding wins. As for what is bound, that is what the precondition's own line already says read literally: "Re-check local items against these newly-changed canon packs" — all local items, measured against those packs. It is also the only reading that works mechanically: local pack names are unrelated to canon pack names, so "only items belonging to the changed packs" has nothing to match up, while sweeping the whole mounted canon is exactly the widening the executor forbids.

It loses nothing because the two precondition arms partition the work: the canon arm fires when declared packs moved (only a moved pack can newly cover an item, so the narrow yardstick is complete for that trigger), and the local-packs-changed arm emits **no** context at all, precisely so fresh local items get swept against the whole mounted canon.

**Changed:** the bound stated in the conventions (what it narrows, what it does not, and that an absent Context block means no bound), "focus" replaced with binding language, and a matching never-bullet.

**Residual noted, not fixed:** the canon arm returns early, so on a cycle where the canon moved *and* local packs changed, fresh local items get only the narrow yardstick and wait for a canon-quiet cycle. That is the precondition's business, not the worker doc's.

### Item 7 — `wiki-growth`'s precondition test

**Premise corrected: a precondition test already exists** — bottom of `packs-tests/product-wiki/pack.test.mjs`, added by #473 when `run_daily` retired and the old `gate` test was replaced. It covers the firing path, the wiki-moved context, and the no-context path.

What it did *not* cover was the two properties most likely to be broken by a well-meaning edit, so those were added:

1. **There is no non-firing arm, deliberately.** A wiki grows on research availability, not repo activity, so the weekly slot *is* the gate. Nothing said so in a test, meaning a "quiet window → skip" arm — reintroducing exactly the repo-activity gate this task exists to avoid — would have gone green. Now asserted across six signal shapes including both defensive ones (`commits` absent; `commits` present with no `touchedPaths`) and a malformed `commits: null`.
2. **The wiki-moved test is a root-anchored prefix yielding exactly one context line.** `docs/product-wiki/` is a different tree, and the dispatch renders each context entry as its own bullet.

**Red-first evidence.** The behaviour is already correct, so this is the mutation method the `writing-tests` skill prescribes as the second form of see-it-fail. Three mutations, each restored:

| Mutation | Result |
| --- | --- |
| A — add `if (touched.length === 0) return { run: false, … }` | `not ok 32`, `not ok 33` — `declined for {}`; 32 pass / **2 fail** |
| B — `startsWith('product-wiki/')` → `includes('product-wiki')` | `not ok 34` (root-anchored); 33 pass / **1 fail** |
| C — one context line per moved path instead of one total | `not ok 34` (one-line shape); 33 pass / **1 fail** |

Source restored: 34 pass, 0 fail. `git diff` on `task.mjs` confirmed clean before committing.

**Sibling item checked:** `tidy-branches`, `tidy-issues` and `tidy-prs` (#480) **all already have precondition tests** in `packs-tests/tidy-repo/pack.test.mjs` — nothing owed there.

### Item 9 — `wiki-growth`'s false subsumption claim

**Confirmed.** `planDispatch` filters `existing` by the dispatch-title prefix and guards at most one open dispatch **issue** per (pack, task); it never looks at pull requests. This task's ceiling is `open-pr`, so a completed run converges and closes its own dispatch issue and leaves the growth PR open. The next weekly slot finds an empty issue family and dispatches freely — finding an open growth PR is the *ordinary* case, not the anomaly `task.md` called it.

No behaviour is wrong today; the danger is that the reasoning hands a future reader an authoritative-sounding licence to delete the one guard that actually covers this, with nothing failing.

**Changed:** `task.mjs` now states what `planDispatch` actually guards and why the preflight is load-bearing; `task.md`'s Preflight leads with the instruction instead of a false reassurance that softened it. The same claim in the precondition's inline comment corrected too.

{"number":542,"title":"product-wiki: every wiki page opens with a Key insights header","body":"A compiled research page is only useful if a human can get its findings without reading it end to end. Every `product-wiki/` page now **opens with `## Key insights`** — a few terse, plain-words lines carrying what the research found, ahead of every other section. The body stays the research record; the header is where a reader decides whether they need it.

Closes #543.

## The contract, and who enforces which half

Split along the pack's existing ownership line, so nothing is double-reported:

- **`product-wiki-page-sections`** gains `Key insights` as a fourth required section — a missing header is reported exactly once, in the same place every other missing section is.
- **`product-wiki-key-insights`** (new, blocking) owns the header's *shape*: it leads every other section, it is bullets only, it carries at least one and at most seven, and no bullet runs past **140 characters** — about one line. A bullet's indented continuation lines count as part of it, so hard-wrapping is free and a wrapped paragraph can't hide.

The tight cap is the point: a header earns its place only if it is faster to read than the page, and the failure mode in practice is a bullet that keeps qualifying itself. The qualifiers belong in the body.

*Which* insights lead, and how plainly they're worded, is judgment — so it lives in prose, not in a check:

- **RULES.md**: conclusions, never a table of contents. One short line per bullet in ordinary words — no qualifying clause, no citation, no hedge, no jargon a newcomer would decode. Prefer what would *surprise* someone who knows the field. Judging obviousness is genuinely hard, so the error preference is stated outright: **when in doubt, keep the line** — a borderline-obvious line costs the reader two seconds, a long careful one costs them the header.
- **The header is a current view, not a log** — a pass that changes a page's top-line understanding rewrites it; a pass that doesn't leaves it alone. The wiki-growth worker gains that reconcile step, plus a must-never-do: leaving a header asserting what the body it heads no longer says.

## Tested against real wikis, not just fixtures

EdFringeNow's three research wikis were the testing ground; the headers land there as [EdFringeNow#146](https://github.com/missingbulb/EdFringeNow/pull/146).

- Before: `page-sections` fires once per page naming the missing header; `key-insights` stays silent (correctly — the missing heading isn't its finding).
- After: all four page checks clean.
- Calibration: a first pass written to the old 300-char cap came out at 140–230 characters per bullet — readable, but paragraphs. Rewritten terse, the same seven findings per page fit in **66–93 characters**, so the 140 cap has real headroom for an honest line while cutting a paragraph off at the knees.

Six new unit tests; four of the six fail if the check's `run` is neutered (the other two are clean-pass tests, correctly insensitive). Full suite 897/897, conformance sweep 0 blocking.

## Fleet propagation

No migration record. Existing members converge through the nightly baselining: a missing header is precisely the "blocking finding that needs judgment" its worker resolves on the maintenance PR. A record also couldn't carry honest telemetry here — wiki pages are discovered *structurally*, which `legacyPresent`'s path-reader cannot enumerate, so it would never auto-retire.

{"number":657,"title":"scheduler: hand the agent its artifacts by identity, not by name","body":"**Owner decision (2026-08-06):** an agent must never locate its working artifacts by a branch or PR *name*. A search that finds nothing is indistinguishable from nothing having been created — and the agent believes it.

That is exactly what happened on Sheepdog: preprocessing opened a maintenance PR **and merged it in the same run** (no `pull_request` CI to gate on), the task doc said to find the *open* one, the agent found none, and correctly-by-its-instructions concluded the cycle had delivered nothing — while a withheld workflow file sat undelivered. [missingbulb/Sheepdog#73](https://github.com/missingbulb/Sheepdog/issues/73) is the agent's own reasoning.

## The mechanism

A worker that opens a branch or PR writes their identifiers into the agent-request file → the scheduler renders them into the dispatch issue → the agent reads them there and nowhere else:

```
### Delivered by preprocessing
These are the artifacts this run created. They are the ONLY ones to work on — do not
search for a branch or PR by name, and if this section is absent, nothing was created.

- PR: #71 (already merged — do not reopen it; open your own PR for further work)
- Branch: `claudinite/maintenance-2026-08-06-l0i4gd`
```

**Absence is authoritative, with no placeholder** — no section means nothing was created, and there is no fallback search, because the fallback is the bug.

## The DESIGN amendment

This amends agent-preprocessing DESIGN §3's "no code→agent data channel" — the rule that *forced* the name-guessing. Recorded as your decision in the doc, and deliberately narrow: the channel carries **identifiers for what this run created**, never findings, never instructions. First line is still the task path, Context is still the binding scope, the agent still reads its behaviour from the task file alone — the executor's label-as-authorization / path-validation model is untouched.

## Swept the corpus, not just the case that bit

| where | change |
|---|---|
| `basics/baselining` | reads the Delivered section; §1 no longer treats a merged PR as an empty cycle; §2b says where the commit goes either way |
| `product-wiki/wiki-growth` | no preprocessing, so a previous run's PR is found by a **`product-wiki-growth` label** it deliberately applies — never a branch pattern. The branch name is now explicitly meaningless. |
| `executor.md` | carries the rule for **every** task, including what a subagent must do with what *it* creates (comment the number on the dispatch issue), and says a task doc telling you to search by name is out of date |

GCEC's `create-extractor` has the same pattern (`claude/extractor/` prefix) and is fixed in its own repo — **that PR must not merge until this one has reached GCEC's mount**, since its task doc will look for a section this engine is what produces.

## One accepted edge, stated not hidden

On the single cycle where an old vendored worker runs beside a freshly converged `task.md`, the issue carries no Delivered section and the agent no-ops. It self-corrects the next cycle (the converge is idempotent and re-delivers), so the cost is one cycle of latency, never a wedge.

## Verification

- `node --test` over the CI test roots: **1167 pass, 0 fail**
- Payload round-trip checked directly, including backward compatibility: a legacy bare-marker worker still requests the agent and simply names no artifacts (`{}` → no section)
- `node engine/checks/check_the_world.mjs`: **0 blocking**, 9 advisory (pre-existing)

Refs #649

{"number":1855,"title":"Answer fleet freshness on the run report, not in an issue per member","body":"Closes #1854

The dashboard's Drift tile measures each member's declaration against canon and recomputes on load. `fleet-roster` measured the same fact from the same source and *additionally* filed a `fleet-drift` issue per unhealthy member — a second surface for one question, and the staler of the two, since it is only ever as current as the last daily sweep.

In `missingbulb/Shepherd` right now that reads as three open drift issues naming members that caught up hours after the sweep read them, beside `GoogleCalendarEventCreator` sitting two days behind with **no** issue at all, because it was still current when that sweep ran. All four states are correct on the dashboard.

So the issue family goes and the measurement stays.

## What changed, by folder

```
packs/claudinite-fleet-sheepdog/tasks/fleet-roster/
  drift-issues.mjs → freshness.mjs
    Deleted convergeDrift and its driftTitle / driftBody / marker / FIXES / LABEL
    supports — the whole issue family. Kept classifyFreshness, probeMount,
    canonVersions and renderFreshnessSummary, which are the measurement and the
    report. renderFreshnessSummary loses its `actions` argument and its
    "(drift issue open)" wording; it still names every behind member.
    The rename is the point rather than churn: two thirds of this module was never
    the issue family, and leaving it named for a mechanism it no longer has is
    exactly the trap that broke pack-badge-row against a converge-wiring export
    removed under it.

  check-fleet-roster.mjs
    Dropped the ensureLabel + convergeDrift call site. freshnessView's `gone`
    bucket went with it — convergeDrift was its only consumer.

  adoption-issues.mjs
    Cross-reference to its counterpart, which is now freshness.mjs. Coverage
    itself is untouched: it still files issues, because no other surface
    answers coverage.

packs/claudinite-fleet-sheepdog/tasks/fleet-baseline/
  force-fleet-baseline.mjs, follow-to-current.mjs
    Import path only. Both already depended on the measurement half, which is
    why the module had to survive rather than be deleted whole.

packs/claudinite-fleet-sheepdog/ (pack root)
  pack.mjs, README.md
    The sweep table and the two header comments that described the roster as
    two issue families. Version 60906.2 → 60907.1.
```

## What proves it

Written first and watched fail against `main`:

- `freshness summary: a behind member is named on the report, with no issue to chase` — the report keeps the behind list and carries no issue wording. This is the regression that would otherwise hide inside the removal: drop the issues and lose the sweep's ability to say what it found.
- `the freshness module offers no way to file an issue` — asserted over the module's export names, so a re-introduced converger fails it whatever it is called.

Two existing `check-fleet-roster` tests asserted on the `gone` bucket and now assert on `outOfScope`, which carries the same repos with their reasons.

`node --test` over the pack: 173 pass, 0 fail. `check_the_world`: 0 blocking, and neither of the two advisories touching this pack is on a file this PR changes.

## Follow-on, outside this repo

Once this lands, the four open `fleet-drift` issues in `missingbulb/Shepherd` get closed and its local rule about triaging them retired. Not in this PR — it is a different repo.

{"number":2182,"title":"A task cadence measures whole UTC periods, not a per-repo anchor","body":"Closes #1995

`taskScheduler.dailyHour`, `weeklyDay` and `monthlyDay` let a repo move the boundaries its cadences were measured against. #1995 measured this repo's own cron across a week: the morning fire time moved **68 minutes** and the evening one **78**, both wider than the 60-minute stagger the ordering rested on. The knob was provably not doing the one job it was kept for.

What it did reliably was put a seam inside every day. Before the anchor hour the current period was still yesterday's, so one run read as consumed at 03:00 and as open at 09:00, and *"has it run today"* was never the question the term answered.

## What changes

A period is now the UTC calendar and nothing else: a day opens at midnight, a week on the Sunday that opened it, a month on its 1st. `anchorInstant` takes a cadence and an instant; `evaluatePreconditions` takes no schedule at all. Two repos asked at the same moment get the same answer.

The term that states it is **`schedule:at-most-<daily|weekly|monthly>`**, which says what it is out loud: a rate limit on the scheduler's own asking, never a claim that there is work to do.

- **`due:<cadence>`** is the same function under the name it was introduced with, accepted **permanently** for the reason `LEGACY_FREQUENCIES` is (a task declaration is member-owned data no vendoring pass rewrites), and rewritten at the door so one spelling reaches every reader downstream. No window, no removal link.
- **`last-run-over:`** is deleted. No declaration in the canon used it, and you confirmed none in the fleet does.

## The cron

The scheduler workflow's two hours came off the same setting. They are now derived from the repo name beside the minute, written once when the file is scaffolded, and **preserved by every converge after**. `.github/workflows/` lands only through a pull request a person merges, so restamping the line would put every member's scheduler behind a human gate on every change to the derivation. **No member's cron moves**, this repo's `44 5,17` included.

## Members

A migration record drops the three keys from each member's own declaration and restates its local-pack task files. It carries the apply stage `migration-apply-stage` asks for: the codemod cannot see the member's own tests, and the last record to rewrite these files landed red on a repo with five of them.

The keys stay accepted-and-unread until #2181, because an unknown key is a blocking settings error and every member carries them until its own converge runs. `legacy-shape-in-use` tells each holder meanwhile.

## Evidence

- Full suite green: **3745 tests, 0 failures**.
- `check_the_world.mjs`: **0 blocking**; every advisory pre-existing.
- `check_the_work.mjs`: **clean**.
- The simulator's 80 scenarios all pass. Several needed real restructuring rather than restatement, because they encoded the 04:00 seam this change removes; `S75` is deleted with `last-run-over:`.

Two bugs found on the way and fixed here: `nextAnchor` looped forever on an unreadable instant, and the contract's door and the codemod spelled an illegal `frequency` differently.

## Folders touched

```
packs/claudinite-tasks/src/contract   the calendar, the period arithmetic, the
                                      schedule: term and the due: alias, the door
packs/claudinite-tasks/src/items      anchors lose the schedule argument
packs/claudinite-tasks/src/adopt      hashedCron derives the hour; the converge
                                      preserves an existing cron line
packs/claudinite-tasks/src/signals    a comment naming the retired reason string
packs/claudinite-tasks/tasks          the usage-fold term; 25 task.json files
                                      restated to the current spelling
packs/claudinite-tasks/migrations     the new record, with its apply stage
packs/claudinite-tasks/docs           PRINCIPLES.md, the executable spec
packs/claudinite-dashboard/src/derive the page's mirrored copy, its cadence door,
                                      the board axis and the roster
packs/claudinite-lifecycle            the cron-shape check text; the advisory
                                      branch that reports a retired key
packs/claudinite-growth/skills        writing-tasks, the vocabulary it teaches
engine/checks/helpers                 the three keys accepted and unvalidated
engine/migrations                     the settings-drop op and the cadence codemod
(root)                                bootstrap stops seeding an anchor
```

Wider than its request implied, and the reason is the finding: `dailyHour` was read by the cadence arithmetic, the cron derivation, the config validator, the dashboard's own copy and every task declaration. That spread is what made it worth removing.

{"number":1976,"title":"Fleet shepherd: every visible repo on the dashboard, each row with one thing to do; ignored and dormant out of the sweeps","body":"Closes #1975

Two halves, and they pull in deliberately opposite directions.

## The sweeps act on less

**Ignored is ignored in every aspect.** A repo on `config.exclude` is skipped before its declaration is read, in the roster walk and in the fit sweep — which never consulted the list at all, so a repo the fleet was told to leave alone could be fingerprinted and handed a work-list issue. Each report names it once under `ignored`, with no verdict. A force naming one is refused rather than written around.

**A dormant member is out of the mount and scheduler questions, and out of fleet-wide operations.** It stays a covered member; the roster sweep no longer measures its freshness or pays for its mount probe. This reverses the standing decision the sheepdog README carried ("It is **not** out of the roster's freshness half"), purged here along with the same claim in `dormancy.mjs`, `fleet-api.mjs` and the `writing-tasks` skill — whose rationale now lives in the growth pack's `references.md` behind `(writing-tasks-3)`. `INCLUDE_DORMANT=true` on a hand-created `fleet-baseline` item stays as the one explicit override.

## The dashboard shows more

**Every repo the viewer can see is on the page**; only a fork is not. Out of the fleet is a *state*, not a filter:

| Row | What it shows | Next |
|---|---|---|
| archived | greyed; core GitHub facts only | **Unarchive →** to GitHub's settings — Claudinite cannot undo an archive |
| ignored | greyed; core GitHub facts only | **Bring back — copy request**, the whole request to paste into a session |
| dormant | Claudinite columns, minus the task-based delays: no minutes estimate, no attention breakdown, queue as a count not a state mix | **Wake — copy request** |
| sleepy | exactly like an active member | its worst item, else its PRs/issues |
| active | as before | **Advance #n →**, else PRs, else issues |
| active, nothing open | as before | 🙂 |

The grid is three bands — the fleet proper worst-first, then **Dormant** and **Out of the fleet**, collapsed by default, opened by any filter. `private` is a tag beside the name; `sleepy` (no meaningful commit in 14 days, dashed) is distinct from `dormant` (declared, solid) and stays in every fleet-wide operation.

**Sleepy's evidence** is the `claudinite-tasks` pack's own `isSubstantiveCommit`, extracted onto `shared-code/`, over one commit-listing call per member. The same classification gives each row's commit graph a **second line** — genuine project work under the total, breaking where the listing did not reach. The full test also drops a commit touching nothing outside `.claudinite/`, which needs a request per commit; that exclusion is skipped and the gap is stated on the mark's hover and in `docs/data-sources.md`. A withheld listing reads `unknown`, never `sleepy`.

### Proof

- `packs/claudinite-dashboard/test/view-fleet.test.mjs` — the Next cell per member state, including the smile carrying its own aria-label.
- `packs/claudinite-dashboard/test/fleet.test.mjs`, `test/activity.test.mjs`, `test/config.test.mjs` — out-of-fleet summaries, the awake-only rollup, the second series' null-where-unclassified rule, and the roster keeping its ignored members.
- `packs/claudinite-fleet-sheepdog/test/tasks/**` — an ignored repo carries no verdict and is never read; a dormant member is not measured however far behind it is, with the awake contrast case beside it.
- `packs/claudinite-tasks/test/substantive-commit.test.mjs` — the published test, including the no-file-list contract.

Refusal-shaped assertions were seen red by mutating the guard they cover (dormancy suppression, the roster's two skips, the classifier, the Next cell's dormant and empty branches) and restoring.

Whole suite: 3464 pass, 1 fail — `engine-pack-lane-shims`, which fails loudly on a shallow clone by design and is unrelated. `check_the_work` and `check_the_world` clean (0 blocking).

**One assumption to confirm:** forks are still off the page. "All accessible repos" would include them, but a fork's work is upstream's, so they stay out — say the word and they become another greyed band.

{"number":732,"title":"product-wiki: raise wiki-growth's ceiling to merged-pr, and stop restating it","body":"Requested directly: put the `wiki-growth` task on auto-merge. Closes #733.

## The problem

`wiki-growth` declared `expected_outcome: 'open-pr'` and its worker doc said "never merges one" outright, so a growth PR waited for a human on **every** member — regardless of what that member had asked for. That is the task's ceiling deciding delivery, which is the member's call: `deliver-pr.md` reads `.claudinite-checks.json` → `maintenance.delivery`, and the same task is meant to land itself on one repo and wait on another with both being correct.

It shows in the standing backlog — 8 open `wiki-growth` PRs across four members, the oldest from 2026-08-02, several pairs now overlapping because a later round researched the same pages the earlier round's unmerged PR had already corrected.

## The second problem, which the one-word flip exposed

The ceiling was written down **five times**: the declaration, a comment beside it, a paragraph in task.md, the Delivery section, and a test assertion. Changing one setting meant editing five places that could disagree — which is what made the first draft of this PR a sprawling prose rewrite instead of a config change.

So the value now lives **only in the declaration**. task.md points at the delivery procedure rather than restating what that procedure decides, and the `agent_model` note gives the actual reason for the model instead of deriving it from the ceiling. Flipping this setting again is a one-line diff.

## The test

Dropped the assertions that mirrored the declaration (`expected_outcome`, `frequency`, `agent_model`, `id`). They can only fail when someone changes the value **on purpose**, so they caught no defect, taxed every deliberate change with a mirrored edit, and taught that the value is prose to be restated. Replaced with two claims that can actually drift apart:

- every signal the precondition reads is declared in `precondition_signals` (else the scheduler never collects it);
- the worker doc `agent_instructions` names exists.

Both seen red by mutation — dropping `'prs'` from the declared signals, and pointing `agent_instructions` at a missing file.

`packs/basics/skills/writing-tests/SKILL.md` gains the general rule — **"Never pin a declaration to itself"** — because the pattern is corpus-wide (64 such assertions across `packs-tests/`), not local to this task. I have not swept the other 63; that is a separate change, and a good `prose-to-checks` candidate since the shape is mechanically detectable.

## What did not change

The `product-wiki-growth` label stays load-bearing: it is how the precondition sees an unreviewed round it must not stack on, so the worker labels the PR whether or not it then lands. The precondition itself, the write-surface rules (never `product-requirements/`), and the "no citable material → no PR" stop condition are untouched.

## Verification

- `node --test $(git ls-files 'packs-tests/*.test.mjs')` — 758 pass, 0 fail.
- `node engine/checks/check_the_world.mjs` — 0 blocking, 17 advisory (all pre-existing `file-placement` / `task-phase-discipline`).","state":"closed","draft":false,"merged":true,"mergeable_state":"unknown","html_url":"https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/pull/732","user":{"login":"missingbulb","id":73882448,"profile_url":"https://github.com/missingbulb","avatar_url":"https://avatars.githubusercontent.com/u/73882448?v=4"},"merged_by":"missingbulb","head":{"ref":"claude/claudinite-task-pr-audit-hzysbc","sha":"5e05574d14f33b2b0b9cfb2f6a4e5cd024742007","repo":{"full_name":"missingbulb/Claudinite"}},"base":{"ref":"main","sha":"2d71e0af1e12eb9ad7ba45b8e87d8c2caab45630","repo":{"full_name":"missingbulb/Claudinite"}},"additions":21,"deletions":17,"changed_files":4,"commits":1,"created_at":"2026-08-09T22:17:02Z","updated_at":"2026-08-09T22:30:06Z","closed_at":"2026-08-09T22:30:04Z","merged_at":"2026-08-09T22:30:04Z"}

@@ -2,8 +2,8 @@
 
 Portable, project-agnostic gotchas for the AWS Serverless Application Model and the API-Gateway/CloudFront stack it deploys — true for any SAM project read cold.
 
-- **esbuild must be a regular `dependency`, not a `devDependency`.** SAM's esbuild builder runs a *production-only* `npm install` in its scratch dir, so a `devDependency` esbuild is skipped and the build fails with "Cannot find esbuild." Declare it in `dependencies`, or put it on the runner's `PATH` before `sam build`.
-- **CloudFront won't forward `Authorization` via a *custom* origin-request policy** — a custom `AWS::CloudFront::OriginRequestPolicy` listing `Authorization` is rejected at deploy ("The parameter Headers contains Authorization that is not allowed"). To forward it to the origin while keeping it out of the cache key (so public GETs share one cached entry), attach the **managed** `AllViewerExceptHostHeader` policy (id `b689b0a8-53d0-40ab-baf2-68738e2966ac`) plus a custom cache policy that omits `Authorization`. Use the *ExceptHostHeader* variant specifically: forwarding the viewer `Host` to an API Gateway origin returns 403.
+- **esbuild must be a regular `dependency`, not a `devDependency`.** SAM's esbuild builder runs a *production-only* `npm install` in its scratch dir, so a `devDependency` esbuild is skipped and the build fails with "Cannot find esbuild." Declare it in `dependencies`, or put it on the runner's `PATH` before `sam build`. (1)
+- **CloudFront won't forward `Authorization` via a *custom* origin-request policy** — a custom `AWS::CloudFront::OriginRequestPolicy` listing `Authorization` is rejected at deploy ("The parameter Headers contains Authorization that is not allowed"). To forward it to the origin while keeping it out of the cache key (so public GETs share one cached entry), attach the **managed** `AllViewerExceptHostHeader` policy (id `b689b0a8-53d0-40ab-baf2-68738e2966ac`) plus a custom cache policy that omits `Authorization`. Use the *ExceptHostHeader* variant specifically: forwarding the viewer `Host` to an API Gateway origin returns 403. (2)
 - **A deploy role must be able to drive the transform and CloudFront, or change-set creation fails with the real reason hidden.** The `Serverless-2016-10-31` transform runs as a macro, so the deploy principal needs `cloudformation:*`, and CloudFront management needs `cloudfront:*`, both at `Resource: "*"` (scope the *data-plane* grants to your stack instead). `sam deploy` surfaces only `Waiter ChangeSetCreateComplete failed` — the actual `AccessDenied` is visible only in the CloudFormation console's **Change sets** tab. Don't paper over it with `AdministratorAccess`.
 - **A brand-new AWS account can't create a CloudFront distribution until AWS verifies it.** The deploy fails `AccessDenied: Your account must be verified before you can add new CloudFront resources` — an account-level anti-abuse gate, not an IAM or template bug. Open a Support case to get the account verified, and launch against the origin URL directly meanwhile.
 - **A failed first `CREATE` must be cleaned up before you retry.** A stack left in `ROLLBACK_COMPLETE` (and a SAM managed-bucket stack stuck in `REVIEW_IN_PROGRESS`) can only be *deleted*, never updated. And any resource with `DeletionPolicy: Retain` survives the rollback orphaned, so the retry then fails `already exists` until you delete the orphan too.

{"number":825,"title":"Pattern-check engine: markdown-section assertions (the product-wiki page grammar)","body":"Closes #824. The Category-4 append, completing the four rounds: text patterns (#790), cross-file tree correspondence (#800), structured data (#820), and now the markdown-section grammar.

## Engine

The section machinery the five product-wiki page checks shared through `lib.mjs` is now engine mechanism, computed **once per file for the whole rule family** inside the shared pass: fenced code blanked with line count preserved, `## ` headings matched case-insensitively with suffix words allowed, a section running to the next `## ` heading, bullet **blocks** (a column-0 bullet plus its indented continuations), and dated bullets validated as **real calendar dates** (the `Date.UTC` rollover round-trip).

`checkSections` entries name a `section` (or `sections` list) and compose from, each optional and each with its own declared message:

- `requirePresent` — the heading must exist (`{section}`)
- `requireFirstOnPage` — no other `## ` heading may precede it (`{first}`)
- `forbidProseLines` — non-bullet, non-continuation lines are findings (`{line}`)
- `eachBulletBlockMatches: { pattern }` — every bullet block must match
- `eachBulletLeadsWithDate: { whenUndated, whenNotRealDate }` (`{date}`)
- `minBullets` / `maxBullets: { count }` (`{bullets}`)
- `maxBulletBlockLength: { characters }` (`{characters}`, `{bullet}`)
- `newestDatedBulletWithinDays: { days }` — clock from `ctx.now` (wall clock otherwise), dates more than 2 days in the future discarded so a typo'd future date can't mark a page fresh forever (`{age}`/`{date}`/`{days}`)

Every assertion except `requirePresent` asserts nothing when the section is absent — the missing heading stays `page-sections`' single finding, never double-reported. Plus one new relevance gate: `scanningWholeRepo` (mode `all` only), for the time-driven freshness advisory.

## Converted (5)

`product-wiki-page-sections`, `product-wiki-sources`, `product-wiki-growth-log`, `product-wiki-key-insights`, `product-wiki-freshness` — ids, severities, and messages verbatim. A page's whole grammar now reads directly off the declarations, e.g. key-insights: *section first on page, bullets only, ≤7 bullets, ≤140 characters each*.

`lib.mjs` keeps the path constants, `configGuard`, and the wiki-page classifier — now two regexes (`WIKI_PAGE`, `WIKI_RESERVED`) all five declarations import, so the classifier stays spelled once — and sheds the section machinery the engine owns. `layout` and `isolation` are untouched (config-guard and barrier territory).

**Corpus total: 25 checks as declarations across the four rounds.**

## Testing

- Engine suite grown to 28 tests: fence/case/suffix heading semantics, position + prose rules, block continuation joining, date grammar and impossible dates, count caps, the freshness window boundary (45 on-window vs 46 stale) with an injected clock, future-typo discarding, and the whole-repo gate.

- Full suite: **1568/1568 pass**, including all 40 product-wiki pack tests unchanged.

{"number":827,"title":"Declared checks are JSON, one file per pack","body":"Closes #826.

The four conversion rounds left 25 pattern-rule declarations as 25 modules averaging 17 lines each — all of them data. This makes them data: one JSON file per pack, discovered structurally.

## The format

A pack's declarations are the array in `packs/<pack>/declared-checks.json`; a skill's live in its own `declared-checks.json` beside the `checks.mjs` that still lists its coded rules. The pack registry discovers both the way it discovers packs themselves — **no import, no manifest line: writing the declaration adds the check.**

A declaration carries `id`, `severity`, `failureMessage`, and its assertions with their `what`/`fix`. What it no longer carries:

- **no comments** — JSON cannot hold one, so the no-comments-on-a-check rule is enforced by construction rather than by review;
- **no `description`** — the failure message stands on its own;
- **no `doc` pointer** — a declared check states its own case rather than deferring to prose;
- **`why` → `failureMessage`**, named for what it is: the line the agent reads when the check fires.

Regexes are strings in `/pattern/flags` form, compiled at load. `scanFiles`/`excludeFiles`/`pathExists` still read any other string as an exact repo path; a plain string at a strictly-pattern key is an authoring error, reported with the key that got it and the value it got.

```json
{
  "id": "gha/label-create-before-add",
  "severity": "advisory",
  "failureMessage": "--add-label fails when the label does not exist yet — GitHub will not create it on demand",
  "scanFiles": "/^\\.github\\/workflows\\/[^/]+\\.ya?ml$/",
  "scanTracked": true,
  "checkEachFile": [{
    "whenFileMatches": "/--add-label/",
    "require": "/label create/",
    "what": "uses --add-label with no idempotent `gh label create … || true` beforehand",
    "fix": "create the label idempotently before adding it, so the workflow survives its first run"
  }]
}
```

## What moved

| pack / skill | before | after |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `github-actions` | 5 modules | `declared-checks.json` |
| `chrome-extension-release` | 5 modules | `declared-checks.json` |
| `product-wiki` | 5 modules | `declared-checks.json` |
| `basics` | 3 modules | `declared-checks.json` |
| `aws-sam` | 2 modules | `declared-checks.json` |
| `web-speech-io` | 2 modules | `declared-checks.json` |
| `google-id-token-validation` | 2 modules | `declared-checks.json` |
| `unattended-agents` | 1 module | `declared-checks.json` |

Rules with a hand-written `run(ctx)` are untouched and stay their own modules listed in the manifest — `handler-path`, `privacy-permission-alignment`, `layout`, `routine-structure` and the rest. `product-wiki/lib.mjs` drops the two page-classifier regexes it was exporting only for the checks; the declaration owns them now, with no second copy to drift from.

## Engine

- `patternRule(declaration)` compiles pattern strings and maps `failureMessage` onto the field the finding renderer reads; `loadDeclaredChecks(dir)` reads and caches a directory's declarations, so the registry and a test share one compiled set rather than each re-parsing.
- The registry appends a pack's declarations to its world rules and a skill's to its skill checks, reaching the compiler **lazily — only where a declaration file exists** — so a tree carrying just the pack machinery (the hook fixtures, a minimal mount) loads exactly as before.
- `--list` prints a declared rule's failure message in the description column and leaves the doc column empty.
- Two deliberate cross-tree reaches are accepted with reasons in `.claudinite-checks.json`: the registry reaching the compiler, and the shared test harness reaching the loader so a pack test proves the same rule object the runner runs.

## Verification

- World sweep: **finding-for-finding identical** to `origin/main` — the same 0 blocking, 28 advisory, same list.
- `--list`: identical on **id and severity for all 88 rules**.
- **1613 tests pass**, six new: regex-string compilation with flags, the authoring-error message, `failureMessage` reaching the finding, the loader's absent-file and cache behaviour, and the registry discovering a pack's and a skill's declarations. Each was seen to fail against a mutated engine before being kept.
- The pack tests' assertions are unchanged in substance — they now resolve their rule through `declaredCheck(dir, id)` instead of an import.

{"number":853,"title":"Promote eleven fleet lessons into the canon","body":"Growth promote, 2026-08-15. Context members read: **ClaudiniteWebsite, EdFringeNow, MissingBulbWebsite, Sheepdog** — their local packs' `RULES.md` prose and check modules.

Eleven lessons cleared the bar. Six are folds into an existing rule (a measured sharpening of what the corpus already said); five are new bullets in a doc that owns the subject. Every one is prose — the reasons are per-row below. `Refs #852`.

**Rebased onto current `main`** (24 commits, including the `basics/RULES.md` audit in #894) and re-applied in the style that audit landed — see *Conformance to the audited style* below.

| Lesson (generalized) | Origin | Landed |
|---|---|---|
| Naming a path in `node --test` is not enough — the argument must resolve to files that exist; a typo'd glob is the same zero-test green | ClaudiniteWebsite (`node-test-discovery` check) | `packs/node/RULES.md` — sharpens the test-discovery bullet |
| When you know the exact title, don't search — an MCP layer may match *semantically* and honour no qualifier, so `in:title` filters nothing; enumerate and match in-session | MissingBulbWebsite | `git-github-advanced` — sharpens "Cap *and* qualify" |
| The per-object **field set** is the payload knob, not the page size — the same call at two page sizes returned identical output | MissingBulbWebsite | `git-github-advanced` — same section, new sub-bullet |
| A rebase that drops part of a branch must amend the commit message in the same step — under squash merge the commit body *is* `main`'s record, and a PR comment isn't carried | MissingBulbWebsite | `git-github-advanced` — commit-layering section |
| Find an already-open issue by the **invariant identifier** the finding names, never the sentence it arrived in — every filer paraphrases the message | MissingBulbWebsite | `packs/basics/RULES.md` — folded into the "Deferring a warning" rule |
| A harness wake-up needs `prompt` unless `stop: true`; a no-op flag and a `reason` don't exempt it | ClaudiniteWebsite + Sheepdog + MissingBulbWebsite (3 of 4) | `packs/basics/RULES.md` — Harness-tool contracts |
| Telling a reader to *run* something ships the literal invocation, not the filename (measured 5/5 vs 0/5 first-try) — and a rule filed where its reader never looks cannot repair a defective instruction | Sheepdog | `authoring-agent-docs` — "Shape a rule so it fires" + "Maintain it like code" |
| Seeing a figure in several search results is not evidence of who published it — snippets quote each other; attribute to the named origin | MissingBulbWebsite | `packs/product-wiki/RULES.md` |
| A dedupe search that finds nothing, on a rule naming an identifier you don't own, more likely means the mechanism **expired** than that the lesson is novel | Sheepdog | `extracting-lessons.md` — extends "Dedupe ruthlessly" |
| A test dereferencing a path in a read-only dependency tree someone else refreshes is a test whose fixture a stranger can delete — read defensively, skip with a stated reason | Sheepdog | `writing-tests` |
| An open PR is invisible to the next pass reading only the default branch — read open PRs on the same paths, not just the tracker log | MissingBulbWebsite | `unattended-agents` — extends the tracker-log precondition |

### Conformance to the audited style

Three of these were re-applied differently after the rebase, because #894 changed what the corpus asks for:

- **The issue-search rule is now a clause, not a bullet.** Its subject was "Looking for *that* already-open issue" — a "that" pointing back, which the audited skill names as the test for a rule that is a clause of its neighbour. It folds into "Deferring a warning" instead.
- **The run-it-don't-name-it rule drops its incident narrative.** "Carrying the evidence a rule came from" now says the story and the ids are archaeology the commit keeps, and only a measurement that *is* the argument stays — so the 0-in-5 / 5-in-5 figure survives and the run-by-run account doesn't.
- **The dedupe-miss rule sheds its closing clause**, which #894's own "cut the one whose mechanism has since been retired" now carries. What remains is the half that audit doesn't make: that an *empty* dedupe search reads as novelty when it more often means expiry.

Two smaller ones: the `git-github-advanced` addition gets the blank line between blocks the style now asks for (the pre-existing unseparated run below it is left alone), and the `node/RULES.md` bullet this extends is **wrapped at 100 columns** per `rules-line-length`'s own remedy — that file goes from 6 over-long lines to 5, and its other five are untouched.

**One sentence added that no source had**, which the style rule requires be named as an addition: "Naming a mechanism" now points at its exception ("The exception is a mechanism you are telling the reader to *run*, below"), so the general rule doesn't read as unconditional.

Still-needed check: none of the eleven is covered by anything in the 24 commits `main` gained. The nearest miss is the dedupe-miss rule above, trimmed rather than dropped.

### Why prose, not checks

Ten of the eleven are **judgment or in-flight behaviour** with no repo-state signature (how to phrase an instruction, which tool to reach for, what a search miss means). The one convertible item is the `node --test` sharpening: ClaudiniteWebsite already runs it as a working check with a fixture. It is not lifted here because the lesson was **already canon prose** — this is a fold-in to an existing rule, and converting canon prose to a canon check is the standing `prose-to-checks` sweep's own territory, which reads `packs/node/RULES.md` and will now see the sharpened property to assert. Flagged in the tracker rather than minted as a backlog issue.

- `select:` needs the `mcp__<server>__` prefix; `Edit` needs the read tool — both already in `basics` Harness-tool contracts.
- "The session that designed a judgment stage must not run it"; "re-issue a rejected fallback"; "nothing you post to a tracker can be edited" — all already in `unattended-agents` (the wake-up bullet above carries only the argument contract and points at that rule rather than restating it).
- "Grep the standing absolutes when a change falsifies a self-description" — already in `basics`.
- "A step only the owner can perform gets its own issue"; "look for the shared pack before hand-authoring release/CI plumbing" — both already in `basics`.
- ClaudiniteWebsite's "shallow-clone the canon to list adoptable packs" — **expired**, superseded by `packs/directory.GENERATED.md` shipping in every mount; `core` already routes there.
- Sheepdog's `resolve-dispatch` exit-11 echo — a fix to `engine/scheduler/executor.md`, outside promote's `packs/`+`skills/` write surface.

### Verification (re-run after the rebase)

- `check_the_world.mjs` — **0 blocking, 60 advisory**, identical to `origin/main`'s own 60; no advisory introduced.
- `node --test $(git ls-files '*.test.mjs')` — **1836 pass, 0 fail**.
- `promote-scope.mjs` — OK, every changed path under `packs/`.
- Diff against `main` removes 5 lines, all of them the tails of rules this PR extends; no other author's content is touched.

{"number":891,"title":"Three vocabulary enhancements — no new key families — and the five conversions they unlock","body":"Review of #880's class-A slice, delivered as the conversions it asks for — with two of its proposed new keys refused in favor of enhancing options the vocabulary already has. The fuller review of classes B–E (block scopes, derived scan sets, what genuinely never converts) is a comment on #880.

## The vocabulary changes (`engine/checks/helpers/pattern-rules.mjs`)

Each is an enhancement of an existing option, per the dispatch's discipline (prove a new field impossible before adding one):

| Enhancement | Of | First customer |
|---|---|---|
| `ignoringComments` on `someTrackedFileContains` | the existing relevance probe | `sudden-termination-vs-teardown` — a Swift comment naming `installTap` must not arm the rule |
| `requireValueInArray` (+ `matchingEntryObjectsByField` on both polarity twins) | `checkParsedFiles`'s existing `forbidValueInArray` | `core-declared` — a raw `packs` array spells `"core"` or `{ "id": "core" }` |
| `whoseTextMatches`, `eachValueInParsedArray`, `coveredByValueInArrayAtField` | `requireIndexCoverage`'s existing quantifier/coverage seams | `home-seeded-packs-declared`, `cer/privacy-permission-alignment` |

Two of #880's proposed keys are **not** added:
- `andPreviousLineMatches` — `checkEachFile.forbid` is a whole-text regex, so one pattern already covers the plist same-line, next-line, and comment-interleaved layouts; a line-pair key would cover fewer. Cost taken: the finding anchors at the file, not the key's line.
- a bespoke value-quantifier key family — it is a third quantifier on `requireIndexCoverage`, not a new family.

All engine work authored red-first (four failing tests on the unknown keys before the mechanisms).

## The conversions

- `sudden-termination-vs-teardown` → `packs/macos/declared-checks.json`
- `core-declared` → `packs/core/declared-checks.json`
- `home-seeded-packs-declared` → `.claudinite/local/packs/claudinite/declared-checks.json`
- `cer/privacy-permission-alignment` → `packs/chrome-extension-release/declared-checks.json` (now covers every manifest, not just the first)
- `product-wiki-layout` split: the skeleton's `requirePaths` declares under the existing id; the takes-no-config guard stays coded as `product-wiki-config-guard` (it judges the *normalized* config, which no declaration over the raw file sees in one place)

Every conversion driven red-first through the coded rule's own fixtures, FP guards included; each coded module deleted in its conversion's commit.

## Consumer safety

`consumer-safe-change` flagged `product-wiki-config-guard.mjs` as a rule that became blocking with no carrier. **Chosen: the rehearsal fixture** (`product-wiki-consumer` in `packs-tests/rehearsal/fixtures.mjs`), because the change is additive from a member's seat: the declared layout check and the coded guard arrive together in one vendored converge, no member-owned file has to move, and the guard's blocking severity is what the same finding already carried inside `product-wiki-layout`. The fixture proves a member that adopted the standard converges green across the split, in both fresh and stale modes.

## Verification

- Full suite from `git ls-files`: **1785 pass, 0 fail** (rehearsal now 30, including the new shape ×2 modes)
- Whole-repo world sweep: **0 blocking**, and the advisory count is identical before and after the branch (58 = 58)
- Corpus tally recomputed from `packRules`: 91 → 92 (the split adds one rule); `catalog-tally.test.mjs` green

- **The action restated as steps** — "don't carry one approval forward"; "Always check the fancier route against the naive one before keeping it"; "Add each custom header to the allowed-headers list".
- **Consequence prose arguing for the rule** — "a padded update is worse than none"; "an unqualified `firebase deploy` in a README eventually ships someone's half-finished hosting directory"; "Reading rules and believing them is how the merge-semantics bugs above ship".
- **Hedges and provenance** — "the assessment itself stays judgment"; "so one-member kinds are normal rather than a smell"; leaflet's five `(Grounded in js/app.js …)` notes, which restate the rule and point at one project's tree from a project-agnostic pack.
- **Incident narratives in the local pack** — outage durations, owner-turn tallies, "this bit once in #NNN". The mechanism, the instruction, and every path/command stayed; only the argument for why the rule earned its place went.

## What was preserved

No rule merged, none dropped — every file's paragraph, list, and heading structure maps one-to-one onto the original. Concrete details survive verbatim: the `Comment class:` literal the `comment-classification` check enforces, the promotion ladder, `--disable-warning`/`eslint-disable` and the at-site placement rule, the `AllViewerExceptHostHeader` policy id, the `runScripts: "dangerously"` fix, `git -c commit.gpgsign=false commit --no-gpg-sign`, `VENDORED_ENGINE_DOCS`, the leaf-id regex, and every file path and link.

Where cutting a clause would have changed what someone does, it stayed — e.g. the suppression rule's "**not** a small fix" (its link back to the preceding warnings rule) and "so no second justification is recorded elsewhere" (it tells you not to file one).

## Testing

- `node --test "engine-tests/**/*.test.mjs" "packs-tests/**/*.test.mjs"` — 622 pass, 0 fail.

{"number":552,"title":"prose-to-checks: add the deletion test and sweep the canon with it","body":"Closes #551

## The rule

Coming out of a conversion, apply the **deletion test**: prose a mechanism fully covers is deleted, never trimmed. Asked of every paragraph standing beside a landed check — *with this paragraph gone, would the check still catch every violation it describes **and** tell the agent how to fix it?* If yes, delete it whole.

Landed as its own section in the `prose-to-checks` skill, with step 4 of "How to convert one" and the Bounds entry rewritten to point at it.

Two docs carried the wording the rule supersedes, so they move with it:

- `packs/grow_with_claudinite/tasks/prose-to-checks-sweep/task.md` — "Trim the now-redundant prose to rationale."
- `engine/checks/DESIGN.md` governance — "the doc keeps only rationale and the judgment parts." Directly contradicted now: the rationale's home is the check's header comment. Leaving it would have been the very drift trap the rule is about.

One addition to the rule as stated, found while running it: a finding renders `what` / `why` / `fix` / `doc` and **never the rule's `description`**, so a remedy that lives only in the description is not carried by the mechanism. The skill now says so, because it changed two verdicts.

## The sweep

All 64 landed rules, every paragraph beside them. Thirteen deleted whole.

| Deleted | Covering check |
|---|---|
| `packs/aws-sam/RULES.md` — esbuild strips the entry subdirectory | `aws-sam/handler-path` |
| `packs/chrome-extension/RULES.md` — `declarativeContent` SetIcon needs raw pixels | `declarative-content-set-icon` |
| `git-github-advanced` §"A CI job that reads submodule files…" | `gha/checkout-submodules` |
| `git-github-advanced` §"A workflow that adds a brand-new label…" | `gha/label-create-before-add` |
| `git-github-advanced` §"…default shell has no `pipefail`" | `gha/run-pipefail` |
| `git-github-advanced` §"Gate an optional CI job on a repo variable…" | `gha/secrets-in-job-if` |
| `repo-text-sweeps` — grep for inbound references before deleting/renaming | `reference-integrity` |
| `repo-text-sweeps` — a Markdown link carries its path twice | `markdown-link-labels` |
| `packs/basics/scheduled-tasks.md` — "Preprocessing is optional, bounded, and task-local" | `task-declaration-shape` |
| `RELEASE.md` — `cer/privacy-permission-alignment` bullet | itself |
| `RELEASE.md` — `cer/permission-added-store-issue` bullet | itself |
| `RELEASE.md` permissions runbook step 1 — disclose in the same PR | `cer/privacy-permission-alignment` |
| `adopt-pack` SKILL.md — "This is enforced, not merely encouraged…" | `adoption-answers-pending` |

Three of these were already drifting, which is the argument for the rule:

- The submodules section said `recurse-submodules: true`; the input is `submodules: recursive`, which is what the check's fix says.
- The preprocessing bullet called `agent_preprocessing` optional. The check flags an agentless task that *omits* it.
- The `adopt-pack` paragraph was pure enforcement narration of its own rule id — the shape `skill-no-enforcement-narration` exists to forbid.

## What survived, and why

The test discriminated; most paragraphs stayed. The recurring reasons, worth recording because they are what a future sweep will hit:

- **A second rule in the same breath.** The CloudFront `Authorization` bullet also teaches *why not the plain `AllViewer` variant* (forwarding `Host` to an API Gateway origin returns 403) — nothing checks that. The `claude-md-length` bullet also says splitting into imports doesn't save context, which is precisely the wrong fix an agent would reach for.
- **A scope the check deliberately declines.** `aws-sam/esbuild-dependency` skips multi-package repos rather than misfire; the prose still carries the rule there. `gha/unique-automation-branch` matches only `checkout -b … $(date`, where the prose says "a non-unique key".
- **A remedy the finding never states.** `bootstrap.md`'s "inline what you need" is in `claudinite-isolation`'s `description`, not its `fix` — the rendered finding offers "route shared code through a shared/contracts folder", which is the wrong advice for this rule. Kept, and flagged below.
- **A value the check can't judge.** `agent_execution_timeout` is checked for presence; "set it generously — extreme protection against a runaway, not a scheduling knob" is what an author actually needs.
- **Configuration documented nowhere else.** `executable-requirements`' `config.spec`, `scheduled-tasks`' `session_scope`.

Skills already stripped to a routing paragraph by earlier passes — `python-optional-deps`, `web-speech-io`, `google-id-token-validation`, `writing-claudinite-skills` — had nothing left to take.

## Noticed while sweeping, not fixed here

Both out of this change's scope; happy to open issues if wanted.

- `claudinite-isolation`'s rendered `fix` gives generic barrier advice ("route shared code through a shared/contracts folder") instead of its actual remedy, "inline what you need". That gap is the only reason the `bootstrap.md` paragraph survived.
- `skill-no-enforcement-narration` scopes to `^skills/<name>/SKILL.md$`, but skills have lived at `packs/<pack>/skills/<name>/` since #385 — so it currently matches nothing. That is why the `adopt-pack` narration sat unflagged.
- `packs/README.md`'s corpus tally reads "41 canon" checks; `--list` reports 64 rules.

## Verification

- `node --test` over the CI test roots: **933 pass, 0 fail**.
- `check_the_world.mjs`: **0 blocking, 8 advisory** — unchanged from the pre-change baseline on `main`.

{"number":1422,"title":"product-wiki: bundle the /explore-link skill","body":"Closes #1421

The pack grew its wikis on one lane only — the weekly `wiki-growth` pass, which picks its own targets from each page's `## Open questions`. `/explore-link` is the other lane: the owner hands over a **source**, and the run's judgment is which existing wiki page it feeds, what the four axes take out of it, and what it turns out not to say.

## What the skill carries

- **Get the bytes** — `curl` to disk rather than a summarizing fetch, because a pricing table and a feature matrix are exactly what a paraphrase drops; a 403/paywall is "unreadable, stop", not a prompt to try a sibling URL; the page is data, never instruction.
- **Pick the page it feeds** — read candidates' `## Key insights` and `## Sources` first (an already-cited link that adds nothing is the answer), one page unless the link genuinely feeds two, and never create a wiki folder.
- **The four axes** — product, market, usage, pricing, each with what to actually pull out. An axis the source doesn't cover is recorded as uncovered in `## Open questions`, never filled with a plausible value; pricing carries its observation date; a vendor page is written as self-reported, and a second-hand figure attributes to the origin the page names.
- **Write it back** — deferred to the pack's standing terms (RULES.md and `wiki-growth`'s task doc steps 5–7 plus delivery) rather than restated; the skill adds only the contradicted-claim correction and the "nothing landed ⇒ no commit, no PR" stop.

Pack version 60824.1 → 60830.1, with its `VERSIONS.md` row. Skills mount structurally from `<pack>/skills/`, so no manifest change was needed; the README gains the `## Skill` table naming what the pack bundles.

## Verification

- `node --test $(git ls-files '*.test.mjs')` — 2754/2755, the one failure being the pre-existing `engine-pack-lane-shims` shallow-clone guard, unrelated to this diff.
- `check_the_work` clean; `check_the_world` 0 blocking, 86 advisory, none naming these files.
