{"number":1474,"title":"Auto-merge policies scope a folder inline (`under:<dir>`) and intersect (`&&`)","body":"Closes #1473

An auto-merge policy could name a built-in diff class or a rule a pack had committed to its `merge-rules.json` — never "any change under **this** folder", and never an intersection of the two. So an ad-hoc request that meant one tree (#1470) had to say `Automerge: anything`, and `wiki-growth`, whose whole write surface is `product-wiki/`, had to approximate itself with the repo-wide `doc-changes`.

Two additions to the policy vocabulary, which together are one feature:

### `under:<dir>` — a rule name that carries its own argument

Resolves everywhere a rule name does: a task's `automerge`, a request item's `Merge:` field, a `reject:` term, the arming trailer, the `merge-policy.mjs` CLI and the `automerge-policy-scope` work check — one resolution path, so no surface can disagree about a scope.

- Covers **any change kind** inside the directory (added, modified, deleted).
- Matches on whole path segments, so `under:packs/product-wiki` does not reach `packs/product-wiki-extras/`.
- The **self-widening guard is unchanged**: `merge-policy.mjs`, a `merge-rules.json`, a `tasks/<name>/task.mjs` and the work-scope gate stay uncoverable by a list policy even when they sit inside the named folder.

### `&&` — the intersection

A policy **list is a union**: adding a term widens, because each changed file need only be covered by one of them. `&&` inside a term is the one narrowing operator — every part must cover the file, and every part's whole-diff constraint (e.g. "one code directory") must hold. `under:product-wiki && doc-changes` is "docs, and only under that folder"; listing the two instead would authorize Markdown anywhere in the repo.

`&` is legal in neither a rule name nor an `under:` path, so the operator can never be read as part of a term. Whitespace around it is accepted wherever a person writes one and canonicalized away by `policyExpression`, so the stamped trailer stays one whitespace-free token and its regex is untouched. A composite (itself a union) or a whole-policy word inside an `&&` term is an authoring error, and an unresolvable part poisons the whole term — all of it fails closed.

Two consequences on the request lane: the `Automerge:` line now reads to the end of the line (an `&&` term may carry spaces) and no longer lowercases its value, since an `under:` path is case-sensitive. `work-item.mjs`'s deliberately-pure grammar mirror gained the `under:` path shape — the existing drift-guard test caught it accepting a path the engine refuses.

### wiki-growth

Declares `` [`under:${WIKI_ROOT} && doc-changes`] `` against the constant its precondition already anchors on, so the round may land its own Markdown pages; a doc elsewhere in the repo and a non-doc file inside the wiki both park it. On a member whose mount predates this vocabulary the policy reads as invalid, which is also a park — never a wider merge.

**Verification.** 12 new tests across `normalizePolicy`/`policyVerdict` and the request-lane drift guard, each watched failing against the pre-change modules (the two that pass both ways do so by fail-closed construction — an unparseable term already authorized nothing). Full suite green: 2776 pass, 0 fail. `check_the_work --changed` clean.

**Not in this change:** decomposing `claudinite-growth`'s two `claudinite-local-pack-md-*` rules into `under:.claudinite/local/packs && doc-changes`. It works — but it rewrites a policy that is correct today, and the swap is a hair wider on file extensions, so it deserves its own decision.","state":"closed","draft":false,"merged":true,"mergeable_state":"unknown","html_url":"https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/pull/1474","user":{"login":"missingbulb","id":73882448,"profile_url":"https://github.com/missingbulb","avatar_url":"https://avatars.githubusercontent.com/u/73882448?v=4"},"merged_by":"missingbulb","head":{"ref":"claude/auto-merge-task-folders-5l4lix","sha":"88e0beea1e3e8f062ef51b1b6d13ce1113bacda1","repo":{"full_name":"missingbulb/Claudinite"}},"base":{"ref":"main","sha":"e4c52479a8a2d6c4bc8d30f69d2db34bd934c7a0","repo":{"full_name":"missingbulb/Claudinite"}},"additions":292,"deletions":33,"changed_files":17,"commits":2,"created_at":"2026-08-30T21:14:09Z","updated_at":"2026-08-30T21:54:53Z","closed_at":"2026-08-30T21:54:50Z","merged_at":"2026-08-30T21:54:50Z"}

{"number":1650,"title":"Path-scoped skills: a pack declares which skill must be loaded before editing files under a pattern","body":"Closes #1648

## The mechanism

- **A skill names the files it must be loaded for** under `force-load-on-file-edits-paths` in its SKILL.md frontmatter `metadata` — the map the harness reserves for a reader's own keys and never acts on. Not the harness's `paths`: that field *limits* when the harness offers a skill at all, so a skill forced for some files would stop being offered for the rest of its remit (observed live: three skills vanished from the Skill tool the moment they carried `paths`, and came back when it was removed). Glob grammar as for path-specific rules, brace expansion included. One reader, `engine/pack_loader/skill-frontmatter.mjs`; one resolver, `engine/pack_loader/path-scoped-skills.mjs`.
- **PreToolUse guard** widens from `Bash` to `Bash|Edit|Write|NotebookEdit`. On a file tool it matches the path against the active packs' forced skills and, when the transcript shows no load of the named skill, blocks with a reason naming it and its SKILL.md path. Loaded: allow. A load is a `Skill` tool call or a `Read` of the skill's own file. Subagent loads count. A guard that cannot decide lets the edit through and logs it.
- **Converge wiring** retargets a guard group already registered under the old `Bash` matcher instead of adding a second group.
- **`skill-loaded-before-editing`** (claudinite-lifecycle work rule): the Stop-time backstop for edits the guard never sees (Bash `sed`, heredocs). Silent with no transcript. It fired on this very session, which is how the writing-tests skill got applied to this PR's own tests.
- **The skills index**, `.claudinite/claudinite-skills.GENERATED.md`: every mounted skill, canon and local, with what loads it — the forced ones and their files first, then the rest by description. Written by the same converge that writes the rules index, kept current by `skills-index-current`, `merge=ours` like its sibling. Not imported by CLAUDE.md.
- **Rehearsal fixture**: the `versioned-local` shape's dated pack bundles a skill carrying the key, so a consumer's own forced skill is proven to mount, index and load.

## The skills that force themselves

- product-wiki `writing-wiki-pages` (new; the page-editing rules moved out of `RULES.md`, which keeps the two rules a reading session needs): `product-wiki/**`
- claudinite-growth `writing-pack-prose`: every `packs/*/RULES.md` and `packs/*/skills/*/SKILL.md`; `writing-tasks`: `tasks/*/task.mjs` and `task.md`
- basics `writing-tests`: test files by name and folder; `authoring-agent-docs`: `CLAUDE.md` and `.claude/rules/`
- claudinite-canon-curation `writing-claudinite-skills`: `packs/*/skills/**`
- chrome-extension `chrome-store-releases` and static-website `static-site-releases`: their config file and vendored workflows

Each already said "use before editing" these. Left alone, with the reason in the conversation: github-actions-scheduling, file-placement, repo-text-sweeps, writing-migration-plans, and the code-content skills.

## Verified

- Full suite green. `check_the_work` and `check_the_world` clean.
- Mutation run: disabling the resolver's match makes the guard test and the rule test fail.
- Real run against this repo: a `Write` on a test file or a pack SKILL.md is blocked with an empty transcript, naming the skill and its file, and allowed with this session's transcript.

## Follow-up

#1662 lists, as suggestions only, which rules in every pack's `RULES.md` could move into forced or activity-triggered skills.

## Delivery

Engine flow, so a forced fleet delivery once merged. No engine version bump: members take the engine at `main` on their next converge, engine before packs in the same run.

{"number":820,"title":"Pattern-check engine: structured-data (parsed JSON/YAML) assertions","body":"Closes #819. The Category-3 append, following the pattern round (#790) and the cross-file tree round (#800): checks whose subject is a **parsed document's fields** are now declarations.

## Engine

Documents are parsed **at most once per scan** — `.json` via `JSON.parse`, `.ya?ml` via the existing minimal YAML parser — through a cache shared by the whole rule family, keeping the one-pass economics. An absent or unparsable document asserts nothing (matching every original check's catch-and-skip posture). Field paths are dotted (`devDependencies.esbuild`); a field counts as present when its value is not `undefined`.

Four new assertion kinds, named to read without the design doc:

- **`checkParsedFile`** — `{ file, whenFieldPresent, requireField | forbidField, what, fix }`: where the guard field is present, another field must be present / absent.
- **`equalParsedValues`** — two parsed fields must be equal; the first file is selected by a path + content probe (`filesMatching` + `whereFileContains`, reproducing `findExtensionManifest`), an absent second file fires `whenSecondMissing` at its own path, and a mismatch fires `whenUnequal` at the first file with `{first}`/`{second}` interpolated.
- **`forEachParsedEntry`** — iterate a document's named entries (e.g. SAM `Resources`) filtered by `whereFieldEquals`, forbidding a value in an array field (`ignoreCase` supported); `{entry}` interpolates the entry name.
- **`checkKeyValueFile`** — dotenv-style schema: the file must exist, hold only `KEY=value` lines and `#` comments, use only the declared keys, and declare every one — each failure mode with its own declared message (`{key}`/`{keys}`/`{line}`).

Plus two relevance gates: `someTrackedFileContains: { pathMatching, text }` and `exactlyOneTrackedFileMatches`.

## Converted (4)

- `cer/version-sync` → `equalParsedValues`
- `cer/release-config` → `checkKeyValueFile`
- `aws-sam/cloudfront-authorization` → `forEachParsedEntry`

- Engine suite grown to 21 tests: each new kind's firing and silent sides, parse-failure tolerance, gate behavior, and a parse-once assertion via a read counter.

{"number":555,"title":"Pack manifest as the single source: routing guidance, skills, scoped rules","body":"Nothing in the corpus said *where a piece of content belongs*, so when a rule, doc, skill or check could plausibly live in more than one pack the decision defaulted to `basics` — which is exactly how the GitHub Actions cron doctrine landed there in this PR's first commit. Fixing that turned into making the pack manifest state what a pack is, and retiring the places that said it a second time.

## The manifest spec (#559)

[`engine/pack_loader/pack-schema.mjs`](engine/pack_loader/pack-schema.mjs) declares every field a `pack.mjs` may carry, which are required, and each one's constraints. The **loader** validates every manifest against it — canon and consumer local packs alike — so an incomplete declaration is a blocking `config` error at load, the same class as invalid JSON in `.claudinite-checks.json`. A required manifest field is part of the pack contract, not a conformance opinion about a repo's content: a check would have to be declared by a pack, run only when that pack is active, and re-derive the manifest by reading its source text.

- **Reported, not fatal** — the pack still loads and still runs its checks; silently disabling a repo's own rules is a worse failure than the one being reported.
- The vocabulary is **closed**, so a typo (`rule:`, `skill:`) fails loudly instead of being ignored forever.

### `ruleRoutingGuidance` — what belongs here, and what does not

```js
ruleRoutingGuidance: {
  belongs: 'workflow YAML and Actions runner platform behaviour: triggers, secrets, permissions, scheduling, artifacts, reusable workflows and their pitfalls',
  excludes: 'git and GitHub command procedure — git-github; release pipeline content for one product — its release pack',
},
```

Both sides required, each capped at **20 words** — a session-context budget, not a style rule: `inject-pack-prose` emits the set as a **routing table at session start**, one row per pack, for every pack *discovered* (a consumer holds only what it vendored, so that set is already what it can route into). `excludes` names the pack that owns the other side, so the table routes rather than merely refuses; a boundary true of every pack carries no routing information and wastes the row. Filled in for all 27 canon packs and the home's two local packs.

### `worldRules` / `workRules` — a rule's scope is its placement

The single `rules` array splits in two, so which list a rule sits in is what makes it world- or work-scoped. The loader flattens both into the `rules` array the runners walk, stamping each rule's scope from its list. A rule module may still carry `scope` — the `runRule` dispatch seam reads it off the rule object to hand work rules their fluent surface — but the two must agree, or it's a load error.

### `skills` — the bundle, declared

`skills: ['merge-to-main', ...]`, held to the `skills/` tree in **both directions**: an undeclared directory is a skill nothing announces, a declared name with no directory is a manifest that lies. What each skill covers stays in its `SKILL.md` frontmatter rather than being copied.

## Pack READMEs

With skills and scoped rules on the manifest, each pack README's checks table and skills table were a second copy — and had already drifted: `basics/README.md` listed a `skill-ownership` check the pack does not carry and omitted `catalog-completeness` and `comment-classification`. Both tables are stripped from every pack README, and the **five files that were nothing else** are deleted: `github-actions` plus the four stub packs, whose one non-derivable sentence (expected first source) moved into the manifest header comment.

The other 22 stay — provenance, design rationale, scope notes against sibling packs, an index of their `RULES.md` prose, none of it in the manifest. `catalog-completeness` now looks for the pack **directory** in the catalog rather than a README inside it.

## The cron doctrine, rehomed (#556)

Out of `packs/basics/scheduled-tasks.md` and into `packs/github-actions/skills/github-actions-scheduling/` — the pack that owns Actions platform behaviour. GitHub's `schedule:` trigger is a request to queue, not a promise to run: late fires, dropped fires with no failure and nothing in the run ledger, and the 60-day inactivity disable ([Upptime's measurement](https://upptime.js.org/blog/2021/01/22/github-actions-schedule-not-working/)). What follows: never let correctness depend on a firing happening or on when it happened; stay idempotent and self-catching; catch up the most recent slot only; keep off `:00`; say "about hourly, best-effort"; don't debug a late run as a bug before checking whether GitHub fired at all.

`packs/basics/scheduled-tasks.md` is unchanged from `main` — the scheduling doctrine stays put, only the platform truth moved.

## Verification

- **945 tests, 945 pass** across the CI test roots, including 12 new tests for the manifest spec and a corpus-wide assertion that every discovered pack loads clean through it.
- `node engine/checks/check_the_world.mjs` → **0 blocking**, 8 advisory — the same pre-existing `file-placement` advisories in `engine/`, none new.
- Fixtures updated where the change reached them: fake-corpus test harnesses copy `pack-schema.mjs` beside the registry, the vendor set grew by that one file, and the demo local packs declare `ruleRoutingGuidance`.","state":"closed","draft":false,"merged":true,"mergeable_state":"unknown","html_url":"https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/pull/555","user":{"login":"missingbulb","id":73882448,"profile_url":"https://github.com/missingbulb","avatar_url":"https://avatars.githubusercontent.com/u/73882448?v=4"},"merged_by":"missingbulb","head":{"ref":"claude/github-actions-scheduling-yupnki","sha":"f9b4523f60b1cf8678ecb0f168ca3dc7ecb3c308","repo":{"full_name":"missingbulb/Claudinite"}},"base":{"ref":"main","sha":"5cf7768a6b4840ada47c87497759b97d9b232976","repo":{"full_name":"missingbulb/Claudinite"}},"additions":601,"deletions":176,"changed_files":56,"commits":5,"created_at":"2026-07-29T13:48:43Z","updated_at":"2026-07-29T16:15:56Z","closed_at":"2026-07-29T16:15:53Z","merged_at":"2026-07-29T16:15:53Z"}

{"number":1684,"title":"Absorb barriers into basics, and stop it interviewing on adoption","body":"Closes #1681

`barriers` was not a pack anyone chose. It carried no fingerprint, and three canon packs pulled it in via `requires` — one of them `claudinite-lifecycle`, which `basics` requires — so it was already active in every member that declares the baseline. That separate identity bought a second catalog row, a second `VERSIONS.md`, a second badge, and an adoption question fired at owners who never adopted anything.

## What changes

- The `barrier` check, the pack-contribution seam and the guide move into `basics` — `worldRules/barrier.mjs`, `barriers.mjs`, `barriers.md`. `packs/barriers/` is gone.
- A repo's graph moves to `config.barriers.rules` on its `basics` entry. The check keeps a legacy read of the old placement for the window between a member's mount converging and its declaration doing so (#1041 showed that can be more than one cycle); #1682 removes it.
- `RENAMED_PACKS` gains `barriers: 'basics'`, so a member declaring the old id activates the survivor rather than nothing. `legacy-shape-in-use` already names such an entry in the holder's own findings — one advisory, one edit, both shapes.
- No `questions`. A pack that arrives through another's `requires` was never adopted, so its interview reaches an owner who did not ask for it.
- All three `requires: ['barriers']` go. Every one of those walls had already become a declared `forbidReferences` check the engine runs, so none needed a second pack declared beside it — and `claudinite-lifecycle` could not have pointed at `basics` anyway, which requires it back.

## The migration record

`absorbedPackConfig` is what a plain id rename cannot do. Two flat `config` objects spread over each other, so the absorbed graph would land under the survivor's own key namespace; and an answer recorded against a retired question would outlive it. The record names both, rather than deriving either from the rename map, which cannot tell an absorption from a rename.

It is gated on the member's own mount carrying the op, because the engine reaches a member on its own release cadence rather than this pack's: an engine without `absorbedPackConfig` would rename the id and leave the graph flat where nothing reads it — a silently unenforced barrier. An unreadable mount reads as "not capable" and the record stays inert.

**It reaches converged members only once an engine release cuts at or above `60904.1`.** Nothing depends on it having run — the rename map resolves the id and the check reads the old placement — so this is hygiene, not correctness. #1682's `Not-before` is written against that release, not against a bare week.

Merging also stops leaving an absorbed pack's `via` naming the survivor, which read as `basics` being required by `basics`.

## Verification

- Whole suite green (`node --test $(git ls-files '*.test.mjs')`), except `engine-pack-lane-shims` — which fails identically on `main` in this sandbox, on its own shallow-clone guard, and passes in CI where the clone has history.
- `check_the_work` 0 blocking; `check_the_world` 0 blocking.
- Every new assertion bites: weakening the config stand-down, the mount-capability probe and the config nesting each turns its own test red, one at a time with the source restored from the index at the moment of mutating.
- The record, driven over this repo's own pre-change declaration, reproduces the hand-converged file byte for byte.

## Also here

Two commits beyond the absorption itself:

- `claudinite-growth`'s `VERSIONS.md` had two rows claiming `60903.5`, failing `pack-version-claimed-once` on `main` before this branch existed. #1650's change takes `60903.6`.
- A re-read of the change against `writing-tests`, `writing-pack-prose` and `writing-claudinite-skills` — the skills these files are force-loaded for, which this session loaded after the fact. It moved a rule that was really rationale out of the local pack's `RULES.md` into its `references.md`, and removed a test assertion that pinned a declaration to itself.

## Folders touched

```
engine/pack_loader/     barriers -> basics joins the rename map
engine/migrations/      applyPackRenames learns absorbedPackConfig: an absorbed entry's
                        config nests under its own id, its named answers are dropped, and
                        a via naming the survivor stops surviving the merge
engine/checks/helpers/  comments stop calling the mechanism a pack of its own
packs/basics/           gains the barrier check, the contribution seam, the guide, and the
                        contributedRules seam on its manifest
packs/barriers/         deleted
packs/claudinite-lifecycle/  the converge record; drops its barriers requirement
packs/product-wiki/, packs/claudinite-canon-curation/  drop theirs
vendoring/              the rehearsal fixture and DESIGN stop describing a pack that is gone
.claudinite-settings.json, .claudinite/local/packs/claudinite/  this repo's own graph moves
                        onto its basics entry; the retired goals answer becomes a
                        references.md entry behind the standing decision already there
```

{"number":1947,"title":"product-wiki: qualitative-evidence methodology in writing-wiki-pages","body":"Closes #1946

## What this is

`product-wiki` claims "market, **user** and competitor research" as its territory, but only the market and competitor halves have a natural public source. Three rules for reading qualitative evidence, added to [`writing-wiki-pages`](https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/blob/claude/elegant-thompson-srrdmb/packs/product-wiki/skills/writing-wiki-pages/SKILL.md) — the skill both sourcing lanes load and the PreToolUse guard forces for every `product-wiki/**` edit, so they reach the session that is actually choosing a source:

- **Quoting a person** — attribute it to the speaker; an asker's or vendor's framing is theirs alone, and a quote answering a leading question is evidence only of what the respondent chose to say inside it.
- **Counting how many people back a finding** — independent voices, not mentions. One thread's ten replies are one voice; a count you cannot establish is absent, not "several". Placed beside the existing "Attributing a figure you saw in several places" rule, whose qualitative sibling it is.
- **Researching what this product's own users need** — the pack's only failure mode that looks healthy to every check it has. A user-research page sourced entirely from review sites, forum threads and competitors' testimonials satisfies `product-wiki-sources`, `-page-sections` and `-key-insights` while describing *other people's* customers. The rule makes the page name the proxy and leave the unanswered question standing.

Prompted by [Kat Laszlo's write-up of repurposing Karpathy's LLM-wiki for product discovery](``https://dev.to/kat_laszlo/i-repurposed-karpathys-llm-wiki-for-product-discovery-it-worked-surprisingly-well-2ngn).``

## What was considered and declined

The article's central structural idea is a **raw immutable evidence layer** feeding the wiki, with drill-down from a synthesized story to the customer quote behind it. The owner declined it, and the decision is recorded with its grounds in the pack's new `references.md`:

- **no first caller** — no repo has qualitative input waiting, and a capability ships with its first caller;
- a committed transcript puts **customer PII in git history permanently**, and the standard would be recommending it rather than merely permitting it;
- the layer's central **"immutable" promise is unenforceable** by checks that read the tracked tree rather than history, so it would be the one part of this standard carried by prose alone.

Also deliberately not imported: feeding wiki evidence to the coding agent as context (`product-wiki-isolation` bars exactly that, and raw customer quotes are the least reviewed thing in the tree), and the article's fixed `customers/`/`stories/`/`features/` folder names (the pack's structural classifier cannot drift).

So: **no layout change, no new reserved child, no new or relaxed checks.** A repo adopting the pack sees no structural difference.

## Folders touched

```
packs/product-wiki/skills/writing-wiki-pages/   three rules on reading qualitative evidence,
                                                placed beside the existing figure-attribution rule
packs/product-wiki/                             references.md created (the pack's first) — each
                                                rule's reaffirmable reason plus the declined-layer
                                                decision and its three grounds
```

## Verification

- `node --test` over the pack's tests plus every references/prose/skill test file: 217 pass, 0 fail.
- `check_the_world.mjs`: 104 findings, all pre-existing `file-placement` advisories; no `product-wiki` findings and none from `references-integrity`, so all three `(n)` markers resolve.
- `check_the_work.mjs` on the diff: clean, exit 0.

No version bump or `VERSIONS.md` row — those are the canon's own tasks' to write after this lands.

{"number":162,"title":"Rewrite generate-project-instructions around class-pack extraction (tested on TLDR)","body":"## Problem

The skill was meant to grow the corpus's library of **reusable instruction packs**, but its text — inherited nearly verbatim from the templates/-era generator prompt (#119, moved in #128) — directs all output at "the default working instructions for **THIS project**", demands "real commands, real paths, real file names", and mentions the reusable seed only in a closing paragraph that still points at the long-gone `.claudinite/templates/` directory. Observed outcome: competent per-repo docs, zero packs extracted.

## The rewrite (commit 1, refined in commits 3–4)

`skills/generate-project-instructions/SKILL.md` is now an **extraction procedure** with packs as the primary deliverable:

- **Packs plus one thin overlay, never a single document** — pack seeds/refinements written as if this project didn't exist, plus a thin project overlay holding only the concrete values for the packs' slots. The old skill's failure mode is named explicitly up front.
- **Facets, not one class** (commit 4, owner feedback): a project decomposes along several pack axes — working-style **class** (`research-project`, `spec-driven-product`), **technology** (an iPhone-app project tomorrow mints `iphone-app` the way `chrome-extension` was minted), **aspect** (a separable slice with its own on-switch: `chrome-extension` vs `chrome-extension-release`), and **domain** (audience/setting that changes how work is done — e.g. a children's-app pack carrying design-review and requirement-processing rules that hold across stacks). The shelf is checked per facet (declare / refine / mint / leave alone); the product itself is never a facet — its rules are the overlay.
- **A per-facet portability strip** — delete the product and stack, keep the loop → class; delete the product and working style, keep the platform → technology/aspect; delete the stack, keep the audience → domain; survives nothing → overlay. Each rule goes to exactly one owner (the facet whose whole population it serves), gated on the promotion ladder and deduped against the corpus. Minting requires several durable rules, not one stray.
- **Refinement path** (commit 3): a pack that fits but that this project's evidence sharpens or contradicts gets a refinement PR to the existing pack, never a fork — each further project sharing a facet is another exemplar, and a rule only one exemplar supports should say so or wait.
- **Delivery through the owner's approval gates** — every pack seed/refinement as a PR against Claudinite (never editing the read-only `.claudinite/` mount); `.claudinite-checks.json` declaration only after merge + mount re-sync (an unknown id fails the blocking `pack-declaration` check); existing projects keep local docs until the growth dedup phase prunes them.

`skills/README.md` catalog line and `bootstrap.md` Part 5 step 3 updated to match.

## Test run 1 — TLDR (commit 2)

Followed the skill end-to-end against `missingbulb/TLDR`:

- **Class facet:** `spec-driven-product` — build and ship a small end-user product against an executable spec: every requirement a numbered leaf claimed by exactly one right-kind proof, expected results owner-owned, releases automatic while `main` stays green.
- **Sort tally:** class rules → the pack seed, distilled from TLDR's self-declared portable material (`dev/requirements/README.md`'s five invariants, `dev/docs/ui-testing-guideline.md`); technology/aspect facets already covered (`chrome-extension`, `chrome-extension-release`, `github-actions`, `node` — 0 new handoffs); TLDR's overlay already exists (`dev/procedures/`) and is untouched, per the no-pre-trim rule. Rules the corpus already owns are **pointed to, not restated** (real-code actuals, re-baselining approval, claim-vs-verify warning → `writing-tests`).

## Test run 2 — GoogleCalendarEventCreator (commit 3)

Ran the skill against `missingbulb/GoogleCalendarEventCreator` — the *origin* of the methodology TLDR adapted, and the more careful treatment. It exercised the refinement path and folded five improvements into the pack, now **25 rules / 8 sections**:

- **Spec boundary** (§1): a leaf is what the harness can assert; the feature-level story stays in prose docs.
- **Singleton kinds + named test lanes** (§2): the kind names the way of asserting, not a population; heavy real-environment kinds gate merge from CI without slowing the default loop.
- **The owner-approval contract's two honest shapes** (§3): artifact-expected (an agent may *propose* the expected for a brand-new leaf, never modify a committed one to pass) vs coded-expected (the assertion *is* the expected — keep it outside the product-writing surface).
- **A supported-targets matrix is spec, not folklore** (new §5): one leaf per supported external target (site/format/provider/locale), proven against a committed real sample with a reviewed exact-values expectation, added via a documented repeatable flow.
- **Gap honesty sharpened** (§6): name the exact boundary of each stub ("confirms our code *asks*, not that the platform *performs*"), mark provisional leaves visibly at the leaf, prefer real validation over the marker.

Kept out on purpose: GCEC's extractor-automation pipeline (unattended-agents territory), folder-is-the-kind harness mechanics and re-baseline popup mechanics (project-level), shared-constants drift guards (universal check already owns them).

- **Acid test (both runs):** no repo path, command, or product noun from either project survives in `RULES.md`.

The seed ships as a real pack (`packs/spec-driven-product/`: `RULES.md` + prose-only `pack.mjs` + rule-table `README.md`, registered in `packs/README.md` and the corpus index). Merging it is the owner-approval gate the skill prescribes; if you want the rewrite without the minted pack, drop commits 2–3.

## Verification

- `node --test checks/test/*.test.mjs` — 75/75 pass (after each commit).
- `node checks/run.mjs` — exit 0 (reference integrity, link labels, pack declaration, task lifecycle all green).
- Consumer simulation: a scratch project declaring `spec-driven-product` gets the pack's prose (all 8 sections) emitted by `packs/load-active-prose.mjs`.

**Follow-ups after merge** (not in this PR, per the skill's own sequencing): TLDR and GoogleCalendarEventCreator declare `spec-driven-product` in their `.claudinite-checks.json` once their mounts re-sync, and the growth dedup phase prunes what the canon now owns from their local docs.

{"number":179,"title":"Guidance: how to render UI image goldens (engine per surface)","body":"## Why

Extracted from a spec-driven-product session (missingbulb/CrosswordChat). The `spec-driven-product` pack's §7 says "embed regenerated renders of the real states" but gives **no method** — the golden-image *rendering* technique had to be reverse-engineered from a sibling repo. The `writing-tests` skill has excellent golden *discipline* (drive through real code, fixed clock, re-baseline approval) but nothing on **how to produce the image**. This fills that gap and routes it to the owning doc.

## What

- **`writing-tests`** — two bullets on rendering a UI *image* golden:
  - **Match the engine to the surface.** Inline-styled SVG / flexbox-only surfaces authored for it render **bit-exact** through a headless rasterizer (satori→SVG, resvg→PNG) with **bundled** fonts — demand a zero-pixel diff. A full shipped page using CSS **grid**, `var()`, `@media`, **emoji**, or **form widgets** is beyond that rasterizer — screenshot it with a **headless browser** (small tolerance, since it isn't bit-exact), self-skipping where no browser is present. Never reshape the product to fit the rasterizer.
  - **Host-injected surfaces**: render against a committed capture of the real host DOM with computed styles flattened inline, mounted by the shipped injector, with the model's boundary named.
- **`spec-driven-product` §7** — points at that method (the pack owns the *what*: approving the gallery is approving the product; the skill owns the *how*).
- **`git-github-advanced`** — a session process-lesson: phantom conformance findings on history you didn't author (a `squash-merge-history`, a pre-existing `warning-suppression`) mean a **stale diff base** in a cloud sandbox — `git fetch origin <default>` and re-run; never rewrite merged history or edit pre-existing code to clear them.

## Tests

Corpus self-checks green (`node --test checks/test/*.test.mjs` → 75/75); `checks/run.mjs` clean.

```entry _pack
## 2026-08-16 · born · Claudinite growth: mint the headless-browser canon pack (#905)
```

```entry fresh-install-driver
## 2026-08-18 · reworded · Promote 4 lessons from EdFringeNow and TLDR (#985)
- **Reason:** the member found a second face of the same reinstall: run from the repo root rather
  than a scratchpad it can dodge the version-mismatch failure outright and still dirty the tracked
  `package.json`, its lockfile and `node_modules`, needing a manual revert before anything can be
  committed. Folded into this rule rather than given one of its own, being the same act with a
  different cost.
```

```entry page-depends-third
## 2026-08-18 · born · Promote 4 lessons from EdFringeNow and TLDR (#985)
- **Reason:** the default network abort this pack already prescribes leaves an unvendored CDN
  library's global undefined, so the render comes back empty and reads as a product bug to anyone
  who does not know the cause - a cost the abort rule creates and does not answer. Landed at the
  prose rung: a runtime judgment with no static repo signature a check could carry.
- **Mechanism:** a RULES.md rule, triggered on "When a page depends on a third-party library loaded
  from a CDN you have not vendored, stub the library's own API surface rather than trying to make
  the CDN reachable.".
```

```entry-defaults
- **Actor:** @missingbulb (owner).
- **Model:** Claude Opus 5, per the commit trailer.
- **Landed:** #1060 (Closes #1057) · pack version 4.
```
```entry _pack
## 2026-08-19 · reworded · Collapse chrome-extension-release into chrome-extension, and stop packs discussing each other (#1060)
- **Reason:** the pack carried a whole `## Boundary` section about what its neighbours own, in
  `RULES.md` and in the README. A pack is a self-contained unit and its neighbours are not its
  subject; a probe found 51 such crossings across 22 packs, each a second copy of what
  `ruleRoutingGuidance.excludes` already carries in one machine-read field - the field the pack
  directory routes a lesson by. Both sites now state what the pack does not cover without naming
  who does. A pointer to another pack's procedure was kept, being what makes the procedure findable.
```

## PR #1248
```entry-defaults
- **Actor:** @missingbulb (owner).
- **Model:** Claude Opus 5, per the commit trailer.
- **Landed:** #1248 (Closes #1246) · pack version 60822.1.
```
```entry _pack
## 2026-08-23 · reworded · Pack manifests by convention: the tree declares the pack (#1248)
- **Reason:** most of what the manifest carried had one correct value, either the one the pack's own
  directory already gave or the one meaning "this pack does not do that", so `id`, `prose`, `badge`,
  `skills`, `worldRules` and `workRules` are resolved from the pack directory and the manifest
  states none of it. `minEngineVersion` rises to the engine release that reads all of it, because a
  manifest with no `id` is dropped outright by a pre-convention engine, which fails the mount
  self-test and stops that member converging at all.
```

## PR #1634
```entry-defaults
- **Actor:** @missingbulb (owner).
- **Model:** Claude, per the commit trailer.
- **Landed:** #1634 (Closes #1632) · pack version 60902.1.
```
```entry _pack
## 2026-09-03 · reworded · Every pack's RULES.md carries rules, not a description of the pack (#1634)
- **Reason:** the file opened with a paragraph saying what the pack covers and a scope note handing
  the ground either side of it to testing and workflow decisions. Neither changes what a session
  does, every session in every declaring repo paid for it, and the README and the manifest's
  `ruleRoutingGuidance` already carried both. Across the corpus the sweep took non-rule prose from
  2,900 words to 1,080.
```

{"number":467,"title":"Tighten every RULES.md to when + what + one non-obvious fact","body":"Closes #466

Every rule in every `RULES.md` — all 18 with rules in them, canon packs plus the local `claudinite` pack — now reads as trigger (when it applies) + instruction (what to do) + at most one clause of why, kept only where the rule would otherwise land as ceremony a reader skips. **17,127 → 15,220 words (−11%)**, structure unchanged everywhere.

## Files

| File | Words |
|---|---|
| `packs/basics` | 1070 → 846 |
| `packs/research-project` | 3299 → 3127 |
| `packs/spec-driven-product` | 1704 → 1506 |
| `.claudinite/local/packs/claudinite` | 1563 → 1273 |
| `packs/executable-requirements` | 1466 → 1384 |
| `packs/chrome-extension` | 1147 → 1058 |
| `packs/aws-sam` | 984 → 885 |
| `packs/web-speech` | 991 → 966 |
| `packs/firebase` | 747 → 679 |
| `packs/flutter` | 744 → 740 |
| `packs/html` | 469 → 371 |
| `packs/leaflet` | 503 → 317 |
| `packs/python` | 496 → 362 |
| `packs/firebase-release` | 456 → 442 |
| `packs/sheepdog` | 367 → 307 |
| `packs/product-wiki` | 351 → 344 |
| `packs/node` | 201 → 145 |
| `packs/tidy-repo` | 211 → 191 |

The four stub packs (`android`, `ios`, `app-store-release`, `play-store-release`) hold a "no rules captured yet" note and no rules, so they are untouched.

## What was cut

- **Enumerations restating the verb** — `hostContains` "matches any host containing that substring"; "Support is then claimed, proven, and counted like any requirement".
- **The action restated as steps** — "don't carry one approval forward"; "Always check the fancier route against the naive one before keeping it"; "Add each custom header to the allowed-headers list".
- **Consequence prose arguing for the rule** — "a padded update is worse than none"; "an unqualified `firebase deploy` in a README eventually ships someone's half-finished hosting directory"; "Reading rules and believing them is how the merge-semantics bugs above ship".
- **Hedges and provenance** — "the assessment itself stays judgment"; "so one-member kinds are normal rather than a smell"; leaflet's five `(Grounded in js/app.js …)` notes, which restate the rule and point at one project's tree from a project-agnostic pack.
- **Incident narratives in the local pack** — outage durations, owner-turn tallies, "this bit once in #NNN". The mechanism, the instruction, and every path/command stayed; only the argument for why the rule earned its place went.

## What was preserved

No rule merged, none dropped — every file's paragraph, list, and heading structure maps one-to-one onto the original. Concrete details survive verbatim: the `Comment class:` literal the `comment-classification` check enforces, the promotion ladder, `--disable-warning`/`eslint-disable` and the at-site placement rule, the `AllViewerExceptHostHeader` policy id, the `runScripts: "dangerously"` fix, `git -c commit.gpgsign=false commit --no-gpg-sign`, `VENDORED_ENGINE_DOCS`, the leaf-id regex, and every file path and link.

Where cutting a clause would have changed what someone does, it stayed — e.g. the suppression rule's "**not** a small fix" (its link back to the preceding warnings rule) and "so no second justification is recorded elsewhere" (it tells you not to file one).

## Testing

- `node --test "engine-tests/**/*.test.mjs" "packs-tests/**/*.test.mjs"` — 622 pass, 0 fail.
- `node engine/checks/check_the_work.mjs` — exit 0.

They resolve to one seam and two false positives: | Commit | Verdict | |---|---| | **#467 `2f3e4e9a`** — "Tighten every RULES.md to when + what + one non-obvious fact" | The only genuine seam | | #853 | **Relocated, not lost** — the text lives at `git-github-advanced/SKILL.md:44` | | #451 | **Converted** — became the `firebase/functions-predeploy-build` check, whose source quotes the removed sentence | #467's own commit message states what it cut: *"consequence prose arguing for a rule rather than enabling it"*. That was July 2026 — **before a `references.md` existed to hold it** (the convention landed in `a13cf4e2`, three commits ago). So recovering it doesn't undo the owner's decision, it completes it: every rule line stays exactly as #467 left it, and the reason moves to the doc built for it. The same message confirms the incident narratives and `#NNN` citations were shed from **the local pack only** — which is what #1567 already recovered. The canon's losses are pure rationale. ## What was recovered — 25 entries across 8 packs Only clauses carrying a **failure mode, cost, frequency, or authority** — something a review can actually weigh. A few of the stronger ones: - **spec-driven-product** — *"An agent that adjusts the expected has quietly transferred ownership of the product to itself."* - **firebase** — the create/merge asymmetry recorded as *the single most common way* a correct-looking ruleset rejects every legitimate write (a frequency claim, which is what earns the rule its place). - **leaflet** — attribution is a licence term: OSM's tile-usage policy requires it, so stripping it breaks the licence. - **html** — the cost argument: *a console read costs the user seconds, a deploy-and-check cycle costs a whole release.* `spec-driven-product` RULES-3 turned out to cross-link `packs/basics/references.md`'s `(writing-tests-1)` (#429) — the same coverage-gate lesson from the other side. I verified that key exists and says what I claim before citing it. ## What was deliberately not recovered - The leaflet **`Grounded in `** notes. #467 cut them for a stated good reason (they restate the rule and point at one project's tree from a project-agnostic pack), and `writing-pack-prose` independently rejects point-in-time code pins. Restoring them would re-import the exact class the convention rejects. - Restatements of the instruction, and hedges that change nothing a reader does. Nothing is invented where nothing was recoverable. ## Verification Three claims are verified **empirically**, not just by provenance — jsdom 30.0.1 on Node v22.22.2: - ✅ `body.innerText` → falsy, so the fall-through to `textContent` is real. **Precision note recorded**: the value is `undefined`, not `null` as the rule's wording says. Behaviour unaffected. - ✅ `

{"number":1634,"title":"Every pack's RULES.md carries rules, not a description of the pack","body":"Closes #1632

The same audit #1625 got, across the other 25 packs. Every one opened its `RULES.md` with a paragraph describing what the pack covers ("Portable, project-agnostic practices for …", "This document defines how the owner wants … run"), and several framed their sections the same way. It changes nothing a session does, every session in every declaring repo pays for it, and each pack's `README.md` plus its manifest's `ruleRoutingGuidance` (what renders into `directory.GENERATED.md`) already carries it — I checked each one before dropping it.

**Dropped:** 25 intro paragraphs; the playbook framing in `research-project` and `spec-driven-product` (what the class is, "a default to adapt, not a contract"); `basics`'s four section preambles, including the skill list the session's own skill roster already carries; `headless-browser`'s scope note; `macos`'s "these are the rules that cost the most to learn" and "Two consequences"; `node`'s "Two that recur".

**Kept as rules, re-keyed:** `macos`'s usage-description paragraph becomes **Reaching for a protected resource**; `research-project`'s interaction-cadence paragraph becomes two bullets; `python`'s three section-shaped rules become trigger-keyed bullets at the ration (280 → 150 words).

**Left alone:** the paragraph-form instruction in `executable-requirements` and `research-project` — it is prose-shaped, but it instructs, and rewriting it is a rewrite of substance rather than this sweep. Corpus non-rule prose is 2,900 → 1,080 words, and what remains is nearly all of that kind. Those two, plus `spec-driven-product`, read as manuals whose procedure would sit better in a skill; worth a separate look.

Pack READMEs take the two new rule rows (`macos`, `research-project`) and recounted word columns where a dropped preamble had been counted into a rule. Every touched pack bumps its version with a `VERSIONS.md` row.

Suite 3104/3104, `check_the_work` clean, `check_the_world` 0 blocking.

{"number":1667,"title":"Rules → skills: the audit's path-forced extractions; description-triggered ones stay prose","body":"Applies #1662 under the owner's bar (set mid-review): a rule leaves `RULES.md` for a skill only where that skill's `force-load-on-file-edits-paths` covers **every** moment the rule is needed. A skill the model would have to pick by description alone is not predictable, so those rules stay in the prose. The first twelve commits moved everything the audit named; the last commit derives the prose back from `main` for everything that had only a description trigger, leaving the fourteen path-forced skills.

**What stays extracted** (all forced by the guard for the files named):

| Pack | Skill | Forced for |
|---|---|---|
| basics | `writing-repo-scanning-checks` | `**/engine/checks/**`, `**/packs/*/worldRules/**`, `**/packs/*/workRules/**`, `**/packs/*/skills/*/checks.mjs`, `**/declared-checks.json` |
| basics | `working-with-generated-files` | `**/*GENERATED*` |
| executable-requirements | `write-a-requirement-leaf`, `write-a-saga`, `deterministic-expecteds` | `dev/requirements/requirements.md`, `dev/requirements/saga/**`, `dev/requirements/**/cases/**` + `shared/**` |
| firebase | `firestore-security-rules`, `firebase-functions`; `create-release-plan` gains `.firebaserc`, `firebase.json` | `**/firestore.rules`, `**/storage.rules`; `functions/**` |
| aws-sam | `sam-template`, `sam-build-and-deps` | `**/template.yaml`, `**/template.yml`; `package.json` + template |
| flutter | `flutter-golden-tests`, `flutter-pubspec` | `**/*_test.dart`, `**/test/**/*.dart`; `**/pubspec.yaml`, `**/pubspec.lock` |
| macos | `macos-app-bundle` (the two plist keys), `macos-entitlements-and-tcc` | `**/Info.plist`, `**/Package.swift`; `**/*.entitlements`, `**/Info.plist` |
| chrome-extension | `extension-host-permissions` | `**/manifest.json` |
| claudinite-fleet-sheepdog | `configuring-the-fleet` | `.claudinite-settings.json` |
| node | `node-test-discovery` | `.github/workflows/**`, `package.json`, `*/package.json` |
| python | `python-optional-deps` gains the extra-declaration rule | `pyproject.toml`, `setup.cfg`, `setup.py` (root or one down) |
| static-website | `static-site-releases` gains the managed-copies rule | its existing `.github/site.config`, `static-site-*` workflows |

Rules whose moment no file edit predicts stayed in or returned to `RULES.md` even where a sibling rule was forced: the bundle build-script rules and the Hardened-Runtime flag (macos), pixel-golden capture code (headless-browser), content-script module loading (chrome-extension), the port-boundary design (flutter), the `# noqa: F401` probe (python), "the version moves with the change" (static-website), the deploy-time SAM failures.

**Also kept from the audit's flagged list**: the four stubs (ios, android, app-store-release, play-store-release) lose their `RULES.md`, the stub note now in a README each; describe-only prose moved to READMEs (executable-requirements' line regex and gate inventory, spec-driven-product's gallery pointer, flutter's web-sandbox SDK note, web-scraping's cache/raw-record rationale, macos' notarized-build line).

**Also in this PR**: `packs/claudinite-growth` had two `VERSIONS.md` rows claiming 60903.5 on `main`, which `pack-version-claimed-once` blocks on every tree; the second row takes 60903.6 and the manifest follows.

**Verification**: full suite `node --test $(git ls-files '*.test.mjs')` — 3187 pass, 1 fail (`engine-pack-lane-shims`, which refuses to run on this shallow clone; not this change). `check_the_world` and `check_the_work` are clean. Every touched pack README's rule table was reconciled 1:1 against its `RULES.md`; the skills index and pack directory were regenerated.

{"number":1565,"title":"Align shared packs' rules and skills to the references convention","body":"Closes #1564

Migrates the shared canon packs onto the `writing-pack-prose` references convention (#1560), per its own migration procedure: shrink-only on the prose side, evidence recovered from what the prose already recorded, nothing invented.

## What moved

Six packs gain a `references.md` and bump their version:

- **basics** — `verify-in-production` sheds its six inline incident narratives (#1121, #1460, the five executor-batch parks, the cross-repo scope-denial parks, the hand-set label incidents #1220/#1265, and #1160's stale-retry), `do-later` its #1160 citation, `writing-tests` its three worked-example parentheticals (#429, #310, the hostname-apex case) — each rule keeps its act-time consequence and ends with a bare `(n)` marker; the evidence lives in the entries. A `check:` entry covers `declared-check-spec-keys` (#1400's fleet-lane trade).
- **claudinite-growth** — `unattended-agents`' three worked-example parentheticals, `writing-tasks`' design-doc pointer (#394), and `writing-pack-prose`'s own fenced-command measurement move to entries; a `check:` entry covers `task-md-only-when-agentic` (#1055).
- **claudinite-canon-curation** — both skills' #385 citations move to entries; a `check:` entry covers `pack-version-claimed-once` (#1482).
- **claudinite-lifecycle** — `adopt-claudinite`'s #1167 citation moves to an entry; `check:` entries cover `conformance-work-scope` (#939) and `rules-index-current` (#807).
- **aws-sam**, **chrome-extension** — `references.md` only, covering `handler-path` (#136, reaffirmable against esbuild's `outbase` documentation) and `declarative-content-set-icon` (#777, reaffirmable against a current Chrome).

## What deliberately did not move

- The technology packs' inline failure modes (macos, headless-browser, static-website, firebase, flutter, node, web-speech, web-scraping, html, leaflet) are **act-time consequence clauses** the convention keeps inline — examined, left unmarked. - Checks guarding repo-internal structure get no `check:` entries: the tree settles them, and `rule-revalidation` scopes them out. Covered checks are the ones whose premise could lapse (platform behaviour, incident-born workarounds).

- `references-integrity` run against the real tree: 0 findings, and proven to bite on a deliberately dangling `(99)` marker before restoring.

{"number":1634,"title":"Every pack's RULES.md carries rules, not a description of the pack","body":"Closes #1632

The same audit #1625 got, across the other 25 packs. Every one opened its `RULES.md` with a paragraph describing what the pack covers ("Portable, project-agnostic practices for …", "This document defines how the owner wants … run"), and several framed their sections the same way. It changes nothing a session does, every session in every declaring repo pays for it, and each pack's `README.md` plus its manifest's `ruleRoutingGuidance` (what renders into `directory.GENERATED.md`) already carries it — I checked each one before dropping it.

**Dropped:** 25 intro paragraphs; the playbook framing in `research-project` and `spec-driven-product` (what the class is, "a default to adapt, not a contract"); `basics`'s four section preambles, including the skill list the session's own skill roster already carries; `headless-browser`'s scope note; `macos`'s "these are the rules that cost the most to learn" and "Two consequences"; `node`'s "Two that recur".

**Kept as rules, re-keyed:** `macos`'s usage-description paragraph becomes **Reaching for a protected resource**; `research-project`'s interaction-cadence paragraph becomes two bullets; `python`'s three section-shaped rules become trigger-keyed bullets at the ration (280 → 150 words).

**Left alone:** the paragraph-form instruction in `executable-requirements` and `research-project` — it is prose-shaped, but it instructs, and rewriting it is a rewrite of substance rather than this sweep. Corpus non-rule prose is 2,900 → 1,080 words, and what remains is nearly all of that kind. Those two, plus `spec-driven-product`, read as manuals whose procedure would sit better in a skill; worth a separate look.

Pack READMEs take the two new rule rows (`macos`, `research-project`) and recounted word columns where a dropped preamble had been counted into a rule. Every touched pack bumps its version with a `VERSIONS.md` row.

Suite 3104/3104, `check_the_work` clean, `check_the_world` 0 blocking.

This pack is the browser itself. Which engine a UI golden should use, the tolerance it may carry,
self-skipping where no browser is present, the re-baselining approval gate, and wiring the run into
a workflow are all deliberately not here — the "zero-diff costs the whole recipe" rule is written to
complement that testing guidance rather than restate or contradict it.

Provenance: distilled from three fleet members that drive a browser from code, independently and
for different reasons. `missingbulb/EdFringeNow` — a pinned-Chromium visual-requirements harness:
fake-origin routing, the font jail, rasterisation flags, clip and bounding-box mechanics.
`missingbulb/CrosswordChat` — browser rasterisation for both goldens and generated build
artifacts: environment binary resolution, stripping runtime-dependent scripts.
`missingbulb/ClaudiniteWebsite` — an interactive responsive check: the window-size-is-not-a-
viewport footgun and the virtual-time budget. The first two solved the cross-machine rendering
problem two different ways, which is what the pinning rules carry.
`missingbulb/EdFringeAllocator` holds a vestigial fourth instance in a retired prototype.

1	// The headless-browser pack: driving a real browser from your own process —
2	// resolving and pinning the build, replacing everything about the page's world
3	// that would otherwise vary, and the capture mechanics. Prose only, and
4	// deliberately so: every rule here is a RUNTIME browser behaviour (a secure
5	// origin gating geolocation, font fallback deciding layout, a scroll dismissing
6	// a hover state) or an authoring judgment about a harness's shape. Neither has a
7	// repo-state signature a check could read without asserting that some particular
8	// call still exists, which pins a point in time rather than a rule.
9	//
10	// Fingerprinted by an actual driver reference in JS/TS source — the module
11	// specifier of a browser-automation package, or a `.launch(` call site — so a
12	// repo that drives a browser from a globally-installed driver (no dependency
13	// entry anywhere) is still recognised. The marker only *suspects* the pack;
14	// declaring it is the project's call, like every pack.
15	
16	const DRIVER_MODULE = /['"](playwright(?:-core)?|puppeteer(?:-core)?)['"]/;
17	const LAUNCH_CALL = /\b(?:chromium|firefox|webkit|puppeteer)\.launch\s*\(/;
18	const SOURCE = /\.(mjs|cjs|js|jsx|ts|tsx)$/;
19	
20	export default {
21	  version: '60920.1',
22	  minEngineVersion: '60822.1',
23	  ruleRoutingGuidance: {
24	    belongs:
25	      'driving a real browser from code — resolving and pinning the build, faking the page world, capture mechanics',
26	    excludes:
27	      'which engine a UI golden needs and its review gate — basics writing-tests; workflow wiring — git-github',
28	  },
29	  marker: 'a browser-automation driver (playwright / puppeteer, or a .launch( call) referenced in JS/TS source',
30	  detect: (ctx) =>
31	    ctx.tracked.some((f) => {
32	      if (!SOURCE.test(f)) return false;
33	      const text = ctx.read(f);
34	      return text !== null && (DRIVER_MODULE.test(text) || LAUNCH_CALL.test(text));
35	    }),
36	};

index 58a0763a..a7a8bbd2 100644
--- a/packs/aws-sam/RULES.md
+++ b/packs/aws-sam/RULES.md
@@ -5,3 +5,13 @@ Portable, project-agnostic gotchas for the AWS Serverless Application Model and
 - **`BuildMethod: esbuild` strips the entry's subdirectory from the Handler path.** With a single entry point in a subdirectory (`EntryPoints: [src/handler.mjs]`), SAM's esbuild builder writes the bundle to `<artifact-root>/handler.js` — esbuild's default `outbase` is the entry's own dir, so the subdirectory is dropped. Set `Handler: handler.handler`, not `src/handler.handler`. `sam build` succeeds either way; the wrong value fails only at first invoke with `Runtime.ImportModuleError: Cannot find module 'src/handler'`.
 - **esbuild must be a regular `dependency`, not a `devDependency`.** SAM's esbuild builder runs a *production-only* `npm install` in its scratch dir, so a `devDependency` esbuild is skipped and the build fails with "Cannot find esbuild." Declare it in `dependencies` (it isn't bundled into the artifact unless the handler imports it), or put it on the runner's `PATH` before `sam build`.
 - **CloudFront won't forward `Authorization` via a *custom* origin-request policy** — a custom `AWS::CloudFront::OriginRequestPolicy` listing `Authorization` is rejected at deploy ("The parameter Headers contains Authorization that is not allowed"). To forward it to the origin while keeping it out of the cache key (so public GETs share one cached entry), attach the **managed** `AllViewerExceptHostHeader` policy (id `b689b0a8-53d0-40ab-baf2-68738e2966ac`) plus a custom cache policy that omits `Authorization`. Cache key and origin forwarding are independent controls — a `CachePolicy` defines the cache key, an `OriginRequestPolicy` defines what reaches the origin — so set them separately to cache public reads yet still deliver `Authorization` for authenticated writes. Use the *ExceptHostHeader* variant specifically: forwarding the viewer `Host` to an API Gateway origin returns 403.
+- **A deploy role must be able to drive the transform and CloudFront, or change-set creation fails with the real reason hidden.** The `Serverless-2016-10-31` transform runs as a macro, so the deploy principal needs `cloudformation:*`, and CloudFront management needs `cloudfront:*`, both at `Resource: "*"` (scope the *data-plane* grants to your stack instead). Under-scoping fails at change-set creation, and `sam deploy` surfaces only `Waiter ChangeSetCreateComplete failed` — the actual `AccessDenied` is visible only in the CloudFormation console's **Change sets** tab. Don't paper over it with `AdministratorAccess`.
+- **A brand-new AWS account can't create a CloudFront distribution until AWS verifies it.** The deploy fails `AccessDenied: Your account must be verified before you can add new CloudFront resources` — an account-level anti-abuse gate, not an IAM or template bug, so it is unfixable in code. Open a Support case to get the account verified, and launch against the origin URL directly meanwhile.
+- **A failed first `CREATE` must be cleaned up before you retry.** A stack left in `ROLLBACK_COMPLETE` (and a SAM managed-bucket stack stuck in `REVIEW_IN_PROGRESS`) can only be *deleted*, never updated — retrying an update errors. And any resource with `DeletionPolicy: Retain` survives the rollback orphaned, so the retry then fails `already exists` until you delete the orphan too.
+- **API Gateway HTTP API (v2) rejects a `chrome-extension://` origin in CORS `AllowOrigins`** with `BadRequestException: Invalid format for origin`, accepting only `http(s)://…` or `*`. An API fronted by a browser-extension (or other non-`http`) origin must therefore set `AllowOrigins: ['*']` and rely on its **JWT authorizer**, not CORS, as the security boundary.
+- **A CDN cache hit is served before the request reaches the origin or its authorizer**, so you cannot enforce request auth on a *cacheable* read without edge compute (Lambda@Edge) — and keying the cache per token destroys the hit rate that justified caching. Treat cacheable endpoints as public by design, and protect only uncached (write / per-user) paths at the authorizer.
+- **Prefer a short CloudFront TTL over per-write cache invalidation.** Invalidation is billed per path beyond a small monthly free allowance, so a write-through design that invalidates on every write is a cost trap; a short TTL plus optimistic local rendering hides the propagation delay from the writer at no per-request charge.
+- **Bundle the AWS SDK into the Lambda artifact rather than relying on the managed runtime's copy.** The runtime doesn't ship every SDK sub-package (a missing one fails only at invoke), and its bundled SDK minor version drifts under you over time. Declare and bundle the SDK packages you import, and pin a non-EOL runtime explicitly rather than letting it float.
+- **Review the change set before applying — `Replacement: True` on a stateful resource is a data-loss hard stop.** Replacement creates a *new, empty* resource and the old data does not follow; a DynamoDB table shows it whenever an immutable property (its `KeySchema`/`AttributeDefinitions`) changes. Enable stack **termination protection** too — it's a one-time CLI/API call (`update-termination-protection`), not expressible in the template body.
+- **Adding a DynamoDB GSI does not backfill existing items.** The `UpdateTable` is additive and indexes only items that already carry the index's key attributes, so rows written before the GSI stay invisible to it until each is rewritten with those attributes. Plan an explicit backfill pass if pre-existing data must appear in the new index.
+- **A custom request header turns even a public GET into a preflighted CORS request.** Any non-simple header (e.g. a client-version header) makes the browser send an `OPTIONS` preflight, so the API's CORS `AllowHeaders` must list that header or the real request is blocked *in the browser* — while server-side unit tests that never run the CORS layer stay green. Add each custom header to the allowed-headers list.

293	## PR #623 · 2026-08-01 · scheduler: let a task claim the run, and have baselining claim it when the mount is overdue
294	- by @missingbulb · model Claude · refs #624 · pack version 1
295	- github-actions-scheduling (reworded), spacing-jobs-apart (born)
296	
297	> The daily anchors stage the nightly chain an hour apart — 02:00 baselining,
298	> 03:00 extract, 04:00 promote — so a repo's mount is converged before anything
299	> reads it. That staging holds only while the cron fires land roughly on time,
300	> and a GitHub `schedule:` fire is dropped and delayed freely. A run that fires
301	> hours late finds every daily slot due at once and dispatches the whole chain
302	> together, so baselining runs BESIDE the tasks whose ground it exists to repair
303	> rather than before them.
304	>
305	> A precondition may now return `exclusive: true` beside `run: true` — "if I run
306	> this cycle, I run alone" — and planRun defers every other due task: no
307	> preprocessing subprocess, no dispatch issue, no inline work. The engine learns
308	> "this verdict claims the run", never which task claims it or why, the same
309	> separation FORCE_TASKS keeps. A forced task is exempt from deferral and cannot
310	> claim, so a hand-started run still does what it was started for.
311	>
312	> Baselining claims the run when the stamp says the mount has not been converged
313	> for more than a day, and stops claiming past three days: days-stale is an
314	> unmerged maintenance PR or a broken converge, which is a human's problem, and
315	> holding every other task back another night does not fix it.
316	>
317	> A deferred slot is spent, not queued — the run succeeds, so the watermark moves
318	> past it and the task runs at its next slot. The run says so in its summary
319	> (`defer —`) and its run record (`deferred`), so the cost is counted, not silent.

## PR #1822 · 2026-09-06 · Give the three canon-curation PR tasks an automerge policy
- by @missingbulb · model Claude Opus 5 · refs #1317, #1821 · pack version 60906.3
- growth-discover-packs (reworded), growth-promote (reworded)

> * Give the three canon-curation PR tasks an automerge policy
>
> growth-discover-packs, growth-promote and upstream-watch were the only
> PR-producing tasks on the shelf with no automerge policy, so every PR they
> opened parked for approval by construction.
>
> Each one's description says its PR is reviewed, owner-gated or owner-approved,
> so the policies are narrow: a policy is "merge if the diff is exactly this
> shape", never "merge". Minting a pack is additive under packs/<new>/ plus the
> two catalog files, so anything that modifies an existing pack's code parks;
> promotion and the upstream sweep write canon prose, so a promotion that also
> ships a blocking check parks for the reader it wants.
>
> Each policy was measured against these tasks' own real pull requests with
> merge-policy.mjs rather than predicted.
>
> That measurement also found what actually parks growth-promote: its task.md

> * A task can decline while one of its own pull requests is open

> fixed path — the two its sibling pending-round terms rest on — can still refuse
> to stack a second round on an unreviewed one. It is the complement of
> `fresh_pr`, which leaves an earlier round open.
>
> The prefix moves to contract/task-branch.mjs, since the gate asks the question
> before the executor has minted anything and neither side may spell it twice, and
> the open-PR signal carries the head ref the listing already returned.
>
> * Four canon tasks change what they do to their pull requests
>
> ci-performance opens a fresh pull request and does not run at all while one of
> its own is still open: a performance fix is argued from an A/B that run measured,
> so a second round cannot be folded into the first one's review.
>
> growth-discover-packs opens a fresh one too — each run authors a different pack
> for a different gap, so folding two into one review puts two unrelated packs in
> front of the owner.
>
> pack-version-history and claudinite-lifecycle/update supersede theirs. Both
> recompute the whole answer from the base, so the round under review holds
> nothing the next one does not, and a green round nobody merged is landed rather
> than closed.
>
> * upstream-watch becomes revalidate-from-source, and supersedes
>
> The task is named for what it does to the shelf — revalidate each pack against
> the sources it declared — rather than for watching something upstream. A month
> whose pull request nobody reviewed is retired by the next month's, which
> recomputes the same answer from the sources and the anchors on the base.
>
> Every live reference follows the name; the VERSIONS rows and the dashboard mock
> keep the old one, being records of what happened.
>
> * ci-performance waits on its own parked run, not on its open PR
>
> The gate is the previous run's state, not the artifact it left: `last-run-not-parked`
> holds a task back while its newest run stands at any of the four parks, where
> `last-run-not-failed` reads only the failure one. An unmerged pull request parks
> on approval, which is not a fault, so the narrower term would let the task stack
> a second round behind an unanswered one.
>
> It reads the park kind the runs bundle already carries, so the branch-family
> recognition goes: no signal field, no taskId through the evaluator, no shared
> prefix module.
>
> `holdsOnFailure` answers true for either term, a task holding behind every park
> holding behind that one too, and the dashboard takes `holdsOnAnyPark` beside it —
> without it a lane parked on approval renders its next calendar anchor while the
> task declines every week.

```entry _pack
## 2026-07-06 - born - Context-relief architecture: packs (prose + checks) and skills, with enforcement (#128)
- **Reason:** the AWS Serverless Application Model and the API-Gateway/CloudFront stack it deploys
  hit the same gotchas in every project read cold, and the context-relief architecture gave that
  body of knowledge a home active only where it applies. The pack's gotchas split between
  structural checks, where a template or package manifest carries a false-positive-free signature,
  and prose for the rest.
```

```entry esbuild-must-be
## 2026-07-06 - born - Context-relief architecture: packs (prose + checks) and skills, with enforcement (#128)
- **Reason:** SAM's esbuild builder runs a production-only `npm install` in its scratch directory,
  so a `devDependency` esbuild is skipped and the build fails with "Cannot find esbuild". Declaring
  esbuild in `dependencies` does not bloat the deployed artifact - it is not bundled unless the
  handler imports it - so the usual objection to the remedy, shipping a build tool to production,
  does not apply.
- **Mechanism:** a RULES.md rule, beside the check that carries its mechanical half.
- **Retire when:** reaffirm against SAM's esbuild builder; retire if it stops running a
  production-only install.
```

```entry cloudfront-wont-forward
## 2026-07-06 - born - Context-relief architecture: packs (prose + checks) and skills, with enforcement (#128)
- **Reason:** a custom `AWS::CloudFront::OriginRequestPolicy` listing `Authorization` is rejected at
  deploy. Cache key and origin forwarding are independent controls - a `CachePolicy` defines the
  cache key, an `OriginRequestPolicy` defines what reaches the origin - which is why the two are
  set separately to cache public GETs on one entry while still delivering `Authorization` for
  authenticated writes.
- **Mechanism:** a RULES.md rule.
- **Retire when:** reaffirm against CloudFront's managed-policy list; retire if a custom policy is
  ever allowed to name `Authorization`.
```

```entry _pack
## 2026-07-06 - born - Context-relief architecture: packs (prose + checks) and skills, with enforcement (#128)
- **Reason:** the AWS Serverless Application Model and the API-Gateway/CloudFront stack it deploys
  hit the same gotchas in every project read cold, and the context-relief architecture gave that
  body of knowledge a home active only where it applies. The pack's gotchas split between
  structural checks, where a template or package manifest carries a false-positive-free signature,
  and prose for the rest.
- **Mechanism:** the pack manifest, fingerprinted on a tracked `template.yaml`/`template.yml`, so
  the pack is offered to a repo that deploys with SAM and to no other.
```
```entry esbuild-must-be
## 2026-07-06 - born - Context-relief architecture: packs (prose + checks) and skills, with enforcement (#128)
- **Reason:** SAM's esbuild builder runs a production-only `npm install` in its scratch directory,
  so a `devDependency` esbuild is skipped and the build fails with "Cannot find esbuild". Declaring
  esbuild in `dependencies` does not bloat the deployed artifact - it is not bundled unless the
  handler imports it - so the usual objection to the remedy, shipping a build tool to production,
  does not apply.
- **Mechanism:** a RULES.md rule, beside the check that carries its mechanical half.
- **Retire when:** reaffirm against SAM's esbuild builder; retire if it stops running a
  production-only install.
```
```entry cloudfront-wont-forward
## 2026-07-06 - born - Context-relief architecture: packs (prose + checks) and skills, with enforcement (#128)
- **Reason:** a custom `AWS::CloudFront::OriginRequestPolicy` listing `Authorization` is rejected at
  deploy. Cache key and origin forwarding are independent controls - a `CachePolicy` defines the
  cache key, an `OriginRequestPolicy` defines what reaches the origin - which is why the two are
  set separately to cache public GETs on one entry while still delivering `Authorization` for
  authenticated writes.
- **Mechanism:** a RULES.md rule.
- **Retire when:** reaffirm against CloudFront's managed-policy list; retire if a custom policy is
  ever allowed to name `Authorization`.
```
```entry aws-sam-esbuild-dependency
## 2026-07-06 - born - Context-relief architecture: packs (prose + checks) and skills, with enforcement (#128)
- **Reason:** the rule's failure mode is a build that breaks, so it is blocking; the signature is
  static - `BuildMethod: esbuild` in a tracked template with esbuild in `devDependencies` only.
- **Mechanism:** check aws-sam/esbuild-dependency, blocking, a coded rule with its own `run(ctx)`.
  Scoped to single-package repos: with more than one `package.json` the SAM function may build from
  a different manifest and a root `devDependency` esbuild for other tooling is legitimate, so the
  check skips rather than misfire.
- **Rejected:** firing on any repo with a SAM template - the adversarial pass showed the
  multi-package case as a false positive.
```

```entry aws-sam-handler-path
## 2026-07-06 - born - aws-sam: two YAML-based checks (handler-path, cloudfront-authorization) via a minimal YAML parser (#137)
- **Reason:** esbuild's default `outbase` is the entry point's own directory, so SAM's esbuild
  builder strips a single entry's subdirectory from the artifact and a subdirectory-carrying
  `Handler` fails only at first invoke with `Runtime.ImportModuleError` - `sam build` succeeds
  either way, so nothing before deploy catches it.
- **Mechanism:** check aws-sam/handler-path, blocking, navigating template structure through a
  minimal dependency-free YAML-subset parser rather than grepping text. Skips where `OutBase` is
  set or there is more than one entry point, the two false-positive cases the adversarial pass
  flagged.
- **Rejected:** a text-grep conversion - the first prose-to-checks pass (#131) rejected this gotcha
  as false-positive-prone because a grep cannot read template structure; the parser is what made it
  convertible.
- **Retire when:** reaffirm against esbuild's outbase documentation and SAM's esbuild builder;
  retire only if either changes that default.
```
```entry aws-sam-cloudfront-authorization
## 2026-07-06 - born - aws-sam: two YAML-based checks (handler-path, cloudfront-authorization) via a minimal YAML parser (#137)

- **Mechanism:** check aws-sam/cloudfront-authorization, blocking, reading the template through the
```

    Declared checks are JSON, one file per pack (#827)
    
    * Declared checks: one file per pack, not one file per rule
    
    The 25 pattern-rule declarations from the four conversion rounds were 25
    modules of ~17 lines each, all data. A declaration is a table row, not a
    module: reading a pack's declared surface meant opening five files, the
    shared constants were re-imported per rule, and each manifest carried an
    import line and a list entry per declaration.
    
    Each pack now keeps its declarations in one declared-checks.mjs — a named
    export per rule (so the tests still import one directly), default export
    the array the manifest spreads into its rule list. The three skills inline
    their declarations into the checks.mjs array they already had. Rules with a
    hand-written run(ctx) stay their own modules.
    
    Nothing behavioural moves: `--list` is byte-identical against main (88
    rules), the world sweep finds the same 0 blocking / 28 advisory, and the
    1607-test suite passes with only import lines changed.
    
    Refs #826
    
    * Declared checks are JSON: no comments, no doc pointer, failureMessage
    
    Owner review on #827: the file that holds only declarations should not be
    code. A pack's declarations are now the array in
    packs/<pack>/declared-checks.json (a skill's in its own beside checks.mjs),
    discovered structurally by the pack registry and compiled by the pattern
    engine — no import, no manifest line; writing the declaration adds the check.
    
    The format drops what the declaration was borrowing from prose. No comments
    (JSON cannot hold one, so the no-comments rule is enforced by construction),
    no `description` and no `doc` pointer — a declaration states its own case —
    and `why` is renamed `failureMessage` for what it is: the line the agent
    reads when the check fires. Regexes are strings in /pattern/flags form,
    compiled at load; a path-or-pattern key still reads a plain string as an
    exact path, and a plain string anywhere else is reported with the key that
    got it.
    
    The registry reaches the compiler lazily, only where a declaration file
    exists, so a tree carrying just the pack machinery loads as before. Both
    deliberate cross-tree reaches are accepted with reasons.
    
    Findings are unchanged: the world sweep is finding-for-finding identical to
    main, and `--list` matches on id and severity for all 88 rules (a declared
    rule now prints its failureMessage where a coded rule prints its
    description, and no doc pointer). 1613 tests pass, six of them new — the
    regex-string compilation, the authoring-error message, failureMessage on the
    finding, the loader's cache, and the registry discovering a pack's and a
    skill's declarations — each seen to fail against a mutated engine.
    
    Refs #826
