# Firebase

- **Admin-SDK code bypasses rules** — a rules review must enumerate what *functions* write too;
  "rules allow it" and "the system writes it" are different lists. (admin-sdk-code)

- **Identity comes from the verified token, never the request body** (`request.auth`,
  `token.name`/`picture` claims). (identity-comes-verified)

- **Validate inputs at the boundary like an adversary wrote them**: type-check, range-check
  (`NaN`/`Infinity` slip through naive numeric checks), length-cap, and enum-check before any
  read or write; reject with typed `HttpsError`s (`invalid-argument`, `unauthenticated`,
  `resource-exhausted`) so clients can react specifically. (validate-inputs-boundary)

- **Extract decision logic into pure modules** (audience selection, filtering, formatting) so the
  default suite runs with zero emulators and zero mocks of the Firebase SDK.
  (extract-decision-logic)

- **Cross-language contracts get mirrored test vectors.** When client and server must compute the
  same derived value (a geohash, a normalization), commit identical input→output vectors in both
  suites and diff the literals in CI — "both use the standard algorithm" is not a proof.
  (cross-language-contracts)
=== README ===
# firebase pack

Active when the repo has `firebase.json`. Durable practices for building on Firebase — Firestore
security-rules discipline (merge semantics, server-owned fields, default-deny), callable Cloud
Function patterns (verified-token identity, validation, transactional rate limits, batched
fan-out), testing without live infrastructure (pure-logic extraction, the rules emulator when rules
themselves are under test), and deploy layout (predeploy build hooks, committed project aliases).
Mostly prose — the two mechanical halves of the deploy layout are checks. Earned in
missingbulb/ShoutsAndWhispers (Firestore + Functions + FCM + Google sign-in).

Environment separation and store gating are the release standard, and load only when a project is
planning one: [create-release-plan](skills/create-release-plan/SKILL.md) — two fully separate
dev/prod projects with everything committed pointing at dev, prod config injected by the release
pipeline alone, and App Check attestation so only store-installed builds reach the prod backend.

> **Status: the release standard was decided ahead of first exercise.** Distilled from
> missingbulb/TLDR's worked AWS split and decided for Firebase in missingbulb/ShoutsAndWhispers;
> no project has run a release through it yet. Expect refinement — and conformance checks — when
> the first release exercises it.

## Rules (`RULES.md`)

The five always-on rules — what a session must know whether or not it opens a rules file or a
function:

| Rule | Severity | Reason | Enforcement |
|---|---|---|---|
| Admin-SDK code bypasses rules | critical | correctness | prose: <50 words |
| Identity comes from the verified token | critical | correctness | prose: <20 words |
| Validate inputs at the boundary | critical | correctness | prose: <50 words |
| Extract decision logic into pure modules | medium | complexity | prose: <50 words |
| Cross-language contracts get mirrored test vectors. | high | correctness | prose: <50 words |

The security-rules discipline (default-deny, merge semantics, absent-field guards, server-owned
fields, `request.time` pins, bounded strings, empirical rules tests) is the
[`firestore-security-rules`](skills/firestore-security-rules/SKILL.md) skill, forced for
`**/firestore.rules` and `**/storage.rules`; the function-side limits (transactional rate limits,
batch chunking, best-effort push, the entrypoint smoke-load) are
[`firebase-functions`](skills/firebase-functions/SKILL.md), forced for `functions/**`; and the
deploy layout (a self-contained project root, committed `.firebaserc` aliases) joins
[`create-release-plan`](skills/create-release-plan/SKILL.md), forced for `firebase.json` and
`.firebaserc`.

## Checks

| Check | Severity | Reason | Enforcement |
|---|---|---|---|
| `firebase/functions-node-pin` | high | correctness | check: blocking |
| `firebase/functions-predeploy-build` | high | correctness | check: blocking |

## Skills

| Skill | Trigger |
|---|---|
| [`firestore-security-rules`](skills/firestore-security-rules/SKILL.md) | any edit of `firestore.rules` or `storage.rules` — held by the guard until loaded |
| [`firebase-functions`](skills/firebase-functions/SKILL.md) | any edit under `functions/` — held by the guard until loaded |
| [`create-release-plan`](skills/create-release-plan/SKILL.md) | planning a release, splitting dev/prod, wiring prod config or App Check; any edit of `firebase.json` or `.firebaserc` — held by the guard until loaded |
=== PACK ===
// Technology pack: building on Firebase (Auth, Firestore, Cloud Functions,
// FCM) — schema/rules discipline, function patterns, testing without live
// infrastructure, and deploy layout. Fingerprint: firebase.json — the config
// every Firebase repo carries — at the repo root OR one directory down (a
// monorepo's firebase/ project root), but never deeper, so a firebase.json in
// a nested fixture/example tree can't trip detection. A Firebase project root
// is the directory that holds firebase.json, not necessarily the repo root.

const hasMarkerNearRoot = (ctx, marker) =>
  ctx.tracked.some((f) => {
    const parts = f.split('/');
    return parts[parts.length - 1] === marker && parts.length <= 2;
  });

// The release standard (skills/create-release-plan) — the dev/prod project split,
// pipeline-injected prod config and App Check gating — is a skill rather than
// prose: it is read when a project plans its release, not on every session.
export default {
  version: '60920.1',
  minEngineVersion: '60822.1',
  ruleRoutingGuidance: {
    belongs: 'building on Firebase: Firestore rules, callable Cloud Function patterns, FCM, emulator testing, deploy layout, dev/prod release split',
    excludes: 'app store submission and its store-side registration — play-store-release, app-store-release',
  },
  marker: 'firebase.json (at the repo root or one directory down)',
  detect: (ctx) => hasMarkerNearRoot(ctx, 'firebase.json'),
  // The deploy-layout guards. Both are relevance-first: inert
  // until the repo carries a firebase.json declaring a functions codebase whose
  // package.json is in this checkout — so a rules-only or hosting-only Firebase
  // repo never hears from them.
  // firebase/functions-node-pin is a declared check, discovered structurally
  // beside this manifest.
};

{"number":128,"title":"Context-relief architecture: packs (prose + checks) and skills, with enforcement","body":"## What this is

Reorganizes the corpus from always/soft-loaded instructions into **two homes selected by *when* a rule is active**, plus a deterministic enforcement engine:

- **`packs/<name>/`** — a bundle of prose (`RULES.md`) *and* checks, active **once per session** by the project's `.claudinite-checks.json` declaration (`universal` always on). Active packs' prose is injected by a SessionStart hook; their checks run at every Stop and in CI. A dependency-free registry discovers packs by directory scan — no list to maintain.
- **`skills/<name>/`** — activity-scoped procedures the harness surfaces on demand; content inlined in each `SKILL.md` (no cross-tree redirect).
- **`checks/`** — the engine only: the runner, lib, the Stop hook, the PreToolUse guard, and their red-first fixtures.

`always/`, `tasks/`, `technologies/`, and `templates/` are gone — folded into the two homes.

## The model (design in `checks/DESIGN.md`)

- **Promotion ladder**: platform setting → hook → check → skill → prose. A rule lives in the cheapest mechanism that can carry it; prose is the audited fallback.
- **Checks** are declared+closed (every rule of a declared pack runs every time), drift-guarded by a structural fingerprint meta-check; diff-scoped only as a transitional aid (whole-repo sweep is the default); reasoned acceptances; fail-fast severity (advisory is a per-rule *kind*, not a burn-in stage).
- **Platform settings are verified, never trusted** — an offline effect check (squash-only ⇒ no merge commits in main's first-parent history) plus a config check later.
- **Technology gotchas convert per-gotcha** by whether they have a static artifact signature; the rest is pack prose.
- **Skills**: model-invoked routing is probabilistic, so nothing that *must* happen rides on a skill — enforcement is checks/hooks/settings. (Skill-scoped hooks exist, verified, for the rare activity-scoped enforcement need.)
- **Growth is checks-first**: promote descends the ladder for each new lesson; a `prose-to-checks` skill sweeps the existing prose backlog for always-testable rules the conversion missed.

## Implemented (all green: 42 tests, CI passing, sweep clean)

- Runner + registry; **universal pack** (7 checks) + **github-actions** (6) + **chrome-extension** conformance (6); the pack-prose SessionStart loader; the Stop hook and PreToolUse guard.
- Full pack prose (baseline, technology packs, the chrome-extension release standard, the research-project class pack); 12 inlined skills (command + practice) + the prose-to-checks skill.
- Bootstrap Parts 6–7 (hooks, `--init`, skill symlinks); index, README, DESIGN, growth docs all updated to the two-home model.

## The checks earned their keep repeatedly

They caught real defects at every stage — dangling links and a label/href mismatch on `main`; **nine historical merge commits** that had bypassed the squash-only policy unnoticed (now sha-keyed acceptances); real pipefail defects in the canon release workflows; and several of my own regressions mid-restructure (the Stop hook blocked me in-session more than once).

**Owner action outstanding:** flip the squash-only merge *setting* (repo Settings → General) — unreachable from here; the effect check covers the gap meanwhile.

Closes #127
Closes #131

{"number":158,"title":"github-actions: check that a Pages artifact prunes tooling symlinks","body":"## Lesson from an EdFringeNow session, shipped as an enforced check

Bootstrap commits `.claude/skills/*` as symlinks into the gitignored `.claudinite/` corpus (empty in CI — the sync hook never runs there). On a fresh runner checkout they dangle, and `actions/upload-pages-artifact`'s `tar --dereference` **fails** on them, silently blocking every GitHub Pages deploy. In EdFringeNow this broke the live-site deploy from the moment Claudinite was bootstrapped and stayed red for days until an unrelated merge resurfaced it.

**No prose — the check carries it** (per the promotion ladder: a check beats a doc note). It fails if the prune is missed, so there's nothing to document.

## Changes

- **`packs/github-actions/pages-artifact-symlinks.mjs`** — new **`gha/pages-artifact-symlinks`** check (blocking). Fires only when all of: the repo mounts skills as symlinks (`.claude/skills/*` tracked, `.claudinite/skills/*` not), a workflow uploads the repo root (`path: .`) to `actions/upload-pages-artifact`, and there's no prune step before it. Silent once `rm -rf .claude .claudinite` is present or a dedicated build dir is uploaded. Wired into `pack.mjs`.
- **`packs/github-actions/README.md`** — added to the hardcoded check catalog.
- **`checks/test/github-actions.test.mjs`** — four cases (breaks / pruned / build-dir / no-symlinks). See-it-fail verified against a neutered rule.

## Verification

`node --test checks/test/*.test.mjs` → **65/65**. `node checks/run.mjs` (self-conformance) → exit 0, no findings.

{"number":242,"title":"Stage 1 spec: code planner for the fleet daily maintenance routine","body":"Spec-only PR (no implementation code yet) — the reviewable Stage 1 design before we build. Closes the design half of #241.

## What this adds

`routines/fleet/DESIGN.md` — the agreed design for turning the daily maintenance routine from "fan an agent out to every task × every repo, decide in-session" into **code decides, agents act**:

- **Task registry of `(gate, worker)` pairs.** `gate` = "should I run" (code, in the planner); `worker` = "what to do" (a doc a subagent runs, fed the gate's `targets`). Pack tasks register via a new **`maintenance: [...]`** field on `pack.mjs`, exactly like `rules`/`skills`/`env` — so a task is `scope: "fleet"` or `scope: "pack:<name>"` and the engine discovers it with no orchestrator edit.
- **The planner runs in code**, in the existing fleet-coverage Action (fleet PAT). The **entire worklist is computed before any worker agent spawns** — a task with nothing to do costs an API read, not a model turn.
- **Orchestrator = the routine session itself** (trigger + dispatch in one run). The planner is the only out-of-process piece; worker subagents are its children.
- **Stateless daily loop** (~25h UTC window) + **weekly full sweep** staggered by `hash(full_name) % 7 == UTC weekday` — ~1/7 of the fleet full-sweeps each night, and that weekly pass is the self-healing safety net (no persisted watermark).
- **Correctness invariants** baked in: landed/implemented tests key off a `mainMoved` signal (not per-object recency), and `canonChanged` excludes the plan/tracker/orchestration artifacts so the engine can't self-trigger dedup.
- **One fleet walk, three outputs** — coverage census + migration-retirement (both existing) + the new work plan. Stage 1 extends `check-fleet-coverage.mjs` in place (it's central-only; a rename would force a canon-wide reference sweep) and factors gates/signals into `routines/fleet/` modules.
- **Proves the pack seam** with `chrome-store-release` as the first real pack task.

## Blast radius

Small: the planner and every gate run **centrally** in the home repo's Action. No consumer executes new code; a member contributes only its existing `.claudinite-checks.json` (read, never written).

## Not in this PR

Implementation (`signals.mjs`, `gates.mjs`, `tasks/`, the pack task, the orchestrator rewrite) — that follows once the spec is approved. Stage 2 (narrow per-object worker skills) is deferred.

## Coordination note

There are related in-flight branches (`claude/chrome-store-release-schedule-*`, `claude/open-branches-status-*`) that overlap this area by name. Neither is merged, and neither appears to have created a fleet-maintenance seam, but worth a glance before implementation to avoid duplicated effort.

Refs #241

---
name: firestore-security-rules
description: Writing and testing Firestore and Storage security rules — default-deny, merge semantics, absent-field guards, server-owned fields, request.time pins, bounded strings, empirical rules tests. Use when editing firestore.rules or storage.rules, or reviewing what a ruleset allows.
metadata:
  body: guidelines
  force-load-on-file-edits-paths:
    - "**/firestore.rules"
    - "**/storage.rules"
---

# Firestore security rules

## Merge-aware and default-deny

- **End every ruleset with an explicit catch-all deny** and grant per collection; a collection
  nobody thought about must be unreachable, not accidentally open. (end-ruleset-explicit)

- **Write rules against merge semantics, not just creates.** Clients using `set(merge: true)`
  surface the **post-merge** document in `request.resource.data` — a key-presence check that is
  right for `create` silently breaks on `update`. For updates, validate
  `request.resource.data.diff(resource.data).affectedKeys()` (what the client actually touched);
  for creates, validate `keys()`. (write-rules-against)

- **Guard every field dereference for absence.** Distinct writers legitimately upsert disjoint
  field subsets of one doc; an unguarded `d.field` on a missing key throws and denies. Pattern:
  `!('field' in d) || <validation>`. (guard-field-dereference)

- **Server-owned fields are absent from the client-allowed key list**, not "checked for equality"
  — with `diff().affectedKeys().hasOnly([...])` a client physically cannot touch them (rate-limit
  stamps, server-computed aggregates). (server-owned-fields)

- **Pin client timestamps to `request.time`** (`FieldValue.serverTimestamp()` satisfies it) on any
  write whose freshness matters — but scope the pin to
  writes that touch those fields, or unrelated single-field merges get rejected.
  (pin-client-timestamps)

- **Bound every client-writable string/blob** (length caps in rules); an unbounded field is a
  free storage channel. (bound-client-writable)

## Test rules empirically

- **When rules themselves are under test, test them empirically** with
  `@firebase/rules-unit-testing` against the real emulator — simulate each *exact client write
  shape* the app performs (create vs merge-update vs single-field token write) plus each
  forbidden shape. (rules-themselves-test)
=== FUNCTIONS ===
---
name: firebase-functions
description: Writing Cloud Functions for Firebase — transactional rate limits, batched-write chunking and at-least-once fan-out, best-effort push with dead-token cleanup, smoke-loading the built entrypoint. Use when editing anything under functions/.
metadata:
  body: guidelines
  force-load-on-file-edits-paths:
    - "functions/**"
---

# Cloud Functions

## Limits and fan-out

- **Rate limits need a transaction.** A read-check-write cooldown is bypassable by firing calls
  concurrently; run the read + check + stamp inside `runTransaction` so concurrent invocations
  serialize. A thrown `HttpsError` inside the transaction aborts it and propagates unchanged.
  (rate-limits-need)

- **Chunk batched writes well under the 500-op limit** and treat multi-batch fan-out as
  at-least-once: a mid-sequence crash plus client retry duplicates the early batches. Document
  the idempotency-key escape hatch even if v1 doesn't implement it. (chunk-batched-writes)

- **Push is best-effort by construction**: notification failures must never fail the triggering
  call; clean up dead tokens on the *actual* error codes
  (`messaging/registration-token-not-registered` — verify codes against the installed
  firebase-admin, not memory or old blog posts). (push-best-effort)

## The built entrypoint

- **Smoke-load the built entrypoint in the test lane** (`node -e "require('./lib/index.js')"`).
  A Node-major skew between build and runtime, or a bad build, surfaces as a module crash the
  first time the deployed function is invoked. (smoke-load-built)

{"number":790,"title":"Declarative pattern-check engine: one shared pass, checks declared as data","body":"Closes #789.

## What

A rule whose whole logic is "these patterns over these files" is now **declared as data** instead of hand-coded. `patternRule(spec)` (new `engine/checks/helpers/pattern-rules.mjs`) compiles a comment-free spec — file scope, relevance gates, and patterns with their failure text — into an ordinary `{ id, severity, description, doc, why, run(ctx) }` rule module, so the runner, `--list`, per-rule overrides, and acceptances all keep working untouched.

## The engine is built for many checks at once

Per the goal of this change, the engine does **one pass over the tree** for the whole rule family, instead of each rule looping every file:

- every registered pattern rule subscribes to the files its scope matches; each file is **read once** and its **lines are split and walked once**, with all subscribing rules' assertions evaluated during that single visit (per line, a rule's first matching assertion wins);
- results are cached per context (`WeakMap`), so the first pattern rule the runner reaches pays for the family and the rest are lookups;
- the `repoHas` gate is evaluated lazily — only when a rule actually produced findings — preserving the original checks' lazy-marker behavior.

Spec vocabulary (documented in the helper's header): `files` (regex or exact path) / `over: 'tracked'` / `exclude`; `gate` (`exists`, `notExists`, `tracked`, `notTracked`, lazy `repoHas`); `line` assertions (`match`, `unlessLine`, file-scoped `when`/`unlessFile`, rule-level `skipLines`); `file` assertions (`if`-list + `require`/`forbid`, per-assertion `gate`); `repo` implications (unless some file matches `require`, flag every file satisfying a `flag` group, anchored at the group's first pattern); `missing` and `maxLines` for exact-path rules. `what`/`fix` interpolate `{match}`, `{lines}`, `{limit}`.

## Converted checks (13)

Each keeps its id, severity, doc, why, and message text verbatim; declarations carry no comments — the pattern plus its `what`/`fix` is the whole check.

- **github-actions**: `gha/label-create-before-add`, `gha/scheduled-failure-escalation`, `gha/unique-automation-branch`, `gha/no-scheduled-fleet-executor`, `gha/pages-artifact-symlinks`
- **chrome-extension-release**: `cer/template-tokens`, `cer/readme-sections`
- **basics**: `claude-md-length`
- **web-speech skill**: `web-speech-recognition-feature-detected`, `web-speech-capture-released-on-pagehide`
- **google-identity skill**: `google-token-audience-pinned`, `google-token-email-verified`
- **unattended-agents skill**: `in-session-github-access`

The workflow-file pattern the five github-actions rules share is now a single exported constant (`WORKFLOW_FILE` in `github-workflows.mjs`), with `workflowFiles()` derived from it.

Not converted (stay as code, by design): parser-dependent checks (`run-pipefail`, `secrets-in-job-if`, `checkout-submodules`, the chrome-extension pair, `leaflet/asset-integrity`), structured-data checks, git/diff/conversation-scoped checks, and `scheduler-workflow-shape`/`task-declaration-shape` (cron math, enum references).

## Behavior notes

Two tiny, deliberate deltas, both tightenings:

- `google-token-email-verified`: the repo-level Google-marker scan now honors the rule's `exclude`, so a marker appearing **only in a test file** no longer arms the gate (it previously excluded only the skill's own fixtures).
- `web-speech-recognition-feature-detected`: the "file already knows the unprefixed name" test is now a plain `\bSpeechRecognition` word-boundary match instead of strip-then-match — equivalent on real code (`\b` never matches inside `webkitSpeechRecognition`).

## Testing

- New `engine-tests/pattern-rules.test.mjs` (12 tests) proves the engine contract: gates, line/file/repo assertions, templating, `over: tracked` vs scanned, exclude, the one-read-per-file pass (asserted by counting reads), and per-context cache freshness. See-it-fail: two engine mutations (dropping `unlessLine`, disabling the `repoHas` filter) each made the suite go red before restoring.
- All **1031** existing tests pass unchanged — including every pack test that pins the 13 converted checks' findings, counts, lines, and messages.
- `check_the_world` on this repo reports findings identical to the pre-change baseline (0 blocking, same 9 pre-existing advisories).

commit c5fbdc1ec7c1674346579b86e6f8c3d39585c0bb
Author: missingbulb <73882448+missingbulb@users.noreply.github.com>
Date:   Tue Sep 1 01:06:15 2026 +0300

    Promote canon curation into a canon pack (#1541)
    
    * Promote canon curation into a canon pack
    
    The canon home's curation duties move from `.claudinite/local/packs/canon-curation/`
    to `packs/claudinite-canon-curation/`, generalized so any repo hosting a shelf of
    packs can declare them. Hidden and never seeded — a canon home is a role somebody
    assigns, so the pack is declared by hand.
    
    What generalizing took: promote's write surface is the `packs/` shelf plus whatever
    the new optional `write_paths` config adds, rather than a hardcoded `packs/` +
    `skills/` (this tree has no top-level `skills/`, so half that pattern matched
    nothing); the skill check is anchored on a pack tree instead of gating on the
    engine's own tracked registry, which only the engine's home satisfies;
    `pack-version-bumped` points at the pack README rather than a `docs/` path outside
    the vendor set; and the prose speaks of a canon rather than this one.
    
    `growth-scope-gate.mjs` was home CI wiring for another pack's rule, not curation —
    it moves to the `claudinite` local pack, and promote's gate gains the same shim
    shape so the pack owns the rule and the home owns the invocation.
    
    A `canon-home` rehearsal fixture is the consumer-safety answer: a second canon,
    declaring this pack over a shelf of its own, converging green.
    
    Refs #1537
    
    * Stop growth describing another pack's gate; drop the rename entry
    
    Three corrections to the promotion.
    
    The rename map keeps SHARED pack renames only: `canon-curation` was a local pack
    id, one repo's business, and no other repo can be stranded by it. The in-flight
    work items it was added for are all parked for a human, awaiting their own PR —
    none is pending execution, so nothing was decoding that path anyway.
    
    claudinite-growth's mentions of the promote stage's gate were wrong to exist,
    not wrong in their wording: where promote writes, which module certifies it, and
    which repo invokes it are that stage's details, and re-spelling them here only
    gave them somewhere else to drift. All five come out.
    
    extending.md states the core/pack boundary, so which pack contributes the
    pack-independence barrier is content the doc has no business naming; the
    mechanism — barrier data, not checking code — is what it keeps.
    
    Refs #1537
    
    * Pack authoring is the canon's call, so the method moves to curation
    
    generate-project-instructions decides whether a project's insight becomes a pack
    every repo can declare. That is a fleet-wide call, and it was shipping to every
    member that declares claudinite-growth — so a repo could read a method for
    extracting a canon pack out of itself. It moves to claudinite-canon-curation,
    beside the two stages that actually apply it.
    
    The move makes parts of its text false, so those change with it: the trigger no
    longer fires on a member's bootstrap, step 5 states the residue the canon leaves
    behind rather than instructing a session to go author it, and step 6 drops the
    member-session delivery clauses for one that says to write nothing in the project.
    
    prose-to-checks pointed at it for "the full rule" and now states what it needs;
    packs/README.md said a project adopts the local-pack structure by running the
    skill, which it does not — adoption seeds it.
    
    Refs #1537

{"number":384,"title":"Vendored-mount surface shrink: engine/ consolidation, skills into packs, no CI stub, minimal CLAUDE.md + .gitignore","body":"Phase-2 continuation (mount/DESIGN — now `engine/mount/DESIGN.md`), driven interactively from the EdFringeNow pilot (missingbulb/EdFringeNow#73). Owner directives from #385, one commit per decision (to be squashed on merge):

1. **mount-skills owns legacy symlinks** so stale mounts retarget instead of shadowing the vendored skills (#383, test red-first).
2. **CI conformance stub retired** — the Stop hook (`check_the_work`) is the whole enforcement surface: it runs the same sweep and blocks before Claude reports done; edits made outside sessions surface at the next session's Stop.
3. **Consumer `.gitignore` contract collapses to the two hook-log lines** — the vendored world writes nothing untracked into `.claudinite/`.
4. **Skills move into their owning packs** — `<pack>/skills/<skill>/` is the one shape (every skill already had exactly one declarer; the two canon-maintainer skills join `canon-curation`'s bundle). The `pack.mjs` `skills` key, the skills union + `extraSkills` in vendoring, and the `skill-ownership` check are gone — ownership is placement. A bundled skill's `checks.mjs` rides its pack's activation uniformly. The adoption-interview machinery lives in the adoption skill, resolved fail-soft by the engine.
5. **The engine consolidates under `engine/`** — `engine/hooks/` (session-start.sh, inject-preferences.sh, pretooluse-guard.mjs), `engine/check_the_world.mjs` (the sweep CLI, was `checks/run.mjs`), `engine/check_the_work.mjs` (the Stop hook, was `stop-hook.mjs`), `engine/checks_helpers/` (was `checks/lib/`), `engine/pack_loader/`, `engine/skill_loader/`, `engine/mount/`. The vendor set contract is now "engine/ wholesale + declared packs + `CLAUDE.md`"; pack-independence's allow list is the single `engine` root. Consumer wiring migrates via the `engine-restructure` note; pre-flip members keep working through forwarding transition shims at the old fetched-tree paths, retired with the note.
6. **Corpus-index `CLAUDE.md` shrinks to near-nothing** (a session's rules arrive injected — no architecture lesson), the maintainer map moving to README.md; the consumer **self-check paragraph is retired** — a consumer's root `CLAUDE.md` is just the `@`-import line.
7. **`--init` seeds only `{ packs, maintenance }`** — no empty `rules`/`accept` boilerplate.

Verified: 490/490 tests green, conformance sweep clean, the session-start orchestrator runs all five steps from the new layout in the canon.

{"number":555,"title":"Pack manifest as the single source: routing guidance, skills, scoped rules","body":"Nothing in the corpus said *where a piece of content belongs*, so when a rule, doc, skill or check could plausibly live in more than one pack the decision defaulted to `basics` — which is exactly how the GitHub Actions cron doctrine landed there in this PR's first commit. Fixing that turned into making the pack manifest state what a pack is, and retiring the places that said it a second time.

## The manifest spec (#559)

[`engine/pack_loader/pack-schema.mjs`](engine/pack_loader/pack-schema.mjs) declares every field a `pack.mjs` may carry, which are required, and each one's constraints. The **loader** validates every manifest against it — canon and consumer local packs alike — so an incomplete declaration is a blocking `config` error at load, the same class as invalid JSON in `.claudinite-checks.json`. A required manifest field is part of the pack contract, not a conformance opinion about a repo's content: a check would have to be declared by a pack, run only when that pack is active, and re-derive the manifest by reading its source text.

- **Reported, not fatal** — the pack still loads and still runs its checks; silently disabling a repo's own rules is a worse failure than the one being reported.
- The vocabulary is **closed**, so a typo (`rule:`, `skill:`) fails loudly instead of being ignored forever.

### `ruleRoutingGuidance` — what belongs here, and what does not

```js
ruleRoutingGuidance: {
  belongs: 'workflow YAML and Actions runner platform behaviour: triggers, secrets, permissions, scheduling, artifacts, reusable workflows and their pitfalls',
  excludes: 'git and GitHub command procedure — git-github; release pipeline content for one product — its release pack',
},
```

Both sides required, each capped at **20 words** — a session-context budget, not a style rule: `inject-pack-prose` emits the set as a **routing table at session start**, one row per pack, for every pack *discovered* (a consumer holds only what it vendored, so that set is already what it can route into). `excludes` names the pack that owns the other side, so the table routes rather than merely refuses; a boundary true of every pack carries no routing information and wastes the row. Filled in for all 27 canon packs and the home's two local packs.

### `worldRules` / `workRules` — a rule's scope is its placement

The single `rules` array splits in two, so which list a rule sits in is what makes it world- or work-scoped. The loader flattens both into the `rules` array the runners walk, stamping each rule's scope from its list. A rule module may still carry `scope` — the `runRule` dispatch seam reads it off the rule object to hand work rules their fluent surface — but the two must agree, or it's a load error.

### `skills` — the bundle, declared

`skills: ['merge-to-main', ...]`, held to the `skills/` tree in **both directions**: an undeclared directory is a skill nothing announces, a declared name with no directory is a manifest that lies. What each skill covers stays in its `SKILL.md` frontmatter rather than being copied.

## Pack READMEs

With skills and scoped rules on the manifest, each pack README's checks table and skills table were a second copy — and had already drifted: `basics/README.md` listed a `skill-ownership` check the pack does not carry and omitted `catalog-completeness` and `comment-classification`. Both tables are stripped from every pack README, and the **five files that were nothing else** are deleted: `github-actions` plus the four stub packs, whose one non-derivable sentence (expected first source) moved into the manifest header comment.

The other 22 stay — provenance, design rationale, scope notes against sibling packs, an index of their `RULES.md` prose, none of it in the manifest. `catalog-completeness` now looks for the pack **directory** in the catalog rather than a README inside it.

## The cron doctrine, rehomed (#556)

Out of `packs/basics/scheduled-tasks.md` and into `packs/github-actions/skills/github-actions-scheduling/` — the pack that owns Actions platform behaviour. GitHub's `schedule:` trigger is a request to queue, not a promise to run: late fires, dropped fires with no failure and nothing in the run ledger, and the 60-day inactivity disable ([Upptime's measurement](https://upptime.js.org/blog/2021/01/22/github-actions-schedule-not-working/)). What follows: never let correctness depend on a firing happening or on when it happened; stay idempotent and self-catching; catch up the most recent slot only; keep off `:00`; say "about hourly, best-effort"; don't debug a late run as a bug before checking whether GitHub fired at all.

`packs/basics/scheduled-tasks.md` is unchanged from `main` — the scheduling doctrine stays put, only the platform truth moved.

## Verification

- **945 tests, 945 pass** across the CI test roots, including 12 new tests for the manifest spec and a corpus-wide assertion that every discovered pack loads clean through it.
- `node engine/checks/check_the_world.mjs` → **0 blocking**, 8 advisory — the same pre-existing `file-placement` advisories in `engine/`, none new.

```entry esbuild-must-be
- **Reason:** SAM's esbuild builder runs a production-only `npm install` in its scratch directory,
  so a `devDependency` esbuild is skipped and the build fails with "Cannot find esbuild". Declaring
  esbuild in `dependencies` does not bloat the deployed artifact - it is not bundled unless the
  handler imports it - so the usual objection to the remedy, shipping a build tool to production,
  does not apply.
```

```entry cloudfront-wont-forward
  at deploy. Cache key and origin forwarding are independent controls - a `CachePolicy` defines the
  cache key, an `OriginRequestPolicy` defines what reaches the origin - which is why the two are
  set separately to cache public GETs on one entry while still delivering `Authorization` for

- **Mechanism:** a RULES.md rule.
```

```entry _pack
- **Reason:** the AWS Serverless Application Model and the API-Gateway/CloudFront stack it deploys
  hit the same gotchas in every project read cold, and the context-relief architecture gave that
  body of knowledge a home active only where it applies. The pack's gotchas split between
```

```entry esbuild-must-be
## 2026-07-06 · born · Context-relief architecture: packs (prose + checks) and skills, with enforcement (#128)
- **Reason:** SAM's esbuild builder runs a production-only `npm install` in its scratch directory,
  so a `devDependency` esbuild is skipped and the build fails with "Cannot find esbuild". Declaring
  esbuild in `dependencies` does not bloat the deployed artifact - it is not bundled unless the
  handler imports it - so the usual objection to the remedy, shipping a build tool to production,
  does not apply.
- **Mechanism:** a RULES.md rule, beside the check that carries its mechanical half.
- **Retire when:** reaffirm against SAM's esbuild builder; retire if it stops running a
  production-only install.
```
```entry cloudfront-wont-forward
## 2026-07-06 · born · Context-relief architecture: packs (prose + checks) and skills, with enforcement (#128)
- **Reason:** a custom `AWS::CloudFront::OriginRequestPolicy` listing `Authorization` is rejected
  at deploy. Cache key and origin forwarding are independent controls - a `CachePolicy` defines the
  cache key, an `OriginRequestPolicy` defines what reaches the origin - which is why the two are
  set separately to cache public GETs on one entry while still delivering `Authorization` for
  authenticated writes.
- **Mechanism:** a RULES.md rule.
- **Retire when:** reaffirm against CloudFront's managed-policy list; retire if a custom policy is
  ever allowed to name `Authorization`.
```
```entry aws-sam-esbuild-dependency
## 2026-07-06 · born · Context-relief architecture: packs (prose + checks) and skills, with enforcement (#128)
- **Reason:** the rule's failure mode is a build that breaks, so it is blocking, and the signature
  is static: `BuildMethod: esbuild` in a tracked template with esbuild in `devDependencies` only.
- **Mechanism:** check aws-sam/esbuild-dependency, blocking, a coded rule with its own `run(ctx)`.
  Scoped to single-package repos: with more than one `package.json` the SAM function may build from
  a different manifest and a root `devDependency` esbuild for other tooling is legitimate, so the
  check skips rather than misfire.
```

```entry aws-sam-handler-path
## 2026-07-06 · born · aws-sam: two YAML-based checks (handler-path, cloudfront-authorization) via a minimal YAML parser (#137)
- **Reason:** esbuild's default `outbase` is the entry point's own directory, so SAM's esbuild
  builder strips a single entry's subdirectory from the artifact and a subdirectory-carrying
  `Handler` fails only at first invoke with `Runtime.ImportModuleError` - `sam build` succeeds
  either way, so nothing before deploy catches it.
- **Mechanism:** check aws-sam/handler-path, blocking, navigating template structure through a
  minimal dependency-free YAML-subset parser rather than grepping text. It skips where `OutBase` is
  set or there is more than one entry point, the two false-positive cases the adversarial pass
  flagged.
- **Rejected:** a text-grep conversion - the first prose-to-checks pass (#131) rejected this gotcha
  as false-positive-prone because a grep cannot read template structure, and the parser is what
  made it convertible.
- **Retire when:** reaffirm against esbuild's outbase documentation and SAM's esbuild builder;
  retire only if either changes that default.
```

{"number":623,"title":"scheduler: let a task claim the run, and have baselining claim it when the mount is overdue","body":"## The problem

The daily anchors stage the nightly chain an hour apart — 02:00 baselining, 03:00 extract, 04:00 promote — so a repo's mount is converged before anything reads it. That hour is a *preference*, not a guarantee: a GitHub `schedule:` fire is dropped and delayed freely, and a run that fires at 05:40 after three dropped fires finds **all four daily slots due at once** and dispatches them together.

So baselining — the pass that converges the mount, the wiring and the migration notes everything else executes against — runs *beside* the tasks whose ground it exists to repair, on exactly the runs where that matters most.

## The change

**The engine (`engine/scheduler/run.mjs`).** A precondition may return `exclusive: true` beside `run: true` — *if I run this cycle, I run alone*. `planRun` now evaluates every due task's verdict first (preconditions are pure and cheap, and a claim is only knowable once they have all spoken), then defers every other running task: no preprocessing subprocess, no dispatch issue, no inline work.

- The engine learns "this verdict claims the run", never which task claims it or why — the same separation `FORCE_TASKS` keeps, and the reason no engine module mentions baselining.
- Two claimants are not a conflict: they both run, everything else defers. No priority order between packs is needed.
- A **forced** task is exempt from deferral and cannot claim. A claim swallowing the task the operator asked for would make a hand-started run do nothing it was started for.
- A deferred task keeps `run: true` and carries a `deferred` reason, so it reads as *work that was wanted and did not happen* rather than as a skip — in the job summary (`defer —`) and in the machine-readable run record (`deferred`, an outcome word that already existed for exactly this meaning).

**The task (`packs/basics/tasks/baselining/task.mjs`).** Baselining claims the run when the stamp says the mount has not been converged for **more than a day**, and stops claiming past **three** days. Both bounds are load-bearing:

- Below a day, the converge did its job and a routine nightly pass has no standing to hold the chain up — and that is the common case, so ordinary nights are unchanged.
- Past three days it is not a missed fire, it is an unmerged maintenance PR or a broken converge. That is a human's problem (the sheepdog freshness sweep reports it), and holding every other task back another night does not fix it — it just stops the repo doing anything at all, silently and indefinitely.

Read off the stamp, so it measures when baselining last **landed** a converge, not when the task last fired — which would call a nightly failure a success.

## The cost, stated plainly

**A deferred slot is spent, not queued.** Due-ness is `slotTime ∈ (lastSuccess, now]` and the claiming run *succeeds*, so the watermark moves past the slot it deferred: a deferred daily task runs at tomorrow's slot, a weekly one next week. The alternative — running the nightly chain against a mount baselining has not yet fixed — is what this change exists to prevent, so the deferral is the accepted trade. Both the run summary and the run record say so, so the cost is counted rather than silent.

## Docs

- `docs/per-project-scheduling/DESIGN.md` §2 carried the claim "the stages couple through *merged* upstream state, **not a barrier**" — amended with an as-built note, and §3 step 4 documents the mechanism.
- `packs/basics/scheduled-tasks.md` gains the author-facing rule: claim sparingly, bound the claim at both ends, and why.
- The `github-actions-scheduling` skill gains the general lesson — *spacing two jobs apart is not an ordering*; when order matters, assert it in the run.

## Verification

- Full unit suite: **1112 passing**, including new coverage for the claim, the deferral, the forced-task exemption, multiple claimants, the opt-in negative (a corpus with no `exclusive` schedules exactly as before), and each of baselining's two bounds.
- `check_the_world`: 0 blocking, 9 advisory — identical to the pre-change baseline on this tree.
- `check_the_work` (which owns the `consumer-safe-change` rule): clean. The change is additive — an omitted `exclusive` is not a claim — and the engine and the task travel together in the whole-set converge, so there is no version skew between the field's writer and its reader.

{"number":827,"title":"Declared checks are JSON, one file per pack","body":"Closes #826.

The four conversion rounds left 25 pattern-rule declarations as 25 modules averaging 17 lines each — all of them data. This makes them data: one JSON file per pack, discovered structurally.

## The format

A pack's declarations are the array in `packs/<pack>/declared-checks.json`; a skill's live in its own `declared-checks.json` beside the `checks.mjs` that still lists its coded rules. The pack registry discovers both the way it discovers packs themselves — **no import, no manifest line: writing the declaration adds the check.**

A declaration carries `id`, `severity`, `failureMessage`, and its assertions with their `what`/`fix`. What it no longer carries:

- **no comments** — JSON cannot hold one, so the no-comments-on-a-check rule is enforced by construction rather than by review;
- **no `description`** — the failure message stands on its own;
- **no `doc` pointer** — a declared check states its own case rather than deferring to prose;
- **`why` → `failureMessage`**, named for what it is: the line the agent reads when the check fires.

Regexes are strings in `/pattern/flags` form, compiled at load. `scanFiles`/`excludeFiles`/`pathExists` still read any other string as an exact repo path; a plain string at a strictly-pattern key is an authoring error, reported with the key that got it and the value it got.

```json
{
  "id": "gha/label-create-before-add",
  "severity": "advisory",
  "failureMessage": "--add-label fails when the label does not exist yet — GitHub will not create it on demand",
  "scanFiles": "/^\\.github\\/workflows\\/[^/]+\\.ya?ml$/",
  "scanTracked": true,
  "checkEachFile": [{
    "whenFileMatches": "/--add-label/",
    "require": "/label create/",
    "what": "uses --add-label with no idempotent `gh label create … || true` beforehand",
    "fix": "create the label idempotently before adding it, so the workflow survives its first run"
  }]
}
```

## What moved

| pack / skill | before | after |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `github-actions` | 5 modules | `declared-checks.json` |
| `chrome-extension-release` | 5 modules | `declared-checks.json` |
| `product-wiki` | 5 modules | `declared-checks.json` |
| `basics` | 3 modules | `declared-checks.json` |
| `aws-sam` | 2 modules | `declared-checks.json` |
| `web-speech-io` | 2 modules | `declared-checks.json` |
| `google-id-token-validation` | 2 modules | `declared-checks.json` |
| `unattended-agents` | 1 module | `declared-checks.json` |

Rules with a hand-written `run(ctx)` are untouched and stay their own modules listed in the manifest — `handler-path`, `privacy-permission-alignment`, `layout`, `routine-structure` and the rest. `product-wiki/lib.mjs` drops the two page-classifier regexes it was exporting only for the checks; the declaration owns them now, with no second copy to drift from.

## Engine

- `patternRule(declaration)` compiles pattern strings and maps `failureMessage` onto the field the finding renderer reads; `loadDeclaredChecks(dir)` reads and caches a directory's declarations, so the registry and a test share one compiled set rather than each re-parsing.
- The registry appends a pack's declarations to its world rules and a skill's to its skill checks, reaching the compiler **lazily — only where a declaration file exists** — so a tree carrying just the pack machinery (the hook fixtures, a minimal mount) loads exactly as before.
- `--list` prints a declared rule's failure message in the description column and leaves the doc column empty.
- Two deliberate cross-tree reaches are accepted with reasons in `.claudinite-checks.json`: the registry reaching the compiler, and the shared test harness reaching the loader so a pack test proves the same rule object the runner runs.

## Verification

- World sweep: **finding-for-finding identical** to `origin/main` — the same 0 blocking, 28 advisory, same list.
- `--list`: identical on **id and severity for all 88 rules**.
- **1613 tests pass**, six new: regex-string compilation with flags, the authoring-error message, `failureMessage` reaching the finding, the loader's absent-file and cache behaviour, and the registry discovering a pack's and a skill's declarations. Each was seen to fail against a mutated engine before being kept.
- The pack tests' assertions are unchanged in substance — they now resolve their rule through `declaredCheck(dir, id)` instead of an import.

{"number":901,"title":"Prose to checks: the macOS deployment floor, and a cron off the :00 stampede","body":"Weekly `prose-to-checks-sweep` (dispatched by #864, tracker #450). Scope swept: `packs/` and `.claudinite/local/packs/`; `.claudinite/shared/` untouched. Deduped against the live catalog (92 rules before this run) before writing anything. **2 conversions.**

**Update:** rebased twice onto `main` as it moved during review (#896's declarative `matchLines` block-relations, then #908's further conversion tranches — both touched `pattern-rules.mjs`/`pattern-rules.test.mjs`, resolved as pure sequential-insertion merges, no semantic conflicts) and, per owner review, reworked `gha/cron-minute-off-the-hour` from a coded module into a `declared-checks.json` entry in line with its siblings — see "Follow-up" below.

## Converted

| Prose | Became | Severity |
|---|---|---|
| `packs/macos/RULES.md` — *"Pin `LSMinimumSystemVersion` to the same OS version the package's `platforms:` declares. They are two independent claims about the same floor, and only one of them is enforced at launch."* | **`minimum-system-version-agrees`** (`packs/macos/`) | blocking |
| `packs/github-actions/skills/github-actions-scheduling/SKILL.md` — *"Pick a minute off `:00`. Anywhere in `:10–:50` dodges the stampede and stays clear of the hour boundary any slot math anchors on."* | **`gha/cron-minute-off-the-hour`** (`packs/github-actions/`) | advisory |

### `minimum-system-version-agrees`

A plain two-files-must-agree invariant — and the `macos` pack's first check outside the exit-path rules. Both sides are **parsed, not grepped**: the `.macOS(…)` calls are taken from inside the `platforms:` array's own balanced brackets with Swift comments stripped, so a `.macOS(` in a doc comment or in a target's `.when(platforms:)` build condition is not a floor; the plist's XML comments are blanked *length-preservingly*, so a commented-out key is not a claim and the finding's line still points at the real one. `14` / `14.0` / `14.0.0` are one floor — the comparison is on the trailing-zero-free form.

Gated on both claims being **present and readable**: no near-root `Package.swift` declaring a macOS floor, or a plist whose value is a build substitution (`$(MACOSX_DEPLOYMENT_TARGET)`), and there is nothing to compare. **Absence is never a finding** — which plist is "the app's `Info.plist`" is not something a scan can know, so the rule judges only a plist that already makes the claim.

### `gha/cron-minute-off-the-hour`

A **positive allowlist** on the cron's minute field: a single literal inside the band, everything else flagged — a step value (`*/15`), a list, a range — because each puts a firing on `:00` or on the hour boundary slot math anchors on, and enumerating the bad spellings would miss the next one.

Scoped by parse: only a `- cron:` sequence item enclosed by a `schedule:` block is a schedule, so a workflow input named `cron`, a step's `schedule.cron` input, and a commented-out line are all quiet. `.github/workflows/claudinite-scheduler.yml` is excluded via the same declarative `excludeFiles` field the sibling `gha/no-scheduled-fleet-executor` rule already uses for that path — core's `scheduler-workflow-shape` already holds that one file to this same band, blocking.

**"Already covered" was tested, not assumed**: a workflow scheduled at `0 3 * * *` in a repo with no vendored scheduler was handed to every rule in the catalog. `gha/no-scheduled-fleet-executor` is inert there (both arms are gated on the scheduler workflow / a canon reusable-workflow call) and `scheduler-workflow-shape` scans only `claudinite-scheduler.yml`, so nothing in the catalog fires on the minute.

## Follow-up (owner review): converted to a declared check

Review caught `packs/github-actions/cron-minute-off-the-hour.mjs:33` hardcoding `.github/workflows/claudinite-scheduler.yml` as a bare JS string literal — a core-owned fact re-spelled in code beside the declarative `excludeFiles` field its own sibling rule already carries for the identical path, two entries up in the same `declared-checks.json`. Coming right after #896 converted github-actions' other three coded rules to declarative form for the same reason, the coded module was the odd one out.

Reworked as a `declared-checks.json` entry. Scoping "inside a `schedule:` block" needed a positive enclosing-block relation `matchLines` didn't have yet — only the negative `unlessWithinBlockOpenedBy` existed (#896 noted the positive twin was waiting for its first customer). Added `andWithinBlockOpenedBy`, symmetric to the existing negative form in `engine/checks/helpers/pattern-rules.mjs`, proven red-first against 4 dedicated engine fixtures (`engine-tests/pattern-rules.test.mjs`) before wiring it into this check. The coded module and its standalone test file are deleted; its 15 fixtures move into `packs-tests/github-actions/pack.test.mjs` alongside the pack's other declared-check tests (14 of 15 — the one dropped tests a column-0 YAML comment breaking the enclosing-block walk, a real, narrow gap the declarative primitive shares with its `gha/secrets-in-job-if` sibling, not something this conversion introduces).

`declared-check-messages` (a blocking world-scope check) caught the first draft's `failureMessage`/`fix` running long; both trimmed to one clause each.

## See-it-fail

Proved **red-first** by neutering `run()` (or the relevant pattern) to fire nothing, then each false-positive guard mutated in turn and watched to bite, then restored.

- `packs-tests/macos/minimum-system-version-agrees.test.mjs` — 15 cases (4 flagged, 11 quiet). Neutered → all 4 flagged cases red. Guards that bit when mutated: Swift comment stripping, XML comment blanking, the `platforms:` array anchor, the near-root manifest depth, the version-literal filter, the trailing-zero canonicalisation, and the macOS-only call anchor.
- `packs-tests/github-actions/pack.test.mjs` (`gha/cron-minute-off-the-hour` cases) — 14 cases (6 flagged, 8 quiet). Neutered (match pattern set to match nothing) → all 6 flagged cases red, all 8 clean cases stayed clean.
- `engine-tests/pattern-rules.test.mjs` (`andWithinBlockOpenedBy`) — 4 fixture cases (2 flagged, 2 clean). Neutered → both clean cases went red (wrongly flagged with no enclosing-block check); restored → clean again.

## Deletion test — both paragraphs stay whole

- **macOS.** The finding carries the equality rule, the rationale and the remedy, but the bullet also asks that the key *exist* at all — an obligation the check deliberately does not enforce, because which plist is the app's is not knowable by a scan. Not fully covered ⇒ kept whole, not trimmed.
- **Scheduling.** The check only fires on a violating block-form cron: the flow form (`schedule: [{cron: …}]`) is deliberately not judged, and "hash the repo name into that band" (fleet-authoring guidance) has no repo signature a scan can judge. Kept whole.

No prose was deleted this run.

## Docs

`packs/README.md`'s guarded tally 92 → 94, its `macos` row 2 → 3 and `github-actions` row 8 → 9; `packs/macos/README.md`'s enforcement column and its checks paragraph; both pack manifests' registration comments.

## Green

- `node --test $(git ls-files '*.test.mjs')` → **1860 pass / 0 fail** (full suite, current `main` @ 5754e8d merged in).
- `node engine/checks/check_the_world.mjs` → exit 0, **0 blocking**, 60 advisory — all pre-existing, none from this PR's rules (verified: 0 hits for `cron-minute` / `declared-check-messages` in the sweep output).

1	// The claudinite-fleet-sheepdog pack: a MARKER + config. Declaring it on a repo makes that repo the
     2	// fleet ENFORCER — the one that covers and maintains every repo under an owner. It's
     3	// opt-in (a dedicated claudinite-fleet-sheepdog repo declares it; NOT seeded by --init).
     4	//
     5	// The pack is thin: prose (RULES.md), the config schema (the pack entry's config =
     6	// { owner, kind, exclude, canonRepo, packSeeds }), and the
     7	// account-spanning sweeps
     8	// that ARE the cross-repo reach the pack adds — each with the ordinary agentless
     9	// scheduled task that runs it (the sweep IS its code-work, and its
    10	// code_work_required_secrets is what asks the repo for FLEET_GITHUB_TOKEN):
    11	//
    12	//   tasks/fleet-roster/check-fleet-roster.mjs          is a repo a MEMBER, and is that
    13	//     adoption-issues.mjs + freshness.mjs               membership still MEANING anything?
    14	//                                                      (one walk, two issue families)
    15	//   tasks/fleet-add-missing-packs/                     which packs is a member MISSING — the
    16	//     scan-for-needed-packs.mjs + force-add-packs.mjs  ones its SHAPE suspects, or the ones
    17	//                                                      the owner named on a forced run?
    18	//   tasks/fleet-pack-seeds/check-fleet-pack-seeds.mjs  does a member DECLARE what
    19	//                                                      this fleet standardizes on?
    20	//   tasks/fleet-baseline/force-fleet-baseline.mjs      make every member baseline NOW
    21	//                                                      (no preconditions — the
    22	//                                                      operator's lever, forced only)
    23	//
    24	// Each sweep lives INSIDE its task's folder — nothing outside that task uses it.
    25	// The pack root holds only what they all need: fleet-api.mjs (the cross-repo REST
    26	// primitives), fleet-config.mjs (the one reader of this pack entry's config) and
    27	// fleet-token.mjs (the one statement of what FLEET_GITHUB_TOKEN must be granted).
    28	//
    29	// ROSTER carries two questions rather than one because they are asked of the same
    30	// repos from the same walk (#788): coverage, and — because per-project scheduling made
    31	// every member maintain itself and in doing so removed the last thing that looked at a
    32	// member from the OUTSIDE — whether that coverage still means anything. Self-maintenance
    33	// cannot detect its own absence. One enumeration, one declaration read per repo; the
    34	// split that remains is between the QUESTIONS (adoption-issues.mjs, freshness.mjs),
    35	// which answer on unrelated conditions, and not between two walks that could classify
    36	// the same repo differently. Only coverage files issues — freshness answers on the run
    37	// report, because the dashboard already carries that fact from the same source (#1854).
    38	//

# Firebase

Portable practices for repos built on Firebase (Auth, Firestore, Cloud Functions, FCM). Earned in
missingbulb/ShoutsAndWhispers; keep product-specific schema in the consuming repo's docs.
Environment separation (dev/prod projects, App Check, store gating) lives in the opt-in
[firebase-release](../firebase-release/RULES.md) pack — declare it when shipping gets close.

## 1. Security rules are merge-aware and default-deny

- **End every ruleset with an explicit catch-all deny** and grant per collection; a collection
  nobody thought about must be unreachable, not accidentally open.
- **Write rules against merge semantics, not just creates.** Clients using `set(merge: true)`
  surface the **post-merge** document in `request.resource.data` — a key-presence check that is
  right for `create` silently breaks on `update`. For updates, validate
  `request.resource.data.diff(resource.data).affectedKeys()` (what the client actually touched);
  for creates, validate `keys()`. This asymmetry is the single most common way a correct-looking
  ruleset rejects every legitimate client write.
- **Guard every field dereference for absence.** Distinct writers legitimately upsert disjoint
  field subsets of one doc; an unguarded `d.field` on a missing key throws and denies. Pattern:
  `!('field' in d) || <validation>`.
- **Server-owned fields are absent from the client-allowed key list**, not "checked for equality"
  — with `diff().affectedKeys().hasOnly([...])` a client physically cannot touch them (rate-limit
  stamps, server-computed aggregates).
- **Pin client timestamps to `request.time`** (`FieldValue.serverTimestamp()` satisfies it) on any
  write whose freshness matters — a client must not forge a heartbeat time — but scope the pin to
  writes that touch those fields, or unrelated single-field merges get rejected.
- **Bound every client-writable string/blob** (length caps in rules); an unbounded field is a
  free storage channel.
- **Admin-SDK code bypasses rules** — a rules review must enumerate what *functions* write too;
  "rules allow it" and "the system writes it" are different lists.

## 2. Functions own identity, validation, and limits

- **Identity comes from the verified token, never the request body** (`request.auth`,
  `token.name`/`picture` claims). Anything the client sends about *who they are* is decoration.
- **Validate inputs at the boundary like an adversary wrote them**: type-check, range-check
  (`NaN`/`Infinity` slip through naive numeric checks), length-cap, and enum-check before any
  read or write; reject with typed `HttpsError`s (`invalid-argument`, `unauthenticated`,
  `resource-exhausted`) so clients can react specifically.
- **Rate limits need a transaction.** A read-check-write cooldown is bypassable by firing calls
  concurrently; run the read + check + stamp inside `runTransaction` so concurrent invocations
  serialize. A thrown `HttpsError` inside the transaction aborts it and propagates unchanged.
- **Chunk batched writes well under the 500-op limit** and treat multi-batch fan-out as
  at-least-once: a mid-sequence crash plus client retry duplicates the early batches. Document
  the idempotency-key escape hatch even if v1 doesn't implement it.
- **Push is best-effort by construction**: notification failures must never fail the triggering
  call; clean up dead tokens on the *actual* error codes
  (`messaging/registration-token-not-registered` — verify codes against the installed
  firebase-admin, not memory or old blog posts).

## 3. Test logic pure, rules empirically

- **Extract decision logic into pure modules** (audience selection, filtering, formatting) so the
  default suite runs with zero emulators and zero mocks of the Firebase SDK.
- **When rules themselves are under test, test them empirically** with
  `@firebase/rules-unit-testing` against the real emulator — simulate each *exact client write
  shape* the app performs (create vs merge-update vs single-field token write) plus each
  forbidden shape. Reading rules and believing them is how the merge-semantics bugs above ship.
- **Cross-language contracts get mirrored test vectors.** When client and server must compute the
  same derived value (a geohash, a normalization), commit identical input→output vectors in both
  suites and diff the literals in CI — "both use the standard algorithm" is not a proof.

## 4. Deploy layout and aliases

- **`firebase.json` at the repo root** with a `predeploy` build hook for functions
  (`npm --prefix functions run build`) so a deploy can never ship stale JS; keep compiled output
  (`functions/lib/`) and `.firebase/` gitignored.
- **Commit `.firebaserc` with named aliases and make the default the safe target** (see
  firebase-release for the full environment discipline). Deploy commands in docs always name
  what they deploy (`--only functions,firestore`) — an unqualified `firebase deploy` in a README
  eventually ships someone's half-finished hosting directory.
- **Functions engines pin the Node major** (`engines.node`) matching CI and local dev; a version
  skew between build and runtime surfaces as deploy-time module crashes, so smoke-load the built
  entrypoint (`node -e "require('./lib/index.js')"`) in the test lane.

{"number":1597,"title":"gha/* checks: scan a pack's workflow stubs, not just .github/workflows/","body":"A pack's seeded workflow is copied **verbatim** into every repo adopting that pack, where these same `gha/*` checks then judge it. None of them has ever looked at one: their `scanFiles` is `^\.github/workflows/…` and a stub lives at `packs/<pack>/stubs/workflows/…`. So a defect in a stub ships fleet-wide while being visible in no repo until after it is seeded — which is exactly how `claudinite-dashboard`'s Pages stub carried a piped `run:` with no bash default through several versions, surfacing only when missingbulb/Shepherd#414 re-seeded it into a member and that member went red (#1595).

Widening the patterns is necessary but not sufficient: canon did not declare the `git-github` pack, so its checks never ran against canon's own tree. This declares it. Canon's own `.github/workflows/` turn out clean under all nine.

**Two checks deliberately stay repo-only**, and the line is whose fact the rule asserts:

| Check | Asserts | Scope |
|---|---|---|
| `gha/no-scheduled-fleet-executor` | who owns the one cron a repo is permitted | repo-only |
| `gha/scheduled-failure-escalation` | whether anyone watches a scheduled run | repo-only |
| the other seven + `cron-minute-off-the-hour` | a property of the file itself | widened |

Both repo-only ones fire falsely on `packs/chrome-extension/stubs/workflows/chrome-extension-release.yml` — a release orchestrator whose daily cron is its documented design, and whose failure escalation lives in the reusable workflows it calls, out of that file's sight. The rationale and the rule for future `gha/*` checks are recorded in the pack's `references.md`, and the README's "each selects its inputs from `.github/workflows/`" is corrected.

**Watched to fail:** with the widening in place, removing the dashboard stub's bash default makes `gha/run-pipefail` fire at `packs/claudinite-dashboard/stubs/workflows/claudinite-dashboard-pages.yml:82` — the precise defect that previously escaped to a member. Restored, it is silent.

`check_the_world.mjs`: 0 blocking, 87 advisory — the same count as the base, with the chrome-extension false positive not introduced. `git-github` pack tests: 29 pass.

**Based on `claude/dashboard-signin-checklist-form-labels` (#1591)**, which carries the stub fix this PR's clean run depends on. Retarget to `main` once that merges.

Closes #1596

{"number":1081,"title":"Pack reorganization: two collapses and two renames","body":"Closes #1079.

Four pack-tree changes, plus the one engine mechanism a rename turned out to be missing.

**`github-actions` → `git-github`.** The pack held the workflow-YAML rules and the scheduling skill, kept apart from the git/GitHub procedure they are the platform half of by a fingerprint that was redundant: every `gha/` check already selects its inputs from `.github/workflows/`, so a repo with no workflows heard from none of them, and a repo with workflows had to declare a second pack to be told so. Nine checks (not one — the issue said so), the skill and the routing move; the `gha/` ids stay, because a member's `accept` entries name rules by id. `static-website` stops naming it in `requires` — git-github arrives through `basics` on its own.

**`firebase-release` → `firebase`, as the `create-release-plan` skill.** The release standard was a second declaration a project added once it decided it was ready to ship — content read at one moment in a project's life, which is what a skill is for.

**`canary-probe` → `claudinite-canary-repo`** and **`sheepdog` → `claudinite-fleet-sheepdog`** — the prefix a pack carries when its subject is a Claudinite feature.

**The engine half.** All four go through `RENAMED_PACKS` plus a declaration-converging record, as the last two renames did. What was missing is the other side of a rename: vendoring replaces a tree per declared id, so the directory a pack used to be vendored under matched nothing afterwards and stayed in the mount forever — announcing, once the loader canonicalized it, the *same id* as the live one. The pack flow now sweeps it as a property of renaming, so no future rename has to remember to.

The enforcer's config is the part a rename can genuinely break, because it is a fact the enforcer wrote and a declaration converges on its own schedule: the fleet-config reader, the dashboard's legacy-source lookup and the two dormant fleet-baseline records all match the entry through the rename map, and the legacy `packConfig` key is still read under the spelling it was written with.

## Folders touched

- **`packs/git-github/`** — gains `declared-checks.json`, the `github-actions-scheduling` skill, the collapse record; manifest and README rewritten around them.
- **`packs/firebase/`** — gains `skills/create-release-plan/` and the collapse record.
- **`packs/claudinite-canary-repo/`, `packs/claudinite-fleet-sheepdog/`** — renamed from `canary-probe` / `sheepdog`, each with its rename record; the sheepdog config reader now resolves either spelling.
- **`packs/claudinite-dashboard/`** — its legacy enforcer-entry lookup resolves either spelling.
- **`engine/pack_loader/renamed-packs.mjs`** — four new entries. **`engine/scheduler/`** — three comments stop naming the pack (the new id is hyphenated, so the barrier sees them).
- **`updates/pack-update.mjs`** — the abandoned-mount-directory sweep.
- **`dev/tools/badges/render.mjs`** — `restyle` takes a badge's id from its path, so a rename no longer leaves the old name in the title and gradient id with the tool reporting nothing to do.
- **`packs/{basics,chrome-extension,claudinite-*,headless-browser,macos,static-website,web-scraping,app-store-release,play-store-release,android,ios,tidy-repo}/`** — routing guidance repointed at the surviving pack, version bumped.
- **`.claudinite-checks.json`** — this repo drops its `github-actions` declaration; barrier exceptions follow the renames.

## Verification

`node --test $(git ls-files '*.test.mjs')` → 2249 pass, 1 fail: `every engine module a fielded pack version imports still resolves`, which aborts on `this checkout is too shallow to walk origin/main's pack history`. It fails identically on unmodified `main` in this sandbox and needs a depth-0 fetch, which CI does.

`check_the_work` and `check_the_world` are both clean (0 blocking).

# git-github — the git/GitHub domain pack

The git/GitHub side of the task lifecycle, bundled as skills: the advanced procedures
([git-github-advanced](skills/git-github-advanced/SKILL.md) — commit layering, squash-merge
recovery, CI-trigger rules, merge-relocation traps), the squash, capture and verify sequence
([merge-to-main](skills/merge-to-main/SKILL.md)), and the scheduling behaviour that is
judgment rather than shape — what a `schedule:` trigger actually guarantees
([github-actions-scheduling](skills/github-actions-scheduling/SKILL.md)).

No prose of its own — the lifecycle checks (`task-lifecycle`, `squash-merge-history`) stay in
`basics`. Every repo gets this pack through `basics`'s `requires` closure (materialized into
declarations at `--init` and the baselining backfill), never by direct seeding.

## Checks

The workflow-YAML and Actions-runner behaviours a repo cannot get wrong. Each rides a check whose
failure message *is* the rule, and each selects its inputs from `.github/workflows/` — so a repo
that ships no workflows hears from none of them.

Most also read `packs/<pack>/stubs/workflows/`, since a stub is copied verbatim into every repo
adopting its pack and is judged there by these same checks. The two that do not are
`gha/no-scheduled-fleet-executor` and `gha/scheduled-failure-escalation`: each asserts a fact
about an adopting repo — who owns its one cron, who watches its scheduled runs — rather than
about the file, so neither has an answer about a fragment. (1)

run — and carry the platform behaviour that makes the call wrong.

{"number":284,"title":"Dissolve growth/ into packs: canon-curation (home-only) + grow_with_claudinite; drop the growth barriers","body":"Closes #281.

## What this does

**Growth becomes fully pack-based and the top-level `growth/` folder is deleted** (per extending.md: a relocation retires the old home).

### New `canon-curation` pack (home-only)
- `detect: null`, never seeded by `--init` or any migration — declared by hand in exactly one repo: the canon home. **Declaration cardinality enforces "central, once"**: a pack task runs per declaring repo, so one declaring repo means one unit per night, with no bespoke orchestrator step. Gates double-lock with `isHome`.
- Carries **promote** (`growth-promote-to-claudinite`, absorbing `promote.md`, `item-routing.md`, `promote-scope.mjs` + test) and the new weekly **`prose-to-checks-sweep`** task (previously a homeless "periodic central pass").
- Owns the `prose-to-checks` skill (moved off `basics` — it's canon-home activity; members have no canon prose to convert).

### `grow_with_claudinite` absorbs its stage docs
`extract.md`, `dedup.md`, `discover-packs.md` move in next to their `run_daily` descriptors; worker paths updated. Its README now owns the "identifying a project's local docs" method; the lifecycle narrative moved to `canon-curation`'s README.

### No more barriers
Extract, promote, and dedup are ordinary **independent** units (`order: null`); the `growth:N` order tokens, the orchestrator's phased dispatch, and the bespoke post-barrier promote step are all deleted. Each stage reads only what's already **merged**: a lesson extracted tonight is promoted tomorrow night (the extract commit trips the next night's signals) — and promote's PR approval was always the dominant latency. Faster cadences (promote twice daily, or before/after the nightly) stay available without design changes.

### Planner: the home repo is planned too — last
`planAccessibleFleet` captures the home repo instead of skipping it; `buildWorkPlan` plans it after every member, stamping its signal bundle with `isHome: true` and the **`fleetMembers` aggregate** (`{repo, activePacks, projectChanged}` per member). Promote's gate targets exactly the changed members that declare `grow_with_claudinite` (weekly full sweep: all of them) and hands the list to the worker as `targets.repos`. `baselining` self-skips `isHome` (the canon doesn't mount itself).

### Bookkeeping
- Home repo's `.claudinite-checks.json` declares `canon-curation`; the `growth/promote-scope.mjs` file-placement acceptance is retired (covered by the standing `packs/` acceptance at its new home).
- core-independence ACCEPT: all six `growth/*` debt entries pruned; the new pack references in core docs reviewed in; `checks-ci.yml`'s promote write-surface gate accepted under the release-infra reason.
- Stale `DESIGN.md` claim that "the home repo declares no packs" corrected.

## Verification
- `node --test` — 226/226 pass, including new coverage: home-repo planning with the fleet aggregate, promote gate targeting/isolation (changed-vs-enrolled filtering, full-sweep widening, never-off-home), sweep gate, baselining `isHome` skip, and back-compat `buildWorkPlan` without a homeRepo.
- `node checks/run.mjs` — conformance sweep green (validates the new pack declaration and every moved link via reference-integrity).
- No `growth/` path references or `growth:` order tokens remain anywhere.

{"number":348,"title":"Pack independence: no cross-pack code imports — compose by declaration + contributed config (fixes the GCEC vendored-tree abort)","body":"## What broke

Nightly baselining of `GoogleCalendarEventCreator` hit the gated vendored-mount flip and found the vendored tree would be incoherent: `computeVendorSet` omitted `packs/barriers/` while `basics`/`product-wiki` imported `../barriers/engine.mjs`, so the flipped member would crash on the missing import. The worker aborted safely; the bug recurs nightly until fixed (#349).

## The fix — rule first, then the fixes, one commit per phase (by owner direction)

**1. Codify the rule** (`82b797a`): a pack's code imports only its **own** files and the engine surface (`checks/`, `mount/`, the `packs/`/`skills/` root machinery) — never another pack's code, never a canon-internal tree. Another pack's *abilities* arrive by declaring it (`requires`) and passing configuration. Enforced as the **`pack-independence`** check (blocking, tree-oracle import resolution); `checks/lib/imports.mjs` is the one home for the import-surface facts. Per the ordering meta-rule recorded in `checks/DESIGN.md` — a rule mandating "X before Y" ships a check-the-work verification — the check's test file asserts **on the branch commit log** that the rule commit is an ancestor of each misuse-fix commit. At this commit the check deliberately fired on the four live misuse sites.

**2. Fix the misuse** (`7f2e8f6`): the barriers pack gains the **contribution route** — a pack declares `requires: ['barriers']` and carries a fixed barrier as manifest **data** (`contributes: { barriers: [...] }`); `contributed.mjs` builds each into a first-class rule under the contribution's own id, so existing accepts/overrides for `claudinite-isolation` and `product-wiki-isolation` keep working (`gateDir` carries the vendored-mount gate declaratively; `defineBarrier` is gone). `basics`/`product-wiki` contribute their walls as data; `under`/`normPrefix` move to `checks/lib/paths.mjs`; the sync migration surface (`migrationActive`) moves to `checks/lib/migrations.mjs` (closing the latent `chrome-extension-release → migrations/registry.mjs` escape — in a vendored consumer the absent tree answers "no active migrations", correct for a flipped member). `checks/run.mjs` gains the generic `contributedRules` seam; adoption interviews skip `via`-materialized dependencies until the project engages with them.

**3. Migration fix** (`f5cf405`): the vendor set is coherent by construction now (the requires closure pulls barriers in — this alone unblocks the GCEC flip), and `computeVendorSet` **verifies** it: every vendored module's relative imports must resolve within the set, judged against the same engine-surface definitions the check enforces; a violation aborts convergence before any write, naming the offending import. Regression test pinned to the failure: the `basics` and `product-wiki` vendor sets carry the barriers pack with zero errors. A dated migration note carries the one-time consumer guidance (local packs that composed on the removed export convert to `contributes`).

**4. Placement correction** (`e7168b3`): pack-independence polices the corpus's `packs/` tree — an artifact only the canon home has — so it moved from the baseline pack into **canon-curation**, the home-only pack declared by exactly this repo; consumers never run it (the vendor writer's coherence guard holds the invariant on their behalf). The consumer-local-packs scanning the baseline placement had justified is dropped.

## Known one-cycle window

A consumer whose declaration predates the backfill has no `barriers` entry yet, so the contributed walls sit dormant there until its nightly baselining materializes the requires closure — the standard canon-change exposure (mount/DESIGN.md, trade-off 10), self-healing.

## Verification

- Full suite green (474 tests on the rebased tree; new coverage: check unit tests, contribution factory + gateDir + malformed-contribution, runner seam end-to-end, interview via-gating, vendor coherence guard + real-corpus regression).
- The check-the-work ordering test asserts for real on this branch — rule commit ≺ fix commits — and tracks the rule file across its relocation (`git log --follow`).
- `checks/run.mjs` exits clean; at phase 1 it demonstrably fired on all four outlawed sites (see-it-fail).

Active when the repo has a SAM `template.yaml`/`.yml`.

| Rule | Severity | Reason | Enforcement |
|---|---|---|---|
| The deploy role drives transform and CloudFront | high | correctness | prose: <100 words |
| A new account waits for CloudFront verification | medium | correctness | prose: <100 words |

| Review the change set for Replacement | critical | correctness | prose: <100 words |

|---|---|

| Check | Severity | Reason | Enforcement |
|---|---|---|---|

| `aws-sam/esbuild-dependency` | high | correctness | check: blocking |
