Pack reorganization: two collapses and two renames (#1081)
* The pack flow sweeps a renamed pack's abandoned mount directory

Vendoring replaces a tree per declared id, and a rename changes the id — so the
directory a pack used to be vendored under matches nothing afterwards and is never
touched again. That copy is not inert: a mounted pack's own id is canonicalized on
load, so the abandoned tree announces the id the live one has and the member runs the
pack twice, one of them frozen at whatever it was renamed from.

Swept as a property of renaming rather than by a record per rename: the map already
says which spellings resolve to a pack, and a cleanup each rename has to remember is a
cleanup some rename will forget.

Refs #1079

* Collapse github-actions into git-github

The pack held the workflow-YAML rules and the scheduling skill, and separated them
from the git/GitHub procedure they are the platform half of. Its fingerprint was the
one thing keeping them apart, and the fingerprint was redundant: every `gha/` check
selects its inputs from `.github/workflows/`, so a repo with no workflows already
heard from none of them, and a repo with workflows had to declare a second pack to be
told so.

The nine checks, the skill and the routing all move into git-github, which every repo
already carries through basics' `requires` closure. The `gha/` ids stay as they are —
a member's `accept` entries name rules by id, and renaming one orphans an acceptance.
`static-website` stops naming the absorbed pack in `requires` for the same reason: the
surviving pack arrives on its own.

Refs #1079

* Collapse firebase-release into firebase, as the create-release-plan skill

The release standard was a second pack a Firebase project declared once it decided it
was ready to ship — a fact about a milestone, kept as a fact about configuration. It
is content read at one moment in a project's life, which is what a skill is for, so it
becomes `create-release-plan` in the pack that owns the technology: the dev/prod
project split, the pipeline-injected prod config, the App Check gate and the promotion
cadence, loaded when a project plans a release rather than declared in advance.

{"number":350,"title":"google-identity: convert the three prose rules into skill-owned check-the-work rules","body":"Converts the `google-identity` pack's three prose rules (PR #-pending on this branch, commit 1b64b32) into deterministic checks, per the owner's direction: keep the pack, add a skill for the activity, move the rules into check-the-work tests, and delete all the prose.

## What changed

**The pack stays, prose-free.** `packs/google-identity/RULES.md` is deleted; `pack.mjs` drops `prose` and now mounts the new skill (`skills: ['google-id-token-validation']`), keeping the pack as the hand-declared anchor (`detect: null` unchanged).

**New skill `google-id-token-validation`** — a minimal SKILL.md (the trigger plus the three rule ids; no re-teaching, so nothing to drift) and a `checks.mjs` owning three rules, discovered by `skills/registry.mjs` and run at every Stop and in CI. The failure message is the instruction:

| Rule | Severity | Signature |
|---|---|---|
| `google-token-audience-pinned` | blocking | a config-format file (yaml/json/toml/tf) declaring the bare Google accounts issuer with no — or an explicitly empty — expected audience |
| `google-client-id-single-origin` | advisory | the same `…apps.googleusercontent.com` literal hardcoded in ≥2 files (a smell to judge: separate deploy units legitimately hold one copy each) |
| `google-token-email-verified` | blocking | handler code reading the `email` claim with no `email_verified` check, or strict-boolean-comparing `email_verified` behind an API Gateway authorizer (which stringifies claims) |

**Relevance gates** (a skill check runs on every repo): rule 1 scopes to config formats bearing the bare issuer origin — the path-form client OAuth URLs never match; rule 3 gates per-file on a verified-claims context and per-repo on a Google-identity marker, and skips test files; all three exclude the skill's own directory so its fixtures never flag the corpus repo. Code-form verifiers (jose/google-auth-library defaults) have no reliable file-scoped signature and are documented out of rule 1's scope.

**Answering "are you sure they weren't checkable?"** — the original commit was too conservative. There is no *universal* signature, but file-scoped signatures cover the grounded cases (the TLDR provenance is exactly rule 1's authorizer-config shape), so the rules convert; the signature-less residue (hand-rolled verifier code) is what the checks' comments document as out of scope.

## Tests

13 new fixture tests (scratch-repo harness), each rule proven both directions — violating fixtures find, clean ones (path-form OAuth URLs, per-deploy-unit copies, string-compared `email_verified`, marker-less repos, test files) stay quiet — and mutation-tested red (neutering `run()` fails exactly the violating-fixture tests). Full suite: 341 pass. Whole-repo sweep: clean (one new `file-placement` acceptance for the engine-lib import, mirroring the `unattended-agents` precedent).

Catalogs updated (`packs/README.md` row, `skills/README.md` entry) to satisfy `catalog-completeness`; the pack's `skills` list satisfies `skill-ownership`.

{"number":361,"title":"Local packs first-class: namespaced declarations; canon-curation moves to local_packs; local run_daily on by default","body":"Closes #360. Closes #364.

Two work packages on one branch. All decisions below are the owner's, recorded as standing decisions in `.claudinite/local_packs/claudinite/RULES.md`.

## 1. Namespace local-pack declarations as `local_packs/<name>` (#360)

Local packs were declared by bare id — the same namespace as canon packs, so a collision was only *caught* by `discoverPacks`' shadow guard, never prevented. The canonical declaration token is now **`local_packs/<name>`**, self-documenting in `.claudinite-checks.json`.

- **Engine, both forms accepted**: `packEntryId` strips the prefix (with `LOCAL_DECL_PREFIX` / `declTokenFor` exported); `loadConfig` normalizes at load, one layer below the runner, so unknown-pack validation *and* the interview/`packConfig` readers see bare ids whichever form the file used; the fleet's member-declaration read normalizes the same way.
- **Rollout**: a baselining declaration-normalization step rewrites members' bare local-pack declarations; the seed-style `local-pack-namespace` migration (`retire: 'auto'`) tracks convergence.

## 2. canon-curation → `.claudinite/local_packs/`; local run_daily ON; segregation via barriers only (#364)

- **`canon-curation` is now the canon home's local pack** (`.claudinite/local_packs/canon-curation/`, declared as `local_packs/canon-curation` — dogfooding package 1). The canon home's curation duties are Claudinite-maintaining-Claudinite: project-specific content on the home's own capture surface.
- **Local-pack `run_daily` scheduling is on by default**: `readLocalTasks` is `buildWorkPlan`'s *default* `localTasksFor` (still injectable; `localTasksFor: null` disables). A local task gates on the member's declaration exactly like a canon task; a descriptor worker path may be pack-relative or repo-root-relative (leading `/`). Every "experimental / not enabled by default / do not pass the seam" statement is purged (planner, local-tasks header, orchestrator routine, fleet DESIGN, packs/extending/skill docs). The moved canon-curation tasks are the path's nightly dogfood — an integration test plans the home's promote unit by serving the *real* descriptor files through a fake GitHub API, proving they are self-contained and worker paths rewrite correctly.
- **Packs-tree segregation is barriers configuration only.** The `pack-independence` code check is retired. The invariant is a barrier the moved pack *contributes* (`requires: ['barriers']` + `contributes`; the same composition `basics` uses for `claudinite-isolation`), keeping the same rule id so acceptances/overrides keep addressing it. Two new **generic barriers capabilities** carry it:
  - `siblings: "<folder>"` — each direct child directory guarded against the rest, expanded from the tree at scan time, fail-closed on an empty expansion;
  - `scope: "imports"` — relative import/require specifiers in code files only, matched across line breaks, resolved as module edges (extension/index completion, no bare/root-relative strings, no name/unique-filename layers, index-less directory import = breakage not crossing), so prose stays free to talk about packs.
- **Adversarially verified**: a workflow fanned out 4 stale-statement sweeps (all clean) plus a semantics reviewer diffing the old check against the new barrier; it surfaced 5 real divergences (untracked files invisible to the resolution index; comment/root-relative and unique-basename false positives; multi-line import false negative; bare-directory resolution divergence) — all fixed red-first, including building the barriers index from tracked **plus in-scope untracked** files. The barrier was also proven live by planting a real cross-pack import in the tree and watching the sweep go red.

## Verification

- All new behavior test-first (seen red before implementation): 65 barriers tests, local-tasks/planner default-seam tests, moved-pack contribution tests, migration probe, loadConfig/runner/registry namespace tests.
- Full suite green: **482 tests, 0 failures** (CI glob now includes `.claudinite/local_packs/*/*.test.mjs`); `node checks/run.mjs --all` clean; SessionStart surfaces (prose injection, skill mounts, interview, discovery) exercised end-to-end in the canon checkout.

{"number":606,"title":"Claudinite growth: extract lessons","body":"Daily growth capture over the window in #599 — commits 8b01f9b, 97b1785, f710ac0, 7f1d386, 6b0669f, 8b236ec; merged PRs #594, #591, #583, #586, #578, #581; touched issues #592, #590 and the rest. Writes only the home's own local pack (`.claudinite/local/packs/claudinite/`), plus the derived tally its guard requires.

## One lesson converts to a check

**`pack-discovery-entry-await`** (blocking) — `discoverPacks` imports every `packs/<name>/pack.mjs` on disk and `scanSkillChecks` imports every `<pack>/skills/<skill>/checks.mjs` beside it, **before activation is consulted**. So a module in that graph that is *also* a CLI entry point gets re-imported while it is still evaluating: a top-level `await` in its entry block never settles, and Node exits 13 having run nothing. That is #581 exactly — `interview.mjs check` deadlocked in every repo under every declaration, and the SessionStart orchestrator's fail-soft read it as a merely-absent note.

Parsed, not grepped: a bare grep for `await` under `packs/` hits every async function, and a grep for the entry guard hits the seven CLI workers that legitimately await at top level and are **not** in the discovery graph. The rule walks the static import graph from the real manifests (a dynamic `import()` is deliberately not followed — it is what makes the cycle harmless), blanks comments and string/template bodies before judging, and stays quiet when it cannot be certain about nesting.

**Red-first**: with `run()` neutered, the two violating fixtures fail and the five guards stay green.

| fixture | |
|---|---|
| top-level await in a module a skill `checks.mjs` imports | **red when neutered** |
| same, reached transitively through a `pack.mjs` | **red when neutered** |
| the safe form — `check(...).catch(...)` | quiet |
| a CLI worker outside the discovery graph | quiet |
| a dynamic `import()` of the offending module | quiet |
| prose and a template-literal code sample about the trap | quiet |
| a repo with no pack tree | quiet |

## Three stay prose

None has a false-positive-free static signature, so they land in that pack's `RULES.md`:

- **Green canon CI is not evidence about a consumer** — the canon's own packs are always already migrated, and #555 / #585 / #588 each passed it cleanly while breaking the fleet (#592). Name the consumer-side evidence in the PR — a migration record, or a demonstration that an unmigrated member stays green.
- **A pack's `RULES.md` is injected into every declaring session** — a deferred idea nobody can act on belongs in `docs/`, and a pack file may not link there, because `docs/` is outside the vendor set and the link dangles in every consumer (#591; the #424 `reference-integrity` class, which is work-scoped and so only sees paths the branch itself deletes).
- **Pick a scheduled task's cadence from how often its signal actually moves** — baselining converges `.claudinite/shared/` nightly, so a `sharedMount` precondition fires nearly every night and spends an opus dispatch each time; `growth-dedup` lost nothing moving to weekly because its signals are window-scoped and `windowStart` widens (#583).

## Considered and skipped

- #594's path-filtered-conformance trap — already landed as `packs/basics/conformance-workflow.mjs`.
- #586's leading-HTML-comment markdown gotcha — tied to one call site, already commented there and pinned by a test.
- #581's "assert stdout, not the exit code" — already carried by this pack's fail-soft SessionStart rule.

## Verification

- `node --test $(git ls-files '*.test.mjs')` → **1029 pass, 0 fail**.
- `node engine/checks/check_the_world.mjs` → **0 blocking**, 9 advisory (all pre-existing `file-placement` in `engine/`).
- `packs/README.md`'s derived corpus tally 67 → 68, as `packs-tests/catalog-tally.test.mjs` requires of any rule added anywhere (it counts local packs too).

Refs #599

{"number":839,"title":"Declarative checks: review document + the implementation it recommends","body":"The #838 review document plus, at the owner's direction, all five implementation bundles it distilled. Eight commits, in dependency order:

1. **Review document** — `docs/declarative-checks/REVIEW.md`: measured census and sweep timings, vocabulary and message analysis, per-rule conversion audit, framework survey (adopt idioms, adopt no tool).
2. **Vocabulary facilities** — `scanFileClasses`/`excludeFileClasses` (shared named file sets), structural self-exclusion of a skill's own content, rule-level `fix` default, `scanIgnoringComments` (string-aware), and full spec-key validation so a typo'd key throws instead of silently asserting nothing.
3. **jwt conversion** — the five jwt rules become two `declared-checks.json` files; the rule modules, both `checks.mjs` and the pack's `scan.mjs` are deleted (~160 net lines out), tests exercise the declared rules through the same fixtures.
4. **Perf** — the barrier scan gets a precomputed completion index + per-context shared scan state (274ms → ~180ms, findings byte-identical), and the base-ref refresh gains a 5-minute per-ref freshness window (1.21s → 0.53s back-to-back; the Stop hook no longer pays the fetch every turn).
5. **Key merges** — `checkParsedFile`/`forEachParsedEntry`/`equalParsedValues` → one select-then-assert `checkParsedFiles`; `listedInFile`/`coveredByGlobLine` → `requireIndexCoverage` with the divergent absence/anchoring semantics declared per entry. Legacy spellings stay accepted (member local packs may carry them; a rename has no fleet carrier) and normalize at load.
6. **Message discipline** — a blocking `declared-check-messages` meta-check (32-word cap per field, no fix repeated within a rule), authored red-first (17 findings), and the rewrite that turns it green. Tally recomputed 89 → 90; the stale basics row corrected.
7. **Barriers rephrase** — the scan engine moves to `engine/checks/helpers/reference-scanning.mjs`; the vocabulary gains `forbidReferences`; the three fixed barriers (claudinite-isolation, product-wiki-isolation, pack-independence) become declared checks in their owning packs, byte-identical findings on the home (minus the `doc` field declared checks drop). The per-repo config rule and the `contributes` seam keep working on the moved engine.

**Consumer safety**: two new rehearsal fixtures/changes — a member whose local pack declares checks in a legacy spelling converges green under the new blocking meta-check; the consumer-safe-change guard was satisfied by fixture (additive change), not record. At merge time, the standing verify-through-a-member rule applies: force a fleet baseline and confirm one member's converge before calling it shipped.

Verification: 1668/1668 tests, world sweep 0 blocking, work sweep clean, barrier-family findings diffed byte-identical against the pre-change baseline.

    Phase 4 step 2: retire run_daily/ and delete the central fleet routine (#473)
    
    * Retire the canon packs' legacy run_daily/ folders
    
    Phase 4 step 2's pack half of the per-project-scheduling migration. Phase 0
    landed tasks/ ADDITIVELY — every canon pack carried both its new
    tasks/<name>/{task.mjs,task.md} and its untouched run_daily/ through the
    rollout — and this deletes the legacy half.
    
    Deleted (five folders, eleven files):
      packs/basics/run_daily/                    baselining.mjs + .worker.md
      packs/grow_with_claudinite/run_daily/       conversation-extract, growth-dedup-
                                                  local-instructions, growth-discover-
                                                  packs, growth-extract-new-instructions
      packs/product-wiki/run_daily/               wiki-growth.mjs + .worker.md
      packs/tidy-repo/run_daily/                  repo-tidy.mjs + .worker.md
      packs/chrome-extension-release/run_daily/   store-release.mjs + .worker.md
    
    Verified equivalent BEFORE deleting, per pack, by reading both sides:
    
    - product-wiki and tidy-repo: tasks/*/task.md is a superset of the retired
      worker doc — every method step, stop condition, delivery rule, tracking rule
      and never-clause survives, re-pointed at the executor and the task's declared
      outcome ceiling. tidy-repo's task.md deliberately drops only the one-time
      "Repo Tidy Tracker" rename block, which was written as temporary ("drop once
      the fleet has converged").
    - basics: NOT a prose superset, by design. The nightly refresh was re-split at
      Phase 1 — the mechanical converge/notes/stamp/delivery moved into
      tasks/baselining/worker.mjs as agent_preprocessing, and task.md is now only
      the residual judgment stage. Every clause of the old worker doc is accounted
      for on one side or the other. Two clauses are deliberately NOT carried:
      queued-repo ADOPTION (a fleet-central act a repo cannot perform for itself —
      it is sheepdog's census's) and the ENROLLMENT-issue close (Phase 4 step 3's
      own line item, not this one).
    - grow_with_claudinite: all four tasks/*/task.md are standalone and complete.
      growth-discover-packs is a deliberate REDESIGN, not a port — per-repo local
      pack authoring, replacing the central canon-pack pipeline.
    - chrome-extension-release: the retired worker doc's Stage 1 (open a
      release-readiness tracking issue) is superseded, not lost —
      tasks/store-release/worker.mjs now dispatches the gated release workflow's
      daily leg, which absorbed that workflow's own 00:30 cron (decision §11.6).
    
    Nothing had to be ported: no behaviour was found living only in a run_daily
    file.
    
    Cleaned up alongside: the five pack.mjs declarations (the run_daily slot is
    gone — the scheduler discovers tasks/<name>/task.mjs structurally),
    product-wiki's freshness check whose fix text named a deleted worker doc, the
    warning-suppression and capture-log comments, and the prose across README.md,
    extending.md, packs/README.md, the pack READMEs/RULES, the merge-to-main,
    generate-project-instructions and unattended-agents skills.
    
    Tests updated to the new reality rather than dropped: the retired descriptors'
    gate tests are re-expressed as PRECONDITION tests beside their packs
    (packs-tests/basics/tasks.test.mjs and the grow/product-wiki/tidy-repo/
    chrome-extension-release files, +20 tests net), and each pack test now asserts
    pack.run_daily is undefined as a drift guard. routines/fleet/plan.test.mjs now
    encodes the real consequence: with no canon-pack descriptors left, the central
    planner emits nothing for a member and only the home's own local-pack promote
    unit for the canon.
    
    Deliberately left standing:
    - routines/auto-all-repos-maintenance.md and the whole routines/fleet/ tree —
      removing the central routine is a separate owner-gated decision (it is this
      migration's rollback) and is not authorized here. CONSEQUENCE, stated plainly:
      its planner now enumerates nothing from the canon packs; the only tasks it can
      still assemble are an unmigrated repo's own local-pack run_daily descriptors.
    - the run_daily/tasks alias and the local_packs dual-root scan (both inside
      routines/fleet/), untouched.
    - .claudinite/local/packs/canon-curation/run_daily/ — a LOCAL pack, outside this
      change's scope. Worth a follow-up: the canon repo declares taskScheduler, so
      the central planner skips it anyway, and tasks/growth-promote/ already exists.
    - in-session-github-access's run_daily/ path match — still load-bearing: a repo
      not yet cut over has its local packs' run_daily descriptors planned into an
      MCP-only session. A new test pins the other side of that boundary (a task's
      agent_preprocessing worker.mjs keeps its GITHUB_TOKEN legitimately).
    - docs/per-project-scheduling/ and migrations/active_migrations/ — history, not
      rewritten.
    
    Verified: 728/728 tests pass (708 before), check_the_world 0 blocking /
    6 advisory — the same six pre-existing file-placement advisories as the
    baseline — and check_the_work clean.
    
    Refs #394
    
    Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
    Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_01LgokEeqgbFvhbLqbYwxHgx
    
    * Delete the central fleet routine and its planner machinery
    
    Phase 4 step 2 of the per-project-scheduling migration. The previous commit
    retired the canon packs' run_daily/ folders but deliberately left the central
    machinery standing as a rollback. The owner has overruled that — no rollback
    scaffolding, no half-measures — so this deletes the old mechanism outright.
    
    Deleted, with the evidence each was dead:
    
    - routines/auto-all-repos-maintenance.md and the whole routines/fleet/ tree
      (plan, registry, local-tasks, schedule, gates, signals, scheduling.md,
      DESIGN.md + four test files). Nothing outside routines/ imported any of it —
      every remaining mention was prose. And the planner could not have planned
      anything: its Phase 0.6 cutover guard skips any repo declaring `taskScheduler`,
      and all twelve fleet members carry that key (read directly from each repo's
      .claudinite-checks.json — Claudinite, GCEC, TLDR, CrosswordChat,
      HelloWorldFlutterApp, LaughCounter, gRatio, VascularColoring, Sheepdog,
      EdFringeNow, EdFringeAllocator, ShoutsAndWhispers; Empty carries no Claudinite
      config at all). The guard died with the planner it guarded.
    
    - The `local_packs` dual-root scan (readLocalTasks read both
      .claudinite/local/packs and the pre-rename .claudinite/local_packs). Dead on
      both arms: the only two members with local packs — GCEC and EdFringeNow — hold
      them under the canonical local/packs root with tasks/, not run_daily/.
    
    - The `run_daily`/`tasks` alias needed no code to begin with (MIGRATION.md's
      as-built note: task conversions were additive, so both trees simply coexisted);
      it retires with the tree that read run_daily.
    
    - .claudinite/local/packs/canon-curation/run_daily/ and its promote.md worker.
      tasks/growth-promote/{task.mjs,task.md} is the live counterpart: same
      participant filter, same `promote: false` opt-out, same declaration-cardinality
      argument. Four clauses lived only in promote.md and were moved into task.md
      first — the mis-placed-code-comment disposition, the post-stub-mint scope
      ceiling ("note them for the owner"), "not a sub-issue" in the tracker bullet,
      and the no-padding prohibition on a minted stub.
    
    - packs/grow_with_claudinite/{extract,dedup,discover-packs,conversation-extract}.md
      — duplicate prose with no invoker since their run_daily descriptors went.
      extract.md and conversation-extract.md were strict subsets of their
      tasks/<name>/task.md, so they went as-is. dedup.md and discover-packs.md were
      NOT: their live-only prose was moved into the task docs first — dedup's whole
      **Strips** bullet (the only definition of a strip anywhere), the *only*
      qualifier and no-growth constraint on **Rephrases**, and the never-grow-an-entry
      bullet that dedup-prune-integrity exists to enforce; discover-packs' anti-
      inference and comprehensiveness rules, the three-axis assignment rule and
      load-bearing-dependency filter, the per-item manifest schema with its `?` flag,
      the "a stub counts as homed" clarification, and the sharpened no-padding rule.
      The "superseded, kept for its method" banner went with discover-packs.md — a
      banner on a dead file is the hedge, not a fix.
    
    Referrers untangled rather than left dangling: dedup-integrity.mjs's and
    promote-scope.mjs's `doc:` fields now point at the live task docs, as do
    extracting-lessons.md, canon-curation's README/item-routing/growth-promote task
    doc, and engine/checks/DESIGN.md. reference-integrity went 43 blocking → 0.
    
    Also swept: README.md and extending.md now describe the per-repo scheduler and
    executor instead of the planner/orchestrator pair; the CI test glob drops
    routines/*/*.test.mjs; gha/no-scheduled-fleet-executor's doc: moves to
    packs/basics/scheduled-tasks.md and its pre-cutover branch no longer claims a
    fleet routine owns the schedule; the two file-placement acceptances for deleted
    planner files are gone, as is `routines` from the barriers core-root list.
    
    in-session-github-access loses its `run_daily/` scope arm: the previous pass kept
    it for "a repo not yet cut over", which is no longer true of any repo. Its test
    is replaced by a drift guard asserting run_daily/ is NOT scanned.
    
    docs/per-project-scheduling/ keeps its references to everything deleted here —
    it is the record of this migration, and rewriting it would falsify it. That is
    now an explicit reference-integrity acceptance rather than an unexplained gap.
    
    Tests: the four routines/fleet/*.test.mjs files were deleted with the machinery
    they covered (45 tests — a test for a deleted planner is not worth preserving).
    Every test covering surviving behaviour was updated, not dropped:
    promote-scope.test.mjs's fixtures moved off routines/ paths, and
    in-session-github-access.test.mjs's moved onto migrations/ ones. 683/683 pass
    (728 before), check_the_world 0 blocking / 6 advisory (the same six pre-existing
    file-placement advisories as the baseline), check_the_work clean, and the vendor
    set computes with no errors at 130 files (134 before — exactly the four deleted
    grow_with_claudinite worker docs; every live tasks/<name>/task.md still ships).
    
    NOT deleted, and why: the CCR trigger "All Missing Bulb Repos - Daily
    Maintenance" (trig_01QYoJT8c74LtPjVMaXhUu3s) is still enabled and its prompt
    names routines/auto-all-repos-maintenance.md. Deleting it is Phase 4 step 1, not
    step 2, and it is account infrastructure rather than repo content — so it is left

{"number":1541,"title":"Promote canon curation into a canon pack","body":"Closes #1537

The canon home's curation duties move from `.claudinite/local/packs/canon-curation/` to `packs/claudinite-canon-curation/`, generalized so **any** repo hosting a shelf of packs can declare them. `hidden`, `seededByDefault: false`, no fingerprint — a canon home is a role somebody assigns, so the pack is declared by hand, the way `claudinite-fleet-sheepdog` and `claudinite-canary-repo` are.

## What generalizing actually took

- **The write surface.** `promote-scope` hardcoded `packs/` + `skills/`; this tree has no top-level `skills/`, so half that pattern matched nothing. It is now the `packs/` shelf (structural — the engine reads a canon's packs from there) plus whatever the new optional `write_paths` config adds, read by the pack's one config reader.
- **The skill check's relevance gate.** It gated on `engine/pack_loader/pack-registry.mjs` being *tracked*, which only the engine's own home satisfies. It is now anchored on a pack tree, which no repo without a shelf has — and the fixture that asserted inertness did so vacuously (its violating text did not match the matcher), so that test was rewritten to assert the anchor.
- **`pack-version-bumped`'s `doc:`** pointed at `docs/versioned-updates/DESIGN.md`, outside the vendor set; it now points at the pack README, and the local-pack roots come from the engine constants instead of a third copy.
- **`item-routing.md`'s Routing section** described `always/` and `tasks/` folders and a root `CLAUDE.md` index — a layout this corpus abandoned. It now routes to a pack on the shelf, read from the catalog and each pack's `ruleRoutingGuidance`.
- **The prose** speaks of *a* canon throughout.

`growth-scope-gate.mjs` was home CI wiring for another pack's rule, not curation — it moves to the `claudinite` local pack, and promote's gate gains the same shim shape (`promote-scope-gate.mjs`), so the pack owns the rule and the home owns the invocation. That is also what keeps core CI from naming a pack.

## `generate-project-instructions` moves too

That skill decides whether a project's insight becomes a pack **every repo can declare** — a fleet-wide call, and it was shipping to every member declaring `claudinite-growth`, so a repo could read a method for extracting a canon pack out of itself. It moves to the curation pack, beside the two stages that apply it.

The move makes parts of its text false, so those changed with it: the trigger no longer fires on a member's bootstrap; step 5 states the residue the canon *leaves behind* rather than instructing a session to author it; step 6 drops the member-session delivery clauses for one that says to write nothing in the project. `prose-to-checks` pointed at it for "the full rule" and now states what it needs, and `packs/README.md` no longer says a project adopts the local-pack structure by running the skill — adoption seeds it.

## claudinite-growth loses its cross-pack mentions

The growth pack described the promote stage's gate — where it writes, which module certifies it, which repo invokes it. Those are that stage's details; re-spelling them in growth only gave them somewhere else to drift. All five are **deleted**, not repointed, and growth's own reasons are stated standalone (its CLI exits 0 without a merge-base because it runs on every PR, not by contrast with a gate that doesn't).

`extending.md` states the core/pack boundary, so which pack contributes the `pack-independence` barrier is content the doc has no business naming; the mechanism — barrier data, never checking code — is what it keeps.

## Consumer safety

A **`canon-home` rehearsal fixture** — a second canon, declaring this pack over a `packs/` shelf of its own, converging green. `consumer-safe-change` fires because the diff adds blocking rule modules under `packs/`, and its two answers are a migration record or a fixture; this change is genuinely additive (an undeclared pack is not even vendored, and nothing seeds this one), so the fixture is the honest one. It is also the only executable evidence for the requirement, since the canon home always satisfies these rules and therefore proves nothing about anyone else. Verified by mutating the fixture's shelf prose and watching the rehearsal go red on `pack-no-enforcement-narration`, then restoring.

## Verification

- `node --test $(git ls-files '*.test.mjs')` — 2851 pass, 0 fail
- `check_the_world` — 0 blocking; `check_the_work` — 0 blocking; self-test — 5 probes pass
- both CI gate shims run from their new paths

## Folders touched

| Folder | What changed there |
|---|---|
| `packs/claudinite-canon-curation/` | the promoted pack: manifest, the new `canon-config.mjs` write-surface reader, the generalized `promote-scope`, both fleet tasks, three checks, `item-routing.md`, and the two skills it now bundles |
| `packs/claudinite-growth/` | `generate-project-instructions` leaves; five mentions of the promote stage's gate removed; `prose-to-checks` states its own rule instead of pointing out of the pack |
| `packs/claudinite-tasks/` | dispatch test's fabricated pack name follows the rename |
| `.claudinite/local/packs/claudinite/` | both CI gate shims now live here, beside the repo's other home-only wiring |
| `vendoring/rehearsal/` | the `canon-home` fixture shape |
| `.github/workflows/` | the two gate steps point at the shims |
| `dev/tools/tests/` | badge-id example path follows the move |

{"number":1674,"title":"claudinite-canon-curation owns the shelf: pack-facing rules and the entry-await check leave the claudinite local pack","body":"Closes #1673

## The split

The `claudinite` local pack keeps what is Claudinite's own: the project's scope and standing decisions, working with the owner and the session's tools, the engine, the mount, the queue and what reaches members, and this repo's test and branch discipline. `claudinite-canon-curation` now owns everything about the packs on a canon's shelf.

**Moved into `packs/claudinite-canon-curation/RULES.md`** (27 rules, its first prose file, grouped under five headings): the `barriers` decision for the `packs/` tree, pack naming (surface-named kebab-case, the `claudinite-` prefix), reading an unmounted skill from the tree, cross-pack prose paths, never quoting a corpus total, pack config defaults and the JSON-Schema decision, no shared logic between sibling packs, pack modules (import-light and no top-level await, namespace-import a new engine export, what a pack that fails to load costs), every check-authoring rule (catalog row and re-run on main, `fix` text, no prose in a declaration, transcript pseudo-turns, Stop-hook fixtures, `doc:` pointers, two signals, sibling surfaces, path-pattern scope, directory names, earning its keep, stacked-PR bumps), and the two prose rules (RULES.md instructs rather than describes; mechanize a re-derived procedure). Their eleven `references.md` entries moved with them, renumbered in the new file's own namespace. Two rules lost a clause that named the pack's own checks, which its narration rule forbids in prose.

**Moved with them:** the `pack-discovery-entry-await` world rule and its test. The `canon-home` rehearsal fixture gains a CLI module inside the shelf pack's own import graph, in the safe `run().catch(…)` form, so the rule's silence on a second canon is rehearsed rather than assumed — and mutating that module to a top-level `await` turns the rehearsal red on exactly this rule, in both modes.

**Dropped rather than moved:** "Deciding whether a line earns its place in `RULES.md`" — `writing-pack-prose` already carries that test.

**Left local, deliberately:** the distribution-model decision (engine code is one of its options), the check-vocabulary naming rule (the vocabulary is the engine's), the legacy-tolerance annotation and its check (its file set spans `engine/`), "create the artifact a check will demand" (session discipline, not authoring), the pack-rename map and engine-shim rules (engine), the version-encoding rules (the engine defines the scheme), `home-seeded-packs-declared` (this repo's hand-maintained declaration under the engine's home gate), and the whole scheduled-tasks section — the task contract's home is `writing-tasks` per those rules' own portable markers, and the queue lessons are executor operation.

Both manifests' `ruleRoutingGuidance` says the new boundary; the pack README carries the rule index and the new check row; `packs/README.md`'s row and the generated rules index follow.

## Verification

Rebased onto `main` after #1680 resolved the `claudinite-growth` version collision this branch had briefly carried a port for; that commit is gone. On the rebased head: the two version tests, the rule index test and the moved rule's own tests pass, and `check_the_work` and `check_the_world` both exit clean. The full suite on the pre-rebase tree passed everything except that collision and the fielded-imports test refusing a shallow clone, which is that test guarding itself.

+++ b/packs/claudinite-canon-curation/RULES.md
+# claudinite-canon-curation — authoring and policing the packs on a canon's shelf
+
+## Naming and placing content on the shelf
+
+- **Wanting a rule about what the `packs/` tree may reference** — declare and configure the
+  `barriers` pack, extending it generically if a capability is missing. Never standalone
+  segregation-checking code.
+
+- **Naming a new canon pack** — kebab-case, named for the surface it serves rather than the first
+  feature you are building for it. The directory name is the public id every member declares, so
+  another casing costs a fleet-wide rename.
+
+- **Naming a pack whose subject is a Claudinite feature itself** — the `claudinite-` prefix
+  (`claudinite-lifecycle`, `claudinite-dashboard`). `claudinite-growth` is grandfathered.
+  (convertible → prose-to-checks) (1)
+
+- **Looking for a skill and not finding it in `.claude/skills/`** — read
+  `packs/<pack>/skills/<name>/SKILL.md` out of the tracked tree. Mounting filters on the literal
+  declaration, so an unmounted skill says nothing about whether its procedure applies. (2)
+
+- **A canon pack's prose naming another pack by literal path** — check the name resolves inside
+  every consumer's vendored tree. `.claudinite/local/packs/<pack>/` exists only in the canon home,
+  so naming a home-only local pack dangles everywhere else it mounts.
+
+- **Wanting to state how many checks or rules the corpus has** — don't. `packs/README.md` states
+  how to count them instead of quoting a number. (3)
+
+## Pack config and shared logic
+
+- **Choosing a value right for nearly every project** — keep it in the pack's own code: ask
+  nothing at adoption, write nothing into member config. Read config as optional; unset means the
+  default, never "misconfigured".
+
+- **Wanting a `.claudinite-settings.json` entry's config validated** — a real JSON Schema the file
+  points at with `$schema`. Never a coded per-pack validation vocabulary or a `configSchema` type
+  system on the manifest. (4)
+
+- **Wanting to share logic between two sibling packs** — never `engine/`, which breaks the
+  package-manager model, and never a pack-to-pack dependency, which breaks independence. Prefer
+  self-describing data; else duplicate, possibly with a drift guard. (5)
+
+## Pack modules and the engine they load against
+
+- **Adding a module under `packs/`** — keep it import-light, and start work after evaluation
+  completes (`check(…).catch(…)`), never in a top-level `await`. Discovery imports every
+  `pack.mjs` before activation is consulted, so a CLI entry point re-imports mid-evaluation and
+  Node exits 13.
+
+- **A pack module consuming a brand-new engine helper export** — import the engine module as a
+  namespace and guard the call with a `typeof` capability check, never a named import: the pack and
+  engine lanes deliver on separate cadences, so a named import of an export the member's engine
+  hasn't reached yet is a link-time `SyntaxError` that faults the whole pack.
+
+- **A pack that fails to load** — it fails the mount's self-test, the converge refuses to land at
+  all, and the member cannot receive the pack version that would have fixed it.
+
+## Writing and keeping checks
+
+- **Adding or changing a check** — update the pack's catalog row, and re-run the suite against
+  current `main` before merging: a whole-tree aggregate is judged post-merge, so a branch's own
+  green never covers it.
+
+- **Writing a check's `fix` text** — name only remedies matching the enforced severity; sessions
+  follow the words, not the `severity` field. An advisory's remedies are act on it or leave it,
+  never a config-acceptance escape.
+

**The roster carries two questions** because they are asked of the same repos from the same walk.

doing so, removed the last thing that looked at a member from the **outside** — self-maintenance
cannot detect its own absence. What is split is the two **issue families** — they close on unrelated
conditions — not the walk.

own entry for that pack — and why `seeds-agree` holds the two to each other.

{"number":190,"title":"firebase pack: detect a firebase.json one directory down (project-root layout)","body":"## Why

The `flutter` and `node` packs already fingerprint their marker at the **repo root OR one directory down**, so a monorepo that nests them (`app/`, `functions/`) is detected. The `firebase` pack was left on an **exact repo-root match** — `ctx.tracked.includes('firebase.json')` — so a repo that groups its Firebase project into a dedicated `firebase/` subfolder went undetected and needed a per-repo `pack-declaration` acceptance to stay honest.

That subfolder layout is legitimate and common: the Firebase CLI locates the project by walking **up** to the nearest `firebase.json`, and resolves every path inside it (`functions.source`, `firestore.rules`, …) **relative to that file** — so the project root can be a subfolder with no config edits. A **Firebase project root is the directory that holds `firebase.json`, not necessarily the repo root.**

(Surfaced by `missingbulb/ShoutsAndWhispers`, which just moved its Firebase files into `firebase/` and hit exactly this gap — the near-root detection covered its `flutter`/`node` markers but not `firebase`.)

## What

- **`packs/firebase/pack.mjs`** — replace the exact-root match with the same `hasMarkerNearRoot` helper `flutter`/`node` use: `firebase.json` at the root or one dir down matches; anything deeper (a fixture/example tree) still doesn't. Marker string and header comment updated to match.
- **`checks/test/pack-detect.test.mjs`** — extend the existing four detection cases (root / one-down / too-deep / no-marker / non-basename) to cover `firebase` alongside `flutter` and `node`.
- **`packs/firebase/RULES.md`** — update the "Deploy layout" bullet: the project root may be the repo root **or** a dedicated subfolder; note the CLI's upward search and relative-path resolution so a subfolder needs no path edits.

## Verification

- `node --test checks/test/*.test.mjs` → **84 pass, 0 fail**.
- `node checks/run.mjs` (corpus self-checks) → exit 0.

Once this lands, consumers that nest their Firebase project (like ShoutsAndWhispers' `firebase/`) auto-detect the `firebase` pack and can drop the firebase acceptance from their declaration.

{"number":451,"title":"prose-to-checks: convert the firebase deploy-layout rules to checks","body":"Daily `prose-to-checks-sweep` run, 2026-07-26. Tracker: #450 (`Claudinite tracker: Prose to Checks`).

Swept the Context's pack paths (`packs/`, `.claudinite/local/packs`) for **existing** prose that was always testable but never converted. Two rules in `packs/firebase/RULES.md` §4 cleared the check-the-world test in `engine/checks/DESIGN.md` — each constrains a static signature in the repo artifact — and no existing check covered either (deduped against `check_the_world.mjs --list`; the firebase pack shipped zero checks).

## What converted

| New rule | Severity | Asserts |
|---|---|---|
| `firebase/functions-node-pin` | blocking | a deployed functions codebase's `package.json` declares `engines.node` |
| `firebase/functions-predeploy-build` | blocking | a codebase whose `package.json` declares a `build` script wires that build as a `predeploy` hook in `firebase.json` |

Both **parse rather than grep**, per the skill: `firebase.json` is parsed (`functions` as one object or an array of codebases; `source` defaults to `functions` and resolves relative to the config's *own* directory, exactly as the CLI does), and the shared reading lives in `packs/firebase/lib.mjs`.

Both are **relevance-first**: silent until the repo carries a `firebase.json` at the pack's marker depth that declares a functions codebase whose `package.json` is in this checkout. A rules-only or hosting-only Firebase repo, and a nested `examples/*/firebase.json`, are all untouched.

## See-it-fail

`packs-tests/firebase/pack.test.mjs` — 13 fixtures. Neutering both `run()` bodies reds exactly the six violating-input tests and leaves every clean and false-positive-guard case green; restored, all 13 pass.

FP guards covered: no `functions` block; codebase absent from the checkout; nested example config; project root one directory down; a plain-JS codebase with no build script; per-codebase judgment in a multi-codebase project.

## Prose trimmed to rationale

The check owns enforcement now, so the two mandates leave `RULES.md`. What did **not** convert stays: the smoke-load-the-built-entrypoint practice (kept, reworded around its rationale) and the `functions/lib/` + `.firebase/` gitignore guidance. Pack README and the `packs/README.md` catalog count updated.

## Verification

- Full offline suite: 675 tests, 0 failures.
- `node engine/checks/check_the_world.mjs`: 0 blocking (6 pre-existing `file-placement` advisories under `engine/scheduler/`, untouched by this change).

Outcome ceiling for this task is `open-pr` — **not** merged and auto-merge **not** armed; a check can break CI or misfire, so this is for the owner's review.

{"number":908,"title":"The remaining conversion tranches: work scope, field-named scan sets, and the value-set consumers","body":"The rest of the conversion order in #880, after #891 / #895 / #896: tranches 4 and 5, plus the re-judgment of what is genuinely left.

## Tranche 4 — the work-scope vocabulary

A declaration may carry `scope: "work"`: it judges the **change**, not the repo, and gains three assertions over surfaces `work.mjs` already exposes.

| assertion | reads | converts |
|---|---|---|
| `checkBranchCommits` | the branch's commit messages since the base | `task-lifecycle` |
| `forbidIntroducedMergeCommits` | merges this change introduces (never the base's own) | `squash-merge-history` |
| `forbidAddedValueInArray` | a parsed array's values, head against base | `cer/permission-added-store-issue` |

Scope stays a *placement* decision: a coded rule's scope is the manifest list it sits in, and a declaration — which has no list — states it, with the registry routing declared specs into `worldRules`/`workRules` so `normalizeManifest` still stamps the one answer.

`forbidAddedValueInArray` compares **sets**, never the text diff — appending a JSON array element re-touches the line above it (the trailing comma), which is exactly why the coded rule read the base.

Side effects worth naming:
- `packs/chrome-extension-release/lib/manifest-permissions.mjs` is deleted with its sole consumer; the four permission keys are now spelled in the two declarations that watch them, with a drift-guard test holding them equal.
- Both converted messages had to come down to the `declared-check-messages` discipline the coded rules never faced.
- `ruleTester` now invokes through `runRule`, so a work-scoped rule gets its fluent surface in a test exactly as in a run.

## Tranche 5 — a third `scanFiles` form: files named by a parsed field

`scanFiles` took a regex or an exact path; it now also takes an object that reads the file set out of **another parsed document** — `inParsedFilesMatching` (+ `whereFileContains`), `namedByField` (fanning out over an array met along the path, `defaultingTo` standing in where an entry omits the name), and `withSuffix` for a field naming a directory. Names resolve against the **naming file's** own directory, and a name pointing outside the run's file set is dropped silently.

The assertion half: `checkParsedFiles`' `everyScannedFile` (read the scan set as documents) and `requireFieldMatching` — `requireField` for the case where a field present but blank is still not a value.

Converts, modules deleted: `web-speech-no-window-api-in-service-worker` (the file an MV3 manifest names as `background.service_worker`, MV3-gated, authored source only — its skill now carries declarations alone, so `checks.mjs` goes too) and `firebase/functions-node-pin`. `firebase/lib.mjs` stays: the predeploy rule still reads the config's own arrays.

## What I did NOT land, and why

Two items from the plan's tranche 1 do not survive contact with their rules:

- **`matchAnyValueOfSet` has no faithful customer today.** For `python-optional-import-top-level` the value set is only half the check: the dist→import-name mapping is a *transform* (`-`/`.` → `_`), and deciding which token of `from a.b import c` is the package is import-statement semantics, not a word-bounded alternation — `from mypkg import tensorflow` would flag. That is precisely the class-C failure mode the rule exists to avoid. For the two narration rules the forbidden-id set is harvested **per scanned file's directory**, which the value-set pair scopes per rule (v2, as the design already noted).
- **`requireFieldValueInSet` for class E's enum slice would add a reader, not remove one.** `task-declaration-shape` stays coded either way (cross-field conditionals), so extracting `FREQUENCIES` from `slots.mjs` by regex leaves the module's own import in place and creates a second, weaker reader of the same source.

The `configSchema` manifest seam — the plan's other named surface — is now #911, as its own issue.

## Verification

`node --test $(git ls-files '*.test.mjs')` after each tranche (1827 pass, 0 fail); `check_the_world` on the whole tree at 0 blocking. Each conversion authored red-first against the coded rule's own fixtures, with the module deleted in the same commit.

{"number":1081,"title":"Pack reorganization: two collapses and two renames","body":"Closes #1079.

Four pack-tree changes, plus the one engine mechanism a rename turned out to be missing.

**`github-actions` → `git-github`.** The pack held the workflow-YAML rules and the scheduling skill, kept apart from the git/GitHub procedure they are the platform half of by a fingerprint that was redundant: every `gha/` check already selects its inputs from `.github/workflows/`, so a repo with no workflows heard from none of them, and a repo with workflows had to declare a second pack to be told so. Nine checks (not one — the issue said so), the skill and the routing move; the `gha/` ids stay, because a member's `accept` entries name rules by id. `static-website` stops naming it in `requires` — git-github arrives through `basics` on its own.

**`firebase-release` → `firebase`, as the `create-release-plan` skill.** The release standard was a second declaration a project added once it decided it was ready to ship — content read at one moment in a project's life, which is what a skill is for.

**`canary-probe` → `claudinite-canary-repo`** and **`sheepdog` → `claudinite-fleet-sheepdog`** — the prefix a pack carries when its subject is a Claudinite feature.

**The engine half.** All four go through `RENAMED_PACKS` plus a declaration-converging record, as the last two renames did. What was missing is the other side of a rename: vendoring replaces a tree per declared id, so the directory a pack used to be vendored under matched nothing afterwards and stayed in the mount forever — announcing, once the loader canonicalized it, the *same id* as the live one. The pack flow now sweeps it as a property of renaming, so no future rename has to remember to.

The enforcer's config is the part a rename can genuinely break, because it is a fact the enforcer wrote and a declaration converges on its own schedule: the fleet-config reader, the dashboard's legacy-source lookup and the two dormant fleet-baseline records all match the entry through the rename map, and the legacy `packConfig` key is still read under the spelling it was written with.

## Folders touched

- **`packs/git-github/`** — gains `declared-checks.json`, the `github-actions-scheduling` skill, the collapse record; manifest and README rewritten around them.
- **`packs/firebase/`** — gains `skills/create-release-plan/` and the collapse record.
- **`packs/claudinite-canary-repo/`, `packs/claudinite-fleet-sheepdog/`** — renamed from `canary-probe` / `sheepdog`, each with its rename record; the sheepdog config reader now resolves either spelling.
- **`packs/claudinite-dashboard/`** — its legacy enforcer-entry lookup resolves either spelling.
- **`engine/pack_loader/renamed-packs.mjs`** — four new entries. **`engine/scheduler/`** — three comments stop naming the pack (the new id is hyphenated, so the barrier sees them).
- **`updates/pack-update.mjs`** — the abandoned-mount-directory sweep.
- **`dev/tools/badges/render.mjs`** — `restyle` takes a badge's id from its path, so a rename no longer leaves the old name in the title and gradient id with the tool reporting nothing to do.
- **`packs/{basics,chrome-extension,claudinite-*,headless-browser,macos,static-website,web-scraping,app-store-release,play-store-release,android,ios,tidy-repo}/`** — routing guidance repointed at the surviving pack, version bumped.
- **`.claudinite-checks.json`** — this repo drops its `github-actions` declaration; barrier exceptions follow the renames.

## Verification

`node --test $(git ls-files '*.test.mjs')` → 2249 pass, 1 fail: `every engine module a fielded pack version imports still resolves`, which aborts on `this checkout is too shallow to walk origin/main's pack history`. It fails identically on unmodified `main` in this sandbox and needs a depth-0 fetch, which CI does.

`check_the_work` and `check_the_world` are both clean (0 blocking).

content.text: {"number":1575,"title":"Recover the rationale #467 cut from the shared packs into references.md","body":"Follow-up to #1567, which did this for the local pack. Same question asked of the **shared canon packs**. Closes #1571 ## What the history actually shows Mining every commit that shrank a still-standing canon rule found **49 shrink events, 43 on rules that still stand**. They resolve to one seam and two false positives: | Commit | Verdict | |---|---| | **#467 `2f3e4e9a`** — "Tighten every RULES.md to when + what + one non-obvious fact" | The only genuine seam | | #853 | **Relocated, not lost** — the text lives at `git-github-advanced/SKILL.md:44` | | #451 | **Converted** — became the `firebase/functions-predeploy-build` check, whose source quotes the removed sentence | #467's own commit message states what it cut: *"consequence prose arguing for a rule rather than enabling it"*. That was July 2026 — **before a `references.md` existed to hold it** (the convention landed in `a13cf4e2`, three commits ago). So recovering it doesn't undo the owner's decision, it completes it: every rule line stays exactly as #467 left it, and the reason moves to the doc built for it. The same message confirms the incident narratives and `#NNN` citations were shed from **the local pack only** — which is what #1567 already recovered. The canon's losses are pure rationale. ## What was recovered — 25 entries across 8 packs Only clauses carrying a **failure mode, cost, frequency, or authority** — something a review can actually weigh. A few of the stronger ones: - **spec-driven-product** — *"An agent that adjusts the expected has quietly transferred ownership of the product to itself."* - **firebase** — the create/merge asymmetry recorded as *the single most common way* a correct-looking ruleset rejects every legitimate write (a frequency claim, which is what earns the rule its place). - **leaflet** — attribution is a licence term: OSM's tile-usage policy requires it, so stripping it breaks the licence. - **html** — the cost argument: *a console read costs the user seconds, a deploy-and-check cycle costs a whole release.* `spec-driven-product` RULES-3 turned out to cross-link `packs/basics/references.md`'s `(writing-tests-1)` (#429) — the same coverage-gate lesson from the other side. I verified that key exists and says what I claim before citing it. ## What was deliberately not recovered - The leaflet **`Grounded in `** notes. #467 cut them for a stated good reason (they restate the rule and point at one project's tree from a project-agnostic pack), and `writing-pack-prose` independently rejects point-in-time code pins. Restoring them would re-import the exact class the convention rejects. - Restatements of the instruction, and hedges that change nothing a reader does. Nothing is invented where nothing was recoverable. ## Verification Three claims are verified **empirically**, not just by provenance — jsdom 30.0.1 on Node v22.22.2: - ✅ `body.innerText` → falsy, so the fall-through to `textContent` is real. **Precision note recorded**: the value is `undefined`, not `null` as the rule's wording says. Behaviour unaffected. - ✅ `

{"number":1647,"title":"A skill opens on what to do, not on what the skill is","body":"Closes #1646

The RULES.md sweeps' shape, applied to the skills against `writing-pack-prose`'s test: a `SKILL.md` may carry procedure at length, but every line must still change what the reader does. Twenty-two openings didn't.

**Self-description dropped** — "This skill is that contract", "This doc gives a portable rule for judging that placement", "Portable, project-agnostic practices for …", "The **artifact** half of lesson extraction". The reader loaded the skill deliberately and its frontmatter description is already in context. Where the opening was carrying an instruction inside the description, it stays as instruction: `file-placement` now opens on how to judge placement, `writing-tasks` on writing against the queue, `improve-comments` on reading the slice as comments.

**Pointers to prose the reader already holds dropped** — "the standing rules live in this pack's `RULES.md`", "general engineering practices live in the basics pack's RULES.md". A mounted skill means a declared pack, so those rules are loaded; the sentence sends nobody anywhere. Pointers to *other on-demand* skills stay (`repo-text-sweeps` → `git-github-advanced` for merge-time relocations, `authoring-agent-docs` → `writing-pack-prose`), because those change which doc gets opened next.

**Provenance dropped** where the pack README already carries it (`firebase/create-release-plan`, checked before removing).

No procedure, decision point or rule was touched. Every touched pack bumps its version with a `VERSIONS.md` row.

Suite 3104/3104, `check_the_work` clean.

content.content:
# Version history

Records for `packs/firebase/pack.mjs`'s `version` field, one row per version, newest first.
A version is cut on `main` after its changes land, so a row names the pull requests that
landed between the previous version and this one; the weekly history task writes the rows
a version is missing and leaves every row that already stands.

| Version | Date | What changed |
|---|---|---|
| 60920.1 | 2026-09-20 | Provenance: the marking pass, every rule marked and every references.md converted (#2178) |
| 60913.1 | 2026-09-13 | Claudinite: pack version history (#1730); State a rule's prose size as a band, not an exact word count (#2009) |
| 60903.2 | 2026-09-03 | The security-rules rules move into the new `firestore-security-rules` skill (forced for `**/firestore.rules`, `**/storage.rules`), the function-side limits and the smoke-load into the new `firebase-functions` skill (forced for `functions/**`), and the deploy layout into `create-release-plan` (now forced for `firebase.json`, `.firebaserc`); `RULES.md` shrinks to the five always-on rules (#1662). |
| 60903.1 | 2026-09-03 | A skill's `SKILL.md` opens on what to do, not on what the skill is: the self-describing framing and the pointers to prose the reader already holds are gone. |
| 60902.1 | 2026-09-02 | `RULES.md` drops the descriptive framing the pack README already carries — the file carries rules only. |
| 60901.1 | 2026-09-01 | Recovers the rationale #467 cut from six rules into a new `references.md` — the merge-semantics frequency claim, token-vs-body identity, why rules are tested empirically, and the `.firebaserc`/timestamp/smoke-load failure modes (#1571). |
| 60822.1 | 2026-08-22 | The manifest stops restating its own tree (#1246): `id`, `prose`, `badge`, `skills`, `worldRules` and `workRules` are resolved from the pack directory and an absent `detect`/`marker` means no fingerprint. Coded rules move into `worldRules/`/`workRules/` and tests into `test/`, which no vendor set ships. `minEngineVersion` rises to the engine release that reads all of it. |
| 60821.1 | 2026-08-21 | This pack's inline version-history comment moved out of `pack.mjs` into this file. |

content.content:
-- **Wanting a rule about what the `packs/` tree may reference** — declare and configure the
-  `barriers` pack, extending it generically if a capability is missing. Never standalone
-  segregation-checking code.
-
-- **Choosing a value right for nearly every project** — keep it in the pack's own code: ask
-  nothing at adoption, write nothing into member config. Read config as optional; unset means the
-  default, never "misconfigured".
-
-- **Wanting a `.claudinite-settings.json` entry's config validated** — a real JSON Schema the file
-  points at with `$schema`. Never a coded per-pack validation vocabulary or a `configSchema` type
-  system on the manifest. (7)
-
-- **Wanting to share logic between two sibling packs** — never `engine/`, which breaks the
-  package-manager model, and never a pack-to-pack dependency, which breaks independence. Prefer
-  self-describing data; else duplicate, possibly with a drift guard. (8)
-
-## Authoring packs, prose and checks
-
-- **Writing anything into a pack's `RULES.md` that describes rather than instructs** — how a
-  mechanism works, or what the pack's own tasks do — not there, where every session in every
-  declaring repo pays for it whether or not it is that session's work. Description belongs in the
-  module header and the pack `README.md`; a worker's policy belongs in the `task.md` it loads.
-
-- **Deciding whether a line earns its place in `RULES.md`** — the test is whether an agent could
-  act differently for having read it.
-
-- **Having a deferred direction, blocked proposal or status to record** — `docs/`, pointed at from
-  the issue or PR. Never a pack file: `docs/` is outside the vendor set.
-
-- **Naming a new canon pack** — kebab-case, named for the surface it serves rather than the first
-  feature you are building for it. The directory name is the public id every member declares, so
-  another casing costs a fleet-wide rename.
-
-- **Naming a pack whose subject is a Claudinite feature itself** — the `claudinite-` prefix
-  (`claudinite-lifecycle`, `claudinite-dashboard`). `claudinite-growth` is grandfathered.
-  (convertible → prose-to-checks) (18)
-- **Looking for a skill and not finding it in `.claude/skills/`** — read
-  `packs/<pack>/skills/<name>/SKILL.md` out of the tracked tree. Mounting filters on the literal
-  declaration, so an unmounted skill says nothing about whether its procedure applies. (20)
-
-- **Adding or changing a check** — update the pack's catalog row, and re-run the suite against
-  current `main` before merging: a whole-tree aggregate is judged post-merge, so a branch's own
-  green never covers it. (portable → `merge-to-main`)
-
-- **Wanting to state how many checks or rules the corpus has** — don't. `packs/README.md` states
-  how to count them instead of quoting a number. (21)
-
-- **Writing a check's `fix` text** — name only remedies matching the enforced severity; sessions
-  follow the words, not the `severity` field. An advisory's remedies are act on it or leave it,
-  never a config-acceptance escape.
-
-- **Wanting prose in a check declaration** — there is none. `packs/<pack>/declared-checks.json`
-  holds no `description` and no comment; the line the agent reads is `failureMessage`.
-
-- **Writing a check that reads the session transcript** — screen the harness's plain-text
-  pseudo-turns, not only tag-wrapped ones. `humanText` in
-  `engine/checks/helpers/session-transcript.mjs` drops an entry starting with `<`, so a marker
-  like `[Request interrupted by user for tool use]` reads as the owner's latest comment. (22)
-
-- **Fixturing a check that fires at the Stop hook** — carry an interruption marker beside a real
-  owner turn. A false positive there spends a whole cycle on something no edit can clear. (23)
-
-- **A doc reached only by following a link out of `RULES.md` or a check's `doc:` line** — if it is
-  a how-to wanted at authoring time, convert it into a skill invocable by description.
-
-- **Moving or renaming a file a check's `doc:` field points at** — grep for and re-verify every
-  `doc:` by hand. Nothing opens the field until the check fires, so a stale pointer sits broken
-  indefinitely.
-
-- **A check built to catch a thing being missing or misnamed** — don't gate its relevance on the
-  single signal it exists to validate, or the failure it catches also silences it. Use two
-  independent signals, either sufficient. (24)
-
-- **Deciding whether an enforced check still earns its keep** — measure its blocking-firing rate
-  against what it buys. A check whose firings are dominated by cases where the agent already did
-  the right thing is a demotion candidate (check → prose-only). (25)
-
-- **A documented multi-step procedure the agent re-derives every run** — mechanize it into a
-  script the agent runs once. That pattern, not the doc's polish, is the signal.
-
-- **A canon pack's prose naming another pack by literal path** — check the name resolves inside
-  every consumer's vendored tree. `.claudinite/local/packs/<pack>/` exists only in the canon home,
-  so naming a home-only local pack dangles everywhere else it mounts.
-
-- **Adding a module under `packs/`** — keep it import-light, and start work after evaluation
-  completes (`check(…).catch(…)`), never in a top-level `await`. Discovery imports every
-  `pack.mjs` before activation is consulted, so a CLI entry point re-imports mid-evaluation and
-  Node exits 13. `pack-discovery-entry-await` enforces the await half only.
-

{"number":618,"title":"Claudinite growth: extract lessons","body":"Growth extract over the window in **#613** — commits `b56a15c`, `6f109e9`, `a76c355`, `710a07d`, `b08baeb`; merged PRs #595, #608, #607, #596, #604. Writes only this repo's own local packs. Armed for auto-merge (squash) — no review requested.

## Added (1) — `.claudinite/local/packs/claudinite/RULES.md`

**A guard over the WHOLE tree is not merge-safe — never merge a rule-adding PR on a green from before `main` moved.**

A guard whose input is the *diff* conflicts when two branches disagree; one whose input is the *whole tree* does not — so both branches are green against their own base, merge cleanly, and `main` lands red with neither PR having done anything wrong. `packs/README.md`'s corpus tally is exactly that shape, and adding a rule means updating two hand-maintained numbers there (the pack's catalog row *and* the corpus tally), only one of which is guarded.

The window's own evidence: #607's suite ran **once**, at 05:30 against its own base, and it merged 12.5h later at 18:07 — by which time #606 had landed its own check and bumped the tally. #607 had bumped its pack's row and never touched the tally, so `main` went red and stayed red for every PR after it until #608 corrected 68 → 69 as an aside.

**Why prose and not a check:** no repo-side check can judge whether a branch's green predates `main` moving. The one deterministic sliver — guarding the per-pack row's count too — would not have caught this incident (that row *was* bumped), and its column has mixed forms (`0 (2 in its skill)`), so a check there would be low-confidence noise. Ladder lands it at prose.

Flagged as a promote candidate for `git-github`'s `merge-to-main`, which today says nothing about merging on a stale green.

## Considered and deduped away

- **#595's consumer-safe gate** (self-test, rehearsal, canary, `consumer-safe-change`) — the lesson is already the RULES.md bullet *"Green canon CI is not evidence about a consumer"*; what landed is the already-enforced implementation of it, not a new lesson.
- **`--strict` on a report-only SessionStart step discards the hook's stdout** — already a comment at its own call site in `engine/hooks/session-start-command.sh`.
- **A fixture sweep inheriting the canon's cwd reports on the wrong repo** — already a comment at its call site in `packs-tests/rehearsal/fixtures.mjs`' driver.
- **#596 / #604 / #608** — canon pack prose and docs; nothing non-portable to this repo's own local packs.
- **Touched issues #609 / #336 / #568** — scoping and triage notes, no durable lesson.

## Tests

`node --test $(git ls-files '*.test.mjs')` — **1101 tests, 0 failures.**

{"number":720,"title":"Claudinite growth: extract lessons","body":"The growth lifecycle's capture stage for slot `d2026-08-09` — both halves over the window bound by issue #711. Two lessons landed, both as prose in `.claudinite/local/packs/claudinite/RULES.md` (the canon home's own local pack). Nothing under `packs/` or anywhere else is touched.

## Conversation half — a canon pack's directory name is kebab-case

From the `#567` capture (`2026-08-08T1815Z`, session `68eacdbd`). The convention holds across every pack in the tree except the grandfathered `grow_with_claudinite`, and nothing in the corpus stated it — so `UserPreferencesStore` shipped and cost a whole-pack rename to `claude-code-web-users-support` a commit later, after the owner asked for *"the appropriate casing for pack names"*. The same correction carries a second half worth keeping: name a pack from the **surface** it serves, not the first feature you are building for it.

**Upgrade pass.** This one is convertible: a check over `packs/*/pack.mjs` directory names carries the whole rule, and the fixture was authored and proven red-first during this run (neutering the pattern failed exactly the two violating fixtures). It is not in this PR because registering any new rule moves `packs/README.md`'s check tally, and a growth-extract run writes only its own local packs. The prose names the conversion so the weekly `prose-to-checks-sweep` — whose PR is reviewed and may touch `packs/` — can land it.

## Activity half — the home is the last repo to receive its own stub changes

From `00b29a2` / #704. Every member's nightly converge writes `engine/scheduler/stubs/claudinite-scheduler.yml` into its `.github/workflows/`; the canon has no mount and no converge, so its copy is hand-maintained and drifts silently from the stub it ships. The canon sat on `actions: read` while the stub had carried `write` since store-release, so the CI dispatch POST 403'd and **only** the canon's own fold PR stranded — ten days (#535). The paired test over the two files already asserted the `overrides` input and said nothing about `permissions`, which is why "there is a test covering both" was not the safety net it read as.

## Considered and rejected

The window's merged PRs carry no review discussion at all (checked #567, #690, #691 — all empty), so the richest artifact source was empty by construction. The rules the window's own commits landed (#684 task shelf-life, #693 self-heal, #659 comment history, #668 escalate-once, #687 full-fleet reports) already live in the canon and restating them locally would be duplication. The `comment-classification` Stop-hook finding recurs in nearly every captured log, but the canon rule and its check already exist and fire. Retention prune is not due — `retention_days` is unset, nothing deleted.

Suite: 1334 tests pass, `check_the_world` 0 blocking.

{"number":1006,"title":"Shim the engine paths fielded pack copies still import","body":"Closes #1004.

Forcing Shepherd's converge immediately after #993 merged found this — which is exactly what that force is for. The run went **green** and the stamp **did not move**: [run 32147342762](https://github.com/missingbulb/Shepherd/actions/runs/32147342762), PR missingbulb/Shepherd#45 open and `needs-human`.

```
pack-manifests: the pack in packs/core failed to load:
  Cannot find module '.../engine/scheduler/slots.mjs'
  imported from '.../packs/core/task-declaration-shape.mjs'
```

## The window nothing closes

The converged tree carried the **new engine** beside the **old `core` pack**. That is not a race — the engine lane and the pack lane are separate PRs on separate cycles, and pack delivery is version-gated per pack, so **every member spends a window holding the new engine and an old pack.**

A `packs/` file importing an `engine/` module is therefore a stale caller of an instantly-current engine. This repo already has the rule for the other lane — *"Changing an export in `updates/*` — empty it, never remove it"* — and this is the same asymmetry one lane over.

It is worse than a broken task: a pack that fails to load fails the mount's self-test, so the converge **refuses to land at all**, and the member cannot receive the pack version that would have fixed it. Self-healing is exactly what it takes away.

#974's precondition asked the right question of the wrong callers: *"deleting `run.mjs` strands any member whose workflow still calls it; none does."* True — three **pack files** import it.

## The fix

`slots.mjs` and `run.mjs` return as thin shims over `calendar.mjs` and `github.mjs`, carrying only what a fielded pack version imports, with the retirement condition stated at the definition (read members' stamped `packVersions`; don't guess a release).

`parseOverrides` is the one body that cannot re-export — its home is now a **pack**, and the engine may not import a pack. So it is duplicated, and the drift guard runs both copies over the same inputs rather than comparing text. Where they legitimately differ (the pack's parser ignores prose, because a work item's Context is prose first), the test asserts the difference instead of hiding it.

## The guard

`engine-tests/scheduler/engine-pack-lane-shims.test.mjs` derives which imports are fielded by walking the pack tree's history, so it needs no hand-kept list. Two things it learned the hard way, both pinned:

- **The trunk, not `--all`.** An import that only existed on an unmerged branch is not fielded. Scanning every ref fires on whatever is in flight — which it did on its first run, against #941's branch.
- **It refuses a shallow checkout.** With no history the scan finds nothing and reports clean — a green run proving nothing. CI uses `fetch-depth: 0`; the test now asserts that rather than assuming it.

Watched failing before green: removing either shim turns it red with the module named.

## Verification

2072 tests pass; `check_the_world` 0 blocking. The lesson is in the canon's local pack, beside the `updates/*` rule it generalizes.

Shepherd re-converges once this lands, which supersedes its #45 — and only then is #974's outstanding `fleet-baseline` `DRY_RUN` meaningful, since Shepherd's vendored worker still reads the old channel until it converges.

+++ b/packs/claudinite-lifecycle/updates/engine-update.mjs
@@ -51,15 +51,22 @@ const canonRoot = dirname(dirname(dirname(dirname(fileURLToPath(import.meta.url)
 // The engine half of a vendor set: the engine tree itself, plus the pack catalog,
 // which is not any one pack's — it ships with every mount whatever the declaration,
 // so nothing in the pack flow owns it.
-// MIGRATION TOLERANCE (#1317): the tasks pack rides the ENGINE lane while the legacy
-// `engine/scheduler/` shims exist. The shims re-export that pack, and the two lanes
-// deliver on separate cycles — so shipping them apart hands every member a window in
-// which its new engine names a pack its mount does not carry yet. That is not a stale
-// import a version gate can cover: the old pack version the member still holds imports
-// `engine/scheduler/*` by name, the shim there resolves to nothing, the pack fails to
-// load, and the self-test gate below refuses to land the converge at all — which also
-// means the member cannot receive the pack that would have fixed it. A shim and its
-// target are one unit; the lane that ships one ships the other. Removed with the shims.
+// MIGRATION TOLERANCE (#1317): the tasks pack rides the ENGINE lane. It began as the
+// rule that a shim and its target are one unit — the canon's `engine/scheduler/`
+// shims re-exported this pack, and shipping the two on separate cycles handed every
+// member a window in which its new engine named a pack its mount did not carry yet.
+// That is not a stale import a version gate can cover: the old pack version the
+// member still holds imports `engine/scheduler/*` by name, the shim there resolves to
+// nothing, the pack fails to load, and the self-test gate below refuses to land the
+// converge at all — which also means the member cannot receive the pack that would
+// have fixed it.
+//
+// Those shims are gone from the canon, so what holds this line now is the lane
+// itself: a member that never declared claudinite-tasks carries the pack only because
+// this puts it on the engine lane, and the pack lane would silently stop delivering
+// it. That is a read of the members' own mounts, which no convergence window answers
+// — the expiry register in engine-tests/install.test.mjs is what brings the question
+// back (#1643).
 // @legacy-tolerance advisory:none retire:#1643
 const LEGACY_SHIM_TARGET = 'packs/claudinite-tasks/';
 export const isEngineFile = (rel) => rel.startsWith('engine/') || rel.startsWith(LEGACY_SHIM_TARGET) || rel === PACK_DIRECTORY_FILE;
