{"number":1315,"title":"Cut the local pack's RULES.md to one trigger and directive per rule","body":"Closes #1312

`.claudinite/local/packs/claudinite/RULES.md` carried 63% of this repo's session rule tokens (~11,500 of ~18,300) and had grown ~900 tokens a day over the preceding week.

**8,435 → 5,359 words (37%), 114 → 154 rules.** Session rule tokens ~18,300 → ~14,000.

Two passes, one commit each.

## Pass 1 — the audit method

The `authoring-agent-docs` audit that #760 and #894 ran on `packs/basics/RULES.md`. That one worked by folding clauses back into parent rules; this file barely had that problem, since `growth-extract` already appends one situation-keyed block per lesson. What it had was **per-rule incident archaeology** — issue ids, dates, quoted owner exchanges, the story behind each rule. Removed, per the skill's own line: *"the commit that added the rule keeps them… a rule that reads as a post-mortem with a directive at the top is the wrong way round."*

Three structural changes, each verified against the tree first:

- **Split out** *Creating the artifact a check will demand* — a trailing clause of the mechanize-a-procedure rule, but a reader can arrive at it without that one.
- **Cut** *Writing check-the-work* — `basics` already carries see-it-fail as the ladder rule, and both load in the same session.
- **Cut** *Judging whether a member is fresh* — it **contradicted** `claudinite-lifecycle`, which loads beside it: the local rule said read `ref`, the canon rule rules out `ref` along with `claudinite.updated`, because the versioned flows stamp versions only. Whichever a session reached first decided the answer.
- **Stripped** *Diagnosing a member's maintenance PR that won't land* to the one diagnosis `claudinite-lifecycle` does not already carry verbatim.

## Pass 2 — one trigger, one directive

67 words/rule was still too long, because most rules carried their reasoning inline and several carried two or three situations in one block. A bundled rule cannot be trimmed without losing one of its situations, so this pass splits first, then cuts.

**113 → 154 rules, mean 35 words, median 35, longest 53.** Reasoning is out; measurements survive only where the number *is* the argument (the 81% wall-clock, the 25-of-26 minutes, the 46 truncated test files).

Representative splits: *Landing a change to what members receive* separated from *Forcing fleet delivery* (the second fires once you have already decided to); *Changing an export in `updates/*`* from its retirement condition; the scheduler-workflow rule from where to move the program.

The header now carries the budget, so appends hold the shape:

> Keep each rule near 40 words: the trigger, the directive, and a consequence clause only where the rule cannot be applied without it. Split a rule that carries two situations; the evidence it came from lives in `VERSIONS.md` and the issue, never here.

## Verification

A subject diff is meaningless across a 113 → 154 split, so coverage was checked two ways:

- **Identifiers** — every backticked identifier the old file named, matched against the new one. Twenty missing: sixteen were examples that re-expressed their rule (`ensure_ascii`, `build_vars`, `git stash`); four were load-bearing and restored — the literal `GET /repos/{o}/{r}/collaborators/{u}/permission`, `converge-item.mjs`, `engine/checks/helpers/session-transcript.mjs`, `pack-discovery-entry-await`.
- **Subjects** — every old rule subject matched to a new rule by shared content words. None unmatched.

`check_the_work` clean. `check_the_world` **0 blocking**, 77 advisory (unchanged), none against this pack. Full suite **2,708/2,708**. No line over 100 bytes, clearing the seven that tripped the advisory `rules-line-length`.

## Carried out separately

The `packs/* → .claudinite/local` barrier gap, which was sitting as a TODO inside a rule, is now #1313 with its four still-dangling `canon-curation` references listed.

The header budget binds sessions that read this file. Holding `growth-extract` itself to it is a change to the two extract skills in the canon — a separate PR, not done here.

{"number":1384,"title":"tidy-repo: an improve-comments task and skill","body":"Closes #1383

The comments in a repo's own source were nobody's work. tidy-repo gains a fourth dimension for them — its first task whose subject is the source rather than the repo's GitHub objects — and loses its `RULES.md`.

## The task

`packs/tidy-repo/tasks/improve-comments/` — weekly, gated on a substantive commit in the window, scoped to the files those commits touched (capped at 40, with the remainder named as out of scope rather than silently dropped). It runs the skill and nothing else.

Its precondition also declines while a PR titled `Claudinite tidy: improve comments` is still open, so a second unreviewed sweep is never stacked on the first over files it may already have touched. That is the `wiki-growth` precedent — read from the pending PR itself, so a PR you opened by hand from the branch gates the round too.

`expected_outcome: 'open-pr'`, and I want to flag that choice rather than bury it: the scope gate proves the diff is comment-only, which is what makes the pass safe to run unattended — it says nothing about whether the comments it wrote are *right*, and a confidently wrong comment is the exact failure this task exists to remove. A human reads the words. If you'd rather these land themselves, it is one line in the declaration.

## The skill

`packs/tidy-repo/skills/improve-comments/` — the method. What to fix, in the order the value falls: a comment that says what the code already says (delete — the most common right answer), one that no longer matches the code beneath it, one that narrates the edit that produced it, a dead `TODO`, and a missing why. What to leave alone: a comment you don't understand, a licence header or lint directive, a suppression's inline reason, a published doc comment.

## The gate

`checks.mjs` beside the SKILL.md, blocking, work-scoped, and self-gating on the pass's pinned commit subject — so it is silent on every ordinary branch and costs a declaring repo nothing.

It strips the comments from both sides of every changed file and compares what is left. The permission is **read, never asserted**: a run that quietly renamed a variable while "improving comments" is exactly what this catches, and a run cannot talk its way past a text comparison. Three shapes fail deliberately — a file whose language the parser cannot read counts as code; an added or deleted code file is never comment-only; and a deleted `README.md` is not an improvement to a README.

`commentOnly` and its checkable-extension set move to `engine/checks/helpers/code-scanning.mjs` beside the `stripComments` they were already built on, with the queue's narrow-diff classifier and this gate as the two callers.

## The pack loses its `RULES.md`

Its four bullets described what the pack's own workers do, and each worker already states its policy — in more detail — in the `task.md` it loads at run time. So the prose charged every session in every declaring repo for a description of four unattended runs it is never part of. What the policy *is*, for a human reading about the pack, is `README.md`'s job, and that is where it now lives. Seven canon packs already ship without prose, `claudinite-tasks` among them, so this is a well-trodden shape.

Three tests used `tidy-repo` as their stand-in for "a pack with prose" and now name one that has some. The rules index is regenerated by its generator, not hand-edited.

The canon rule that should have caught this named only "a paragraph that explains how a mechanism works". Widened in `.claudinite/local/packs/claudinite/RULES.md` to the shape that got past it: anything in a `RULES.md` that describes rather than instructs.

A survey of the other packs found no second case — `claudinite-fleet-sheepdog` is the only other `RULES.md` naming its own tasks, and it is the right shape, opening by saying what the pack *is* belongs in its README and this file is what a session there has to get right.

## Verification

- `packs/tidy-repo/test/skills/improve-comments/checks.test.mjs` — 9 cases. Seen to fail on the four blocking ones with the gate's filter short-circuited.
- Two new rehearsal fixtures (`tidy-repo-member`, fresh and stale) prove a member declaring tidy-repo converges green with the new blocking rule mounted — the `consumer-safe-change` answer, and the honest one here since the rule is additive and inert on any branch that is not this pass.
- Full suite: 2753/2753. `check_the_world` and `check_the_work`: 0 blocking.

{"number":222,"title":"Growth promote (2026-07-11): portable lessons into canon","body":"Growth lifecycle **phase 2 (promote)** for 2026-07-11. Reads the fleet's local `.md` docs, generalizes the portable lessons, dedupes against the whole corpus, and routes each survivor to its one owning doc. Tracker: #99.

Origins this run were **gRatio** (research/engineering discipline) and **TLDR** (never-promoted chrome-extension / aws-sam / GitHub-Actions technology gotchas). The mature repos (GoogleCalendarEventCreator, CrosswordChat, HelloWorldFlutterApp) had already tagged their portable rules as canon-owned, so their candidates deduped out; EdFringeNow / EdFringeAllocator import only canon (no local docs).

All landed on **rung 5 (prose)** — each is judgment or platform-gotcha knowledge with no clean static signature authorable-and-fixture-able unattended, matching the existing prose in these packs. One exception is flagged for a future check in the conformance backlog (API Gateway v2 CORS rejecting a `chrome-extension://` origin has a static signature in a SAM template).

### Promoted

**`packs/research-project/RULES.md`** (§11)
- Beat the naive baseline before adopting a more sophisticated/signal-driven method; and a signal good for *visualising/validating* a structure isn't necessarily valid for *defining/gating* it.

**`skills/engineering-practices/SKILL.md`**
- Prove a behaviour-preserving optimisation is *actually* identical (fingerprint outputs + fuzz every branch) before accepting it; leaving a hot path un-optimised on a risk/reward call is legitimate.

**`packs/chrome-extension/RULES.md`** (4 new + 1 fold)
- Multi-account silent refresh needs `login_hint`.
- Tokens at rest: `storage.session` for the token, only the non-secret email in `storage.local`, no refresh-token-at-rest.
- Runtime opt-in host access: `optional_host_permissions` + `chrome.permissions.request()` in a foreground gesture + dynamic `registerContentScripts()` + re-sync on worker start.
- Side-panel open/closed state via a `Port` (no is-open API; `sidePanel.open()` needs Chrome 116+).
- Fold: don't add `host_permissions` merely to reach your own CORS-enabled backend (sharpens the existing CORS bullet).

**`packs/aws-sam/RULES.md`** (10)
- Deploy-role transform/CloudFront scope + masked `ChangeSetCreateComplete failed`; new-account CloudFront verification gate; failed-`CREATE` cleanup (`ROLLBACK_COMPLETE` + orphaned `Retain`); API Gateway v2 CORS rejects `chrome-extension://`; cache-hit-before-authorizer; short-TTL-vs-invalidation cost; bundle-the-SDK + pin runtime; changeset `Replacement: True` data-loss + termination protection; DynamoDB GSI no backfill; custom-header preflight.

**`skills/git-github-advanced/SKILL.md`** (2)
- A workflow definition only takes effect once on the default branch (`pull_request` uses the base branch's files).
- A CI OIDC `sub` is matched case-sensitively by the cloud trust policy (hintless assume-role failure).

{"number":890,"title":"Rephrase the local pack's rules: trigger-keyed, and a third the words","body":"Closes #889.

The home's local pack had grown to 57 claim-first entries over 622 lines and ~8,900 words, most of them a title followed by the narrative of the incident that produced them. Applies the method `authoring-agent-docs` records under **"Shape a rule so it fires"** — the one `basics/RULES.md` was rephrased with.

- **Every rule is keyed to the act that brings a reader to it**, in bold, first: *"Changing an export in `updates/*`"*, *"Judging whether a member is fresh"*, *"Running the test suite"* — findable by scanning the left margin, and firing at the moment the mistake is about to be made rather than describing a state nobody notices.
- **Grouped under the surface each concerns** — standing owner decisions; the owner and the session's tools; authoring packs, prose and checks; the engine, the mount and what reaches members; scheduled tasks; proving a change; editing, branching and merging — instead of one flat 47-item list.
- **Cut to the directive plus what it takes to obey it.** Incident narratives, dates, session ids, issue archaeology and owner quotes are gone; a measured figure survives only where the number itself is the argument (a `Claude_Code_Remote` retry running to 81% of a session's tool wall-clock; a glob reaching 37 of 65 test files).
- **Two entries merged into one block** — the canon-side "read `packs/directory.GENERATED.md`" rule and the member-side one that opened *"The same blindness on the member side…"*. A subject needing a "that" pointing back is a clause, not a situation of its own.

No rule dropped, weakened or strengthened: **57 bullets in, 57 out — 622 lines / 8,870 words → 243 lines / 2,878 words.** Wrapping now also clears `rules-line-length` for this file (34 over-long lines before, plus one in the header).

{"number":1563,"title":"Weekly-task preconditions: dormant members, and the local-pack question nobody needed to ask","body":"Closes #1562

An audit of all nine `frequency: 'weekly'` tasks, against two questions: does the precondition wake on a declared-dormant repo, and does it wake on a repo where nothing it works has moved. Six were already correct (`ci-performance`, `tidy-prs`, `improve-comments`, `growth-dedup` are movement-gated; `wiki-growth` is calendar-triggered by design; `fleet-add-missing-packs` runs no agent). Two findings, and a third that came out of review.

## 1. The fleet signal now reads dormancy

`readFleet` skipped forks, archived repos and the canon but never read `dormant`. A member that declared itself out of the recurring work was still enumerated, still probed, still window-scanned, and still landed in the member list `growth-discover-packs` (weekly, opus) and `growth-promote` (daily, opus) sweep. Every other fleet reader already calls `isDormant` — the signal layer was the one that did not. The skip sits beside the fork/archived ones rather than in each consuming precondition, so a dormant member costs neither an opus sweep nor the per-member probes.

## 2. Nothing asks whether a repo has local packs any more

The first pass here gated `prose-to-checks-sweep` and `rule-revalidation` on `localPacks.present === false`, reasoning that a member which has captured nothing has no `.claudinite/local/packs`. That reasoning was wrong, and the owner caught it: `seedRepoLocalPack` (`engine/converge-wiring.mjs:262`) creates the directory with a `pack.mjs` and a `RULES.md` at adoption, and the nightly deliberately never re-seeds or removes it — *"a repo that deleted its local pack made a real choice."* The seeded `RULES.md` ships carrying `<!-- Nothing yet. The growth lifecycle writes here; so may you. -->`, so a member that has captured nothing reads as **present with an empty corpus**: the gate tested the directory when the thing that is empty is the content.

So the presence question is answered by assumption everywhere, and every probe asking it was pure cost:

- `signals/fleet.mjs` drops the per-member `hasLocalPacks` contents read — one API call per member per collection, on a daily task — and computes the window scan for every declaring member.
- `signals/index.mjs` drops `present` from the `localPacks` signal; `signals/local.mjs` and `signals/context.mjs` drop the checkout probe behind it.
- `growth-dedup` gates on movement alone; `growth-promote` participates a member on its declaration.
- The two gates from the first pass are reverted — both tasks are unconditional again, as they were.

## 3. Not changed: the weekly cadence itself

Splitting the weekly "do-all" sweeps into daily "do-today's" ones was considered and not done. Every weekly task with a repo-side scope is *already* a movement-gated full sweep, and full scope is load-bearing where it exists (`tidy-prs`: a PR verdict is relative to the others, so the mover cannot be judged alone). Against it: `tasks-dispatch` DESIGN §3, #582 (`growth-dedup` moved daily → weekly for exactly this reason), and the standing rule that a precondition firing nearly every night buys noise, not freshness.

## Verification

- Each change written test-first and watched fail: the dormant member was enumerated; the fleet fixture's presence route now throws if anything probes it; the rewritten reachability test goes red when `changedInWindow` is stubbed.
- Reachability pinned end to end in `signal-context.test.mjs` — real checkout → real ctx → the precondition — under both local roots.
- Full suite: `node --test $(git ls-files '*.test.mjs')` → 2913 tests, 0 failures. `check_the_work` clean, `check_the_world` 0 blocking.

{"number":1651,"title":"A task doc opens on what the run does","body":"Closes #1649

Third pass of the sweep (#1625, #1632, #1646), over the 15 `tasks/*/task.md` workers, against the bar `unattended-agents` sets for them: checklist altitude, outcomes and bounds and judgment criteria, a pointer where another doc owns the procedure, a why-clause only where the rule is surprising.

**Stage labelling dropped** — "The growth lifecycle's capture stage", "the growth lifecycle's central stage", "The tidy sweep's fourth dimension, and the only one whose subject is the repo's own source". Each opening now states the act instead.

**Self-justification dropped** — `growth-discover-packs`' "This is the only thing that notices…", "**Why central.**", "The trigger is the weekly anchor and nothing else", "A new canon pack is read by every repo…" (its first paragraph already says the PR is the owner's to approve); `rule-revalidation`'s opening essay on which prose expires, compressed to the instruction plus the one why-clause that motivates it; `prose-to-checks-sweep`'s "Weekly, deliberately" and its comparison with growth-extract, kept only as the scope bound; `growth-extract`'s unattended-vs-in-session blockquote, whose two operative halves are already in *Output* and *What this task must never do*.

**Restated procedure dropped** — `growth-extract` said "the method lives in its skill… don't re-derive any of it here" and then re-derived the prose-to-checks conversion (declaration, rule module, see-it-fail fixture, deletion test) a paragraph later. The step is now its trigger and its scope bound; the skill keeps the method. Its `since:` paragraph likewise keeps the instruction and drops the explanation of the two-week window.

Scope statements, Context bounds, the MCP-only access splits, the never-do lists and the judgment-sharpening why-clauses ("Nothing downstream catches a bad lesson") are untouched. Three packs bump with a `VERSIONS.md` row.

Suite 3104/3104, `check_the_work` clean.

{"number":1779,"title":"Rules to checks with the four-moment mechanisms: 27 bullets retired across basics, the home pack and canon-curation","body":"Closes #1760
Refs #1672

The conversion pass the owner asked for once #1711 landed, bounded to the three packs every session in this repo loads. Method: the `prose-to-checks` skill's triage and deletion test over the inventory's A–D rows (`docs/declarative-checks/rule-inventory.md`, whose basics and home rows now each record their conversion or the reason they stay).

## Accounting (the session summary's estimator, words ÷ 0.75)

| Pack | bullets retired | trimmed | tokens removed | tokens added |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| basics | 6 | 0 | 477 | 0 |
| claudinite (home) | 18 | 1 | 802 | 25 |
| claudinite-canon-curation | 3 | 2 | 206 | 32 |
| **all** | **27** | **3** | **1485** | **57** |

Net −1428 rule tokens on every session here, on top of #1711's −434.

## 1. The deletion test on prose a landed check already covered

Twelve bullets stood beside the guards #1711 landed. Ten go whole (Grep context, wake-up prompt, pipe-tail, pkill; AskUserQuestion cost, bare sleep, GitHub through the shell, `commit -a`, merge of `main`, rules append-only, `git pull`); one keeps only the half no guard sees (reading a tool result the harness saved to a file); and "Waiting on GitHub CI" goes once the shell guard also sees a `Monitor` poll and a command after `do`/`then`/`else` (a keyword counts only after a separator, after the widened anchor denied its own author's heredoc). The retired rules' reference entries key on their checks now.

## 2. New conversions, each with a violating and a clean fixture

| Prose (pack) | Became | Scope · severity |
|---|---|---|
| Filing an issue that belongs under another (basics) | `sub-issue-without-parent` | action · advisory |
| Searching for a tool with ToolSearch (basics) | the `searching-for-a-tool` skill, loaded on any ToolSearch and on an empty result | trigger |
| Recording a migration's plan… never a MIGRATION.md (home) | `migration-record-in-docs` | world · blocking |
| Wanting to verify or read something across members (home) | `cross-repo-verify-line` | action · advisory |
| Wanting to read a public sibling repo (home) | `add-repo-for-a-public-clone` | action · advisory |
| Sending a screenshot rendered from a scratch harness (home) | `scratch-screenshot-caption` | action · advisory |
| Checking whether an actor may trigger… never `author_association` (home) | `author-association-as-permission` | world · blocking |
| Changing an export in `updates/*` (home) | `updates-export-removed` | work · blocking |
| Picking a compact date-encoded identifier (home) | `year-last-digit-rollover` | world · blocking |
| Mutating a file to see a check fail (home) | `checkout-restores-index` | action · advisory |
| Editing a repo's JSON config (home) | `settings-json-reserialized` | action · advisory |
| Naming a new canon pack — kebab-case half (curation) | `pack-directory-kebab-case` | world · blocking |
| Wanting to state how many checks or rules (curation) | `corpus-count-in-prose` | world · advisory |
| Wanting prose in a check declaration (curation) | already covered by basics' `declared-check-spec-keys`; the coverage is now a tested claim, not a reasoned one | — |
| A canon pack's prose naming another pack — the home-only half (curation) | `home-only-path-in-canon-prose` | world · blocking |
| A pack module consuming a brand-new engine export (curation) | `named-import-of-new-engine-export`, a work-scope two-pass over the change's added engine exports | work · blocking |

Every blocking check carries `since: 2026-09-06`, so it advises for two weeks. The vocabulary gains one key, `forbidTrackedPathsMatching` (the mirror of `requirePaths`), with its engine test.

## 3. Attempted and withdrawn

`history-test-shallow-guard` (a test walking git history must guard a shallow clone) fired on six real tests, every one walking the history of a fixture repo it created itself. Fixture history cannot be told from the real repository's by a static signature, so the check is withdrawn and the bullet stays, with the reason on its inventory row.

## 4. Logged, not converted

Twenty-three rows, each with its reason in the inventory. The recurring reasons: the mark needs a fact no input carries (a diff's implied folders, a queue item's issue number, an open PR this session); a literal ban has legitimate hits today (`missingbulb/` in the canon URL and a migration record, `Number(doc.version)` on an integer format); the rule is judgment wearing a form (describes-vs-instructs, "a literal sentence"); or the one sanctioned exception would need a silent `excludeFiles` a declaration cannot explain.

## 5. The Stop backstop is advisory (a design correction surfaced by this work)

Widening a guard mid-session re-judged a call that had already run, and the Stop hook blocked on a finding no edit could clear. The transcript is append-only, so `actionFindings` now records every guard finding at Stop as advisory — the count and the diagnosis — and the hook, where a block still prevents the call, is the one place the declared severity blocks. A denied call's finding says so. The design and the checks README carry the rule.

## Standing hit

`migration-record-in-docs` finds `docs/per-project-scheduling/MIGRATION.md`, the one tracked violation; #1775 retires it into #390 and waits on this PR.

## Verified

Full suite green (3249 tests). `check_the_world` 0 blocking: the new checks fire only on that standing hit. `check_the_work` 0 blocking; its advisories are the `rules-append-only` records of these deliberate removals and the session's own guard firings.

{"number":1822,"title":"Give the three canon-curation PR tasks an automerge policy","body":"Closes #1821

`growth-discover-packs`, `growth-promote` and `upstream-watch` were the only PR-producing tasks on the shelf with no `automerge` policy, so every PR they opened parked for approval by construction — #1762, #1712 and #1685 are all theirs.

I pushed back on this first, on the grounds that each task's `description` says its PR is *reviewed* / *owner-gated* / *owner-approved*. The owner reaffirmed, and the resolution that honours both is a **narrow** policy: a policy is "merge if the diff is exactly this shape", not "merge". The surprising diff still parks.

## The policies

| Task | Policy | What still parks |
|---|---|---|
| `growth-discover-packs` | `under:packs && file-additions`, `under:packs && doc-changes` | any *modification* to an existing pack's code |
| `growth-promote` | `under:packs && doc-changes` | a promotion that ships check code or a manifest change |
| `upstream-watch` | `under:packs && doc-changes` | anything beyond the pack prose it reconciles |

## Measured, not predicted

Each policy was run through the real engine against these tasks' own PRs with `merge-policy.mjs --base <merge-base> --policy …`:

**#1780** (growth-discover, the cloudflare-workers pack) — every file covered, `AUTOMERGE: yes`:
```
covered:under:packs&&doc-changes      packs/README.md
covered:under:packs&&file-additions   packs/cloudflare-workers/{README.md,RULES.md,badge.svg,pack.mjs}
covered:under:packs&&doc-changes      packs/directory.GENERATED.md
```

**#1715** (growth-promote) — parks, correctly: it adds a blocking check (`worldRules/task-worker-restores-main.mjs` + its test) and five `pack.mjs` bumps.

## What actually parks growth-promote

Measuring found the real blocker. `growth-promote`'s task.md line 35 told the run to **bump the `version` of every pack it edited**, and claimed *"the run's own Stop sweep reds on a pack edit that leaves the number alone."*

Both halves are false. `pack-version-bump`'s README is the authority:

> This task is the one writer of that number… **No pull request bumps a version itself, and nothing checks that one did.**

```entry write-rules-against
## 2026-07-08 · born · Add executable-requirements pack; fill the flutter pack stub (#165)
- **Reason:** the create/merge asymmetry was recorded as the single most common way a
  correct-looking ruleset rejects every legitimate client write - a frequency claim, which is what
  earns the rule its place over the many other ruleset mistakes available. A client using
  `set(merge: true)` surfaces the post-merge document, so a key-presence check that is right for
  `create` silently breaks on `update`.
- **Mechanism:** a RULES.md rule, triggered on "Write rules against merge semantics, not just
  creates.".
- **Retire when:** Reaffirm if merge-shaped writes are still the dominant client pattern; retire if
  the project's clients stop using `set(merge: true)`/`update`.
```

```entry guard-field-dereference
- **Reason:** distinct writers legitimately upsert disjoint field subsets of one document, and an
```

```entry server-owned-fields
## 2026-07-08 · born · Add executable-requirements pack; fill the flutter pack stub (#165)
```

```entry _pack
## 2026-07-08 · policy-changed · the fingerprint matches a firebase.json one directory down (#190)
- **Source:** missingbulb/ShoutsAndWhispers, which had just moved its Firebase files into
  `firebase/` and went undetected.
- **Reason:** a Firebase project root is the directory holding `firebase.json`, not necessarily the
  repo root - the CLI walks up to find the file and resolves every path inside it relative to that
  file, so a dedicated subfolder needs no config edits and is a legitimate common layout. Matching
  at the root only left such a repo needing a per-repo acceptance to stay honest. One directory
  down and never deeper is the bound, so a fixture or example tree cannot trip detection; flutter
  and node already fingerprinted that way.
- **Mechanism:** `detect` on the pack manifest, matching `firebase.json` at depth one or two.
```

## PR #393 · 2026-07-22 · Scope-split conformance checks: fluent work context, independent world/work runners
- by @missingbulb · model Claude Fable 5 · refs #392 · pack version 8
- interview-answer-stale (born)

> * Fluent work(ctx) helper: shorter check-the-work rules, cached context reads
>
> Add engine/checks/helpers/work.mjs — a null-safe fluent surface over ctx
> (conversation().ownerTurns().last(), jsonPair, deadLinks,
> danglingReferences, addedLines, branchCommits, introducedMerges,
> filesContaining) — and rewrite the check-the-work rules against it,
> trimming preamble comments to the load-bearing whys. Cache ctx.read and
> ctx.readBase for the sweep: checks are read-only over an immutable
> snapshot, and each readBase was a git subprocess per call.
>
> * Work rules take the work object: scope: 'work' on the rule, runRule dispatch
>
> A rule declaring scope: 'work' now receives the fluent work view as its
> run argument — the signature itself shows the rule judges the change, not
> the repo. runRule (engine/checks/helpers/work.mjs) is the single dispatch
> seam, used by the runner and every rule test; world rules keep the raw
> ctx until a fluent world object lands (future change). The raw surface a
> work rule still needs (files, read, exists, branch, commits, packConfig)
> is delegated on Work, so work rules never touch ctx.
>
> * Split the runner by scope: check_the_world runs world rules, check_the_work runs work rules
>
> The single runner ran every rule regardless of scope, so 'check the
> world' meant 'run everything' and the work-scoped rules had no home of
> their own. Extract the sweep pipeline into engine/checks/sweep.mjs and
> give each scope its own thin entry: check_the_world.mjs runs the
> repo-state rules plus the settings/interview diagnostics (themselves repo
> state); check_the_work.mjs runs the rules judging the current change,
> each dispatched with the fluent work view. A rule's scope ('work' or the
> world default) decides which sweep runs it, in one place.
>
> The Stop gate moves into engine/hooks/stop-command.mjs, which now
> fast-exits then runs BOTH runners (work with the transcript) so the
> session still sees every finding; CI runs both too. Also rename the work
> rules' run argument w -> work and the transcript locals to
> lastOwnerTurn / lastFeatureTurn, and re-home the barriers interview
> exception onto sweep.mjs where the coupling now lives.
>
> * World sweep moves to the test/CI flow; Stop hook runs work scope only
>
> The two scopes fire at different times because they answer different
> questions. The work sweep judges the change in front of the session and
> stays on the Stop hook (per-turn, with the transcript). The world sweep is
> a whole-repo invariant assertion — the shape of a test suite — so it runs
> wherever the project runs its tests, as its own standalone
> check_the_world.mjs step (never a language-specific test file: a non-Node
> consumer's runner can't load one, and the sweep is the engine's own
> always-vendored Node CLI).
>
> stop-command.mjs now runs only check_the_work.mjs — no more running both
> runners every turn. Bootstrap wires the world step into the project's
> test/CI flow, adding a minimal flow where the repo has none. This
> supersedes the original #385 stance (Stop as the whole enforcement
> surface, no consumer CI); the design record, README, bootstrap.md, and the
> adopt-claudinite skill are updated to match, and the canon ci.yml models
> the pattern.
>
> Adds engine-tests/hooks/stop-command.test.mjs pinning that Stop surfaces
> work findings and not world ones.
>

{"number":1890,"title":"claudinite-tasks: roles as folders — src/<role>/, typed world ports, queue/ frozen as ABI","body":"Link **S1** of #1869. Refs #1869 #1478 — this is one link of a longer chain, so it closes neither.

`packs/claudinite-tasks/` was the old flat `engine/scheduler/` copied in whole (#1326): 32 modules at the root, a `queue/` that was both workflow ABI and most of the logic, and REST paths spread over a dozen modules. Every module now sits in the role it plays, and the graph between the roles is enforced rather than described.

## What moved where

| Folder | What lives there |
|---|---|
| `src/contract/` | what a task declares and what it means — `task-contract`, `task-declaration{,-text}`, `task-defaults`, `task-terms`, `task-trailer`, `model-map`, `precondition-policy`, `calendar`, `merge-policy`, `built-in-tasks`, `discover`, `dormancy`, and the new `precondition.mjs` (the seam extracted from the executor) |
| `src/items/` | the work item as data — `work-item`, `leases`, `anchors`, `apply-status`, `read`, `run-record`, `tracker`, `usage-format`, `pr-fields`, and `pick-order` (also extracted from the executor) |
| `src/world/` | the only outward edges — `github.mjs` (the REST client and **every** call site's operation, named), `actions.mjs`, `sessions.mjs`, `git.mjs`, `processes.mjs`, `clock.mjs` |
| `src/signals/` | `index`, `context`, `fleet`, `for-task` (was `queue/signals.mjs`) |
| `src/schedule/` | `run` (was `queue/scheduler-run`), `readiness`, `create-work-item`, `drain-dispatch` |
| `src/execute/` | `loop` (was `queue/executor`), `heartbeat`, `suspend`, `target`, `code-work`, `code-work-run`, `prework-run`, the three env bags |
| `src/session/` | `converge-item`, `verify-outcome`, `record-exec`, `resolve-dispatch`, `validate-dispatch`, `dispatch` |
| `src/deliver/` | `land-pr`, `deliver-generated`, `deliver-pr.md` |
| `src/recover/` | `janitor-rules`, `workflow-failure`, `continuation` |
| `src/adopt/` | `converge-workflows`, `hash-minute` |
| `queue/` | the six frozen entry points as runnable shims, `instructions.md`, `tasks/implement-request/` — nothing else |
| `test/` | mirrors `src/`; `test/sim/` moved only its import paths |

`packs/claudinite-tasks/*.mjs` is now `pack.mjs` alone.

## Enforcement, landed with the tree

Two declared checks in `packs/claudinite-canon-curation/declared-checks.json`, both silent on the moved tree:

- **`tasks-stage-barriers`** — `forbidReferences` beside the existing `pack-independence` edge. `contract/` and `items/` name no stage and no world; `world/` imports at most `contract` and `items`; each stage imports only `contract`, `items`, `world`, `signals` and the stages below it (`execute` → `deliver`, `session` → `deliver`); nothing under `src/` imports `queue/` or `shared-code/`. Every rule's scope is non-empty against the real tree.
- **`tasks-world-edges-live-in-world`** — a line match keeping `fetch(`, `process.env`, `node:child_process`, argless `new Date()` and `Date.now(` under `src/` inside `src/world/` only.

## Deviations from the brief, and why

- **`pick-order.mjs` sits in `src/items/`, not `src/schedule/`.** Both stages ask it — the executor to choose what to claim, the scheduler run for `pickableCount`'s drain gate — and `items/` is the only role both may import. Putting it in `schedule/` would have created the execute → schedule edge the extraction exists to remove.
- **`continuation.mjs` sits in `src/recover/`, not `src/execute/`.** It escalates on `workflow-failure`'s surface, so placing it in `execute/` would have created an execute → recover edge. It is recovery by what it does.
- **`new Date()` is read as the argless clock read.** #1869's *End state* writes `new Date()`; the S1 text writes `new Date(`. Forbidding the latter would have moved `calendar.mjs` and every ISO-string parse into `world/`, which is arithmetic rather than an outward edge. The check forbids the clock read and leaves parsing where it is used; the module header says so.
- **The GitHub port is a module of named operations over the injected `gh`, not yet a bound port object.** Every REST path the pack calls is spelled in `src/world/github.mjs` and nowhere else, which is what makes the edge countable. Converting the *seam* from `gh(path)` to a port object means rewriting every test's fake, which is H1's job (`test/sim/world/`) and would have changed tests here, against this link's own shape.
- **`evaluatePrecondition`'s window arithmetic moved with it.** `defaultWindowMs` / `windowDaysOf` / `DAY_MS` are declaration-derived, so they live in `src/contract/precondition.mjs`; `src/signals/for-task.mjs` republishes them under the names its callers and tests already use.
- **`shared-code/github.mjs` also publishes `src/world/actions.mjs`.** `SCHEDULER_WORKFLOW_FILE`, `EXECUTOR_WORKFLOW_FILE` and `actionRepoContext` moved out of the REST client into the Actions port; the dashboard reads two of them through `shared-code`, so the published surface is unchanged from outside.
- **`isQueueItem` moved from `src/items/read.mjs` to `src/items/work-item.mjs`.** The dashboard loads it in a browser, and `read.mjs` now imports the GitHub port; the decoder is vocabulary, so it lives with the vocabulary and `read.mjs` republishes it.

## Slot-era survivors

`git log main -- packs/` names no fielded importer of `run.mjs` or `slots.mjs`, so both are deleted. That retires the `parseOverrides` drift guard against `claudinite-fleet-sheepdog/param-bag.mjs` with them — `parseOverrides` had no non-test caller and no second copy is left to drift. The shim test's remaining row now watches the frozen `queue/` entry points instead, which is the live version of the same claim. `dispatch.mjs`, `resolve-dispatch.mjs` and `validate-dispatch.mjs` **are** fielded — `executor.md`'s routine runs `resolve-dispatch.mjs`, `shared-code/work-items.mjs` publishes `dispatch.mjs` and the task-janitor's worker imports it — so they moved to `src/session/` rather than retiring.

## Frozen surfaces

The six `queue/*.mjs` are runnable entry points: they import the real module, run its named entry when invoked directly, and **name** what the old path published rather than leaving it to `export *` — which also carries `pickOrder` and `evaluatePrecondition`, the two names that left the executor. `queue/instructions.md` and `executor.md` stay put and address the new homes from a base they derive from their own location (`<pack>` = `<here>/..`). `queue/tasks/implement-request/` did not move: `pathTo()` resolves the task by that literal path, which is written into every adopted issue's machine block.

`shared-code/` stays the published surface, unrenamed, re-exporting from the new internal homes — **no consumer's non-test import changes**. The `consumer-safe-change` rule is discharged by the re-export shims, which is the third answer its own fix text names; no migration record or rehearsal fixture is needed because nothing is removed.

## Exit, read on this branch

- `node --test $(git ls-files '*.test.mjs')` — **3393 pass, 1 fail**. The one failure is `every engine module a fielded pack version imports still resolves`, which asserts `origin/main~50` exists before trusting its history walk; this checkout is shallow at exactly 50 commits, so it fails identically on `main` (verified). CI checks out with `fetch-depth: 0`.
- `node engine/checks/check_the_world.mjs` — silent.
- `node engine/checks/check_the_work.mjs` — silent.
- `ls packs/claudinite-tasks/*.mjs` lists `pack.mjs` alone; the six `queue/*.mjs` are shims.
- `test(` calls across the touched test files: 1157 before, 1157 after.

V1 (#1873) reads this repo's own scheduler and executor runs green from the shim paths once this merges.

{"number":2047,"title":"Scope claudinite-growth to local packs, give the shelf its own tasks","body":"Closes #2044

## The problem

`claudinite-growth`'s sweeps declare `automerge: ["under:.claudinite/local"]`, but a `pack_paths` config entry in this repo's `.claudinite-settings.json` widened them onto the canon shelf. The corpus and the policy therefore disagreed by construction: every canon-side run produced a diff its own policy could not cover, and parked. [#1973](https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/pull/1973) (*"no automerge policy covers a canon-pack diff"*) and [#1974](https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/pull/1974) (`AUTOMERGE: no`) are both sitting on exactly that.

Widening the growth policy would have been the wrong repair — it authorises every member's growth task to write a tree it must never touch.

## What changed

**A pack owns a corpus; a config key no longer names one.**

- **`claudinite-growth` writes `.claudinite/local/packs/` exclusively.** `pack_paths` is retired — from both task docs, the pack's README and `pack.mjs`, `writing-tasks`' example, and this repo's settings entry (now a bare `"claudinite-growth"`).
- **`claudinite-canon-curation` gains the two canon-side tasks**, `canon-prose-to-checks` and `canon-rule-revalidation`, both `automerge: ["under:packs"]`. The corpus is `canon-config.mjs`'s roots — the shelf plus whatever `write_paths` adds — so nothing here names a particular canon.
- **The method moved to where a second caller can load it.** prose-to-checks already had a skill; rule-revalidation's method lived entirely inside its `task.md`, so it becomes the new **`revalidating-rules`** skill. Both skills now state the action and name no corpus — the `task.md` supplies that.
- **`growth-write-scope` widens to all four growth runs.** It already gated extract and dedup by pinned commit title, which is the "applies to the task only" placement the split needs; the two sweeps are now the same write surface, so the corpus's own rule (*widen to the structurally-identical sibling in the same change*) applies. The canon twins title their runs `Claudinite canon: …` so this gate reads them as out of its scope.
- **The boundary is stated as prose** in both packs' `RULES.md`, with `references.md` entries carrying the owner decision behind it.

## Two declaration choices worth a look

- **`canon-rule-revalidation` states no `repo-active`.** Its trigger is a *platform* moving, which no repo-side signal sees, and every declaring member reads the shelf whether or not this repo was touched. The member-side twin keeps `repo-active` because a local pack nobody works with costs nobody anything.
- **Both new tasks use `amend_existing_or_create_new_pr`,** per the standing rule that a run recomputing the whole answer accumulates one PR. Note the existing `claudinite-growth/rule-revalidation` still declares `supersede_existing_pr`, which predates that rule — left alone here rather than widened into this change.

## See-it-fail

- The two new positive cases on `growth-write-scope` were watched red first (`not ok 32`, `not ok 33` — a sweep touching `packs/` went unflagged), then green after the regex widened.
- The refusal case (canon twins not gated) can't be written red, so the guard was mutated instead — `^Claudinite (?:growth|canon):` — watched to bite (`not ok 34`), and restored from the index.

## Verification

- Whole suite: **3551 pass, 0 fail** (`node --test $(git ls-files '*.test.mjs')`).
- `check_the_world.mjs`: **0 blocking**, 173 advisory — all pre-existing `file-placement`, `design-doc-status-banner` and one `rules-line-length` in `packs/node`.
- `check_the_work.mjs`: silent.
- Skills index regenerated with the generator, not by hand.

## Folders this touched

| Folder | What changed there |
|---|---|
| `packs/claudinite-growth/` | corpus fixed to the local packs in both task docs; `revalidating-rules` skill added and rule-revalidation's method moved into it; `prose-to-checks` skill stops naming a corpus; `growth-write-scope` widened to all four runs; boundary rule added to `RULES.md`; `pack.mjs` header states the exclusivity |
| `packs/claudinite-canon-curation/` | two new tasks over the shelf with their declarations and worker docs; counterpart rule in `RULES.md` |
| `.claudinite/` | the growth pack entry loses its `pack_paths` config; skills index regenerated |

## PR #594 · 2026-07-31 · basics: name the path-filtered-conformance trap as a rule
- by @missingbulb · model Claude Opus 5 · refs #590, #592 · pack version 8
- conformance-workflow (born)

> * docs: record the fleet-settings alignment as a future direction
>
> Two repo settings decide whether a member's baselining can deliver at all,
> and converging them alongside the sheepdog freshness sweep would be the
> natural home — a sweep keeps them true where adoption only sets them once.
> It is blocked on credential scope: FLEET_GITHUB_TOKEN is not an admin
> token, and both endpoints require admin on the member.
>
> Recorded in docs/future-directions.md rather than the sheepdog pack's
> RULES.md. RULES.md is injected into every session that declares the pack,
> so it is the wrong place for an idea nobody can act on — a deferred
> direction should cost no context. The new file is documentation only, and
> carries no link from any vendored pack file (a pack reaching into the
> canon's docs/ would dangle in every consumer).
>
> * basics: name the path-filtered-conformance trap as a rule
>
> auto-merge is a queue for CHECKS, so three CI shapes exist and only one
> of them silently fails:
>
>   no pull_request workflow  -> baselining merges directly (#588). Coherent.
>   an UNFILTERED sweep       -> runs, auto-merge lands on green. Correct.
>   a PATH-FILTERED sweep     -> the arm succeeds and no check ever runs.
>

{"number":2045,"title":"Five canon tasks change what they do to their pull requests","body":"Closes #2042

| task | was | now |
|---|---|---|
| `basics/ci-performance` | amend | `fresh_pr`, and declines while its own previous run is parked |
| `claudinite-canon-curation/growth-discover-packs` | amend | `fresh_pr` |
| `claudinite-canon-curation/pack-version-history` | amend | `supersede_existing_pr` |
| `claudinite-lifecycle/update` | amend | `supersede_existing_pr` |
| `claudinite-canon-curation/upstream-watch` | `fresh_pr` | renamed `revalidate-from-source`, `supersede_existing_pr` |

### The new precondition term

(1) gates on the previous run's own state (owner, in session): `last-run-not-parked` holds a task back while its newest run stands at **any** of the four parks, where the existing `last-run-not-failed` reads only the failure one. An unmerged pull request parks on `approval` — not a fault — so the narrower term would let ci-performance stack a second round behind an unanswered one. Re-queueing the parked item is what puts the next run in front of it.

It reads the `park` kind the `runs` bundle already carries, so no collector changed and no caller learned a new argument.

Two readers follow from it:

- `holdsOnFailure` answers true for either term — a declaration holding behind every park holds behind the failure one, and the fleet roster would otherwise call a held lane open.
- The dashboard takes `holdsOnAnyPark` beside it. Without that, a lane parked on approval renders its next calendar anchor while the task silently declines every week, which is the "nothing goes red when a task stops running" failure this vocabulary exists to avoid.

### One thing to weigh on `update`

The amend shape it leaves behind was built around slow member CI: it force-pushed the same branch and deliberately skipped a push whose tree was unchanged, so a member waiting on a long run kept its checks. Under `supersede_existing_pr` every cycle mints a new branch, so a PR whose CI has not concluded within a cycle can be superseded before it does — `pullDisposition` returns `wait`, and `planTarget` supersedes everything that is not `merge`. The compensation is that a green-but-unmerged round is now *landed* rather than rewritten, which is the failure that stranded members before. Worth a look if any member's CI runs longer than a day.

### Verification

- The term's test was written first and watched fail on the unknown term, then green across all four park kinds and the not-a-park cases.
- `packs/claudinite-tasks` 1102 pass / 0 fail; `packs/claudinite-dashboard` 355 pass / 0 fail, both run directly.
- `check_the_work` and `check_the_world`: exit 0, no blocking findings.

Pack versions and `VERSIONS.md` rows are the canon's own tasks' to write after this lands.

{"number":2176,"title":"Provenance: the mechanism — the grammar, the tool, the checks, the forced skill, the record","body":"**Step 1 of the provenance plan** — it advances #2169 and closes nothing. Automerge policy: `nothing` (engine flow and a contract member files must satisfy). The design is `docs/provenance/DESIGN.md` (#2136); no pack is marked here — that is step 2, the next PR in the stack.

## What lands

**The grammar, once** — `engine/checks/helpers/provenance.mjs`: the entry grammar (`## <date> · <kind> · <one line>`, the closed kinds, the fields, born first, Mechanism where the kind demands it), the slug marker that ends a rule and names its file, how a pack's carriers are enumerated under either root and which file each names, the audit every check composes, and the two codemods: `markPack` (a proposed marker per unmarked rule and guideline, a `body` per skill from its shape, an empty file per carrier — idempotent, writes no entry) and `convertReferences` (each `references.md` key becomes an entry on the element it named, numeric markers become slugs, a workflow skill's numbers leave the step, the doc goes). The promotion reduction (`reduceText`) is here too.

**The member side** — `engine/migrations/registry.mjs` gains `markProvenance`, a named codemod op like `updateTaskSchedulingFields`, and the record `packs/claudinite-growth/migrations/2026-09-21-provenance-marking/` declares it, so a member's local packs are converted and marked at the converge that delivers this growth version, with no session and nobody remembering. The update flows' io gains `remove` for the doc the conversion retires.

**The growth pack** — `provenance.mjs` (`mark [--dry-run]`, `check`, `convert-references`, `append [--changed]`, `reduce [--public]`, `history`; the append reads one entry from stdin, validates it, and refuses one that reads as a secret through the capture scrub); `provenance-integrity` (world, blocking, `since` 2026-09-20: every carrier names a live file, every file parses; empty files and a pack-root `references.md` are advisory branches, the latter the tolerance #2170 retires) and `provenance-change-recorded` (work, blocking: a carrier whose decision-bearing text changed carries its entry, a file only grows, a deleted carrier's file ends `retired`) replacing `references-integrity`; the `changing-pack-elements` skill forced on every pack file under either root (it held my own edits in this session until loaded, which is the mechanism working); the `backfilling-provenance` skill; `writing-pack-prose`'s references section is now the provenance section; the extraction, dedup, conversion and revalidation skills end with the append, revalidation filling an empty file it meets.

**Curation, preferences, the home** — two rules on the shelf (a README carries use, a carrier change carries its entry) and the descriptive-prose rule's new destination; the promote task carries the reduced file and marks the promoted rule; `generate-project-instructions` mints `_pack.md`; the preferences pack's rule and the advisory `preferences-provenance` check (a preference's file beside the store, existence only); the home's rule on a built design doc moves the owner-decision record onto the element's file.

**The boundaries** — a pack-root `provenance/` never vendors (fixture and real-corpus tests; the real-corpus half asserts absence alone until the marking pass creates the folders, then step 2 adds the non-vacuity guard); the barrier grammar gains the `<folder>/*/<name>` carve-out and the shelf's siblings rule carves `packs/*/provenance` out, so a decision log may name what it explains.

## Decisions taken beyond the design

- **The parser and codemods live in the engine, not the growth pack, and the record is the growth pack's, not the lifecycle pack's.** A migration record's vocabulary is closed to named ops shipped with the engine ("one op with one meaning, not a general escape hatch"), so the member-side marking needs an engine op, and an engine op cannot import a pack. The record sits under the pack whose corpus it marks, as `task-cadence-terms` did. The plan named the lifecycle pack; noted on #2169.
- **Every pack importer of the new helper uses a namespace import with a `typeof` guard** — the `named-import-of-new-engine-export` check's ask, since the two lanes deliver on separate cadences.
- **A marker the line cannot hold within 100 bytes goes on a continuation line of its own**, so the marking pass is one appended line per rule and a re-wrap is nobody's.
- **A marker reads at the end of a rule's lead paragraph, before any nested list**, or at the block's end where a rule was marked after its list.
- **The record's version is `60930.1`, past the landing day on purpose**: the bump task cuts the number after the change lands, so a record cannot know it; a value past the landing day keeps the record in range for the first converge after the pack update reaches a member and drops it out once the pack bumps past it.
- **The rehearsal fixture stays on the retired convention** as the record's own test bed: the converge converts and marks it, and the sweep then reads the marked pack.
- **Two `file-placement` advisories on the helper stand deliberately** (it reaches `engine/pack_loader/` for the skill frontmatter and the folder names): the reach is the cross-cutting concern the fix text names, and the helper sits with the check helpers because the checks and the registry are its consumers.

## What the grace window means

Both checks carry `since: 2026-09-20`, so the shelf's backlog — 60 skills with no body, 29 rules files with unmarked rules, 22 `references.md` — reads as advisory in the world sweep until step 2 lands; after 2026-10-04 it blocks. Step 2 is the next PR in this stack.

## Validation

- Suite: 3797 tests pass, the new ones red-first (the helper, the registry op, the CLI, both checks, the preferences check, the vendor set, the barrier grammar).
- Work sweep: silent. World sweep: 0 blocking, 664 advisory — 428 of them the new check's own grace-window findings above, the rest main's.
- Hook latency: no hook changed.

> * Declarative checks review: generality, messages, conversion scope, performance, technology survey
>
> The five-question review #838 commissioned as a document: measured census
> and sweep timings, vocabulary consolidation targets, message discipline,
> the per-rule conversion audit's verdicts, the two engine quick boosts, and
> the linter-field survey with per-tool verdicts and embeddability conclusion.
>
> * Declared-check vocabulary: file classes, skill self-exclusion, fix default, comment-blind scan, key validation
>
> Five authoring facilities the review (#838 $4/$2) called for, all additive:
> scanFileClasses/excludeFileClasses name shared file sets instead of
> hand-repeated regexes; a skill's declarations structurally exclude the
> skill's own content in every mount shape; a rule-level fix is inherited by
> assertions that don't override it; scanIgnoringComments reads the
> string-aware comment-blanked view so a comment naming a forbidden token
> never fires; and every spec key at every level is validated against the
> vocabulary at load, so a typo'd key throws instead of silently asserting
> nothing.
>
> * The five jwt rules are declared checks
>
> The review's cleanest conversion (#838 $3): all five rules were one
> mechanism — select non-test source, gate on the library import, bail on an
> escape word anywhere in the file, flag matching call lines — which is
> exactly scanFileClasses + excludeFileClasses + whenFileMatches +
> unlessFileMatches + matchLines. The rule modules, both checks.mjs and the
> pack-local scan.mjs are gone; the skills' declared-checks.json carry the
> rules, and the tests exercise the declared rules through the same fixtures.
> The testFiles class learns the _test.<ext> suffix convention scan.mjs knew.
>
> * Barrier scan: precomputed completion index and per-context shared scan state
>
> The review measured the barrier rule at 274ms — 61% of the home sweep's
> rule time (#838 $4) — with two hotspots: extension/index completion
> probing the tree 23 times per unresolved candidate, and per-edge
> re-extraction of per-line candidates. buildIndex now precomputes a
> completion index (probe order preserved as ranks), and the file lines,
> per-line candidates, and candidate resolutions are cached against the
> context, shared across edges and across every barrier-family rule in one
> sweep. A character prefilter skips lines that cannot hold a candidate.
> Byte-identical findings on the home repo, 284ms → ~180ms, with the
> cross-rule sharing worth more on repos with overlapping edge sets.
>
> * The base-ref refresh runs once per freshness window, not once per run
>
> The fetch is the sweep's dominant wall-clock cost (~0.7s healthy, 8s
> timeout when not — #838 $4), and the Stop hook pays it on every turn with
> tracked changes. A marker in the git dir records which ref was refreshed
> and when; a run within five minutes of a successful refresh of the SAME
> ref trusts it and skips the network. Per-ref on purpose — a fetch of some
> other ref says nothing about this base — and the staleness the window
> admits is the class the fetch's own failure tolerance already accepts,
> now bounded. Measured back to back: 1.21s then 0.53s.
>
> * Merge the parsed-document and index-coverage assertion families
>
> The vocabulary's single-use long tail (#838 $1): checkParsedFile,
> forEachParsedEntry and equalParsedValues were one select-then-assert idea

{"number":1569,"title":"Retire jwt-advisory-watch; keeping a pack current becomes canon curation's upstream-watch","body":"Closes #1568

A pack's `tasks/` are work every **member** repo runs, so `jwt-advisory-watch` charged the fleet for
a duty that is the canon's — and made it unrepeatable: one bespoke watcher per pack that wanted one.
The task is deleted, and the duty moves to the shelf's curator.

## How a pack declares its upstream

An optional `## Upstream` section in the pack's `README.md`, one line per source — what to watch,
where it publishes, and the state the pack's content was last reconciled against:

```md
## Upstream

- **RFC 8725 — JWT Best Current Practices** — https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc8725
  — reconciled through RFC 8725 (BCP 225), February 2020
```

Presence of the section is the whole opt-in, and silence is a legitimate answer — most packs teach
something that does not move on anyone else's clock. The reason a source is worth watching, and what
a reconciliation concluded, stay in the pack's `references.md`.

## The task

`claudinite-canon-curation/upstream-watch` — monthly, opus, `expected_outcome: 'pr'` with
`automerge: 'nothing'`. It greps the shelf for the section, reads what each source published since
its anchor, corrects the packs that were dated by it (bumping their versions), and advances the
anchors — **only** for a source it actually read, so a refused fetch leaves its window open instead
of silently swallowing it. No signal gates it: the trigger lives outside the repo, exactly as it did
for the task it replaces. It reads the shelf and nothing else — no member repo, and no member's
dependency manifests.

A clean month is still a PR: the anchor diff is the record that the shelf was checked, and it is
what windows the next run.

## What this deliberately drops

The retired task scanned a member repo's own lockfiles for JWT libraries sitting inside an advisory's
affected range. That is dependency-update tooling, not pack content, and nothing here replaces it.

Members need no cleanup: a standing work item whose task file is gone converges to
`task:status:rejected` on its next pickup.

## Folders touched

```
packs/jwt/                          the task deleted; the manifest header, README and
                                    VERSIONS row rewritten around the new Upstream section,
                                    which carries the RFC, advisory-database and Handbook
                                    sources with their anchors

packs/claudinite-canon-curation/    the new tasks/upstream-watch/ (declaration + worker doc);
                                    the pack's stated duties widened to keeping the shelf
                                    current, and its version bumped

packs/claudinite-lifecycle/         one adoption-policy fixture re-pointed off the deleted
                                    task's vendored path onto a live one
```

{"number":256,"title":"Pack discovery: a run_daily task that manifests → suggests → populates → opens a canon PR","body":"Closes #251, closes #265.

## The gap

Fleet coverage is measured per **repo** ("does this repo mount Claudinite?"), never per **technology** ("does every technology this repo uses have a pack?"). So a technology a repo uses that no pack covers — a project on Python + Swift + Mac DMG distribution, say — is structurally invisible: its lessons land only in the project's own local docs, no pack home is ever created, and the next project on the same stack re-derives from scratch.

## `growth-discover-packs` — a regular scheduled task, one pipeline

It is an ordinary **`run_daily` task** on `grow_with_claudinite` — the fleet planner picks it up per member on that member's **weekly full sweep** and the orchestrator dispatches it like any unit. **No bespoke central step** (the way `promote` is special-cased outside the plan), no engine change. It still **executes centrally** in the sense that matters: like every worker it runs in the home-repo session with the fleet token, so it reads the member and opens PRs against the **canon**.

For the member it's handed, it runs the whole pipeline end to end:

1. **Manifest** the member's stack — an evidence-grounded catalogue across three axes (**Technologies**, **APIs & external services**, **Deployments & distribution**), each entry citing the file that proves it and marked `core`/`supporting`/`vestigial`. Decides nothing about packs.
2. **Suggest** new packs — check the manifest against the pack shelf; a technology is homed (skip) when any pack owns it (a stub counts), or an open pack-authoring PR exists, or it's `vestigial`. The rest are candidates — **on first sight** (owner-directed posture).
3. **Populate** — author a pack by distilling real rules and checks from how the member actually uses the technology (the worked example), rung-triaged on the promotion ladder (mechanizable rule → check + fixture; nameable procedure → skill; else prose), with a `detect` fingerprint when reliable so it self-declares on future repos.
4. **Open** one PR per authored pack, against the canon.

Steps 1 and 2 stay **distinct levels of analysis** — cataloguing a stack vs. judging whether the canon needs a pack — kept sequential, never conflated.

## Why this shape

- **Central, and conforms to the regular scheduler** (owner-directed). The planner is per-member and skips the home repo; `promote` is the lone central-once task, special-cased. Rather than copy that bespoke wiring, pack discovery is a normal per-member task whose worker executes centrally (fleet token → canon PRs). Over a week the staggered full sweep covers the fleet; a shelf + open-PR check keeps **first sight** from double-authoring.
- **Grounded, never invented** — the member *is* the worked example; every rule is cited, none padded, and no empty stub is opened to fill later. Defers the pack-authoring method to `generate-project-instructions`.

## Files

- `growth/discover-packs.md` — the worker: the four steps, the approved manifest prompt (step 1), grounded authoring, per-pack canon PR.
- `packs/grow_with_claudinite/run_daily/growth-discover-packs.mjs` — the task descriptor (gate on the member's weekly full sweep), registered in `pack.mjs`.
- `packs/grow_with_claudinite/README.md`, `growth/README.md`, `routines/auto-all-repos-maintenance.md` — wiring and the units list.
- `routines/fleet/fleet.test.mjs` — a gate test: weekly-only, `order: null`.

## Verification

`node checks/run.mjs` → exit 0. `node --test` → 165 pass, 0 fail.

Sibling PR **#257** teaches promote's lesson-path to mint into a pack when a lesson's technology has no home (the narrow, lesson-triggered complement).

{"number":242,"title":"Stage 1 spec: code planner for the fleet daily maintenance routine","body":"Spec-only PR (no implementation code yet) — the reviewable Stage 1 design before we build. Closes the design half of #241.

## What this adds

`routines/fleet/DESIGN.md` — the agreed design for turning the daily maintenance routine from "fan an agent out to every task × every repo, decide in-session" into **code decides, agents act**:

- **Task registry of `(gate, worker)` pairs.** `gate` = "should I run" (code, in the planner); `worker` = "what to do" (a doc a subagent runs, fed the gate's `targets`). Pack tasks register via a new **`maintenance: [...]`** field on `pack.mjs`, exactly like `rules`/`skills`/`env` — so a task is `scope: "fleet"` or `scope: "pack:<name>"` and the engine discovers it with no orchestrator edit.
- **The planner runs in code**, in the existing fleet-coverage Action (fleet PAT). The **entire worklist is computed before any worker agent spawns** — a task with nothing to do costs an API read, not a model turn.
- **Orchestrator = the routine session itself** (trigger + dispatch in one run). The planner is the only out-of-process piece; worker subagents are its children.
- **Stateless daily loop** (~25h UTC window) + **weekly full sweep** staggered by `hash(full_name) % 7 == UTC weekday` — ~1/7 of the fleet full-sweeps each night, and that weekly pass is the self-healing safety net (no persisted watermark).
- **Correctness invariants** baked in: landed/implemented tests key off a `mainMoved` signal (not per-object recency), and `canonChanged` excludes the plan/tracker/orchestration artifacts so the engine can't self-trigger dedup.
- **One fleet walk, three outputs** — coverage census + migration-retirement (both existing) + the new work plan. Stage 1 extends `check-fleet-coverage.mjs` in place (it's central-only; a rename would force a canon-wide reference sweep) and factors gates/signals into `routines/fleet/` modules.
- **Proves the pack seam** with `chrome-store-release` as the first real pack task.

## Blast radius

Small: the planner and every gate run **centrally** in the home repo's Action. No consumer executes new code; a member contributes only its existing `.claudinite-checks.json` (read, never written).

## Not in this PR

Implementation (`signals.mjs`, `gates.mjs`, `tasks/`, the pack task, the orchestrator rewrite) — that follows once the spec is approved. Stage 2 (narrow per-object worker skills) is deferred.

## Coordination note

There are related in-flight branches (`claude/chrome-store-release-schedule-*`, `claude/open-branches-status-*`) that overlap this area by name. Neither is merged, and neither appears to have created a fleet-maintenance seam, but worth a glance before implementation to avoid duplicated effort.

Refs #241

{"number":320,"title":"Vendored mount (phase 1): vendor writer, claudinite-isolation check, consumer CI stub","body":"Phase 1 of #315, on top of the merged #317 foundation.

**`mount/apply-vendor.mjs`** — the local vendor writer: converges a consumer's `.claudinite/shared/` to the canon tree the module ships in (whole-set rebuild — stale files vanish, local edits revert; `local_packs/` and everything else untouched) and advances the `claudinite` stamp in the same operation. Errors abort **before any write** — the transactional contract from the design: a failed refresh leaves the repo running its old snapshot. Pulls in canon skills a consumer's own local packs require (via `discoverPacks`), with a CLI for the adoption/refresh flows. 4 hermetic tests.

**`packs/basics/claudinite-isolation.mjs`** — the isolation rule from the design: outside the wiring set (root `CLAUDE.md`, `.claude/`, `.gitignore`, `.gitattributes`, `.github/workflows/`, the settings file, and `.claudinite/` itself incl. `local_packs/`), nothing may reference `.claudinite/`. Composed on the barriers pack's exported engine (the fixed-graph pattern `product-wiki` established), `crossingExcuse` pointing at `accept`. Gated on `.claudinite/shared/` existing, so it is **inert in the canon repo and in every pre-flip consumer** — it arms per-repo as the flip lands. Works because the barrier engine's reference index builds from `ctx.tracked`: vendored files stay resolvable as reference *targets* while `buildContext` keeps them out of scanning. Red-first fixture test (gate off → silent; violating file → blocking finding; wiring files + local_packs → open).

**`packs/basics/stubs/claudinite-checks-ci.yml`** — the consumer CI backstop: 3 steps, running `node .claudinite/shared/checks/run.mjs` from the checkout (full history + real PR head, per the canon CI's own precedent). Inert until the phase-2 flip materializes it into consumers.

**Lessons capture** (`git-github-advanced`) — from this session's merge: a session's app-scoped push to an existing PR fires no `synchronize` CI run (PR-open and merge-API events do fire); gate by running CI's commands locally and rely on the post-merge push run.

**`mount/DESIGN.md`** — phase-1 status, and the refined flip gitignore shape (keep `.claudinite/*` ignored with `shared/` + `local_packs/` re-included, so legacy flat leftovers and a stale environment's stray sync stay invisible).

Full suite green (371 tests), conformance sweep clean. Still open in phase 1 (next increment): the baselining task absorbs the fleet-side vendor refresh; bootstrap.md rewritten fresh-path-only. Then the phase-2 gated flip note (pilot: GoogleCalendarEventCreator) + dual-shape discovery.

{"number":396,"title":"scheduler: due-slot math + schedule config key (Phase 0 groundwork)","body":"Starts the vendored Actions scheduler for per-project maintenance scheduling (#394, DESIGN §2–3, MIGRATION Phase 0). This is the first, pure, well-tested slice of `engine/scheduler/`; **no behavior change** — nothing schedules or dispatches yet.

## What's here

- **`engine/scheduler/slots.mjs`** — the stateless due-slot math the scheduler runs each hour over the Actions run ledger (no watermark file). The whole model: consider only the *single most-recent* scheduled slot per frequency, and it's due iff its time falls in `(lastSuccess, now]`.
  - Misses self-heal to exactly one catch-up per frequency — never a backfill storm.
  - Hourly never backfills (its most-recent slot is always the current hour).
  - First run (no prior success) evaluates every frequency — the fresh-adoption smoke test.
  - Resolves the daily anchor ± offsets (anchor-dated slot ids, including the `daily-2h` hour-wrap when `dailyHour < 2`), the weekly weekday, and the monthly day-of-month with month-length clamping.
  - Pure: `now` and `lastSuccess` are always injected, so due-ness is deterministic and fully testable.

- **`schedule` config key** — added to `CONFIG_KEYS` with load-time range validation (`dailyHour` 0–23, `weeklyDay` Sun–Sat, `monthlyDay` 1–31). Absence is legal (defaults live in `slots.mjs`); its declaration is the per-repo cutover marker for the rollout.

## Tests

- `engine-tests/scheduler/slots.test.mjs` — slot math across the seven frequencies: miss→catch-up, double-run dedupe, first-run, hour-wrap, month-clamp, weekly rollback, hourly no-backfill, the full daily growth chain.
- `engine-tests/context.test.mjs` — `schedule` validation: valid / partial / absent, plus out-of-range and misshaped values.

Full suite green (508 tests) and the conformance sweep is clean for this change (0 blocking).

## Not in this PR (follow-on Phase 0 work)

`run.mjs`, `discover.mjs`, the signal collectors, `dispatch.mjs`, `validate-dispatch.mjs`, `verify-outcome.mjs`, `model-map.mjs`, `executor.md`, the workflow stub, the task-folder conversions, new checks, and the doc rewrites — each lands separately on top of this foundation.

{"number":836,"title":"A `core` pack: Claudinite's own surface, mandatory in every member","body":"Closes #835 (phase 1).

The mount, the pack declaration, bootstrapping, adopting packs and the scheduled-task contract were split across the two packs that happen to be seeded everywhere — `basics` (working discipline) and `grow_with_claudinite` (lesson capture). Neither claims that territory in its `ruleRoutingGuidance`, so a session extracting a lesson about Claudinite itself read both hosts as an honest "no pack owns this".

## The scope, and what it disqualifies

Every rule `core` holds judges a **member's Claudinite status** — is this repo declared, converged, isolated, gated, scheduled. A rule about how the **canon's own content** is maintained is not its, however much it looks like one.

| From | To |
|---|---|
| `basics/` — `claudinite-isolation`, `rules-index-current`, `conformance-workflow`, `scheduler-workflow-shape`, `task-declaration-shape`, `task-declaration-matches-folder`, `task-phase-discipline`, `scheduled-tasks.md` | `core/` |
| `grow_with_claudinite/` — the `adopt-claudinite` and `adopt-pack` skills, the `adopt-requested-packs` task | `core/` |

`catalog-completeness` is the worked example of what fails the test and stays in `basics`: it can only fire in the corpus repo, and what it guards is a hand-maintained index. No rule's id, severity or behaviour changed; the catalog goes 89 → 90, and the one new rule is `core-declared`. `basics` keeps `requires: ['core', 'git-github']`; `barriers` now arrives through `core`, which contributes the isolation wall.

## How "mandatory" is actually enforced

Three facts in three places, held together by `packs-tests/core/mandatory.test.mjs`:

1. **The edge** — `basics` requires `core`. `basics` is seeded everywhere, so its closure is the carrier.
2. **The content** — proven, not assumed: `computeVendorSet(['basics'])` lays down 23 `packs/core/` files, the seed record among them. Nothing else is needed for a member to *have* the pack.
3. **The declaration** — the one thing the closure does *not* carry into a running member. `resolveDeclaredPacks` only materializes a dependency when a declaration is being written, which happens at `--init` and nowhere else; nothing in the update flows rewrites a member's `packs` list, deliberately, since that file also holds its interview answers and every reviewed `accept`. So `packs/core/migrations/2026-08-14-core-seed/` carries it, via the `declarePacks` op — seed-never-override, idempotent. Without it `core` would be mounted and inert, because `isActive` reads the literal list.

**`core-declared` is not what makes the pack mandatory.** Activation reads the literal declaration, so the rule does not run in a member that has no entry — the edge and the record are what put it there, and both run outside any check. What the rule adds is the third state: an entry deleted by hand in a repo whose other packs still hold the declaration open. It reports; it cannot rescue. It ships **advisory** on the `conformance-workflow` precedent (and the #555 failure both are drawn from): blocking would turn every member red on its very next update, before the record has reached it. Promotion is a one-line change, in phase 2.

## What is deliberately *not* here

`basics/tasks/update/` — the self-refresh task. A member runs it from its **vendored** copy at `.claudinite/shared/packs/basics/tasks/update/`, and `discoverTasks` finds only a task whose pack is *literally* declared. Moving the directory before every member's declaration carries `core` means a run that dies between the two writes leaves that member with no update task at all — and nothing left that could deliver it one. Owner decision, 2026-08-14: it moves in a second PR, once the forced fleet pass is read back per member.

## Rebased onto #837

`main` moved under this branch: the declarative-check conversion landed and touched exactly these files — `basics`' manifest, its pack test, and `catalog-completeness`, which is no longer a module. `packs/basics/pack.mjs` was rebuilt from main's version with this branch's edits re-applied rather than resolved line by line; `catalog-completeness` keeps main's shape as a `declared-checks.json` row in `basics`.

## Verification

- `node --test $(git ls-files '*.test.mjs')` — **1656 pass, 0 fail** on the rebased tree.
- `check_the_world` on the canon — **0 blocking, 28 advisory**, unchanged from the base commit.
- `engine/selftest.mjs --strict` — 5 probes pass (both moved skills re-mount).
- `discoverTasks` against the home's real declaration resolves `core/adopt-requested-packs`, 0 errors.
- Rule catalog is 90 and `packs/README.md`'s tally agrees.
- The home declares `core` itself: baselining's backfill is gated `!isHome`, so nothing would ever deliver it here — `mandatory.test.mjs` pins that too.
