{"number":1029,"title":"Rename core → claudinite-lifecycle, grow_with_claudinite → claudinite-growth, and move the scheduled-task contract between them","body":"Closes #1022.

Three moves, landed together because the third only makes sense once the first two have names to move between.

## What changed

- **`core` → `claudinite-lifecycle`.** The pack owns a member's Claudinite *status* — the vendored mount, the declaration, adoption, the self-refresh update — and `core` said none of that.
- **`grow_with_claudinite` → `claudinite-growth`**, kebab-case like every other pack (the underscore spelling was the grandfathered one).
- **The scheduled-task authoring contract moves** — `scheduled-tasks.md`, `task-declaration-shape`, `task-declaration-matches-folder`, `task-prework-env`, `task-phase-discipline`, and the one prose rule that points at the doc — from the first pack to the second. Those five ask whether a task is *written* correctly, which is authoring; every check left behind asks whether Claudinite is *working* in this repo, which is the sentence that pack's README already used to justify all of them.

`claudinite-growth` gains a `RULES.md` for the one rule that came with the contract, so the net prose a session loads is unchanged — it moved, it did not grow.

## The hazard, and what actually handles it

Pack activation matches a declared id **literally**. A member whose `.claudinite-checks.json` says `core` while its mount ships `claudinite-lifecycle` does not get a degraded pack — it gets **none**, and that pack carries the `update` task, so the machinery that would deliver the repair is the machinery that went missing. Same class as #1004: a green run, an unmoved stamp, and no route back in.

A declaration rewrite alone cannot close that, because the rewrite is one half of a two-half converge and any ordering leaves a window. So the load-bearing piece is `engine/pack_loader/renamed-packs.mjs` — one map, every legacy spelling straight to today's, applied at **four** seams where a pack id is read:

| Seam | Why it is a seam |
|---|---|
| `packEntryId` — the declared id | the entry a member wrote before the rename |
| `canonicalPackVersions` — the stamped `packVersions` key | a version under an old key reads as *never installed*, so the install flow re-stamps it at latest having run **no** records in its gap |
| `parseWorkItemTitle` — a work item's `<pack>/<task>` | the title sits on an open issue that outlives any converge; read literally the tick files a second item and orphans the first |
| `discoverPacks` — a mounted `pack.mjs`'s own id | the record moves a member's mount *directory*, but the tree inside is only replaced once the canon ships a version above the one that repo has |

That fourth one is why both renamed packs are bumped past the versions `main` carries: without the bump a member's stamp already satisfies the target, the tree is never replaced, and the mount holds a `pack.mjs` still announcing `core` under a directory named `claudinite-lifecycle`.

Local packs are exempt at every seam — that namespace belongs to the repo, so `local/core` stays `core`.

## The migration record

`engine/migrations/2026-08-19-pack-renames/` — an **engine** record, not a pack one, because a pack record lives under `packs/<id>/migrations/`, which is precisely the directory this change renames. The engine flow also runs before the pack flow in one converge, which is the order this needs: the declaration converges first, the pack flow then reads it and vendors the renamed trees in the same run.

It does two things — moves the stale mount directories (via `aliases`, which fires because the canonical path does not exist yet at that point in the flow), and rewrites the declaration.

The rewrite patterns are deliberately **narrow**. `core` is an ordinary word and an ordinary directory name; a pattern loose enough to catch every spelling also rewrites a member's own `{ "from": "core", "to": "ui/*" }` barrier rule and silently unhooks it. Each pattern can only match a `packVersions` key, an entry object's `id`, or an element of the `packs` array itself. What that misses stays readable anyway via the tolerance above — a trade this record can make and one without that tolerance behind it could not. Both halves are pinned by a test, and the loose-pattern regression was watched failing before the narrow one went in.

## Other consequences

- `core-declared` → `claudinite-lifecycle-declared`. The id named the pack, so it could not survive the rename. Worth flagging: check ids appear in members' `accept` lists, and no alias facility exists for them — this one is blocking-critical and not meaningfully waivable, but it is a real vocabulary change.
- Three test fixtures copied `engine/pack_loader/` file-by-file and broke fail-soft on a new sibling module — mounting nothing and reporting success. They copy the directory now.
- Two reviewed barrier exceptions added, plus `engine/migrations` as a structural carve-out — which the repo's own barriers `goals` text already said it wanted ("migrations/ is deliberately NOT core here"). The one finding on `pattern-rules.mjs` was fixed by deleting the flagged phrase rather than waiving it: a generic engine comment was using a pack name as an example.
- Historical rows in `.claudinite/local/usage.GENERATED.json` keep the old spelling. They are a per-day record of what ran under the name it had.

## Verification

- Full suite: **2132 passing, 0 failing** (`node --test $(git ls-files '*.test.mjs')`).
- `check_the_world`: **0 blocking**.
- `check_the_work`: **1 blocking**, below.
- New assertions were each watched failing first — the legacy-id map, the mounted-stale-id path, and the migration record's narrow patterns.

## The one thing still open

`check_the_work` blocks on `engine-release-record`: **ENGINE_VERSION 5 has no canary rehearsal run.** The bump is not optional — it is what puts the record in every member's gap — so the release gate is correctly refusing until the canary has qualified this tree. Dispatching `canary-rehearsal.yml` against this branch runs a real converge against the canary repo under `FLEET_GITHUB_TOKEN`, which is a world-reaching action, so I have left it for you rather than firing it. Once it passes, its run id replaces `not yet` in the version 5 row.

{"number":783,"title":"The update runner, and the skew guard both mechanisms obey","body":"The last unbuilt piece of #768's Phases 1–3, plus the guard that makes flipping a repo safe. You chose canary-first, and this is what has to land before any flip can mean anything.

**Still inert for every member**: each repo declares no mechanism, is served by baselining, and the new worker exits before it clones. Nothing changes until a declaration says otherwise.

## The skew guard moves into the engine

It was in `updates/`, which is canon-internal and never vendored — so baselining's worker, which runs from a member's own **mount**, could not have read it. A guard only half the system obeys is worse than none, so it now lives at `engine/served-by.mjs` and both sides read one definition.

**Baselining now stands down** for a repo the update flows serve, first thing, before any clone or write. Quiet and agentless: a repo served elsewhere is not an anomaly.

One lag worth naming: a member's worker is only as new as its last converge, so a repo flipped before its mount carries this check keeps baselining for one more cycle. That is the safe direction for the lag to point — it converges twice by the old mechanism rather than falling between the two. **Nothing can be served by both, and nothing by neither.**

## The runner

`packs/basics/tasks/update/` — a task in the same 02:00 slot, with the same two-stage shape as baselining. Its worker clones canon fresh and executes the *clone's* flows, never the mount's stale copies; delivers on a dated branch; and acts on `terminalFor`:

- **merge** → the shared landing helper, per the repo's delivery setting.
- **needs-human** → PR stays open, labelled, run stops.
- **apply-stage** → the agent stage is requested with its brief; nothing merges first.

**Engine before packs, always.** A pack declares the minimum engine it runs on and the pack flow enforces that against what the repo *has* — so running packs first would check every one against yesterday's engine and block updates the very next step would have made legal. And a refused engine update wins the terminal outright: nothing downstream of it is trustworthy, including a pack flow that never ran.

The I/O half is deliberately modelled line-for-line on baselining's rather than improved. That worker is the proven pattern; a cleverer second shape would be a second set of the same bugs.

## Tests

The git-free surface — branch naming, the PR text a human reads when a run stops, and **both halves of the stand-down**, each driven through the real `main()` against a real directory because the property that matters is that they stand down *before* the clone. Plus a drift guard across the seam: every terminal the runner branches on must be one the flows can actually produce.

The clone/push/PR half awaits the live pilot, as baselining's does.

## What has to happen before the canary is flipped

1. This merges.
2. The canary **converges once** so its mount carries the new engine and the new worker. **Its converge is currently broken** — it has been stamped 2026-08-05 for seven days ([Sheepdog#168](https://github.com/missingbulb/Sheepdog/issues/168)) — so that is the real first step, and flipping before it would strand the repo with neither mechanism running a current worker.
3. Then write `maintenance.mechanism: "updates"` into its declaration and watch a full cycle.

## Verification

1541 tests green, `selftest --strict` green, work checks clean, world advisories identical to `origin/main`.

Refs #768

{"number":1285,"title":"prose-to-checks-sweep: guard the mount against edits, at the tool call and at Stop","body":"## Summary

Re-derived against today's `main`. The branch was conflicted and half its content had been overtaken, so this is the sweep run again from the rule inventory's own rows — the worklist this repo's rules name — rather than a fresh reading of the prose.

**The `doc-pointer-resolves` half is dropped as a duplicate.** `doc-pointers-resolve` (declared, blocking, `since: 2026-09-04`, landed in #1675) already covers it. Not reasoned out — tested, as the skill requires: a local-pack rule module was given a broken `doc:` and the existing check fired on it, in the local pack the original PR built its own check to reach. Inventory row 58 named `reference-integrity` as the carrier, which never read the field; corrected and dated.

**Lifecycle rule 1 converts at class D**, the rung the inventory assigns it, in two halves:

- **`shared-tree-edit-guard`** — a declared action guard. It denies an `Edit`, `Write` or `NotebookEdit` aimed inside `.claudinite/shared/`, and the shell writes that reach the same tree (`sed -i`, a redirect, `tee`, `rm`, `truncate`). This is the moment that matters: it stops the write instead of reporting it afterwards.
- **`shared-tree-immutable`** — a work-scope module, the Stop-time backstop for a write no hook saw (a script, a `git apply`, a member running hook-less). It **cannot** be a declaration, which is why it drops off the declared rung: `repo-context.mjs` filters the mount out of the scanned set, so `ctx.changedFiles` never carries a path under it and every path-matching work key is blind there by construction. It reads the branch's own commits instead. The update flow is exempt by the commit title its worker composes — verified against `tasks/update/worker.mjs:236`, where the PR title *is* the commit message.

**The prose stays whole.** The deletion test is binary, and the paragraph carries something neither check does: *where a vendored rule lives*. A guard that only speaks once an edit is already aimed at the tree never answers that. So no `RULES.md` deletion, unlike the original PR.

### What the original PR claimed that this one doesn't

`consumer-safe-change` is discharged with a **rehearsal shape**, not the comment in `fixtures.mjs` the original used. The fixture *failed the rehearsal* before it was right — which is the proof a comment cannot give, since a comment satisfies the check by touching the file. Stated honestly: it shows a member converging green with the new rule riding its mount; it does **not** show the rule firing, because the rehearsal runs `selftest` and `check_the_world` and never `check_the_work`.

Also dropped: the rule module's `runCli` body (no caller here, unlike `growth-write-scope`'s CI gate), and the `pack.mjs` version bump and `VERSIONS.md` rows — a canon pack's version is the canon's own tasks' to write after the change lands, and writing them by hand is what made this branch conflict in the first place.

## Changed folders

- **`packs/claudinite-lifecycle/`** — the action guard added to `declared-checks.json`; the work-scope backstop as a new `workRules/` module; `README.md` gains both check rows and names them on the rule they enforce. Rules discovery is a filesystem scan, so `pack.mjs` needs no entry.
- **`vendoring/rehearsal/fixtures.mjs`** — one new consumer shape, a member keeping its difference in `.claudinite/local/packs/` beside the mount.
- **`docs/declarative-checks/rule-inventory.md`** — lifecycle row 1 → `X` with its carriers and the reason the declared backstop is unbuildable; row 58's carrier corrected; the lifecycle totals row moved.

## Test plan

- [x] `node --test $(git ls-files '*.test.mjs')` — 3398 pass, 0 fail
- [x] `node engine/checks/check_the_world.mjs` — 0 blocking; advisory count unchanged at 102 against `main`, so neither check adds noise to the real tree
- [x] `node engine/checks/check_the_work.mjs` — clean
- [x] See-it-fail on all four negative assertions: the update-flow exemption, the shared-root filter, the Bash match and the `file_path` match were each mutated in turn and the matching test went red, then restored
- [x] The guard's false-positive pass runs the mount the way the corpus really does — `node .claudinite/shared/engine/…`, `grep … > /tmp/out`, `sed -n`, `cat`, and an `rm` of an unrelated path in the same command — and stays silent on all of it

**One thing reviewers should know:** the guard fires on a heredoc that *writes a test fixture* spelling one of the banned commands — it did so on this PR's own test file. That is the form check doing its job on a shape it cannot distinguish from the real thing without parsing shell, and it costs an advisory line, not a denial. Both checks carry `since: 2026-09-06`, so they run advisory in members until 2026-09-20.

Refs #1274

{"number":393,"title":"Fluent work(ctx) helper: shorter check-the-work rules, cached context reads","body":"Closes #392.

## What

Reworks Claudinite's conformance checks into **two fully independent scope runners** that fire at **different times**, gives the check-the-work rules a fluent context, and strips all pack-specific machinery out of the engine runners.

### Fluent `work` context
- `engine/checks/helpers/work.mjs` — a null-safe fluent view over `ctx`. A rule declares `scope: 'work'` and its signature becomes `run(work)`; `runRule(rule, ctx)` is the single dispatch seam. API: `work.conversation().ownerTurns().last()` (null-object turn — no guard ladders), `work.jsonPair(file)`, `work.deadLinks()`, `work.danglingReferences(tolerated)`, `work.addedLines()`, `work.branchCommits()`, `work.introducedMerges()`, `work.filesContaining()`, plus delegated raw surface. Full `work`/`lastOwnerTurn`/`lastFeatureTurn` naming, no abbreviations.
- `ctx.read` / `ctx.readBase` cached per sweep.
- Eight work rules converted to `scope: 'work'` / `run(work)`.

### Two independent runners, no shared pipeline
`check_the_world.mjs` and `check_the_work.mjs` are fully independent — **neither imports the other, and neither names any pack.** They share only two scope-blind mechanism helpers:
- `run-active-pack-rules.mjs` — run the active packs' rules a predicate admits (also attaches the discovered packs to `ctx.packs` for rules that reason about pack metadata).
- `report-findings.mjs` — apply config, sort, print, return the blocking count.

### The engine names no pack
The world runner used to import the adoption-interview machinery from a specific pack — the sole reason for a `barriers` core/content exception. That's gone:
- The generic `questions` **manifest-shape validator** moved into the **pack loader**, so a malformed `questions` field is an ordinary load fault in `packErrors`, reported pack-agnostically.
- The interview **hygiene** (a stored answer whose question its pack no longer declares) is now a **skill-owned world check** in the lifecycle pack's `adopt-claudinite` skill, reading `ctx.packs`. It rides that pack's activation like any skill check — a repo without the lifecycle pack never runs it.
- `--init` no longer prints pending questions (the adopt skill + the SessionStart interview-check step drive the interview).
- The `barriers` exception for `check_the_world.mjs` is **deleted** — and the barrier check actively enforces the boundary (a pack mention, even in a comment, is flagged BLOCKING; verified by mutation).

The world runner's only non-rule work now is **pack-agnostic config/load integrity** (malformed JSON, unknown setting/pack, broken `pack.mjs`, thrown `contributes` seam) — the loader reporting it couldn't assemble its inputs, naming no pack.

### Different timings
- **Work → the Stop hook.** `stop-command.mjs` runs `check_the_work.mjs` only — the per-turn feedback loop, with the transcript.
- **World → the project's test/CI flow**, as a standalone `node …/check_the_world.mjs` step (not a language-specific test file — it's the engine's always-vendored Node CLI). Bootstrap wires it in, adding a minimal flow where the repo has none. **CI runs the world sweep only.**
- This **supersedes the original #385 decision** (Stop as the whole enforcement surface, no consumer CI). DESIGN.md, `engine/checks/README.md`, `bootstrap.md`, the `adopt-claudinite` skill, and the top-level README are updated; canon `ci.yml` models the pattern.

## Verification
- Full suite green throughout: **491 tests** (added `engine-tests/hooks/stop-command.test.mjs`).
- See-it-fail by mutation at each step: `Turns.last`, `danglingReferences`, `jsonPair`, the `runRule` scope dispatch, the Stop-hook work-only behavior, the barrier guard on the work runner's independence, the interview-hygiene skill check running via the runner, and the loader's malformed-`questions` validation each made a check bite; every mutation restored byte-identical.
- End-to-end: on a fixture carrying both a world (`warning-suppression`) and a work (`reference-integrity`) violation — `check_the_world` reports only the world one, `check_the_work` only the work ones, and the Stop hook surfaces only work. `--list`/`--init` intact. Both sweeps run clean on this repo (0 blocking); the world runner names no pack.

Also removed three broken `.claude/skills/` symlinks (pre-#385 layout leftovers).

content.text:
{"number":401,"title":"Pack adoption: interview-in-manifest, adopt-pack skill, enforcing check","body":"Closes #400.

Makes adopting a pack a first-class, interviewed act instead of a per-request improvisation.

## What

- **`adopt-pack` skill** (`packs/grow_with_claudinite/skills/adopt-pack/`) — the narrow flow for turning packs on in an already-adopted member: declare → run each added pack's adoption interview and record answers → re-vendor → scaffold what the pack now demands → land through the review gate. Whole-repo bootstrap/refresh stays `adopt-claudinite`.
- **`adoption-answers-pending`** — a work-scope, blocking check: a pack *newly declared on the branch* must record an answer for every adoption question it asks. Reuses `interviewState` (so `via`-materialized dependencies ask nothing) and only fires for packs added in this branch (a pack already in the base is never re-litigated). This reconciles an enforcing "check-the-work" with the existing design where a *pending* answer is only a mild SessionStart note — nightly/unattended runs never block. Adds `packs`/`config` accessors to the fluent `work` context.
- **`product-wiki` questions** — `product`, `users`, `market`, recorded as intent (the pack takes no config); they scope which wikis get seeded and what the competitor research measures against.
- **`executable-requirements` questions** — `ui_testing` (the UI-test harness / visual-golden path) and `requirements_source` (existing doc / issue tracker / fresh → `config.spec`).
- **`executable-requirements` standard** — two conventions made explicit: the requirement line stays a scannable one-liner with expanded detail collapsed behind a `<details>` block (clean GitHub review), and kind selection favors the **simplest owner verification** — a short test driving to a state plus a visual golden the owner checks by sight — maximizing the share of requirements verified by looking.

## Why

Adopting `product-wiki` without knowing the users/market/product yields a hollow skeleton; adopting `executable-requirements` without deciding the UI-test mechanism and requirements source defers the two choices that shape every requirement. Baking the questions into the manifests and enforcing answers on the adding branch puts the interview where the owner is present.

## Testing

- Fixture tests for the new check: added-unanswered blocks; fully answered is clean; a pack already in the base stays silent; a `via`-only dependency asks nothing.
- Manifest assertions for both packs' new questions.
- Full suite green (556 tests); world sweep 0 blocking; work green.

{"number":594,"title":"basics: name the path-filtered-conformance trap as a rule","body":"`maintenance.delivery: auto-merge` arms GitHub's auto-merge, which is a **queue for checks**. Three CI shapes exist, and only one fails silently:

| shape | outcome |
|---|---|
| no `pull_request` workflow at all | baselining merges directly (#588) — coherent |
| an **unfiltered** conformance flow | the sweep runs, auto-merge lands on green — correct |
| a **path-filtered** flow | the arm succeeds and **no check ever runs** — the PR waits forever |

The third is invisible from every angle: the repo looks like it has CI, `hasPrCi` is true, the arm reports success, and the maintenance PR simply never lands. TLDR sat in it — all three of its test workflows filter to `extension/**`, `server/**`, `dev/requirements/**`, so a mount-only diff matched nothing. The same filters had also hidden two blocking `claudinite-isolation` findings on its `main` for as long as they'd existed (fixed in TLDR#156, which adds the workflow).

## The rule

`packs/basics/conformance-workflow.mjs` — a member should have a workflow running `check_the_world` on **every** pull request, unfiltered.

**Advisory, deliberately.** Shipping it blocking would turn every member lacking the workflow red on its very next baselining — which is exactly the #555 failure mode this rule exists to make less likely: a required thing added to the canon with no path for consumers to comply first. It becomes blocking once the fleet carries the workflow, and the promotion is a one-line change with the reasoning recorded in the file.

Relevance-first on the vendored mount, so it is inert in any non-member. A repo with **no** `pull_request` workflow is deliberately not flagged — that is #588's coherent shape, not a defect.

## Verification

Full CI test set **1029 pass / 0 fail**; `check_the_world` **0 blocking, 9 advisory** (all pre-existing `file-placement`). Ten see-it-fail cases, including the exact TLDR shape, and verified firing against the real TLDR tree before the fix and silent after it. `packs/README.md` corpus tally updated 66 → 67 in the same change, as its guard requires.

Refs #592

{"number":839,"title":"Declarative checks: review document + the implementation it recommends","body":"The #838 review document plus, at the owner's direction, all five implementation bundles it distilled. Eight commits, in dependency order:

1. **Review document** — `docs/declarative-checks/REVIEW.md`: measured census and sweep timings, vocabulary and message analysis, per-rule conversion audit, framework survey (adopt idioms, adopt no tool).
2. **Vocabulary facilities** — `scanFileClasses`/`excludeFileClasses` (shared named file sets), structural self-exclusion of a skill's own content, rule-level `fix` default, `scanIgnoringComments` (string-aware), and full spec-key validation so a typo'd key throws instead of silently asserting nothing.
3. **jwt conversion** — the five jwt rules become two `declared-checks.json` files; the rule modules, both `checks.mjs` and the pack's `scan.mjs` are deleted (~160 net lines out), tests exercise the declared rules through the same fixtures.
4. **Perf** — the barrier scan gets a precomputed completion index + per-context shared scan state (274ms → ~180ms, findings byte-identical), and the base-ref refresh gains a 5-minute per-ref freshness window (1.21s → 0.53s back-to-back; the Stop hook no longer pays the fetch every turn).
5. **Key merges** — `checkParsedFile`/`forEachParsedEntry`/`equalParsedValues` → one select-then-assert `checkParsedFiles`; `listedInFile`/`coveredByGlobLine` → `requireIndexCoverage` with the divergent absence/anchoring semantics declared per entry. Legacy spellings stay accepted (member local packs may carry them; a rename has no fleet carrier) and normalize at load.
6. **Message discipline** — a blocking `declared-check-messages` meta-check (32-word cap per field, no fix repeated within a rule), authored red-first (17 findings), and the rewrite that turns it green. Tally recomputed 89 → 90; the stale basics row corrected.
7. **Barriers rephrase** — the scan engine moves to `engine/checks/helpers/reference-scanning.mjs`; the vocabulary gains `forbidReferences`; the three fixed barriers (claudinite-isolation, product-wiki-isolation, pack-independence) become declared checks in their owning packs, byte-identical findings on the home (minus the `doc` field declared checks drop). The per-repo config rule and the `contributes` seam keep working on the moved engine.

**Consumer safety**: two new rehearsal fixtures/changes — a member whose local pack declares checks in a legacy spelling converges green under the new blocking meta-check; the consumer-safe-change guard was satisfied by fixture (additive change), not record. At merge time, the standing verify-through-a-member rule applies: force a fleet baseline and confirm one member's converge before calling it shipped.

Verification: 1668/1668 tests, world sweep 0 blocking, work sweep clean, barrier-family findings diffed byte-identical against the pre-change baseline.

{"number":949,"title":"Growth promote: 20 lessons from 8 members' local packs","body":"Central promote stage of the growth lifecycle (`canon-curation/growth-promote`), dispatched via #870.

**Targets swept** (per the dispatch's Context — local packs changed in the window): ClaudiniteWebsite, EdFringeNow, GoogleCalendarEventCreator, LaughCounter, MissingBulbWebsite, Sheepdog, TLDR, VascularColoring.

Read every target's local packs (`RULES.md` prose and any local checks), generalized each candidate, and deduped against the **whole** corpus before landing anything — most candidates were rejected as already-covered (several already promoted from these same repos in earlier runs). 20 genuinely new, portable lessons survived; all landed at the prose rung — each is judgment, in-flight/runtime behavior, or signature-less tool-usage knowledge, so none had a reliable static signature a check could carry.

One commit per landing file:

- `packs/basics/RULES.md` — Grep's silent `output_mode` default, verifying claims about real named people, an egress block vs. a publisher 403, a litmus test for cross-file comment content, piping through `tail` losing the exit code, proving a repo-scanning check silent against real sources.
- `packs/git-github/skills/git-github-advanced/SKILL.md` — a locally-refused git mutation after a server-side merge, a shallow checkout breaking `git merge-base`, preferring `git push` over the MCP file-write tools' transcription risk, recognizing a CI infrastructure outage, `get_job_logs`'s `failed_only`/`job_id` requirement.
- `packs/core/RULES.md` + `packs/core/scheduled-tasks.md` — a duplicate dispatch trigger as your own claim-echo, resolving a mounted skill's links against its real canon path rather than the `Skill` tool's announced base directory.
- `packs/grow_with_claudinite/extracting-lessons.md` — never capture a rule that teaches routing around a permission/security denial (directly relevant to this task's own judgment).
- `packs/grow_with_claudinite/skills/unattended-agents/SKILL.md` — a `[Merge Without Review]` warning on a licensed unattended merge is expected, and a background subagent sharing the parent's working directory can make its WIP/branch look like the parent's own.
- `packs/basics/skills/writing-tests/SKILL.md` + `packs/basics/skills/bug-investigation/SKILL.md` — restoring a see-it-fail mutation via `git checkout`/`stash` not a stale `.bak`, testing a retry/requeue helper twice with a different actor for identity-arbitrated mechanisms, a stateful simulator modeling what the real engine writes not the rule's stated intent, and quoting a run's own log rather than reasoning forward from a bug theory.
- `packs/headless-browser/RULES.md` — reinstalling a browser-driver package can pull a version mismatched with the environment's pinned browser.

**Notable rejections** (already covered, confirmed by reading the current canon rather than assumption): the `search_issues`/`fields`/`per_page` MCP-token-limit cluster (ClaudiniteWebsite, MissingBulbWebsite, Sheepdog, GoogleCalendarEventCreator) — already fully covered in `git-github-advanced`'s "Cap and qualify" section; `ScheduleWakeup` needing `prompt` (ClaudiniteWebsite) — already in `basics/RULES.md`; several git/GitHub, Playwright/headless-browser, HTML-parsing and research-methodology items from EdFringeNow, GoogleCalendarEventCreator, LaughCounter, MissingBulbWebsite and VascularColoring that matched existing canon rules verbatim or near-verbatim (confirming those repos were earlier promotion sources). Full per-lesson breakdown logged on the tracker issue.

No stub pack minted — every landing lesson had an existing canon owner.

{"number":2075,"title":"Dashboard: sign-in as the only way in, a GitHub-shaped account menu, and a signal for stale seeded files","body":"Three issues, one change: the two the canary's page made visible, and the canon gap under both.

Closes #2069
Closes #2070
Closes #2071

## Sign-in is the only way in (#2069)

The token provider goes, and with it the paste box, the `signin-how` fork and `credentialAdvice`'s two-way split. The two things the issue said this had to answer rather than assume:

- **An unconfigured deployment.** It cannot sign anybody in, so the gate says the dashboard is not finished being set up and names `CLAUDINITE_DASHBOARD_CLIENT_ID` and `CLAUDINITE_DASHBOARD_EXCHANGE_URL`. The standing privacy prose is hidden on that screen — it answers "what does this page do with my credential", which is not the question in front of someone who cannot get one. Those two variable names moved into one browser-safe module (`src/read/signin-vars.mjs`) that both the page and `tooling/deployment-config.mjs` read, so the gate cannot send an owner to set a variable the build ignores.
- **Local development.** `tooling/serve.mjs` reads the developer's own token from the environment (`DASHBOARD_DEV_TOKEN`, else `GITHUB_TOKEN`/`GH_TOKEN`) and hands it to the page in the config it now synthesizes — overlaid on a real `dashboard.config.json` where the checkout has one. The page keeps it for the tab only, whatever **Remember me** says, and it is a development affordance by construction: the site build writes a fixed list of config keys and `devToken` is not on it.

`pack.mjs`'s adoption handover stops being a decision and becomes an instruction, and the README's "Two ways to get one" becomes one.

## The account menu (#2070)

Header naming the account, then full-width rows of one icon and one label, sections separated by hairline rules, sign-out last. The rate pill gets a labelled row rather than floating unnamed.

**The one decision the issue asked to settle**: the caching paragraph goes behind a disclosure in the menu's last section, not onto the gate. Reload and Clear cache are the two levers whose effect it explains, so it sits with them; the gate is already the screen that explains the credential.

## Stale seeded files (#2071)

`seeded-file-stale`, a world advisory shaped like `executor-workflow-secrets`: it reads each active pack's own `seedOps` and compares the member's copy against the template that pack's *mount* ships — which is its stamped version's template, so this is the issue's first option without needing a second mechanism to carry the version.

**The comparison rule**, since exact match is too strict: the copy must carry every *significant* line of the template (comments, blanks and indentation dropped from both sides); lines the member added are its own business. So drift means "the pack moved, you did not". This costs something real and the module says so — a member that deliberately edited a template line reads as missing it, and advisory is the answer to that rather than a narrower comparison that would go quiet on exactly the reshape this exists to catch.

**Inert in this repo** — no pack declared here has `seedOps` — so its four tests carry it, each proven against a mutation of the rule.

## The removed export

Deleting `setPastedToken` trips the blocking `consumer-safe-change` check. Per your call, the discharge is a rehearsal fixture rather than a shim — and rather than a ceremonial one, it is the shape the check's own comment says no fixture had: `mount-importing`, a local pack whose rule imports the engine out of `.claudinite/shared/`. That is where a dropped canon name fails at *load*, taking the member's pack, its self-test and its whole converge with it. Verified by pointing the fixture at a name the mount does not export and watching both rehearsals go red.

## Verification

- Full suite green: 3676 pass, 0 fail.
- `check_the_world` and `check_the_work` both exit 0; the advisory set is byte-identical to `main`'s, so this adds no new findings.
- Every new test seen red first, by mutating the code it guards and restoring.
- `serve.mjs` driven for real: the synthesized config carries the token, the page still serves 200.

{"number":1645,"title":"Legacy behaves like deprecated: the guideline, the annotation, and the advisories","body":"Closes #1637

A legacy tolerance was the one thing this corpus could add with no removal written and nothing
telling its holders to move. The audit found ~28 declaration sites across `engine/` and `packs/`;
none warned anybody, and `engine/version.mjs` carried a stated end date that had passed six days
earlier with nothing arranged to notice.

## The guideline (`packs/basics`, portable)

`RULES.md` gains one rule — a tolerance is scaffolding: it ships with an advisory firing where the
old shape is still in use, and with its removal already a link in the migration's chain, gated on a
condition that reads back true rather than on a date. The *Planning a migration* bullet names that
removal among the code written before approval, and `writing-migration-plans` gains the section
behind it: the three things that ship with a tolerance, why a date gate fails in both directions,
making an unreadable gate the chain's **first link** rather than a caveat in the removal's brief,
and the asymmetry that decides between a narrow policy and `nothing`.

## The advisories — the half that reaches the holders

| Rule | Reads | Reports |
|---|---|---|
| `legacy-shape-in-use` (lifecycle) | the repo's own declaration and stamp | retired file name, `claudinite`/`maintenance` blocks, top-level `packConfig`, `taskScheduler.endpoints`, the `local_packs/` prefix, a renamed pack id, an integer version, the `updates` alias |
| `legacy-task-fields` (tasks) | `tasks/<name>/task.mjs` **source** | `agent_preprocessing*`, `prework*`, `after`, and the one-word outcome ceilings |
| `legacy-check-spellings` (growth) | `declared-checks.json` | the pre-merge `eachValueInParsedArray` spelling |
| `cer/release-workflows` (chrome-extension) | the orchestrator | its tolerated `@main` shape, which used to return silently |

All advisory, permanently: the old shape works, so none of these may stop a member's build. Each
names the edit that moves the repo forward. The task rule reads *source* because the contract's
door renames the fields away before anything downstream can see them — which is exactly what made
that tolerance invisible. Engine constants are namespace-imported and `typeof`-guarded: the two
lanes converge on separate cycles, so a pack sits beside an engine that predates a symbol, and
there the advisory simply drops rather than faulting the pack.

## The annotation — the half that schedules the removal

Every legacy declaration now carries `// @legacy-tolerance advisory:<rule|none> retire:#<issue>`
directly above it, so `grep -rn '@legacy-tolerance' engine packs` **is** the register.
`legacy-tolerance-scheduled` (local pack, blocking after its grace) holds both halves: a tolerance
with nothing above it, and an annotation the register cannot parse. It anchors at column 0, which
is what tells a tolerance point from a `const legacy =` inside a function, and its test runs it
against the real tree rather than only a fixture.

`advisory:none` claims no member file can hold the old shape; the local pack's rule obliges the
retire issue to say what does read the holder instead.

## The removals

#1638 tracks them as four links, each an ad-hoc queue item behind #1639 (the one human step: the
fleet clearance report has to exist in Shepherd before anything here can read a gate) with a
`Not-before:` giving the fleet a month of converges. #1640 and #1641 are `Automerge: nothing` —
a member holding a retired spelling gets *no* pack, loses the `update` task that would deliver its
repair, and the only way back is a hand-run against that repo. #1642 carries a narrow
predicted-folder policy; #1643 stays `nothing` because it spans four packs by construction.

`engine/version.mjs`' tolerance is re-gated here on the fleet's own state rather than the date it
missed.

## Verification

`node --test $(git ls-files '*.test.mjs')` — 3127 pass, 0 fail. `check_the_world` 0 blocking,
`ci-work-scope` clean. Each new check was seen failing before it was believed: the annotation check
against a stripped annotation in `settings-file-names.mjs`, and `legacy-shape-in-use`'s test with
two of its branches disabled (3 of 11 tests failed).

1	# product-wiki pack
2	
3	The self-growing product research wiki standard: a repo keeps its
4	market/user/competitor research as agent-maintained wikis under `product-wiki/` -
5	compile findings once, refine in place, cite everything - walled off from the
6	code so nothing can silently depend on
7	unreviewed research, with one human-reviewed crossing point. Declared by the
8	project (fingerprint: `product-wiki/product-requirements/README.md` — the sink is
9	the standard's one structural constant). Takes **no config**: the layout is the
10	standard.
11	
12	## The standard
13	
14	- `product-wiki/` at the repo root. Two reserved children with fixed meaning:
15	  **`product-wiki/product-requirements/`** — the human-reviewed distillation of the
16	  wikis into product requirements, the **only** `product-wiki/` content the rest of
17	  the repo may reference, never auto-grown — and **`product-wiki/sample-data/`** —
18	  small illustrative assets a wiki claim points to (never test fixtures).
19	- **Everything else under `product-wiki/` is wiki space** — any names, any nesting.
20	  A wiki page is a `README.md` at depth ≥ 2 under `product-wiki/` outside the two
21	  reserved subtrees. The folder is the classifier; there is no wikis manifest
22	  to drift, and a renamed wiki folder is still a wiki folder — still checked,
23	  still barred.
24	- Every wiki page **opens with `## Key insights`** — up to seven bullets, one
25	  terse plain-words line each, carrying what the research found, ahead of every
26	  other section. The body is the research record; the header is what makes it
27	  readable, so a human who reads only the header understands what was researched
28	  and what came of it.
29	- Every wiki page also carries `## Sources` (every source bullet carrying its
30	  real URL), `## Growth log` (dated bullets, newest change appended per pass),
31	  and `## Open questions` (the research backlog the growth passes work from).
32	- Growth is scheduled research: the pack's weekly scheduled task
33	  ([tasks/wiki-growth/task.md](tasks/wiki-growth/task.md)) reads
34	  the wikis, researches what their own open questions flag, writes back cited,
35	  and delivers an unmerged PR. Most passes correctly change nothing.
36	
37	## Rules (`RULES.md`)
38	
39	Two rules, for the sessions that only read the wiki:
40	
41	| Rule | Severity | Reason | Enforcement |
42	|---|---|---|---|

## Branch and commits

Branch `claude/prov-headless-browser-git-github`, off `origin/main` at `27d1ab15`. Not pushed, no PR opened. Working tree clean.

- `bb7a9d52` — Provenance: backfill headless-browser (25 files, +264 / -28)
- `a732489d` — Provenance: backfill git-github (22 files, +415 / -10)

## headless-browser

- **Files written:** 22 provenance files (`_pack` + 21 rules), all previously empty, plus a new `_declined.md`.

## git-github

- **Files written:** 19 provenance files (the 19 that were empty), plus a new `_declined.md`. The six already-filled files (`gha-checkout-submodules`, `gha-label-create-before-add`, `gha-run-pipefail`, `gha-secrets-in-job-if`, `git-github-advanced`, `merge-to-main`) were not touched.
- **Entries added:** 41. `_pack` 3 (born #384; merged #1081; reworded #1248). Skill `github-actions-scheduling` 2 (born #555; moved #1081). Seven guidelines born #555; `spacing-jobs-apart` born #623. `gha-pages-artifact-symlinks` 5 (born #158, converted #790, moved #827, moved #1081, severity-changed #1597); `gha-unique-automation-branch` 5 (born #128, …same chain); `gha-scheduled-failure-escalation` 5 (born #128, converted #790, moved #827, moved #1081, severity-changed #1597 kept repo-only) + 1 (severity-changed #1671, widened to `workflow_run`/`repository_dispatch`) = 6; `gha-no-scheduled-fleet-executor` 4 (born #242, #790, #827, #1081); `gha-cron-minute-off-the-hour` 3 (born #901, moved #1081, severity-changed #1597); the four action guards (`issue-labels-overwrite`, `pull-request-head-unqualified`, `codeload-tarball-fetch`, `search-code-lower-bound`) born #1671. Plus 1 declined entry.
- **README bytes:** 2691 → 2550. **pack.mjs bytes:** 1360 → 1044.
- `node packs/claudinite-growth/provenance.mjs check git-github` — listing printed, exit 0.

## Declined candidates

- `packs/headless-browser/provenance/_declined.md` — the Playwright/headless-browser candidates #949 rejected as already covered verbatim by this pack (EdFringeNow, GoogleCalendarEventCreator, LaughCounter, MissingBulbWebsite, VascularColoring).
- `packs/git-github/provenance/_declined.md` — the ten git/GitHub candidates #1671 kept as prose in `git-github-advanced` because none had a signature the four-moment check vocabulary can carry.

## Landed keywords: brief vs. pull request body

Every one read off the body via `pull_request_read`.

- PR #905: brief said `Refs #642`, body says **no keyword at all** — "Tracker: #642". Written as `#905 (tracker #642)`.
- PR #384: brief said `Refs #383, #385`, body says **`Fixes #383`. Refs #385**. Written as `(Fixes #383, Refs #385)`.
- PR #128: brief did not draft it; body says **`Closes #127` / `Closes #131`** (commit trailer has no ref line).
- PR #790: commit trailer `Refs #789`, body says **`Closes #789`**.
- PR #827: brief said `Refs #826`, body says **`Closes #826`**.
- PR #1060: commit trailer `Refs #1057`, body says **`Closes #1057`**.
- PR #1081: commit trailer `Refs #1079`, body says **`Closes #1079`**.
- PR #1248: commit trailer `Refs #1246`, body says **`Closes #1246`**.
- PR #1597: brief said `Refs #1596`, body says **`Closes #1596`**.
- PR #1634: commit trailer `Refs #1632`, body says **`Closes #1632`**.
- PR #555: brief said `Refs #556, #559`, body carries **no keyword** — the two issues appear only as inline parentheticals. Written as `(issues #556, #559)`.
- PR #623: brief said `Refs #624`, body carries **no issue reference at all**. Written with no issue clause.
- PR #901: brief said `Refs #864`, body says **"dispatched by #864, tracker #450"**, no keyword. Written as `(dispatch #864, tracker #450)`.
- Agreeing: #949 (`Refs #99`), #985 (`Refs #983`), #1671 (`Refs #1202, #1308, #1408, #1435, #1657, #1672`), #158 (`Refs #157`), #242 (`Refs #241`).

## `born` dates moved, with proof

All nine git-github checks were drafted `born` at **#827 "Declared checks are JSON, one file per pack"**, which only moved existing declarations into `declared-checks.json`. Corrected:

- `codeload-tarball-fetch`, `issue-labels-overwrite`, `pull-request-head-unqualified`, `search-code-lower-bound` → **#1671, 2026-09-06**. `git log -S'<id>' --reverse -- packs` returns `83f5e8d7` as the only introducing commit, and #1671's body lists all four under "Converted to checks". They did not exist at #827 (a JSON parse of `declared-checks.json` at `343a5eb0` shows nine ids, none of them these four).
- `gha/pages-artifact-symlinks` → **#158, 2026-07-07** (`a8b8c4fa`, `git log --follow packs/github-actions/pages-artifact-symlinks.mjs`, PR title "github-actions: check that a Pages artifact prunes tooling symlinks").
- `gha/unique-automation-branch`, `gha/scheduled-failure-escalation` → **#128, 2026-07-06** (`05eb43c8`, same `--follow` walk).
- `gha/no-scheduled-fleet-executor` → **#242, 2026-07-12** (`864ee44f`; its diff adds `packs/github-actions/no-scheduled-fleet-executor.mjs` with `id: 'gha/no-scheduled-fleet-executor'`).
- `gha/cron-minute-off-the-hour` → **#901, 2026-08-16** (`16400423`; converted from the scheduling skill's "Pick a minute off :00" prose, then reworked into the declaration in the same PR).

The brief also drafted `reworded` for **all nine** checks at #896, #901 and #1597 indiscriminately. #896 converted only `run-pipefail`, `checkout-submodules` and `secrets-in-job-if` (none in my set) — no entry written. #901 touched only `cron-minute-off-the-hour`. For #1597 I parsed both sides of the JSON and found exactly seven ids changed; of my set only `pages-artifact-symlinks`, `unique-automation-branch` and `cron-minute-off-the-hour` widened, and the two that stayed repo-only got an entry saying so with the reason.

`github-actions-scheduling` and its seven #555 guidelines: verified the `born` date is genuinely #555 and not a carrier move — #555's own first commit wrote the platform truth into `packs/basics/scheduled-tasks.md` and its second moved it into the new skill, so the element is born in that pull request. The later move into this pack (#1081) is its own `moved` entry.

## Other defects confirmed and corrected

- **Defect 3 confirmed for headless-browser.** The brief listed `60902.1 2026-09-02 "RULES.md drops the descriptive framing…"` under "version rows no commit here claims". `git show aaa7938b -- packs/headless-browser/VERSIONS.md` shows that commit (#1634) adding the row in its own diff. Recorded as a `_pack` entry with that version.
- **Defect 5 applied.** Worked both READMEs by reading them. headless-browser's `## Boundary` section's Provenance paragraph, the dependency-manifest justification and the prose-only justification all moved onto entries; git-github's rationale for the two repo-only checks moved onto those two entries.
- **No commit inventory row was passed blind.** Read the diffs behind #915, #969, #1060, #1081, #1105, #1108, #1248, #1634, #2009 for headless-browser and the git-github equivalents. #1060 and #1248 were "NOTHING DRAFTED" rows that did decide something (the cross-pack prose purge, the manifest convention) and now carry entries; #1108 turned out to be a "tick" → "scheduler run" terminology rename with no decision, #1081 for headless-browser only repointed an `excludes` string, and #2009 only recomputed a README table — none of those got an entry.
- **No new tool defect found** beyond the four listed (the brief's over-broad per-commit fan-out of `reworded` across all nine checks is defect 2's blast radius rather than a separate one).

## Verification

- `node engine/checks/check_the_world.mjs` → **0 blocking, 33 advisory**, none naming `headless-browser` or `git-github` (grepped). No `provenance-change-recorded` advisory fired — no file needed the sanctioned truncate-and-rewrite, since all 41 target files were genuinely empty.
- `node --test packs/git-github/test/pack.test.mjs` → 35 pass, exit 0. `headless-browser` carries no `test/` directory.
- No long dashes in anything written (the five pre-existing git-github provenance files that carry them were not touched).
- No carrier changed: the diff is `provenance/`, `README.md` and `pack.mjs` for the two packs only. No `VERSIONS.md` row, no version bump.

## One thing to note

Neither commit references a tracking issue — I was not given its number. Add `Refs #<n>` in the PR bodies if the aggregation needs it.

{"number":384,"title":"Vendored-mount surface shrink: engine/ consolidation, skills into packs, no CI stub, minimal CLAUDE.md + .gitignore","body":"Phase-2 continuation (mount/DESIGN — now `engine/mount/DESIGN.md`), driven interactively from the EdFringeNow pilot (missingbulb/EdFringeNow#73). Owner directives from #385, one commit per decision (to be squashed on merge):

1. **mount-skills owns legacy symlinks** so stale mounts retarget instead of shadowing the vendored skills (#383, test red-first).
2. **CI conformance stub retired** — the Stop hook (`check_the_work`) is the whole enforcement surface: it runs the same sweep and blocks before Claude reports done; edits made outside sessions surface at the next session's Stop.
3. **Consumer `.gitignore` contract collapses to the two hook-log lines** — the vendored world writes nothing untracked into `.claudinite/`.
4. **Skills move into their owning packs** — `<pack>/skills/<skill>/` is the one shape (every skill already had exactly one declarer; the two canon-maintainer skills join `canon-curation`'s bundle). The `pack.mjs` `skills` key, the skills union + `extraSkills` in vendoring, and the `skill-ownership` check are gone — ownership is placement. A bundled skill's `checks.mjs` rides its pack's activation uniformly. The adoption-interview machinery lives in the adoption skill, resolved fail-soft by the engine.
5. **The engine consolidates under `engine/`** — `engine/hooks/` (session-start.sh, inject-preferences.sh, pretooluse-guard.mjs), `engine/check_the_world.mjs` (the sweep CLI, was `checks/run.mjs`), `engine/check_the_work.mjs` (the Stop hook, was `stop-hook.mjs`), `engine/checks_helpers/` (was `checks/lib/`), `engine/pack_loader/`, `engine/skill_loader/`, `engine/mount/`. The vendor set contract is now "engine/ wholesale + declared packs + `CLAUDE.md`"; pack-independence's allow list is the single `engine` root. Consumer wiring migrates via the `engine-restructure` note; pre-flip members keep working through forwarding transition shims at the old fetched-tree paths, retired with the note.
6. **Corpus-index `CLAUDE.md` shrinks to near-nothing** (a session's rules arrive injected — no architecture lesson), the maintainer map moving to README.md; the consumer **self-check paragraph is retired** — a consumer's root `CLAUDE.md` is just the `@`-import line.
7. **`--init` seeds only `{ packs, maintenance }`** — no empty `rules`/`accept` boilerplate.

Verified: 490/490 tests green, conformance sweep clean, the session-start orchestrator runs all five steps from the new layout in the canon.

# claudinite-canon-curation

Curation duties for a **canon** — a repo whose own `packs/` tree is a shelf of Claudinite packs
that other repos vendor. Declaring this pack is what makes a repo that canon's home: it takes on
promoting its members' lessons onto the shelf, sweeping the fleet's stacks for technologies the
shelf does not yet home, keeping what the shelf already teaches current with those technologies,
and policing the shelf's own content.

Nothing in the pack names a particular canon. The shelf is `packs/` because that is where the
engine reads a canon's packs from, so every rule and task here is anchored there and is inert in a
repo that keeps no shelf. `hidden`, never seeded, no fingerprint: a canon home is a role somebody
assigns, so the pack is declared by hand.

A canon that runs Claudinite as an ordinary member reads its own packs from the mount, so its shelf
is content it *publishes* rather than content it runs — and the rules here are what police it. The
Claudinite home repo is the one exception, running the engine from its own root, and that changes
nothing about this pack.

**Declaration cardinality is the mechanism.** A pack's tasks run once per *declaring* repo, so a
canon declared by its one home repo yields exactly one work item per task per occurrence — "central,
once" with no bespoke orchestrator step. Un-declaring the pack freezes canon absorption without
touching the members' side ([claudinite-growth](../claudinite-growth/README.md)).

## Configuration

The pack entry takes one optional key, read by [canon-config.mjs](canon-config.mjs):

```json
{ "id": "claudinite-canon-curation", "config": { "write_paths": ["packs", "skills"] } }
```

`write_paths` names any corpus root **beside** the `packs/` shelf that a promoted lesson may land
in — a canon that organizes some shared content outside its shelf says so here. The shelf is always
a corpus root and is never removable. Unset is the ordinary case, not a misconfiguration.

The two fleet tasks reach every member, so both declare `invocation_endpoint: 'fleet'` — a key into
the declaring repo's own `taskScheduler.endpoints`, mapping to a routine whose sources are that repo
**and every participating member**. That cross-repo reach is the whole reason a second endpoint
exists, and is exactly what must stay off the endpoint an ordinary hand-off calls. Reach is a
property of **which endpoint is called**, and of nothing else: there is no session scope anywhere in
the system, and no label routes a hand-off ([the writing-tasks
skill](../claudinite-growth/skills/writing-tasks/SKILL.md)). An endpoint the repo has not configured
— or one whose token secret is unset — converges the item to human triage naming what is missing,
on the item itself; if a task has quietly stopped producing anything, its most recent work item says
why.

## What it carries

| Task | Runs when | Where it lands |
|---|---|---|
| `growth-promote` | a participating member changed its local packs in the window | a PR against the canon's default branch |
| `growth-discover-packs` | weekly, over every covered member | a PR against the canon's default branch, plus an adopt issue in each member that evidenced the pack |
| `revalidate-from-source` | monthly, over the packs that declared an upstream source | a PR against the canon's default branch, superseding the month before's if it is still open |
| `pack-version-bump` | daily when commits landed under `packs/`, and on every push to the canon's default branch (its workflow) | a commit straight onto the canon's default branch |
| `pack-version-history` | weekly, when commits landed under `packs/` | a self-landing PR touching only `packs/*/provenance/VERSIONS.md` |
| `canon-prose-to-checks` | weekly, on a canon somebody worked in that week | a PR converting the shelf's always-testable prose into checks |
| `canon-rule-revalidation` | weekly | corrections to shelf rules whose environment claim no longer probes true |

### Rules (`RULES.md`)

| Rule | Severity | Reason | Enforcement |

| Growth actions over the shelf | high | correctness | prose: <50 words |

### Checks

| Check | Severity | Reason | Enforcement |
|---|---|---|---|
| `pack-no-enforcement-narration` | medium | complexity | check: blocking |
| `pack-discovery-entry-await` | critical | correctness | check: blocking |
| `pack-version-log-ordered` | high | correctness | check: blocking |
| `skill-no-enforcement-narration` | medium | complexity | check: blocking |
| `pack-independence` | high | correctness | declared check: blocking |

`pack-independence` and `tasks-stage-barriers` are barrier **data**, not code: `forbidReferences`
entries in [declared-checks.json](declared-checks.json), compiled by the engine's reference
scanning. The [barrier guide](../basics/barriers.md) documents the edge vocabulary.

- `tasks-stage-barriers` holds the tasks pack's role graph one-directional — `contract/` and
  `items/` name no stage, `world/` carries no stage's policy, and a stage imports only what sits
  below it. `tasks-world-edges-live-in-world` is its other half: GitHub, the environment,
  subprocesses and the clock are reached through that pack's `src/world/` and nowhere else, so a
  run can be driven at a chosen instant against a fake world. The pack is guarded from OUTSIDE by
  `tasks-pack-read-through-its-surface`, which it declares itself — a consumer reads it through
  `public/` or not at all, and that cannot be a barrier here because the reference scanner
  never sees a test file and this pack's checks never reach a member's own tree.

- **[tasks/growth-promote/](tasks/growth-promote/task.md)** — the growth lifecycle's central stage:
  read the changed members' local packs, **generalize** the portable lessons, route each to the
  right home on the shelf, and open a PR for the owner to approve. When a portable lesson's
  technology has no pack home, it mints a fingerprinted **stub pack** (in its own dedicated PR).
  This is the sole judgment gate before shared canon.
- **[tasks/growth-discover-packs/](tasks/growth-discover-packs/task.md)** — the weekly **fleet
  sweep** for technologies the shelf does not yet home: read every member's stack, fold the members
  into one view (so first-sight dedup is free — the third member using a technology is the same gap
  as the first), and open an owner-reviewed PR authoring the missing `packs/<tech>/`. A pack is
  authored because particular members' files demonstrated it, so each of those members also gets an
  issue asking it to adopt the pack once the PR merges and its mount carries it. It is the only
  stage that authors a pack at all — a member's local packs are what adoption seeded, and
  growth-extract writes rules into those. (Promote's stub-minting is narrower still: one lesson's
  technology, minted as a seed; this task authors from the whole fleet's usage.)
- **[tasks/revalidate-from-source/](tasks/revalidate-from-source/task.md)** — the monthly reconciliation of the
  shelf against the technologies it teaches: read what each declared source has published since its
  anchor, correct the packs that were dated by it, and advance the anchors. **Keeping a pack current
  is the canon's duty, not the pack's** — a pack's tasks are work a member repo runs, so a pack
  watching its own technology would put the duty on every consumer and make it unrepeatable. It
  reads no member and no member's dependency versions; the shelf is the whole subject.

  A pack opts in with an `## Upstream` section in its `README.md`, one line per source:

  ```md
  ## Upstream

  - **RFC 8725 — JWT Best Current Practices** — https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc8725
    — reconciled through RFC 8725 (BCP 225), February 2020
  ```

  What to watch, where it publishes, and the state the pack's content was last reconciled
  against — the anchor the next run windows on, advanced only for a source that run actually
  read. Silence is opt-out: a pack with no section is one nobody has claimed a moving upstream
  for, and this task does not give it one. The reason a source is worth watching, and what a
  reconciliation concluded, belong in the pack's `references.md`.

- **[tasks/pack-version-bump/](tasks/pack-version-bump/README.md)** — the one writer of a pack's
  `version`. A pack's directory reaches a member only when the canon's number exceeds the
  member's, so every shipping change needs a fresh one and no two changes may share one; the
  worker reads the base branch after a merge, finds each pack's last bump and cuts today's next
  version for every pack with a shipping change since. A pull request never bumps a pack itself,
  and no check asks it to. The canon's `pack-versions.yml` workflow runs the same worker on every
  push to the default branch; the daily task covers the merges GitHub turns into no push run.
- **[tasks/pack-version-history/](tasks/pack-version-history/README.md)** — the weekly derivation
  of each pack's `VERSIONS.md` from git: which pull requests landed between one version and the
  next. Rows already written stand; only the versions with no row gain one.
- **[item-routing.md](item-routing.md)** — the shared worthiness + routing method promote (and an
  owner-requested retrospective pass) defers to, so every decision about admitting and placing an
  item is made the same way.
- **[promote-scope.mjs](promote-scope.mjs)** — the write-surface gate on promote's PRs: promote may
  write only under the corpus roots above. The canon's own CI invokes its `runCli`, keyed on the
  promote branch prefix; nothing in a tree marks a diff as a promote run, so the gate cannot
  self-gate.
- **[skills/extract-packs-from-a-project/](skills/extract-packs-from-a-project/SKILL.md)** — the
  pack-writing method both tasks above apply: decompose a project into its facets, sort its rules to
  the one owner each, author the packs those facets earn. Whether a project's insight becomes a pack
  every repo can declare is the canon's call, so the method sits with the stages that make it rather
  than in what a member reads.
- **[skills/writing-claudinite-skills/](skills/writing-claudinite-skills/SKILL.md)** — authoring a
  skill in the corpus. Canon-side activity: a member authors no corpus skills.

## The growth lifecycle — three independent stages, no barriers

How a lesson is learned in a consuming project, lifted onto the shelf when it's portable, and pruned
back out of the project once the canon owns it. Two packs split it by who declares them:
**[claudinite-growth](../claudinite-growth/README.md)** (member-side: extract + dedup, seeded,
opt-out by removal) and **claudinite-canon-curation** (this pack, the central stage).

**The corpus is what splits them, not the action.** A growth task writes
`.claudinite/local/packs/` exclusively — in a member the shelf is a read-only mount the next
converge replaces whole — so the two actions that also need doing *to the shelf*, converting its
prose to checks and revalidating its environmental claims, are this pack's `canon-prose-to-checks`
and `canon-rule-revalidation`. They load the growth pack's skills for the method and differ from
their member-side twins only in the corpus their worker names and the policy that bounds it
(`under:packs` here, `under:.claudinite/local` there).

```
EXTRACT   per member    → auto-merging PR against the member's default branch  (claudinite-growth)
PROMOTE   central, once → PR against the canon's default branch                (this pack)

content.content:
PROMOTE   central, once → PR against the canon's default branch                (this pack)
DEDUP     per member    → PR against the member's default branch               (claudinite-growth)
```

All three are ordinary, **independent** planner units — there is no barrier and no phase ordering.
Each stage reads only what is already **merged**: promote processes whatever sits on members'
default branches when it runs, so a lesson extracted tonight is promoted **tomorrow** night (the
extract PR's merge shows up in the next night's local-pack signal), and reaches other members' dedup
once the promote PR is approved and merged. That approval was always the dominant latency, so
barrier machinery would buy little; if the cadence ever matters, promote can run more often without
any design change.

**Review gates by blast radius, not uniformly.** Promote opens a PR — it's the sole judgment gate
before the shared canon every member reads, so it always needs a human eye. Dedup opens a PR too — a
wrongful prune deletes a real local lesson. Extract lands through an **auto-merging PR** against the
member's default branch — it writes only that project's own local packs, so it earns a CI gate and a
PR trail but not a human reviewer; auto-merge keeps the fleet's daily lesson-capture from flooding
review requests.

**Central execution, no plumbing.** Promote runs from the canon home repo with a fleet-wide token,
so it reads every participating member and opens its canon PR directly there — no consumer-side
Action, no cross-repo PAT, no labelled-issue up-path. The planner hands its gate the `fleetMembers`
aggregate (which members changed, and what they declare), and the gate hands the worker the changed
participants as `targets`.

The session-scoped sibling of this nightly lifecycle — mining a single working session for lessons —
lives with [the growth pack's extract-from-conversations
skill](../claudinite-growth/skills/extract-from-conversations/SKILL.md), and the member-side method
docs (extract, dedup, and how a project's local packs are identified) live with
[claudinite-growth](../claudinite-growth/README.md).

# core

Claudinite's own surface in a repo that runs it: the vendored mount, the declaration that activates a
pack, adopting Claudinite and adopting a pack, and the contract every scheduled task is written to.

**Mandatory.** `basics` `requires` this pack, so the closure vendors its content and materializes its
declaration wherever a declaration is written; the one-time `core-seed` migration record declares it
into members that already exist. Removing the entry is not an opt-out — it is drift, and `claudinite-lifecycle-declared`
reports it.

## Rules (`RULES.md`)

| Rule | Severity | Reason | Enforcement |
|---|---|---|---|
| Reading a rule that arrived from Claudinite | high | correctness | prose: <50 words + checks (`shared-tree-edit-guard`, `shared-tree-immutable`, `claudinite-isolation`) |
| Finding a mounted skill's real path | medium | complexity | prose: <100 words |
| Wanting a pack's rules to apply here | high | correctness | prose: <50 words + check (`claudinite-lifecycle-declared`) |
| Adding a pack | medium | complexity | prose: <50 words |
| Setting a project up on Claudinite | medium | complexity | prose: <20 words |
| Deciding which pack owns a lesson | medium | complexity | prose: <100 words |
| Judging whether Claudinite is current here | medium | correctness | prose: <100 words |
| Answering "why did the mount not update" | medium | correctness | prose: <50 words |
| A referenced file absent from the mount | medium | correctness | prose: <100 words |
| An engine comment citing a design doc | low | complexity | prose: <100 words |
| A silent check run is clean | low | complexity | prose: <50 words |
| Pushing a change the world sweep scans | medium | complexity | prose: <50 words |

## Checks

Each of these asks the same kind of question: **is Claudinite working in this repo** — declared,
converged, gated, scheduled. A repo can fail any of them silently, which is why they are checks and
not prose: the session that has lost its rules is the session least able to notice.

| Check | Severity | Reason | Enforcement |
|---|---|---|---|
| `claudinite-lifecycle-declared` | critical | correctness | check: blocking |
| `rules-index-current` | critical | correctness | check: blocking |
| `claudinite-isolation` | high | complexity | check: blocking |
| `shared-tree-edit-guard` | high | correctness | check: blocking |
| `shared-tree-immutable` | high | correctness | check: advisory |
| `conformance-workflow` | high | correctness | check: advisory |
| `conformance-work-scope` | high | correctness | check: advisory |
| `seeded-file-stale` | high | correctness | check: advisory |
| `scheduler-workflow-shape` | high | correctness | check: blocking |
| `legacy-shape-in-use` | medium | complexity | check: advisory |
| `skill-loaded-before-editing` | high | correctness | check: blocking |
| `skills-index-current` | medium | correctness | check: blocking |

What goes wrong when one fires:

- `claudinite-lifecycle-declared` — this pack's entry is gone from `.claudinite-settings.json`, so none of the rules above run and the session cannot tell.
- `rules-index-current` — the generated index is missing, stale or unimported: the repo's packs contribute no prose to any session.
- `claudinite-isolation` — the repo's own code reaches into `.claudinite/`, so the next canon refactor is a breaking migration for code the canon does not own (a declared `forbidReferences` barrier edge).
- `conformance-workflow` — nothing in CI runs the world sweep unfiltered on a pull request, so conformance is ungated and the maintenance PR never lands.
- `conformance-work-scope` — CI gates the tree but not the change, so every commit-scoped rule is enforced only where a session's Stop hook happens to run.
- `seeded-file-stale` — a file some pack seeded at adoption has fallen behind that pack's template, and since a seeded file is never converged nothing else would ever say so: the member goes on running a copy whose pack has moved.
- `scheduler-workflow-shape` — the vendored scheduler's cron, concurrency or dispatch guard has drifted: staggering, double-run safety or manual runs break.

The **task contract** and its checks are deliberately NOT here. Those ask whether a task is
*written* correctly, which is authoring; every check above asks whether Claudinite is *working* in
this repo. They live with the rest of the authoring surface.

The scope cuts the other way too: a rule about how the **canon's own** content is maintained is not
this pack's, however much it looks like one. `catalog-completeness` — `packs/README.md` lists every
`packs/<name>/` — reads as Claudinite machinery and is not: it can only fire in the corpus repo, and
what it guards is a hand-maintained index, not a member's status. It stays with the other
doc-integrity rules.

`skill-loaded-before-editing` is the Stop-time half of **path-scoped skills**: a skill names
the files it must be loaded for under `force-load-on-file-edits-paths` in its SKILL.md frontmatter
`metadata` (the harness's own `paths` is a limiter on when it offers a skill, so it cannot carry
this), the engine's PreToolUse guard holds a file tool aimed there until the session has
loaded that skill, and this rule catches the edits the guard never saw (a `sed`, a heredoc) by
asking the diff the same question. Both read one resolver,
`engine/pack_loader/path-scoped-skills.mjs`. A load is a `Skill` tool call or a `Read` of the
skill's own SKILL.md. `skills-index-current` keeps the generated
`.claudinite/claudinite-skills.GENERATED.md` — every mounted skill with what loads it, the
scoped ones first — naming what the declared packs actually bundle.

## Skills

| Skill | For |
|---|---|
| [`adopt-claudinite`](skills/adopt-claudinite/SKILL.md) | setting a project up on Claudinite for the first time — mount, hooks, checks, skills — and re-baselining one to pick up updates |
| [`adopt-pack`](skills/adopt-pack/SKILL.md) | adding a pack to a repo that already runs Claudinite: declare, interview, re-vendor, scaffold, land |

The adoption skills bundle two more checks of the same kind, over the answers a member stores
against each declared pack's questions:

| Check | Severity | Reason | Enforcement |
|---|---|---|---|
| `adoption-answers-pending` | medium | complexity | check: blocking |
| `interview-answer-stale` | low | complexity | check: advisory |

## Tasks

| Task | when it runs | Runs when |
|---|---|---|
| `update` | `due:daily` | the mount is behind the canon, or a declared pack moved |
| `adopt-requested-packs` | never — no `preconditions`; only from the item the fleet places | the repo carries an open pack-adoption request |

`update` is the per-repo self-refresh — the task that converges a member's mount and stamps it. It
is why `claudinite-lifecycle-declared` is blocking: a member runs `update` from its **vendored** copy, and
`discoverTasks` finds only a literally-declared pack's tasks, so a repo that loses this pack's entry
loses its self-refresh, and nothing is left that could deliver it one. That is also why the task
arrived here a change later than the rest of the pack — it moved only once every non-dormant member's
declaration had been read back and confirmed to carry `core`.

`legacy-shape-in-use.md` is one of the 23 files that agent is filling right now, on a base predating #1917 — so the fix is a rebase plus one appended entry, not a conflict. Same for `git-github-advanced.md`, which is conversion-filled and needs a `strengthened` entry for the two sections #2206 added; since today's date falls after its placeholder `2026-09-14`, a plain `append` takes it without the truncate-and-rewrite dance.

Three packs verified so far, all exact:

| Pack | Files | Entries | README | pack.mjs |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `flutter` | 17+`_declined` | 30 | 3294→3314 | 2328→1865 |
| `firebase` | 16+6 rewritten | 47 | 3483→3733 | 1825→1144 |

Two genuinely new tool defects came out of this one, neither in the filed issues, and both explain damage already done. First: the wrong `Landed` keyword isn't merely a per-PR derivation a reader corrects once — `brief` pre-fills it into the `entry-defaults` fence, which `apply` then copies onto *every* entry beneath it. On #165 alone that single wrong keyword would have reached 29 entries across two packs. That is the mechanism by which [#2213](https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/pull/2213) shipped eleven wrong lines from one mistake. Second: a file holding only the conversion's entry is invisible in both outputs — `check` marks it not-empty, `brief` drafts nothing for it — so six firebase files carried a `born` date six weeks off and nothing in the tooling pointed at them. A run working the printed lists literally would have left all six. I'll add both to the issues rather than leave them in a transcript.

> ⚠️ Still open: three agents running (`claudinite-canon-curation`+`web-speech`, `claudinite-lifecycle`+`claudinite-fleet-sheepdog`, `product-wiki`+`spec-driven-product`). Five packs verified, none pushed. Flagging in case you want a deeper hop.

## Tool defects beyond the six listed

1. **`brief` invents `reworded` drafts from a whole-file diff.** At #1779 it drafted `reworded` for `pack-independence`, `tasks-stage-barriers` and `tasks-world-edges-live-in-world`; `git show 899a087d -- packs/claudinite-canon-curation/declared-checks.json` shows that commit adds four *other* ids and touches none of those three. Two of them did not yet exist. Same shape in web-speech: #908 drafted `reworded` for `web-speech-capture-released-on-pagehide` and `web-speech-recognition-feature-detected`, whose declarations that commit does not touch. So a draft against a multi-entry JSON file must be checked per id, not per file.
2. **`brief` classifies a carrier *conversion* as `reworded`.** Every coded-module → declaration move (#827, #908, #839, #361) drafted `reworded` with no `Mechanism`; the correct kind is `converted`, which the skill requires `Mechanism` on. Similarly a task's `automerge`/`expected_outcome`/precondition change (#1563, #1822, #2045) drafts `reworded` where the kind is `policy-changed`, and a relocation (#1674, #384) drafts `reworded` where it is `moved`.
3. **The brief's element list is scoped to `packs/<pack>/`, so it misses a pack's own pre-relocation history entirely.** web-speech's skill and its two checks lived at the repo root `skills/web-speech-io/` until #384; canon-curation lived at `packs/canon-curation/` then `.claudinite/local_packs/canon-curation/` until #1541. Neither path appears in the commit inventory, which is the structural cause of most of the wrong `born` dates above — not just the "named by the file carrying it today" case in defect 2.
4. **Defect 3 confirmed and generalized.** web-speech's "version rows no commit here claims" listed 60904.1, 60903.1 and 60902.1; all three are claimed (#1693, #1647, #1634 respectively, each of which touches `VERSIONS.md` in its own diff).
5. Confirmed defect 1 (13 disagreements above), defect 2, defect 3 and defect 5 (web-speech's "README sentences that read as history" printed `(none)` while the README carried a whole `## Provenance` section). Defect 4 did not bite: both packs' owed files were genuinely empty, so `apply` took them in date order with no truncation needed. Defect 6 did not bite either — web-speech's `checks.mjs` aggregator was deleted at #908, and all three of its check ids have their own provenance files today.

One judgment call to flag: I kept the `Model` field the brief derives from each historical commit trailer (e.g. `Claude Fable 5, per the commit trailer`), reading your "no model identifier beyond that trailer" constraint as being about *my* attribution rather than about the provenance grammar's own evidence field. Say the word if you want those stripped.

A repo that still says `updates` reads as `invalid` — undeclared, with the offending value attached — which resolves to the default, which is `versioned`, which is what that repo meant. `servedByUpdates` still answers `true` there, so nothing is wedged, and no production caller reads `.invalid`.

The advisory that named this shape (`legacy-shape-in-use`) had a guard that made it go inert the moment the constant left. That would have retired the advisory together with the thing it was warning about, so it now carries the name as a literal and says what a member actually gets: a declaration nothing recognises, served from the default.

The `engine/scheduler/` shims that originally justified it are gone from the canon, but what holds the line now is the lane itself: a member that never declared `claudinite-tasks` carries the pack *only* because of this, and the pack lane would stop delivering it with no error anywhere — the silent failure the issue names.
